0. ROOT STATEMENT

For every
  \nu > 0,  0 < T < \infty,
  u_0 \in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3),  div u_0 = 0,

define the solution sets \mathscr E, \mathscr N, \mathscr M,
\mathscr V and \mathscr D in Section 2. Then

  \mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T) = \mathscr N_\nu(u_0;T),

  \mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T) \cong \mathscr M_\nu(u_0;T)
                         \cong \mathscr D_\nu(u_0;T),

  \mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T) \cong \mathscr V_\nu(u_0;T).

All bijections are explicitly defined below. Their inverses preserve initial
data, the time interval, pressure normalization, kinetic energy, and viscous
dissipation. They commute with restriction to shorter time intervals.

Interpretation:
  NSE = incompressible Newtonian continuum mechanics
        with the specified constitutive law
        \sigma = -p I + 2\nu D(u).

The theorem concerns a continuum configuration space of infinite dimension.
Finite-dimensional mechanics occurs in the exact shear subsystem of
Section 12 and the finite Galerkin lift of Section 13.

1. SCOPE, NOTATION, AND CONFIGURATION SPACE

1.1. Fixed geometry and physical parameters

  \Omega := \mathbb T^3 = \mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3,
  \int_\Omega 1\,dx = 1,
  \rho := 1,
  \nu > 0,
  f := 0,
  t \in [0,T].

The density normalization identifies the dynamic and kinematic viscosities.
No boundary traction condition is needed on the periodic domain.

All fields in the root theorem are jointly C^\infty in time and space,
up to the temporal endpoints. Smoothness up to endpoints means that all
one-sided endpoint derivatives extend continuously.

  C^\infty_\sigma(\Omega)
  := {v \in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3): div v = 0}.

No zero-mean condition on velocity is imposed. Spatially constant
divergence-free test fields are included.

1.2. Matrix conventions

Eulerian indices: i,j,k \in {1,2,3}.
Material indices: \alpha,\beta,\gamma \in {1,2,3}.
Repeated indices are summed.

  (D_x u)_{ij} := \partial_{x_j}u_i,
  (D_a V)_{i\alpha} := \partial_{a_\alpha}V_i,

  (div_x Q)_i := \partial_{x_j}Q_{ij},
  (Div_a M)_i := \partial_{a_\alpha}M_{i\alpha}.

Scalar gradients are column vectors. Matrix norms and pairings are
Frobenius norms and pairings unless an operator norm is explicitly indicated.

  D(u) := (D_xu + (D_xu)^{\mathsf T})/2,
  D_tu := \partial_tu + (u\cdot\nabla)u,
  E(u) := (1/2)\int_\Omega |u|^2 dx.

Pressure normalization:
  \int_\Omega p(t,x)\,dx = 0  for every t.

1.3. Material configurations

  Q := Diff^\infty_{\mathrm{vol},0}(\Omega),

the identity component of the smooth orientation-preserving
volume-preserving diffeomorphism group.

A smooth material path satisfies
  \eta(t)\in Q,
  \eta(0)=id.

Its identity-normalized lift has the form
  \widetilde\eta(t,a)=a+\xi(t,a),
  \xi(t,a+m)=\xi(t,a),  m\in\mathbb Z^3.

Hence the following derivatives are globally well-defined:
  V := \partial_t\eta,
  F := D_a\eta,
  A := F^{-1},
  J := det F.

For paths in Q:
  J \equiv 1.

The inverse \eta(t)^{-1} is jointly smooth by the parameter-dependent
inverse-function theorem.

2. THE FIVE SOLUTION SETS

2.1. Eulerian NSE: \mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T)

Pairs (u,p) satisfying

  u_t + (u\cdot\nabla)u = -\nabla p + \nu\Delta u,             (E1)
  div u = 0,                                               (E2)
  u(0)=u_0,                                                (E3)
  \int_\Omega p(t,x)\,dx=0.                                (E4)

Both u and p are smooth in the sense of Section 1.

2.2. Newtonian material momentum balance: \mathscr N_\nu(u_0;T)

Smooth pairs (u,p) satisfying (E2)--(E4), with

  \sigma(u,p) := -pI+\nu(D_xu+(D_xu)^{\mathsf T}),             (N1)

and, for the identity-normalized flow \eta_u of u,

  d/dt \int_{\eta_u(t,A_0)} u(t,x)\,dx
    = \int_{\partial(\eta_u(t,A_0))}\sigma(t,x)n\,dS            (N2)

for EVERY smooth material region A_0 \subset \Omega.
In particular, all sufficiently small smooth coordinate balls are allowed.

The constitutive law (N1) is part of the definition.
Whole-torus momentum conservation alone is not the predicate (N2).

2.3. Material Newtonian system: \mathscr M_\nu(u_0;T)

Smooth pairs (\eta,\pi), with \eta(t)\in Q, satisfying

  \eta_{tt}
    = -A^{\mathsf T}\nabla_a\pi
      +\nu Div_a(D_aV\,A A^{\mathsf T}),                     (M1)

  \eta(0)=id,  V(0)=u_0,                                   (M2)
  \int_\Omega\pi(t,a)\,da=0.                               (M3)

Here V=\eta_t and A=(D_a\eta)^{-1}.

The diffusion order under the stated convention is exactly

  D_aV\,A A^{\mathsf T}
    = D_aV\,F^{-1}F^{-\mathsf T}.

The constraint \eta(t)\in Q includes det D_a\eta=1 and global
invertibility; neither is omitted from the definition.

2.4. Reduced Lagrange-d'Alembert system: \mathscr V_\nu(u_0;T)

Smooth velocities u with div u=0 and u(0)=u_0 satisfying, for every

  w \in \mathscr W :=
  {w\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\Omega;\mathbb R^3):
       div w=0,\ w(0,\cdot)=w(T,\cdot)=0},

the identity

  \int_0^T\int_\Omega
     u\cdot[w_t+(u\cdot\nabla)w-(w\cdot\nabla)u]\,dx\,dt
    -\nu\int_0^T\int_\Omega D_xu:D_xw\,dx\,dt
  = 0.                                                       (V1)

The test class includes spatial constants multiplied by smooth
time functions vanishing at the endpoints.

2.5. Material Lagrange-d'Alembert system: \mathscr D_\nu(u_0;T)

Smooth paths \eta(t)\in Q with \eta(0)=id and \eta_t(0)=u_0.
For v\in T_\eta Q, define

  L(\eta,v) := (1/2)\int_\Omega |v(a)|^2\,da,

  R(\eta,v) :=
    (\nu/2)\int_\Omega
      |D_x(v\circ\eta^{-1})(x)|^2\,dx.

Let \eta_s(t) be any smooth variation through Q with

  \eta_{s=0}(t)=\eta(t),
  \eta_s(0)=\eta(0),
  \eta_s(T)=\eta(T),

and put W:=\partial_s\eta_s|_{s=0}. Require

  d/ds|_{s=0}\int_0^T L(\eta_s,\partial_t\eta_s)\,dt
    -\int_0^T D_vR(\eta,\eta_t)[W]\,dt
  = 0.                                                       (D1)

The derivative D_vR is the fibre derivative at fixed \eta.
It is not the total constrained variation of R along \eta_s.

The initial velocity is a condition on the solution path.
The virtual variations fix the endpoint configurations.

Lemma FLOW_VOLUME. For every smooth u on [0,T]\times\Omega, the system

  \eta_t(t,a)=u(t,\eta(t,a)),  \eta(0,a)=a                    (3.1)

has a unique smooth flow of diffeomorphisms on the whole interval.

Proof.
The periodic lift of u and its spatial derivatives are bounded on
[0,T]\times\Omega. The classical smooth ODE theorem applies uniformly
on every bounded time interval. Compactness precludes spatial escape.
The reversed-time ODE from any (t,x) supplies the inverse flow.
Smooth dependence on parameters supplies joint smoothness.

Differentiate (3.1) in a:

  F_t=((D_xu)\circ\eta)F.                                   (3.2)

Jacobi's determinant formula and cyclicity of the trace give

  J_t
    =J tr(F^{-1}F_t)
    =J tr(F^{-1}((D_xu)\circ\eta)F)
    =J(div u)\circ\eta.                                     (3.3)

Thus div u=0 and J(0)=1 imply J=1.

Conversely, for a smooth path \eta(t)\in Q, define

  u:=V\circ\eta^{-1}.                                       (3.4)

Then (3.2)--(3.3) hold, and J=1 implies div u=0.

Finally,

  V_t
    =\partial_t[u(t,\eta(t,a))]
    =[u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u]\circ\eta
    =(D_tu)\circ\eta.                                       (3.5)

The initial-value identity is

  u(0)=V(0)\circ\eta(0)^{-1}=u_0.                           (3.6)

This proves FLOW_VOLUME. \square

Lemma PIOLA_TRANSFORM. Let \eta be a smooth orientation-preserving
diffeomorphism, F=D_a\eta, A=F^{-1}, J=det F. For every smooth
Eulerian matrix field Q,

  (div_x Q)\circ\eta
    = J^{-1}Div_a(J(Q\circ\eta)A^{\mathsf T}).                (4.1)

Proof.
The cofactor entries in dimension three are

  (cof F)_{i\alpha}
    =(1/2)\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{\alpha\beta\gamma}
      (\partial_\beta\eta_j)(\partial_\gamma\eta_k).

Therefore

  \partial_\alpha(cof F)_{i\alpha}=0.                        (4.2)

In the first differentiated term, the second derivatives are symmetric
in \alpha,\beta and contract against the antisymmetric epsilon tensor.
In the second term, the cancellation uses \alpha,\gamma.

Since cof F=JA^{\mathsf T},

  \partial_\alpha(JA_{\alpha j})=0.                         (4.3)

Consequently,

  [Div_a(J(Q\circ\eta)A^{\mathsf T})]_i
    =\partial_\alpha[JQ_{ij}(\eta)A_{\alpha j}]
    =JA_{\alpha j}(\partial_{x_k}Q_{ij})(\eta)F_{k\alpha}
    =J(\partial_{x_j}Q_{ij})(\eta),

because F_{k\alpha}A_{\alpha j}=\delta_{kj}.
This proves (4.1). \square

Lemma MATERIAL_DIFFERENTIALS. With V=u\circ\eta and \pi=p\circ\eta,

  (D_xu)\circ\eta=D_aV\,A,                                  (4.4)
  (\nabla_xp)\circ\eta=A^{\mathsf T}\nabla_a\pi,              (4.5)
  (\Delta_xu)\circ\eta
    =J^{-1}Div_a(JD_aV\,AA^{\mathsf T}).                     (4.6)

Proof.
The chain rule gives

  D_aV=((D_xu)\circ\eta)F,
  \nabla_a\pi=F^{\mathsf T}((\nabla_xp)\circ\eta).

This proves (4.4)--(4.5).
Apply (4.1) with Q=D_xu to obtain (4.6). \square

For incompressible material paths, J=1, so

  (\Delta_xu)\circ\eta=Div_a(D_aV\,AA^{\mathsf T}).            (4.7)

Theorem EULERIAN_MATERIAL_IFF. The maps

  \Phi(u,p):=(\eta_u,p\circ\eta_u),

  \Psi(\eta,\pi):=
       (\eta_t\circ\eta^{-1},\pi\circ\eta^{-1})

are inverse bijections

  \Phi:\mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T)\longrightarrow\mathscr M_\nu(u_0;T),
  \Psi:\mathscr M_\nu(u_0;T)\longrightarrow\mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T).

Proof: forward direction.
By Section 3, \eta_u(t)\in Q and \eta_u(0)=id.
Pull (E1) back by \eta_u and apply (3.5), (4.5), and (4.7):

  \eta_{tt}
    =-A^{\mathsf T}\nabla_a\pi
      +\nu Div_a(D_aV\,AA^{\mathsf T}).

The initial conditions follow from (3.1).
Volume preservation gives

  \int_\Omega\pi(t,a)\,da
    =\int_\Omega p(t,x)\,dx=0.                              (5.1)

Thus \Phi(u,p)\in\mathscr M.

Proof: reverse direction.
Given (\eta,\pi)\in\mathscr M, set u=V\circ\eta^{-1},
p=\pi\circ\eta^{-1}. These fields are smooth.
Equation (3.3) with J=1 gives div u=0.
Push (M1) forward by \eta^{-1}, using (3.5), (4.5), and (4.7);
the result is (E1).
Equation (3.6) gives u(0)=u_0.
Equation (5.1) gives the pressure normalization.

Proof: inverse identities.
Direct substitution gives \Psi\Phi=id.
For (\eta,\pi)\in\mathscr M, the reconstructed u satisfies
\eta_t=u\circ\eta and \eta(0)=id. Uniqueness of the smooth ODE flow
therefore gives \eta_u=\eta. Hence \Phi\Psi=id. \square

Gauge and labels.
If p_1 and p_2 produce the same u, then \nabla(p_1-p_2)=0.
Connectedness gives p_1-p_2=c(t); zero mean gives c=0.
Fixing \eta(0)=id removes arbitrary material relabelings.

Theorem NEWTON_NSE_IFF.
  \mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T)=\mathscr N_\nu(u_0;T).

Proof.
For a pair satisfying the common constraints, let \eta be its
volume-preserving flow and V=u\circ\eta. For every admissible A_0,

  \int_{\eta(t,A_0)}u(t,x)\,dx=\int_{A_0}V(t,a)\,da.

Therefore,

  d/dt\int_{\eta(t,A_0)}u\,dx=\int_{A_0}V_t\,da.              (6.1)

The divergence theorem and change of variables give

  \int_{\partial(\eta(t,A_0))}\sigma n\,dS
    =\int_{\eta(t,A_0)}div_x\sigma\,dx
    =\int_{A_0}(div_x\sigma)\circ\eta\,da.                    (6.2)

Thus (N2) is equivalent to

  \int_{A_0}[V_t-(div_x\sigma)\circ\eta]\,da=0
  for every admissible A_0.                                 (6.3)

A continuous vector field whose integral vanishes over every small ball
vanishes pointwise: otherwise a nonzero component has a fixed strict
sign on a sufficiently small ball. Hence

  V_t=(div_x\sigma)\circ\eta.                                (6.4)

By (3.5),

  (6.4) \iff D_tu=div_x\sigma.                              (6.5)

The explicit constitutive law gives

  div_x\sigma
    =-\nabla p+\nu\Delta u+\nu\nabla(div u)
    =-\nabla p+\nu\Delta u.                                 (6.6)

Equations (6.5)--(6.6) are precisely (E1).
Every step is reversible. \square

Full Piola-stress form.
Define

  \mathsf P
    :=J[-\pi I+\nu(D_aV A+(D_aV A)^{\mathsf T})]A^{\mathsf T}.

The material Newton equation is

  J\eta_{tt}=Div_a\mathsf P.                                (6.7)

Under J=1 and div u=0, (6.7) reduces to (M1).
The transposed-gradient contribution vanishes after incompressibility:

  [div_x((D_xu)^{\mathsf T})]\circ\eta
    =[\nabla(div u)]\circ\eta=0.

Lemma PERIODIC_PRESSURE_RECOVERY.
Let r\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\Omega;\mathbb R^3) satisfy

  \int_\Omega r(t,x)\cdot\varphi(x)\,dx=0
  for all \varphi\in C^\infty_\sigma(\Omega), every t.        (7.1)

Then there exists a unique smooth real pressure p such that

  r=-\nabla p,\qquad \int_\Omega p(t,x)\,dx=0.               (7.2)

Proof.
Use the Fourier convention

  \widehat r(t,k)
    :=\int_\Omega r(t,x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x}\,dx,
  k\in\mathbb Z^3.

Taking \varphi=e_j in (7.1) gives

  \widehat r(t,0)=0.                                        (7.3)

For k\ne0, test against sine and cosine fields polarized along any
real vector z with z\cdot k=0. Hence

  \widehat r(t,k)\in span_{\mathbb C}\{k\}.                   (7.4)

Define

  \widehat p(t,0):=0,

  \widehat p(t,k)
    :=-\frac{k\cdot\widehat r(t,k)}{2\pi i|k|^2},
    \qquad k\ne0.                                           (7.5)

Then

  -2\pi i k\,\widehat p(t,k)
    =\frac{k(k\cdot\widehat r(t,k))}{|k|^2}
    =\widehat r(t,k).                                       (7.6)

All time derivatives of the Fourier coefficients of r decay faster
than every polynomial, uniformly on [0,T]. Formula (7.5) preserves
this property. Thus the Fourier series defines smooth p.

Reality follows from

  \widehat p(t,-k)=\overline{\widehat p(t,k)}.

Equations (7.3), (7.5), and (7.6) prove (7.2).
Uniqueness follows from connectedness and zero mean. \square

The constant-mode test is necessary for this proof: it eliminates
the harmonic constant component. No separate harmonic-vanishing
premise is imposed.

Lemma RAYLEIGH_IDENTITY.
For smooth periodic divergence-free u,

  2\int_\Omega|D(u)|^2\,dx
    =\int_\Omega|D_xu|^2\,dx.                               (8.1)

Proof.
Expand the symmetric gradient:

  2\int|D(u)|^2
    =\int|D_xu|^2
      +\int(\partial_j u_i)(\partial_i u_j).

Periodic integration by parts gives

  \int(\partial_j u_i)(\partial_i u_j)
    =-\int u_i\partial_i(div u)=0.                          (8.2)

Hence (8.1). \square

Consequently, with

  \mathcal R(u):=\nu\int|D(u)|^2
               =(\nu/2)\int|D_xu|^2,

the derivative in a divergence-free direction w is

  \mathcal R'(u)[w]
    =\nu\int D_xu:D_xw
    =-\nu\int\Delta u\cdot w.                               (8.3)

Theorem REDUCED_LDA_NSE_IFF.
For a smooth divergence-free u with u(0)=u_0,

  u\in\mathscr V_\nu(u_0;T)
  \iff
  \exists!p:\ (u,p)\in\mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T).                 (8.4)

Proof.
Define

  r:=u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u-\nu\Delta u.                        (8.5)

For w\in\mathscr W, temporal and spatial integration by parts give

  \int_0^T\int u\cdot w_t
    =-\int_0^T\int u_t\cdot w,                              (8.6)

  \int u\cdot(u\cdot\nabla)w
    =-\int((u\cdot\nabla)u)\cdot w,                         (8.7)

  -\int u\cdot(w\cdot\nabla)u
    =-\int w\cdot\nabla(|u|^2/2)=0,                         (8.8)

  -\nu\int D_xu:D_xw
    =\nu\int\Delta u\cdot w.                               (8.9)

Therefore (V1) is equivalent to

  \int_0^T\int_\Omega r\cdot w\,dx\,dt=0
  for all w\in\mathscr W.                                  (8.10)

Take w(t,x)=\chi(t)\varphi(x), with
\chi\in C_c^\infty((0,T)) and
\varphi\in C^\infty_\sigma(\Omega).
The fundamental lemma in time gives (7.1) for 0<t<T.
Continuity extends it to t=0,T.

Lemma PERIODIC_PRESSURE_RECOVERY gives unique normalized smooth p
with r=-\nabla p. This is (E1).

Conversely, if (E1) holds, then r=-\nabla p and

  \int_0^T\int r\cdot w
    =\int_0^T\int p\,div w=0.

Reverse (8.6)--(8.9) to obtain (V1). \square

Pressure compatibility.
Taking divergence of (E1) gives

  -\Delta p
    =\sum_{i,j}(\partial_i u_j)(\partial_j u_i),
  \qquad \int p=0.                                         (8.11)

The right-hand side has zero spatial mean, by integration by parts.
Thus pressure, including p(0), is determined by velocity.
It is not additional independent initial data.

Lemma VARIATION_CORRESPONDENCE.
Let \eta(t)\in Q and u=\eta_t\circ\eta^{-1}.
For a smooth endpoint-fixed variation \eta_s(t), define

  W:=\partial_s\eta_s|_{s=0},
  w:=W\circ\eta^{-1},
  u_s:=\partial_t\eta_s\circ\eta_s^{-1}.

Then

  div w=0,\qquad w(0)=w(T)=0,                               (9.1)

  \delta_wu:=\partial_su_s|_{s=0}
    =w_t+(u\cdot\nabla)w-(w\cdot\nabla)u.                   (9.2)

Every w\in\mathscr W is realized by such a variation.

Proof.
Differentiation of det D_a\eta_s=1 at s=0 gives

  tr(F^{-1}D_aW)=0,

which is div w=0 after composition by \eta^{-1}.
Endpoint fixation gives the endpoint conditions.

Differentiate
  \partial_t\eta_s=u_s\circ\eta_s
in s. Since W=w\circ\eta,

  W_t=[w_t+(u\cdot\nabla)w]\circ\eta,

whereas differentiating the right-hand side gives

  W_t=[\delta_wu+(w\cdot\nabla)u]\circ\eta.

Thus (9.2).

For the converse, let \Phi_s^t be the s-flow of w(t,\cdot), and put

  \eta_s(t):=\Phi_s^t\circ\eta(t).

Each \Phi_s^t is volume preserving because div w=0.
At t=0,T the vector field w vanishes, so \Phi_s^t=id.
This variation realizes W=w\circ\eta and therefore (9.2). \square

Lemma FIBRE_DISSIPATION.
At fixed \eta, put u=v\circ\eta^{-1} and w=W\circ\eta^{-1}.
Then

  D_vR(\eta,v)[W]=\nu\int_\Omega D_xu:D_xw\,dx.              (9.3)

Proof.
At fixed \eta,

  (v+sW)\circ\eta^{-1}=u+sw.

Differentiate the quadratic functional R. \square

Theorem MATERIAL_LDA_IFF.
The correspondence

  u \longmapsto \eta_u,
  \eta \longmapsto \eta_t\circ\eta^{-1}

is a bijection
  \mathscr V_\nu(u_0;T)\cong\mathscr D_\nu(u_0;T).            (9.4)

Proof.
Volume preservation gives

  L(\eta,\eta_t)=E(u).                                      (9.5)

For the actual variations of Lemma VARIATION_CORRESPONDENCE,

  \delta\int_0^T L\,dt
    =\int_0^T\int_\Omega u\cdot\delta_wu\,dx\,dt.             (9.6)

By (9.3), the virtual dissipative work is

  \int_0^T D_vR(\eta,\eta_t)[W]\,dt
    =\nu\int_0^T\int_\Omega D_xu:D_xw\,dx\,dt.               (9.7)

Thus (D1) is exactly (V1).
Every permitted w is realized, and every permitted variation produces
such a w. The flow inverse identities are those of Section 5. \square

The virtual-work prescription is
  \delta Action - \int D_vR[W]\,dt=0.

It does not mean
  \delta\int(L-R)\,dt=0,
nor does it replace D_vR[W] with \mathcal R'(u)[\delta_wu].

Theorem NSE_CLASSICAL_MECHANICS_EQUIVALENCE.

  NEWTON_NSE_IFF
  + EULERIAN_MATERIAL_IFF
  + REDUCED_LDA_NSE_IFF
  + MATERIAL_LDA_IFF

imply

  \mathscr E=\mathscr N,
  \mathscr E\cong\mathscr M,
  \mathscr E\cong\mathscr V,
  \mathscr V\cong\mathscr D,
  \mathscr M\cong\mathscr D.                                (10.1)

For the last bijection, the forward map forgets the normalized
material pressure:

  (\eta,\pi)\longmapsto\eta.

Its inverse is constructive:

  \eta
    \longmapsto u=\eta_t\circ\eta^{-1}
    \longmapsto r=u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u-\nu\Delta u
    \longmapsto p \text{ by (7.5)}
    \longmapsto (\eta,p\circ\eta).                          (10.2)

The pressure reconstruction is unique; hence forgetting \pi loses
no solution information.

All assumptions are those of Sections 1--2.
There is no additional certificate, smallness assumption, or
unresolved analytic premise in the stated smooth correspondence.
The definition of each solution set, including smoothness, remains
part of its exact scope. \square

11.1. Energy and dissipation

For (u,p)\in\mathscr E,

  d/dt E(u)
    =\int u\cdot u_t
    =-\int u\cdot(u\cdot\nabla)u
      -\int u\cdot\nabla p
      +\nu\int u\cdot\Delta u.

The first term is
  -\int u\cdot\nabla(|u|^2/2)=0.

The pressure term is
  \int p\,div u=0.

Therefore

  d/dt E(u)
    =-\nu\int|D_xu|^2
    =-2\nu\int|D(u)|^2.                                    (11.1)

For every 0\le t\le T,

  E(u(t))+\nu\int_0^t\|D_xu(s)\|_2^2\,ds=E(u_0).           (11.2)

Material identities:

  E(u)=\frac12\int_\Omega|V|^2\,da,                         (11.3)

  \int_\Omega|D_xu|^2\,dx
    =\int_\Omega|D_aV\,A|^2\,da.                            (11.4)

Thus the exact mechanical energy balance is

  d/dt \frac12\int_\Omega|V|^2\,da
    =-\nu\int_\Omega|D_aV\,A|^2\,da
    =-2R(\eta,\eta_t).                                      (11.5)

11.2. Momentum

Integrate (E1) over \Omega:

  d/dt\int_\Omega u\,dx=0.                                 (11.6)

Equivalently,

  \int_\Omega V(t,a)\,da=\int_\Omega u_0(a)\,da.             (11.7)

11.3. Smooth uniqueness

Let (u,p),(v,q)\in\mathscr E for the same data. Set z=u-v.
Then

  z_t+(u\cdot\nabla)z+(z\cdot\nabla)v
    =-\nabla(p-q)+\nu\Delta z,
  div z=0,\quad z(0)=0.

Taking the L^2 pairing with z gives

  \frac12\frac d{dt}\|z\|_2^2+\nu\|D_xz\|_2^2
    =-\int z_i z_j\partial_jv_i
    \le\|D_xv\|_\infty\|z\|_2^2.                            (11.8)

Since v is smooth on the compact spacetime cylinder,
\|D_xv\|_\infty is integrable in time.
Gronwall's inequality and z(0)=0 give z=0.
The normalized pressure is then unique.
The bijections transfer uniqueness to all four formulations.

11.4. Restriction and global correspondence

For 0<T_1<T_2, restriction of a solution to [0,T_1] commutes with
\Phi,\Psi and with the Lagrange-d'Alembert correspondences.

For the material and Eulerian maps, this follows from uniqueness of
the flow and the pointwise inverse formulas. For the variational
formulations, it follows from their established equivalence to (E1).

Define a global smooth solution as one whose restriction to every
finite time interval belongs to the corresponding smooth class.
Then

  \mathscr E_\nu(u_0;[0,\infty))
    \cong\mathscr M_\nu(u_0;[0,\infty))
    \cong\mathscr D_\nu(u_0;[0,\infty)).                     (11.9)

Forward construction: compatible finite-time flows patch by ODE
uniqueness. Reverse construction: the inverse configuration map is
smooth locally around every finite (t,x); the reconstruction formulas
apply on each finite interval.

In particular,

  [\exists global smooth NSE solution from u_0]
  \iff
  [\exists global smooth material Newtonian solution from (id,u_0)].
                                                                  (11.10)

For fixed u_0, define the finite existence-time sets

  I_E(u_0):={T>0:\mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T)\ne\varnothing},
  I_M(u_0):={T>0:\mathscr M_\nu(u_0;T)\ne\varnothing}.

Then

  I_E(u_0)=I_M(u_0).                                        (11.11)

The theorem proves correspondence and equivalence of nonemptiness.
It does not assert global nonemptiness for every smooth u_0.

12. EXACT SHEAR / DAMPED PARTICLE SUBSYSTEM

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C15

ML-G02 = eq_zero_of_abs_deriv_le_mul_abs_self_of_eq_zero_right
M03 = SingularClosure.critical_integral_inner_laplacian_self
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L12
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = The exact shear ansatz, trigonometric normalization and mass 1/2 are proved separately.
Full signatures and source URLs: Sections 22--24.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

Fix k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1} and define

  c:=\nu(2\pi k)^2>0,
  u(t,x):=\dot q(t)e_1\sin(2\pi kx_2),
  p:=0,
  q(0):=0.

Direct computation gives

  div u=0,
  (u\cdot\nabla)u=0,
  \Delta u=-(2\pi k)^2u.

Therefore

  (u,0)\text{ satisfies NSE}
  \iff
  \ddot q+c\dot q=0.                                       (12.1)

For \dot q(0)=a_0,

  \dot q(t)=a_0e^{-ct},
  q(t)=\frac{a_0}{c}(1-e^{-ct}).                            (12.2)

The actual material flow is

  \eta(t,a)=
     (a_1+q(t)\sin(2\pi ka_2),\,a_2,\,a_3),                 (12.3)

with inverse

  \eta(t)^{-1}(x)=
     (x_1-q(t)\sin(2\pi kx_2),\,x_2,\,x_3).                 (12.4)

Thus det D_a\eta=1 and \eta(t)\in Q for every finite t.

The scalar trajectory and the Eulerian shear trajectory determine
one another because q(0)=0. The initial scalar velocity is a_0.

Exact mechanical normalization:

  L_{\mathrm{shear}}(q,\dot q)=\frac14\dot q^2,
  R_{\mathrm{shear}}(q,\dot q)=\frac c4\dot q^2.              (12.5)

Hence

  \frac d{dt}\partial_{\dot q}L_{\mathrm{shear}}
    -\partial_qL_{\mathrm{shear}}
    +\partial_{\dot q}R_{\mathrm{shear}}
  =\frac12(\ddot q+c\dot q).                                (12.6)

The effective mass for the unnormalized sine mode is 1/2.
Using \sqrt2\,e_1\sin(2\pi kx_2) instead gives unit mass.

This is an invariant subsystem of the actual NSE, with no Galerkin
approximation. Its global solution is explicitly given by (12.2).

13.1. Finite Galerkin vector field

Let E_N be a finite real divergence-free Fourier space invariant under
\Delta, and P_N its L^2 orthogonal projection.
Choose an L^2 orthonormal real basis \varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_{d_N}.
Write

  u_N=\sum_{j=1}^{d_N}a_j\varphi_j.

The projected equation

  \partial_tu_N
    =\nu\Delta u_N-P_N((u_N\cdot\nabla)u_N)                  (13.1)

is an ODE

  \dot a=F_N(a),\qquad a\in\mathbb R^{d_N},                  (13.2)

with a polynomial vector field F_N.

Energy cancellation gives

  \frac12\frac d{dt}|a|^2
    =-\nu\|D_xu_N\|_2^2\le0.                               (13.3)

Since F_N is locally Lipschitz and a remains bounded, the finite ODE
has a global forward solution for every finite initial a(0).

13.2. Exact cotangent lift

On T^*\mathbb R^{d_N}, define

  \omega:=\sum_j da_j\wedge db_j,
  \mathcal H_N(a,b):=b\cdot F_N(a).                          (13.4)

Canonical Hamilton equations are

  \dot a=\partial_b\mathcal H_N=F_N(a),
  \dot b=-\partial_a\mathcal H_N=-DF_N(a)^{\mathsf T}b.       (13.5)

Thus

  a\in Sol(\dot a=F_N(a))
  \iff
  (a,0)\in Sol(X_{\mathcal H_N}),                            (13.6)

and these maps give a bijection onto the invariant branch b=0.
Invariance follows from uniqueness for the homogeneous linear
b-equation. Every full lifted solution projects to a base solution.

The unrestricted lifted solution set additionally depends on b(0).
The zero section is Lagrangian:

  \omega|_{b=0}=0.

The conclusion is an invariant Hamiltonian realization, not a
symplectic identification of the original a-space.

13.3. Exact scope of the lift

For every a,

  \mathcal H_N(a,0)=0.                                      (13.7)

The Hamiltonian level set \mathcal H_N=0 therefore contains arbitrarily
large a. Conservation of this Hamiltonian cannot bound |a| on the
zero section.

An arbitrary E_N produces a projected approximation of NSE.
It is an exact subsystem of the full equation only if the full
divergence-free NSE vector field leaves E_N invariant.
The shear space in Section 12 has this invariance.

Use the Fourier Sobolev norm
  \|v\|_{H^s}^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}
     (1+4\pi^2|k|^2)^s|\widehat v(k)|^2.

With \lambda_{\max,N} the largest Laplace eigenvalue in E_N,

  \|u_N\|_{H^s}
    \le(1+\lambda_{\max,N})^{s/2}\|u_N\|_2
    \qquad(s\ge0).                                         (13.8)

For expanding Fourier spaces the coefficient depends on N.
This estimate is not a uniform high-regularity estimate for the
full-PDE limit.

14. KINETIC-HAMILTONIAN OBSTRUCTION AND INFINITE LIFT SCOPE

14.1. Exact kinetic-Hamiltonian obstruction

Let (u,p) be a smooth unforced NSE trajectory with
D_xu(t_*)\not\equiv0 at some time t_*.
By (11.1),

  E'(t_*)=-\nu\|D_xu(t_*)\|_2^2<0.                          (14.1)

An autonomous Poisson realization generated by H=E instead satisfies

  E'={E,E}=0,                                               (14.2)

by antisymmetry of the bracket.

Therefore there is no such realization reproducing this trajectory
with the specified kinetic-energy Hamiltonian.

An explicit nonconstant global trajectory is supplied by Section 12
with a_0\ne0:

  E(t)=\frac{a_0^2}{4}e^{-2ct},
  E'(t)=-\frac{ca_0^2}{2}e^{-2ct}<0.                        (14.3)

The excluded class is precisely:
  autonomous pure Hamiltonian evolution with H equal to the physical
  kinetic energy along the identified trajectory.

This does not exclude auxiliary states, different Hamiltonians,
time-dependent Hamiltonians, or contact formulations.

14.2. Formal infinite cotangent lift

The finite construction alone does not produce a forward smooth
Hamiltonian flow for arbitrary auxiliary PDE initial data.

Along the exact base trajectory u=0, the quadratic convection term
has zero derivative. The formal cotangent equations therefore reduce to

  u_t=\nu\Delta u,
  b_t=-\nu\Delta b.                                         (14.4)

For k\in\mathbb Z^3,

  \widehat b(t,k)
    =e^{\nu(2\pi)^2|k|^2t}\widehat b(0,k).                  (14.5)

Example:
  b(0,x)=e_2\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-n}\cos(2\pi nx_1).

This is a smooth divergence-free field. For every t>0, its proposed
coefficients in (14.5) grow faster than every polynomial.
Fourier coefficients of a periodic distribution have at most
polynomial growth; hence no distribution-valued forward solution
with these coefficients exists.

Thus a full-PDE Hamiltonian evolution requires a separate
function-space and time-direction formulation. No such extension
is used in the root equivalence.

  finite-time continuation of bounded finite-dimensional ODE solutions;
  inverse-function theorem with parameters;
  chain rule and Jacobi determinant identity;
  periodic integration by parts and divergence theorem;
  fundamental lemma for smooth temporal test functions;
  Fourier representation of smooth functions on the torus;
  Gronwall's inequality.

All nontrivial bridges specific to this equivalence are derived
explicitly in Sections 3--10.

17. STRENGTHENING ROUND I: OPERATOR CONJUGACY AND QUANTITATIVE GEOMETRY

All hypotheses and solution classes remain those of Sections 1--2.

17.1. Transport isometry

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C19
ML-I02 = MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.integral_comp'
ML-H04 = MeasureTheory.L2.inner_def
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L02
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Construct the measure-preserving measurable equivalence before integral transport.
Full signatures and source URLs: Sections 22--24.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

For each fixed t, define
  U_\eta f:=f\circ\eta,
  U_\eta^{-1}h:=h\circ\eta^{-1}.

Since det D_a\eta=1,
  \int_\Omega g\circ\eta\,da=\int_\Omega g\,dx.

Therefore, for 1<=p<infinity,
  \|U_\eta f\|_{L^p_a}=\|f\|_{L^p_x},
and the same identity holds for p=infinity.

In particular,
  U_\eta:L^2_x(\Omega;\mathbb R^3) -> L^2_a(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)
is a surjective real-linear isometry, and
  <U_\eta f,U_\eta g>_{L^2_a}=<f,g>_{L^2_x}.

The equality applies componentwise to vectors and matrices.

17.2. Conjugated differential operators

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C03,C20
ML-O08 = HasFDerivAt.comp
ML-O15 = Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv
ML-O18 = ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt
M02 = SingularClosure.critical_integral_inner_coordinateDerivative
M03 = SingularClosure.critical_integral_inner_laplacian_self
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L03,L04
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Operator conjugacy is at fixed time; the time derivative is the material derivative.
Full signatures and source URLs: Sections 22--24.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

For smooth material vector fields H and smooth material scalars h, set
  D_\eta H:=D_aH A,
  div_\eta H:=tr(D_aH A),
  grad_\eta h:=A^{\mathsf T}\nabla_a h,
  \Delta_\eta H:=Div_a(D_aH A A^{\mathsf T}),
  \Delta_\eta h:=div_a(A A^{\mathsf T}\nabla_a h).

The chain rule and Piola identity prove, at each FIXED time,
  D_\eta U_\eta f=U_\eta D_xf,
  div_\eta U_\eta f=U_\eta div_x f,
  grad_\eta U_\eta g=U_\eta\nabla_x g,
  \Delta_\eta U_\eta f=U_\eta\Delta_xf.

Equivalently,
  \Delta_\eta=U_\eta\Delta_xU_\eta^{-1}.                    (17.1)

For spacetime fields, the correct time identity is
  \partial_t(U_\eta f)
    =U_\eta(\partial_tf+(u\cdot\nabla)f).                   (17.2)

Thus neither U_\eta nor its conjugated projections are treated as
time-independent operators.

Integration by parts transfers exactly:
  <grad_\eta h,H>_a=-<h,div_\eta H>_a,                       (17.3)
  -<H,\Delta_\eta H>_a=\int_\Omega|D_aH A|^2\,da.           (17.4)

The latter operator is symmetric on smooth periodic test fields:
  <H,\Delta_\eta K>_a=<\Delta_\eta H,K>_a.                  (17.5)

17.3. Quantitative distortion and ellipticity

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C20
ML-D01 = HasDerivAt.norm_sq
ML-G01 = norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le
ML-G03 = le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L04,L11
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = The exact exp(integral b) bound uses a variable-coefficient integrating factor.
Full signatures and source URLs: Sections 22--24.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

Define
  b(t):=\|D_xu(t)\|_{L^\infty,\mathrm{op}},
  K(t):=\int_0^t b(s)\,ds.

For every finite smooth interval, K(t)<infinity.
Let B:=(D_xu)\circ\eta=D_aV A. Then
  F_t=BF,
  A_t=-AB.                                                  (17.6)

The integral equations give
  \|F(t)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}
    <=1+\int_0^t b(s)\|F(s)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}\,ds,
  \|A(t)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}
    <=1+\int_0^t b(s)\|A(s)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}\,ds.

Integral Gronwall yields
  \|F(t)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}<=e^{K(t)},
  \|A(t)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}<=e^{K(t)}.                   (17.7)


Equivalent scalar proof for later formalization:
for every fixed label and vectors h,xi,
  (d/dt)|F h|^2<=2b(t)|F h|^2,
  (d/dt)|A^{\mathsf T}xi|^2<=2b(t)|A^{\mathsf T}xi|^2.
The integrating factor exp(-2K(t)) gives the same operator bounds.
This route uses ordinary scalar derivatives and requires no derivative
of the spatial supremum norm.

Since A^{-1}=F, for every material covector \xi,
  e^{-2K(t)}|\xi|^2
    <=\xi^{\mathsf T}A A^{\mathsf T}\xi
    <=e^{2K(t)}|\xi|^2.                                     (17.8)

Consequently,
  e^{-2K(t)}\|D_aH\|_2^2
    <=-<H,\Delta_\eta H>_a
    <=e^{2K(t)}\|D_aH\|_2^2.                               (17.9)

This is quantitative ellipticity on every stipulated finite smooth
interval. No interval-independent upper bound on K is asserted.

17.4. Pressure-free constrained Newton equation

Define the Eulerian Leray projection by its Fourier multipliers:
  \widehat{\mathbb P f}(0):=\widehat f(0),
  \widehat{\mathbb P f}(k)
    :=[I-k k^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2]\widehat f(k), k!=0.

Each nonzero-frequency matrix is a self-adjoint orthogonal projection.
Therefore \mathbb P is a contractive L^2 orthogonal projection,
preserves smoothness, and commutes with \Delta.

Define
  \mathbb P_\eta:=U_\eta\mathbb P U_\eta^{-1}.               (17.10)

For a smooth material field H,
  \mathbb P_\eta H=H  iff  div_\eta H=0.

For a smooth H in ker \mathbb P_\eta, Fourier inversion gives a unique
zero-mean scalar h with H=grad_\eta h. The zero Fourier mode is absent
because \mathbb P(0)=I.

If \eta(t)\in Q and V=\eta_t, then div_\eta V=0 and
\mathbb P_\eta\Delta_\eta V=\Delta_\eta V.
Applying \mathbb P_\eta to (M1) gives
  \mathbb P_\eta\eta_{tt}=\nu\Delta_\eta\eta_t.               (17.11)

Conversely, suppose \eta(t)\in Q has the root initial data and satisfies
(17.11). Then
  \mathbb P_\eta(\eta_{tt}-\nu\Delta_\eta\eta_t)=0.
The smooth gradient-kernel identity produces unique normalized \pi
such that
  \eta_{tt}-\nu\Delta_\eta\eta_t=-grad_\eta\pi.
This is (M1). Thus
  MATERIAL_NSE
    iff
  [\eta(t)\in Q and \mathbb P_\eta\eta_{tt}
                       =\nu\Delta_\eta\eta_t].              (17.12)

The projection in (17.11) acts on acceleration. No identity
V_t=\nu\Delta_\eta V is substituted for this constrained equation.

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

Differentiate
  0=div_\eta V=tr(D_aV A).

Using A_t=-A D_aV A,
  0=tr(D_aV_t A)-tr((D_aV A)^2).

Therefore
  div_\eta V_t=tr((D_aV A)^2).                              (17.13)

Apply div_\eta to (M1). Operator conjugacy and div_\eta V=0 give
  -\Delta_\eta\pi=tr((D_aV A)^2),
  \int_\Omega\pi\,da=0.                                    (17.14)

The sign in (17.13) is positive.
The matrix D_aV A is the full velocity Jacobian, not its symmetric part.
Here tr(B^2)=sum_{i,j} B_ij B_ji is generally sign-indefinite;
it is not the Frobenius square sum_{i,j} B_ij^2. Its spatial integral
vanishes by the divergence constraint and periodic integration by parts.

17.6. Explicit finite-slab construction and smooth flow dependence

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C01
ML-O01 = IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
ML-O02 = IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_hasDerivWithinAt_continuousOn
ML-O03 = ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_right
ML-O04 = ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_left
ML-O05 = lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le
ML-O06 = ContDiffAt.to_localInverse
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L01
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Uniform boundedness gives the full chosen slab; difference quotients give smooth dependence.
Full signatures and source URLs: Sections 22--24.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

Let U_*=sup_{[0,T]xOmega}|u| and
K_*=sup_{[0,T]xOmega}||D_xu||_op.
Periodic lifting gives the same global spatial bounds on R^3.

For initial points in a closed ball of radius r about x_0, choose
R>=r+U_*T. Then
  U_* max(T-0,0-0)<=R-r.
Together with continuity and the K_*-Lipschitz estimate, this is exactly
the finite-slab bound package of ML-O01--ML-O02.
There is no smallness condition K_*T<1.

Trajectory uniqueness gives
  eta(t,a+k)=eta(t,a)+k, k in Z^3,
and consistency of constructions on overlapping initial balls.
Time reversal supplies the inverse trajectory from each (t,x).

To derive differentiability in a, first solve the linear matrix equation
  F_t=B F,  F(0,a)=I,
  B(t,a)=D_xu(t,eta(t,a)).

For a coordinate unit vector e and h!=0, define
  Q_h(t,a)=[eta(t,a+he)-eta(t,a)]/h,
  B_h(t,a)=int_0^1 D_xu(t,eta(t,a)
                  +theta[eta(t,a+he)-eta(t,a)]) dtheta.

The fundamental theorem of calculus gives
  (Q_h)_t=B_h Q_h,  Q_h(0,a)=e.
Consequently
  |Q_h(t,a)|<=exp(K_*t).

Continuous dependence and uniform continuity of D_xu on the periodic
compact spacetime cylinder give B_h->B uniformly on the time slab,
locally uniformly in a.
Subtracting the equation for F e and applying the integrating factor
to its norm bound gives
  sup_{0<=t<=T}|Q_h(t,a)-F(t,a)e|
    <=T exp(K_*T) sup_{0<=t<=T}||B_h(t,a)-B(t,a)||_op
    ->0.

Continuous dependence for the linear equation gives continuous F.
Thus D_a eta=F, and (3.2) is derived from actual parameter derivatives.

For m>=2, construct a candidate symmetric m-linear tensor Y_m
by the following inhomogeneous linear equation. The forcing is the
iterated-chain-rule expression for fixed directions h_1,...,h_m:
  partial_t Y_m[h_1,...,h_m]
    =B Y_m[h_1,...,h_m]
     +sum_{P={C_1,...,C_l} partition of {1,...,m}, l>=2}
        D_x^l u(t,eta)
          [Y_{|C_1|}[h_i:i in C_1], ...,
           Y_{|C_l|}[h_i:i in C_l]],
  Y_m(0)=0.

Here C_1,...,C_l are the blocks of P. Each has at most m-1 elements.
Hence the forcing depends only on already constructed lower derivatives.
Applying the preceding difference-quotient argument inductively identifies
Y_m=D_a^m eta and proves continuity of every spatial derivative.

The identity eta_t=u(t,eta) then gives all time and mixed derivatives,
including the stipulated one-sided endpoint derivatives.
The inverse trajectories prove bijectivity. The derivative F is
invertible: solve A_t=-AB, A(0)=I. Then (AF)'=0 and AF(0)=I, so AF=I.
For finite square matrices this implies FA=I as well.
The parameter-dependent inverse-function theorem gives a jointly smooth
inverse family in the temporal interior. For zeta(t,x)=eta(t)^{-1}(x),
  D_x zeta=A(t,zeta),
  partial_t zeta=-A(t,zeta)V(t,zeta).
Continuity of the inverse family and induction on these formulas extend
all derivatives to the temporal endpoints with the stipulated one-sided
interpretation.

This supplies the smooth-dependence argument used in C01.
Its Lean realization remains L01; source continuity is not promoted
to source C-infinity dependence.


18. STRENGTHENING ROUND II: QUANTITATIVE PRESSURE AND ENERGY

18.1. Explicit pressure multiplier

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C23

Let
  m:=\int_\Omega u_0\,dx,
  z(t,x):=u(t,x)-m.

Momentum conservation gives \int z=0.
The field z is the raw fluctuation; it is not yet the Galilean-transformed
solution of Section 19.2.

Since div u=0,
  -\Delta p
    =div div(u\otimes u)
    =div div(z\otimes z).                                  (18.1)

The second equality follows because m is spatially constant and div z=0.
For k!=0,
  \widehat p(k)
    =-\sum_{i,j}\frac{k_i k_j}{|k|^2}
                       \widehat{z_i z_j}(k),
  \widehat p(0)=0.                                         (18.2)

Equivalently,
  \nabla p=-(I-\mathbb P)((z\cdot\nabla)z).                 (18.3)

Indeed, (m\cdot\nabla)z is divergence free and is annihilated by
I-\mathbb P.

18.2. Explicit L2 pressure estimates

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C23
ML-F07 = UnitAddTorus.hasSum_sq_mFourierCoeff
ML-H03 = Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le
ML-I02 = MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.integral_comp'
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L15
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Componentwise Parseval and the rank-one multiplier give constant one.
Full signatures and source URLs: Sections 22--24.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

For k!=0, the Frobenius norm of k k^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2 is 1.
Cauchy-Schwarz therefore gives
  |\widehat p(k)|^2
    <=\sum_{i,j}|\widehat{z_i z_j}(k)|^2.

Sum over k and apply scalar Parseval to each tensor component:
  \|p\|_2^2
    <=\int_\Omega\sum_{i,j}|z_i z_j|^2\,dx
    =\int_\Omega|z|^4\,dx.

Hence
  \|p\|_2<=\|u-m\|_4^2.                                   (18.4)

By contractivity of I-\mathbb P and pointwise matrix Cauchy-Schwarz,
  \|\nabla p\|_2
    <=\|(z\cdot\nabla)z\|_2
    <=\|z\|_\infty\|D_xz\|_2
    =\|u-m\|_\infty\|D_xu\|_2.                             (18.5)

Volume preservation transfers these bounds:
  \|\pi\|_{L^2_a}<=\|V-m\|_{L^4_a}^2,                      (18.6)
  \|A^{\mathsf T}\nabla_a\pi\|_{L^2_a}
    <=\|V-m\|_{L^\infty_a}\|D_aV A\|_{L^2_a}.              (18.7)

For the unweighted material pressure gradient, (17.7) gives
  \|\nabla_a\pi\|_2
    <=e^{K(t)}\|V-m\|_\infty\|D_aV A\|_2.                  (18.8)

Let r(t,x) be any jointly smooth residual on [0,T]\times\Omega.
For every j,m in \mathbb N, repeated spatial integration by parts
and differentiation under the fixed-domain integral give finite constants
C_{j,m} with
  |\partial_t^j\widehat r(t,k)|
    <=C_{j,m}(1+|k|)^{-m}
  for all t in [0,T], k in \mathbb Z^3.                    (18.9)

One construction bounds the L1 norms of \partial_t^j r and its
coordinate derivatives of order m uniformly in t; compactness and
joint smoothness make those bounds finite.

For the pressure coefficients in (7.5), k!=0,
  |\partial_t^j\widehat p(t,k)|
    <=\frac{|\partial_t^j\widehat r(t,k)|}{2\pi|k|}.          (18.10)

After any prescribed spatial derivative of order q, choose m>q+3.
The resulting differentiated series is absolutely uniformly convergent
on [0,T]\times\Omega. Apply the same argument to every temporal order.

Thus the pressure recovered in Section 7 is jointly smooth up to
the temporal endpoints. This supplies an explicit uniform-decay
derivation of the time-regularity step.

Define
  E_fl(t):=(1/2)\|u(t)-m\|_2^2.

By Parseval and |k|^2>=1 for k!=0,
  \|D_xu\|_2^2
    =4\pi^2\sum_{k!=0}|k|^2|\widehat z(k)|^2
    >=4\pi^2\|z\|_2^2
    =8\pi^2 E_fl.                                         (18.11)

The energy identity gives
  E_fl'=-\nu\|D_xu\|_2^2
        <=-8\pi^2\nu E_fl.

The integrating factor e^{8\pi^2\nu t} therefore proves
  E_fl(t)<=e^{-8\pi^2\nu(t-s)}E_fl(s),

  (1/2)\|V(t)-m\|_2^2
    <=e^{-8\pi^2\nu(t-s)}(1/2)\|V(s)-m\|_2^2.              (18.13)

19.1. Quantitative stability and correct material comparison

Let u,v be two smooth NSE velocities on the same finite interval.
Their initial data may differ. Set d=u-v.
Section 11.3 gives
  (d/dt)\|d\|_2^2
    <=2\|D_xv(t)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}\|d\|_2^2.

The integrating factor proves
  \|u(t)-v(t)\|_2^2
    <=\|u(0)-v(0)\|_2^2
       exp(2\int_0^t\|D_xv(s)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}\,ds).  (19.1)

Let \eta_u,\eta_v be the identity-normalized material flows and define
  \rho_t:=\eta_v(t)^{-1}\circ\eta_u(t).

Then
  V_u-V_v\circ\rho_t=(u-v)\circ\eta_u,
so
  \|V_u-V_v\circ\rho_t\|_{L^2_a}
    =\|u-v\|_{L^2_x}.                                      (19.2)

Thus (19.1) transfers to this exact aligned material comparison.
No same-label estimate for V_u-V_v is inferred from (19.1).

Strain refinement.
Because d^{\mathsf T}(D_xv)d=d^{\mathsf T}D(v)d, define
  S_v(t):=\|D(v(t))\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}},
where D(v) is the symmetric strain from Section 1.
Then the stronger estimate is
  \|u(t)-v(t)\|_2^2
    <=\|u(0)-v(0)\|_2^2 exp(2\int_0^t S_v(s)\,ds).         (19.1a)

If u and v have the same initial mean, their difference remains
mean zero. Retaining viscous dissipation and applying (18.11) gives
  \|u(t)-v(t)\|_2^2
    <=\|u(0)-v(0)\|_2^2
       exp(2\int_0^t S_v(s)\,ds-8\pi^2\nu t).              (19.1b)

The exact relabeling equation follows by differentiating
\eta_v(t,\rho_t(a))=\eta_u(t,a):
  \partial_t\rho_t
    =(A_v\circ\rho_t)(V_u-V_v\circ\rho_t).                  (19.2a)

19.2. Exact arbitrary-mean / mean-zero Galilean adapter

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

For the conserved mean m, define
  \widetilde u(t,x):=u(t,x+mt)-m,
  \widetilde p(t,x):=p(t,x+mt).                            (19.3)

Then
  \partial_t\widetilde u
    =u_t(t,x+mt)+(m\cdot\nabla)u(t,x+mt),
  (\widetilde u\cdot\nabla)\widetilde u
    =((u-m)\cdot\nabla)u(t,x+mt).

Adding yields
  \partial_t\widetilde u
     +(\widetilde u\cdot\nabla)\widetilde u
    =[u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u](t,x+mt).

Hence \widetilde u,\widetilde p satisfy the same NSE with viscosity \nu,
  \int_\Omega\widetilde u=0,
  \widetilde u(0)=u_0-m,
  \int_\Omega\widetilde p=0.

The inverse is
  u(t,x)=\widetilde u(t,x-mt)+m,
  p(t,x)=\widetilde p(t,x-mt).                             (19.4)

Thus this is a bijection on the same time interval.

For the corresponding material paths,
  \eta_u(t,a)=\eta_{\widetilde u}(t,a)+mt,
  F_u=F_{\widetilde u},
  V_u=V_{\widetilde u}+m,
  \pi_u=\pi_{\widetilde u}.                                (19.5)

Kinetic energy splits as
  E(u)=|m|^2/2+E(\widetilde u).                             (19.6)

The raw fluctuation z=u-m instead satisfies
  z_t+(z\cdot\nabla)z+(m\cdot\nabla)z
    =-\nabla p+\nu\Delta z.
The translation in (19.3) is essential.

19.3. Periodic Euclidean lift / quotient-torus adapter

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C28
ML-I01 = UnitAddTorus.integral_preimage
ML-F01 = UnitAddTorus.mFourierCoeff
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L16
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Match EuclideanSpace coordinates, quotient smoothness and normalized Haar measure explicitly.
Full signatures and source URLs: Sections 22--24.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

Let \pi_Q:\mathbb R^3 -> (\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^3 be the quotient map.
Smooth torus fields correspond bijectively to smooth coordinate-unit-
periodic fields U on \mathbb R^3 via U=u\circ\pi_Q.

Proof.
The quotient map is a local diffeomorphism, so pullback preserves
smoothness and all local differential identities.
Conversely, integer-translation invariance gives a unique descended
function; local sections of \pi_Q show it is smooth.
Coordinate-unit periodicity implies integer-translation invariance
by iteration and negative-translation substitution.

Normalized Haar integration is
  \int_{\mathbb T^3}f
    =\int_{(0,1]^3}f\circ\pi_Q.
The boundaries have Lebesgue measure zero, so [0,1]^3 gives the same
integral for smooth fields.

For source integration:
  UnitAddTorus (Fin 3)
    <-> functions (Fin 3 -> UnitAddCircle),
  SingularClosure.Vec
    = EuclideanSpace \mathbb R (Fin 3).

The coordinate linear equivalence and the Haar/fundamental-cell
identification must be instantiated explicitly in Lean.
No automatic definitional equality of these types is assumed.

19.4. Exact energy normalization adapter

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L16
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Methlib physicalEnergy=2E_TXT; dissipative factors must be scaled accordingly.
Full signatures and source URLs: Sections 22--24.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

The inspected Methlib source defines
  SingularClosure.physicalEnergy(U)
    =\int_{unitCube}\sum_{j:Fin 3}(U(x)_j)^2.

Under the quotient/lift correspondence,
  E_TXT(u)=physicalEnergy(U)/2.                            (19.7)

Likewise its physicalDissipation is the integral of the squared
full Jacobian, agreeing with \|D_xu\|_2^2.
Therefore
  (physicalEnergy)'=-2\nu physicalDissipation
transfers exactly to
  E_TXT'=-\nu\|D_xu\|_2^2.

Methlib's timeDerivative uses
  derivWithin (fun s => U(s,x)) (Ici 0) t.

For a globally defined smooth nonnegative-time trajectory:
  t>0: this equals the ordinary time derivative;
  t=0: this equals the right derivative.

For a finite [0,T] trajectory, equality with that convention is local
for 0<=t<T after selecting a function extension agreeing on [0,T].
Since T>0, Ici 0 contains a full neighborhood of T. Its within derivative
at t=T is therefore two-sided and is not determined by the finite
trajectory. The closed-interval theorem uses the corresponding
left/within-[0,T] derivative there.

The inspected GlobalSmoothNSE predicate quantifies globally on
nonnegative time and includes mean-zero conditions.
The finite-time root is therefore not replaced by that predicate.
For genuinely global smooth trajectories, the Galilean and
quotient/lift adapters apply without changing the temporal scope.

    (hv : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, LipschitzOnWith K (v t) (s t))

    (hf' : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (v t (f t)) (Ici t) t)
    (hfs : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, f t ∈ s t)
    (hg : ContinuousOn g (Icc a b))
    (hg' : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt g (v t (g t)) (Ici t) t)
    (hgs : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, g t ∈ s t)
    (ha : f a = g a) :
    EqOn f g (Icc a b)

PICARD–LINDELOF STRUCTURE: EXACT HYPOTHESES
IMPORT=Mathlib.Analysis.ODE.PicardLindelof
BLOB_SHA=a692cd5696e93c9bc84c79499323faa0313baf4a
URL=https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d/Mathlib/Analysis/ODE/PicardLindelof.lean#L79-L88
RAW_URL=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d/Mathlib/Analysis/ODE/PicardLindelof.lean
structure IsPicardLindelof {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) {tmin tmax : ℝ} (t₀ : Icc tmin tmax) (x₀ : E) (a r L K : ℝ≥0) : Prop where
  /-- The vector field at any time is Lipschitz with constant `K` within a closed ball. -/
  lipschitzOnWith : ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, LipschitzOnWith K (f t) (closedBall x₀ a)
  /-- The vector field is continuous in time within a closed ball. -/
  continuousOn : ∀ x ∈ closedBall x₀ a, ContinuousOn (f · x) (Icc tmin tmax)
  /-- `L` is an upper bound of the norm of the vector field. -/
  norm_le : ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, ∀ x ∈ closedBall x₀ a, ‖f t x‖ ≤ L
  /-- The time interval of validity -/
  mul_max_le : L * max (tmax - t₀) (t₀ - tmin) ≤ a - r

C01: STRONGER FINITE-SLAB ROUTE
Let U,K bound |u| and |D_xu| on [0,T]×T³, transferred to the periodic lift.
lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le gives spatial K-Lipschitz continuity.
For initial ball radius r and center x0, choose Picard radius a≥r+UT,
tmin=0, tmax=T, t0=0, L=U. Then L*max(T−0,0−0)≤a−r.
The verified existence endpoint therefore supplies trajectories on the entire chosen slab.
No smallness assumption K*T<1 is present in IsPicardLindelof.
Uniqueness gives equivariance η(t,a+k)=η(t,a)+k and consistency on overlapping initial balls.
Time reversal gives inverse trajectories.
The substantial remaining adapter proves C∞ dependence on (t,a),
identifies parameter differentiation with F_t=(D_xu∘η)F, and yields a smooth inverse family.
A ContinuousOn or LipschitzOnWith conclusion must not be read as C∞ parameter dependence.

C01: JACOBIAN ADAPTER TARGET (NOT AN EXISTING MATHLIB NAME)
JACOBI_FIN3:
If each F_ij(t) is differentiable and F'=BF, then (det F)'=(trace B)det F.
Expand Matrix.det_fin_three, use scalar product/sum rules, and perform finite polynomial algebra.
F'=BF itself requires the C01 smooth-dependence adapter and mixed derivative symmetry.
With div u=0: J'=0, J(0)=1 ⇒ J=1 by the interval constant-derivative argument.
This route needs no pre-existing generic determinant-derivative theorem.

C02: PIOLA ADAPTER TARGETS (NOT EXISTING MATHLIB NAMES)
PIOLA_FIN3:
For C² η, Cof(Dη):=adjugate(Dη)ᵀ satisfies
Σ_α ∂_α Cof(Dη)_{iα}=0.
Expand Matrix.adjugate_fin_three; use product rule and mixed partial symmetry.
Piola itself does not require det(Dη)≠0.
For invertible F, prove Cof(F)=J F⁻ᵀ by adjugate/inverse algebra.

PULLBACK_DIVERGENCE_FIN3:
Div_a(J(Q∘η)Aᵀ)=J(div_x Q)∘η.
The differentiated cofactor term vanishes by Piola.
The chain-rule term collapses through F A=I.

C03: MATERIAL LAPLACIAN ADAPTER TARGET
PULLBACK_LAPLACIAN_FIN3:
Use Q=D_xu and D_aV=(D_xu∘η)F:
(Δ_xu)∘η=J⁻¹ Div_a(J D_aV A Aᵀ).
At J=1: (Δ_xu)∘η=Div_a(D_aV A Aᵀ).
For symmetric Newtonian stress, its additional transposed-gradient term pulls back ∇div u;
discard that term only after incompressibility has been established.

MIXED DERIVATIVE DEFINITION
IsSymmSndFDerivAt 𝕜 f x :=
  ∀ v w, fderiv 𝕜 (fderiv 𝕜 f) x v w = fderiv 𝕜 (fderiv 𝕜 f) x w v.
Source: Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Symmetric.lean, lines 91–92, same pin.

DEPENDENCY ADAPTERS

PRESSURE_P01:
  smooth real vector field on UnitAddTorus(Fin 3)
  -> complex scalar component coefficients with the chosen measure.
PRESSURE_P02:

  -> FourierCoeff(∂_j f)(k)=2*pi*i*k_j*FourierCoeff(f)(k), including k_j=0.
PRESSURE_P05:

  p_hat(0)=0;
  p_hat(k)=-(k·r_hat(k))/(2*pi*i*|k|^2), k≠0;

  mean-zero pressure normalization -> uniqueness.

REPRESENTATION / SCOPE ADAPTERS
1. Vec = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3); Field = Vec → Vec.
   Torus fields are actual coordinate-unit-periodic lifts on R^3.
2. SmoothSigmaZero and GlobalSmoothNSE impose zero mean. Our B-tier root
   allows arbitrary velocity mean. Prefer the general spatial calculus
   endpoints below. Do not silently replace the root predicate with
   GlobalSmoothNSE. A mean/finite-time adapter is an additional theorem.
3. Methlib timeDerivative is derivWithin on Ici 0. Our root is on [0,T]
   with right derivatives at zero and left derivatives at T. Restriction,
   locality, and endpoint-convention lemmas must be explicit.
4. physicalEnergy and coefficientEnergy equal squared L2 norm, not its half.
   E_TXT = physicalEnergy/2. Existing derivative is -2ν D; TXT derivative
   is -ν D after scaling by 1/2.
5. Galerkin cutoffModes excludes k=0; root Fourier reconstruction must keep
   the constant-mode residual test. General velocity mean is not supplied
   by a zero-mode-free Galerkin state.
6. AX6 is a separate uniform squared-enstrophy budget proposition. It is
   unnecessary for the exact smooth mechanics-equivalence root.
7. No source-read result promotes any endpoint to A_TIER.

abbrev Vec := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
abbrev Field := Vec → Vec
abbrev Velocity := ℝ → Field
abbrev Pressure := ℝ → Vec → ℝ
def SpatialPeriodic {E : Type*} (f : Vec → E) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Vec) (i : Fin 3), f (x + unitVector i) = f x
def PressureMeanZero (p : Vec → ℝ) : Prop :=
  IntegrableOn p unitCube volume ∧ (∫ x in unitCube, p x) = 0
def coordinateDerivative (a : Field) (i : Fin 3) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  fderiv ℝ a x (unitVector i)
def divergence (a : Field) (x : Vec) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, coordinateDerivative a i x i
def gradient (p : Vec → ℝ) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin 3 => fderiv ℝ p x (unitVector i))
def laplacian (a : Field) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, fderiv ℝ (coordinateDerivative a i) x (unitVector i)
def convection (a : Field) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  fderiv ℝ a x (a x)
def timeDerivative (u : Velocity) (t : ℝ) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  derivWithin (fun s : ℝ => u s x) (Ici (0 : ℝ)) t
structure SmoothSigmaZero (a : Field) : Prop where
  smooth : ContDiff ℝ ∞ a
  periodic : SpatialPeriodic a
  divergence_free : ∀ x : Vec, divergence a x = 0
  mean_zero : MeanZero a

def gradientSquareDensity (v : Field) (x : Vec) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3, (coordinateDerivative v i x j) ^ 2
def physicalEnstrophy (v : Field) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∫⁻ x in unitCube, ENNReal.ofReal (gradientSquareDensity v x)
def sixEnstrophy (N : ℕ) (c : FourierCoeff) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑ A : Fin 6, physicalEnstrophy (finiteSynthesis N (spectralChannel A c))
def budget6 (N : ℕ) (c : ℝ → FourierCoeff) (T : ℝ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∫⁻ t in Icc (0 : ℝ) T, (sixEnstrophy N (c t)) ^ 2
def AX6Statement : Prop :=
  ∀ (ν : ℝ), 0 < ν → ∀ (a : Field), SmoothSigmaZero a →
    ∀ (T : ℝ), 0 < T → ∃ M : ℝ≥0,
      ∀ (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → ∀ g : GalerkinSolution ν a N,
        budget6 N g.coeff T ≤ (M : ℝ≥0∞)

CRITICAL GAP REGISTER FOR MECHANICS EQUIVALENCE

G01. General material-flow construction on T^3, joint smooth inverse,
     eta(0)=id, and conversion from Euclidean periodic lifts to the torus.
     No fitting completed material-flow endpoint was located in the
     inspected active SingularClosure files.

G02. Jacobi determinant evolution, cofactor Piola identity, transformed
     divergence, material Laplacian, and determinant-one preservation.
     Existing spatial derivative definitions are concrete; the specific
     eta-dependent transformations still need Lean proofs.

G03. Measure-preserving material change of variables, arbitrary-region
     momentum differentiation, and Cauchy traction/divergence equivalence.
     Periodic IBP does not by itself prove moving-domain transport.

G04. Residual annihilation against all solenoidal test fields => zero Leray
     coefficients, including the constant coefficient. Existing M06/M07
     provide the multiplier/recovery half, not the test-annihilation half.

G05. Smooth residual r(t,x) => rapid Fourier coefficients uniformly with
     all time derivatives on [0,T], joint smooth recovered pressure, and
     pressure uniqueness. Existing M08 is spatial ContDiff only.
     M21--M24 below index the additional spatial decay/synthesis lemmas;
     uniform temporal differentiation remains a separate adapter.

G06. True variations through Diff_vol, delta u = w_t+[u,w], realization of
     every endpoint-fixed solenoidal w, and fibre derivative D_v R at fixed
     eta. These are not supplied by an NSE solution/energy theorem.

G07. Explicit inverse maps between finite-time solution sets; no existing
     GlobalSmoothNSE endpoint is itself the requested bijection.

G08. Canonical finite cotangent lift and invariant branch b=0. M16 gives
     actual RHS smoothness and M17 actual forward Galerkin existence;
     Hamilton equations and inverse trajectory correspondence remain
     separate elementary finite-dimensional proofs.

G09. Arbitrary-mean and temporal-boundary compatibility must preserve
     the exact root scope. Do not infer the universal zero-mean AX6 target
     from the unconditional formulation-equivalence theorem.

    (fun q : (ℤ × ℤ) × ℤ => ![q.1.1, q.1.2, q.2])).filter
      (fun k => k ≠ 0 ∧ galerkinFreqSq k ≤ (N : ℤ) ^ 2)

ADAPTER BOUNDARIES

A. M21--M24 supply spatial coefficient calculus and inverse-synthesis inputs.
   They do not alone discharge pressure temporal uniformity. To apply them
   to a smooth residual r(t,x), still prove time-differentiation of its actual
   Fourier coefficients, uniform summability on compact time slabs for all
   mixed derivatives, and joint smoothness of the reconstructed pressure.

B. M25 is finite-only. Its sharp 4*pi^2 constant can be transferred to an
   infinite mean-zero smooth field by a separately established convergence
   or full Parseval argument. Do not cite M25 as already declaring that
   infinite-field theorem.

C. CriticalPositiveSolenoidalTest is a predicate on ALL positive times.
   Its fields do not require NSE or zero mean, but they do require global
   positive-time smoothness, periodicity, and solenoidality. These premises
   are not supplied automatically by a solution known only on [0,T].
   For an interior t, a localized smooth temporal cutoff can be a route to
   an extension meeting the test predicate, followed by derivative locality.
   That construction is an adapter, not an extra conclusion of M26/M27.

D. Methlib timeDerivative uses derivWithin on Ici 0. A finite root matches
   it using the local germ for 0<=t<T. At t=0 it is right-sided; M26/M27
   themselves require t>0. At t=T>0, Ici 0 gives an ordinary two-sided
   derivative, so a compatible extension beyond T must be selected, or a
   within-[0,T] endpoint formulation must be proved separately.

E. No finite-interval argument here establishes GlobalSmoothNSE. A Galilean
   change of frame removes a conserved mean while preserving the finite
   interval; it supplies no extension to all nonnegative times.

F. physicalEnergy has no factor 1/2. M28 differentiates ||u||_2^2 with
   derivative 2*physicalFieldInner(u,d). The B-tier kinetic energy is half
   this quantity.

27. ROUND IV. TRANSPORTED LERAY PROJECTION, NORMAL ACCELERATION,
AND THE PROJECTED METRIC CONNECTION

ROOT_SCOPE:
  \nu>0; 0<T<infinity; \Omega=\mathbb T^3 with volume 1.
  Smooth fields and identity-normalized smooth volume-preserving paths.
  All velocity means are retained.
  The Eulerian and material pressures have spatial mean zero.
  No change to the root theorem's hypotheses or conclusions.
  Checkpoints: C31--C34.
  Existing checkpoints C01--C30 retain their exact scopes.

NOTATION:
  \mathcal H_x=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3),
  \mathcal H_a=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3).
  \mathscr S=C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3), dense in either Hilbert space.
  P=\mathbb P is the full-mean Eulerian Leray projection of Section 17.4.
  Q=I-P.
  P(0)=I in Fourier coordinates, so constant vector fields belong to ran(P).
  For k!=0, P(k)=I-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2.

For a stipulated path \eta(t) in the root configuration space:
  U_t f=f\circ\eta(t),
  u=\eta_t\circ\eta(t)^{-1},
  V=\eta_t=U_tu,
  P_t=U_t P U_t^{-1},
  Q_t=I-P_t=U_t Q U_t^{-1}.
  \mathcal T_t=ran(P_t), \mathcal N_t=ran(Q_t).
  D_u f=(u\cdot\nabla)f.
  b(t)=||D_xu(t)||_{L^\infty,\mathrm{op}}.

The operators U_t:\mathcal H_x -> \mathcal H_a are surjective linear isometries.
Hence P_t is the orthogonal projection onto \mathcal T_t.
On smooth fields,
  H in \mathcal T_t iff div_\eta H=0,
  H in \mathcal N_t iff H=grad_\eta q
    for a unique smooth zero-mean scalar q.
All scalar/vector pullbacks have the componentwise meaning fixed earlier.


C31. TRANSPORTED_PROJECTOR_DERIVATIVE

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C31
NEW_SOURCE_ENDPOINTS = ML-N05,ML-N07,ML-N09,ML-N13,ML-N14
EXISTING_SOURCE_ENDPOINTS = ML-I02,ML-O08,ML-O09,ML-O18
SCOPE = The transported projector is proved differentiable in L2 operator norm.
        No operator-norm derivative of U_t is assumed.
NEW_LEAN_ADAPTER = construct the bounded Leray commutator, extend the
                  dense-core integral identity, and prove operator-norm C1.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

C31.1. Smooth-core differentiation

For a smooth time-dependent Eulerian field f,
  d/dt (U_t f(t)) = U_t(f_t+D_u f).                         (IV.1)

For a fixed smooth material field H, put g(t)=U_t^{-1}H.
Applying (IV.1) to U_tg(t)=H gives
  g_t=-D_u g.                                               (IV.2)

P is independent of time and preserves smooth fields. Therefore
  d/dt(P_tH)
    =U_t(D_u Pg-PD_u g)
    =U_t[D_u,P]U_t^{-1}H.                                  (IV.3)

At this stage, [D_u,P] is defined on the smooth core.
A bounded extension is proved next.


C31.2. Exact bounded commutator identity

Fix a time. Let M_u be the bounded matrix-multiplication operator
  (M_u f)(x)=(D_xu(x))f(x).
Then
  M_u^*f=(D_xu)^{\mathsf T}f,
  ||M_u||<=b(t), \quad ||M_u^*||<=b(t).                      (IV.4)

For smooth divergence-free h, direct differentiation yields
  div(D_u h)
    =sum_{i,j} (\partial_i u_j)(\partial_j h_i)
    =div((D_xu)h).                                         (IV.5)
The discarded terms in the two divergences vanish respectively by
div h=0 and div u=0.
Thus D_u h-(D_xu)h is divergence-free, and
  QD_uP=QM_uP                                               (IV.6)
on smooth fields.

For a smooth scalar \phi,
  D_u(\nabla\phi)
    =\nabla(D_u\phi)-(D_xu)^{\mathsf T}\nabla\phi.            (IV.7)
Every smooth Qf is a gradient; P annihilates gradients. Hence
  PD_uQ=-PM_u^*Q.                                          (IV.8)

Using I=P+Q,
  [D_u,P]=QD_uP-PD_uQ
         =QM_uP+PM_u^*Q.                                  (IV.9)

Define the right-hand side on all of \mathcal H_x:
  K_u:=QM_uP+PM_u^*Q.
This is a bounded operator. Its adjoint satisfies
  K_u^*=PM_u^*Q+QM_uP=K_u.                                 (IV.10)

For z in \mathcal H_x, the two summands of K_uz are orthogonal:
  QM_uPz in ran(Q), \quad PM_u^*Qz in ran(P).
Consequently
  ||K_uz||_2^2
    =||QM_uPz||_2^2+||PM_u^*Qz||_2^2
    <=b(t)^2(||Pz||_2^2+||Qz||_2^2)
    =b(t)^2||z||_2^2.
Thus
  ||K_u||_{\mathcal H_x->\mathcal H_x}<=b(t).               (IV.11)

This proves boundedness directly; no pseudodifferential estimate is required.

Let
  M_t=U_tM_uU_t^{-1},
  (M_tH)(a)=B(t,a)H(a),
  B(t,a)=D_xu(t,\eta(t,a))=D_aV(t,a)A(t,a).
Then
  M_t^*H=B(t,a)^{\mathsf T}H(a),
  K_t:=U_tK_uU_t^{-1}
      =Q_tM_tP_t+P_tM_t^*Q_t,                              (IV.12)
  K_t^*=K_t,\qquad ||K_t||<=b(t).                          (IV.13)
The conjugation in (IV.12) is an identity of bounded operators at each time.


C31.3. Operator-norm differentiation

For H in the smooth material core, (IV.3) and (IV.12) give
  P_tH-P_sH=int_s^t K_rH\,dr.                              (IV.14)
The integrand is continuous in L2 because every expression on the smooth
core is jointly smooth in the stipulated finite slab.

For 0<=s<=t<=T, (IV.13) implies
  ||(P_t-P_s)H||_2
    <=(int_s^t b(r)\,dr)||H||_2.
The smooth core is dense and P_t,P_s are bounded. Hence
  ||P_t-P_s||_{\mathrm{op}}<=int_s^t b(r)\,dr.              (IV.15)

In particular t->P_t is operator-norm continuous.

The coefficient B(t,a) is jointly smooth on the compact slab. Therefore
  ||M_t-M_s||_{\mathrm{op}}
    <=sup_a ||B(t,a)-B(s,a)||_{\mathrm{op}} ->0.
Now (IV.12), with operator-norm continuous P_t,Q_t,M_t, shows that K_t is
operator-norm continuous. This conclusion does not follow from strong
continuity of U_t alone; it follows from the explicit bounded formula.

The Bochner integral of K_r now exists in the Banach space
\mathcal L(\mathcal H_a,\mathcal H_a). By (IV.14) and density,
  P_t-P_s=int_s^t K_r\,dr                                  (IV.16)
as an operator identity.

The Banach-space fundamental theorem of calculus yields
  P_t'=K_t
      =U_t[D_u,P]U_t^{-1}
      =Q_tM_tP_t+P_tM_t^*Q_t                               (IV.17)
in operator norm on (0,T), with the corresponding one-sided derivatives
at t=0,T. The commutator expression denotes the bounded extension (IV.9).
Moreover,
  (P_t')^*=P_t',\qquad ||P_t'||<=b(t).                      (IV.18)

The compact-slab smoothness of B gives operator-norm smoothness of M_t.
The polynomial differential equation (IV.17) consequently bootstraps P_t
to C^\infty in operator norm, with the same endpoint convention.
Only C1 is needed in C32--C34.

For any two orthogonal projections P_1,P_2 on a Hilbert space,
  P_1-P_2=P_1(I-P_2)-(I-P_1)P_2.
The two outputs on the right are orthogonal, and both projections are
contractive. Thus
  ||(P_1-P_2)z||^2
    <=||(I-P_2)z||^2+||P_2z||^2=||z||^2.
Together with (IV.15),
  ||P_t-P_s||_{\mathrm{op}}
    <=min{1, int_s^t b(r)\,dr}, \quad s<=t.                 (IV.19)

For every spatially constant vector c,
  P_tc=c, \qquad P_t'c=0.                                 (IV.20)
Thus the zero Fourier mode has not been removed.


C32. PROJECTOR_OFFDIAGONAL_IDENTITIES_AND_NORMAL_ACCELERATION

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C32
NEW_SOURCE_ENDPOINTS = ML-N01,ML-N02,ML-N05,ML-N06,ML-N08,
                       ML-N10,ML-N11,ML-N12,ML-N15
EXISTING_SOURCE_ENDPOINTS = ML-O18,ML-I02
SCOPE = Differentiate P_t^2=P_t only after C31 proves operator-norm C1.
NEW_LEAN_ADAPTER = bounded projection derivative block algebra and
                  identification with the root pressure.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

C32.1. Orthogonal block structure

Since P_t^2=P_t, differentiation in the Banach algebra of bounded
operators gives
  P_t'P_t+P_tP_t'=P_t'.                                   (IV.21)

Left and right multiplication by P_t, followed by cancellation, gives
  P_tP_t'P_t=0.                                            (IV.22)
Likewise, with Q_t=I-P_t,
  Q_tP_t'Q_t=0.                                            (IV.23)

Hence
  P_t'=Q_tP_t'P_t+P_tP_t'Q_t,                             (IV.24)
  P_t'(\mathcal T_t) subset \mathcal N_t,
  P_t'(\mathcal N_t) subset \mathcal T_t.                  (IV.25)

Because (P_t')^*=P_t', the two offdiagonal blocks are mutual adjoints.
For H in \mathcal T_t or H in \mathcal N_t,
  <P_t'H,H>_a=0.                                          (IV.26)

C32.2. Differentiated moving tangency

Let H(t) be any smooth material field with P_tH(t)=H(t).
Differentiation gives
  Q_tH_t=P_t'H.                                           (IV.27)

For the path velocity V=\eta_t, volume preservation gives P_tV=V.
Consequently
  Q_tV_t=P_t'V
    =U_tQ((u\cdot\nabla)u).                                (IV.28)

For a root NSE solution, applying Q to its Eulerian momentum equation,
and using Qu_t=0, Q\Delta u=0 and Q\nabla p=\nabla p, gives
  Q((u\cdot\nabla)u)=-\nabla p.
With \pi=p\circ\eta,
  P_t'V=Q_tV_t=-grad_\eta\pi.                              (IV.29)

Thus the normal acceleration is exactly the normalized pressure force.
Its instantaneous power vanishes:
  <-grad_\eta\pi,V>_a=0.                                  (IV.30)

Let m=int_\Omega u(t,x) dx=int_\Omega V(t,a) da be the conserved
velocity mean. Constants satisfy P_t'm=0. Thus P_t'V=P_t'(V-m),
and the bound in C31 gives the sharper estimate
  ||grad_\eta\pi||_2<=b(t)||V-m||_2
                    =b(t)||u-m||_2.                       (IV.31)
Equivalently, ||grad p||_2 obeys the same bound. Combining with C23,
  ||grad p||_2=||grad_\eta\pi||_2
    <=min{||D_xu||_{infinity,op}||u-m||_2,
          ||u-m||_infinity||D_xu||_2}.                     (IV.31a)
For the second term, Q((u dot grad)u)=Q(((u-m) dot grad)u), because
(m dot grad)u is divergence-free, and Q is an L2 contraction.
No interval-independent bound on b(t) is asserted.


C33. SYMMETRIC_BILINEAR_NORMAL_FORM

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C33
NEW_SOURCE_ENDPOINTS = ML-N05,ML-N08,ML-N09
EXISTING_SOURCE_ENDPOINTS = ML-O18,ML-O19,ML-O20
SCOPE = Smooth tangent fields; real bilinearity and symmetry.
        No bounded L2 x L2 bilinear extension is asserted.
NEW_LEAN_ADAPTER = divergence-free Lie-bracket identity and normal form.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

Fix one configuration \eta and smooth tangent material fields H,K:
  P_\eta H=H,\qquad P_\eta K=K.
Put
  h=U_\eta^{-1}H,\qquad k=U_\eta^{-1}K,
so div h=div k=0.

Define
  \mathcal B_\eta(H,K)
    :=U_\eta Q((h\cdot\nabla)k).                           (IV.32)

This is a real-bilinear map on smooth tangent fields and has values
in the smooth normal space:
  P_\eta\mathcal B_\eta(H,K)=0.                            (IV.33)

Direct component differentiation gives
  div((h\cdot\nabla)k-(k\cdot\nabla)h)=0:
the second-derivative terms vanish by div h=div k=0, and the remaining
two sums cancel after exchanging their indices. Therefore
  Q((h\cdot\nabla)k)=Q((k\cdot\nabla)h),
and hence
  \mathcal B_\eta(H,K)=\mathcal B_\eta(K,H).                (IV.34)

Equivalently,
  \mathcal B_\eta(H,K)
    =U_\eta Q((D_xk)h)
    =U_\eta Q((D_xh)k).                                    (IV.35)

Contraction of Q and unitarity of U_\eta imply the exact tame estimate
  ||\mathcal B_\eta(H,K)||_2
    <=min{
       ||D_xk||_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}||h||_2,
       ||D_xh||_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}||k||_2
      }.                                                   (IV.36)

For a smooth tangent field H(t)=U_th(t) along \eta(t), (IV.1) gives
  Q_tH_t=U_tQ(D_u h)
        =\mathcal B_{\eta(t)}(V,H).                        (IV.37)
Since h_t is divergence-free, its projection under Q vanishes.
Combining (IV.27) and (IV.37),
  P_t'H=\mathcal B_{\eta(t)}(V,H).                          (IV.38)

In particular, for a root NSE solution,
  \mathcal B_\eta(V,V)
    =P_t'V
    =-grad_\eta\pi.                                        (IV.39)

Symmetry in (IV.34) is an identity of the specified normal-valued
bilinear form. No assertion of a bounded bilinear operator on the
whole L2 tangent space is made.


C34. PROJECTED_METRIC_CONNECTION_AND_COVARIANT_DAMPED_NEWTON

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C34
NEW_SOURCE_ENDPOINTS = ML-N03,ML-N04,ML-N08,ML-N09
EXISTING_SOURCE_ENDPOINTS = ML-D02,ML-I02,ML-O09
MATHEMATICAL_DEPENDENCIES = C03,C04,C21,C31,C32,C33
SCOPE = Exact along-path metric derivative and an equivalent constrained
        Newton equation on the fixed smooth solution class.
NEW_LEAN_ADAPTER = define the along-path derivative and prove its
                  metric identity and inverse solution correspondence.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

C34.1. Definition and Eulerian representation

For a smooth tangent field H(t) along \eta(t), define
  \nabla_t^\eta H:=P_tH_t.                                (IV.40)

This derivative remains tangent. It is real-linear in H and satisfies,
for a smooth real scalar function f(t),
  \nabla_t^\eta(fH)=f'H+f\nabla_t^\eta H.                   (IV.41)

Writing H=U_th with div h=0, (IV.1) yields
  \nabla_t^\eta H
    =U_tP(h_t+D_u h)
    =U_t(h_t+P((u\cdot\nabla)h)).                          (IV.42)

The complete ambient derivative decomposes as
  H_t=\nabla_t^\eta H+\mathcal B_\eta(V,H).                 (IV.43)

C34.2. Metric compatibility

For smooth tangent H,K,
  d/dt <H,K>_a=<H_t,K>_a+<H,K_t>_a.
Since P_t is self-adjoint and fixes H,K,
  d/dt <H,K>_a
    =<\nabla_t^\eta H,K>_a+<H,\nabla_t^\eta K>_a.           (IV.44)

Thus (IV.40) is a metric-compatible projected derivative along every
stipulated path. Formula (IV.44) is the exact asserted metric property.

C34.3. Covariant damped Newton equation

For V=U_tu and div u=0,
  \Delta_\eta V=U_t\Delta u in \mathcal T_t.               (IV.45)

The material NSE is
  V_t=-grad_\eta\pi+\nu\Delta_\eta V.
Projection therefore gives
  \nabla_t^\eta V=\nu\Delta_\eta V.                        (IV.46)

Conversely, let \eta(t) be a smooth path in the root configuration
space with
  \eta(0)=id,\qquad \eta_t(0)=u_0,
and suppose (IV.46). Put u=V\circ\eta^{-1}.
By (IV.42) and (IV.45),
  u_t+P((u\cdot\nabla)u)=\nu\Delta u.                       (IV.47)

The smooth mean-zero Poisson problem
  -\Delta p=div((u\cdot\nabla)u),\qquad int_\Omega p=0       (IV.48)
has the unique solution supplied by the already proved periodic
pressure recovery. Since
  Q((u\cdot\nabla)u)=-\nabla p,
equation (IV.47) is exactly
  u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla p+\nu\Delta u.                (IV.49)

With \pi=p\circ\eta, (IV.39),(IV.43),(IV.46) recover
  V_t=\nu\Delta_\eta V-grad_\eta\pi.                        (IV.50)

Hence the root Eulerian solution set is in explicit bijection with
smooth configuration paths satisfying (IV.46) and the root initial data.
The maps are precisely the previously fixed flow/reconstruction maps;
the pressure is uniquely reconstructed by (IV.48).
The root finite-time scope and all velocity means are preserved.

C34.4. Energy identity in covariant form

Using metric compatibility and the established material Laplacian identity,
  d/dt (1/2)||V||_2^2
    =<\nabla_t^\eta V,V>_a
    =\nu<\Delta_\eta V,V>_a
    =-\nu||D_aV A||_2^2.                                  (IV.51)

Constants are retained in \mathcal T_t and annihilated by \Delta_\eta.
No additional smallness condition and no global-in-time existence
conclusion have been introduced.

28. STRENGTHENING ROUND V: CLOSED STOKES OPERATOR AND RAYLEIGH GEOMETRY

Scope: the unit-volume torus and viscosity nu>0 of Sections 1--2.
A configuration eta in Q is FIXED throughout Sections 28.1--28.7.
