The operator Acal_eta is distinguished from the matrix A=(D_a eta)^(-1).

28.1. Actual Hilbert spaces and Fourier coordinates

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C35
ML-S01 = memℓp_gen_iff
ML-S02 = lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum
ML-S03 = HilbertBasis.hasSum_repr_symm
ML-S04 = lp.hasSum_single
ML-S05 = LinearPMap.mem_adjoint_domain_of_exists
ML-S06 = LinearPMap.adjoint_apply_eq
ML-S08 = LinearIsometryEquiv.ofLinearIsometry
M30 = SingularClosure.smoothFourierSynthesis_divergence_free
M31 = SingularClosure.datumFourierCoeff_laplacian
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L21
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Exact real solenoidal basis, weighted domain, dense partial-operator adjoint and transported graph core.
Full added signatures/source URLs: Sections 32--35.
ADDITIONAL_SOURCE_INDEX_V1_3:
  M44 = SingularClosure.SMOOTH_DATUM_MEM_TORUS_SOBOLEV
  M45 = SingularClosure.torusDatumL2_fourierBasis_repr
  STRENGTHENED_CHECKPOINTS = C53,C54; Section 39.
  Exact added signatures and source contexts: Sections 40--42.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

Let
  H:=L^2(T^3;R^3),
  H_sigma:={u in H : div u=0 in distributions},
  H_sigma,0:={u in H_sigma : integral u=0}.

For k in Z^3, use the actual normalized Fourier coefficients
  u_hat(k):=integral_{T^3} u(x) exp(-2*pi*i*k.x) dx.

The distributional solenoidal condition is exactly
  k.u_hat(k)=0  for every k!=0.                              (28.1)
Reality is exactly
  u_hat(-k)=conj(u_hat(k)).
The k=0 coefficient is the vector mean.

Proof of the reverse implication in (28.1).
A smooth periodic scalar test function has derivative Fourier series
converging in L2. Its finite Fourier partial sums therefore approximate
its gradient in L2. Pairing u with each such finite gradient gives zero
by k.u_hat(k)=0. Passage to the L2 limit gives the distributional identity.
The forward implication follows by testing sine and cosine characters.
Each Fourier coefficient is a continuous linear functional on L2.
Consequently H_sigma and H_sigma,0 are closed real Hilbert subspaces.

An explicit real orthonormal basis is available.
Choose one k from each pair {k,-k}, k!=0, forming Z^3_+.
For each k choose an orthonormal basis e_{k,1},e_{k,2} of k^perp in R^3.
The vectors
  e_1,e_2,e_3,
  sqrt(2)e_{k,r} cos(2*pi*k.x),
  sqrt(2)e_{k,r} sin(2*pi*k.x),
  k in Z^3_+, r in {1,2},                                  (28.2)
form an orthonormal basis (phi_j)_{j in I} of H_sigma.
Orthogonality follows from integration of Fourier characters.
Completeness follows from (28.1), reality, and actual Fourier uniqueness.

Let I_c contain the three constant modes and I_+ the remaining indices.
Set
  kappa_j:=0 for j in I_c,
  kappa_j:=4*pi^2*|k|^2 for the modes associated with k!=0.
Then
  -Delta phi_j=kappa_j phi_j,
  kappa_j>=4*pi^2 for j in I_+.
The minimum 4*pi^2 is attained, e.g. by
  phi_*(x):=sqrt(2)e_1 sin(2*pi*x_2).

The coordinate map
  F_sigma:H_sigma -> ell^2(I;R),
  F_sigma(u)_j:=<u,phi_j>
is a surjective real-linear isometry. Thus
  ||u||_2^2=sum_j |F_sigma(u)_j|^2.
The mean-zero subspace corresponds exactly to coordinates zero on I_c.

28.2. Exact domain and selfadjoint diagonal operator

Define the actual periodic Sobolev spaces by
  H^r_sigma
    :={u in H_sigma :
        sum_j (1+kappa_j)^r |F_sigma(u)_j|^2 < infinity},
  r in {1,2}.

These definitions agree with weak-derivative H^r on the torus.
Indeed, Fourier coefficients of the weak derivative partial^alpha u are
  (2*pi*i*k)^alpha u_hat(k).
For r=1,2, summing their squared component norms gives weights equivalent
to (1+4*pi^2|k|^2)^r. Conversely a finite weighted coefficient sum produces
each weak derivative in L2 by Fourier reconstruction, and testing smooth
Fourier partial sums verifies the weak-derivative identity.

Define Acal on H_sigma by the exact domain
  D(Acal):=H^2_sigma
          ={u in H_sigma : sum_j kappa_j^2 |u_j|^2<infinity},
  (Acal u)_j:=kappa_j u_j.                                 (28.3)

The second equality of domains follows from u in ell^2 and
  kappa^2 <= (1+kappa)^2 <= 2(1+kappa^2), kappa>=0.
The vector Acal u is well-defined in H_sigma by the weighted ell^2 condition.
For smooth solenoidal u, it equals the actual differential field -Delta u.

Denseness.
Finite Fourier sums belong to D(Acal) and are dense in H_sigma.
Their mean-zero versions are dense in H_sigma,0.

Closedness.
Suppose u_n -> u and Acal u_n -> v in H_sigma.
Coordinate evaluation is continuous; hence
  (u_n)_j -> u_j,
  kappa_j(u_n)_j -> v_j.
Therefore v_j=kappa_j u_j for every j. Since v is in ell^2,
u belongs to D(Acal) and Acal u=v. Thus the graph is closed.

Symmetry.
For u,v in D(Acal), Cauchy--Schwarz justifies the sums and gives
  <Acal u,v>=sum_j kappa_j u_j v_j=<u,Acal v>.              (28.4)

Exact adjoint domain.
By the definition of the adjoint of a densely defined real Hilbert operator,
y belongs to D(Acal^*) exactly when some z in H_sigma satisfies
  <Acal x,y>=<x,z>  for every x in D(Acal).
Testing x=phi_j gives
  z_j=kappa_j y_j.
Since z is in ell^2, y belongs to D(Acal), and Acal y=z.
Conversely, y in D(Acal) satisfies this pairing identity with z=Acal y
by (28.4). Therefore
  D(Acal^*)=D(Acal),   Acal^*=Acal.                         (28.5)
No bounded-operator spectral theorem is used to bypass the domain.

Nonnegativity and kernel.
For u in D(Acal),
  <u,Acal u>=sum_j kappa_j |u_j|^2>=0,
  ker Acal=span_R{e_1,e_2,e_3}.                             (28.6)

Smooth core.
Let C_sigma:=C^infinity_sigma(T^3).
For u in D(Acal), truncate its Fourier coefficients to |k|<=N.
Then u_N is in C_sigma and
  ||u_N-u||_2 ->0,
  ||Acal u_N-Acal u||_2 ->0.
Thus C_sigma is a graph core, and the closure of
  (-Delta)|_{C_sigma}
is exactly the operator (28.3).
The smooth core and the closed L2 operator domain are distinct objects.

28.3. Fixed-configuration transported operator

By C19, the pullback
  U_eta f:=f circ eta
is a surjective real-linear L2 isometry with inverse U_eta^{-1}.
Define
  S_eta:=U_eta H_sigma,
  S_eta,0:=U_eta H_sigma,0,
  phi_j^eta:=U_eta phi_j.

The phi_j^eta form a real orthonormal basis of S_eta.
The mean is preserved, so S_eta,0 is the mean-zero part of S_eta.
Constants remain the same constant vector fields.

Define
  D(Acal_eta):=U_eta H^2_sigma,
  Acal_eta:=U_eta Acal U_eta^{-1}.                          (28.7)

Equivalently, with V_j:=<V,phi_j^eta>,
  V in D(Acal_eta) iff sum_j kappa_j^2 |V_j|^2<infinity,
  Acal_eta V=sum_j kappa_j V_j phi_j^eta.                  (28.8)

Applying the proofs of Section 28.2 to this transported basis yields:
  D(Acal_eta) is dense in S_eta;
  Acal_eta is closed, selfadjoint and nonnegative on S_eta;
  ker Acal_eta is exactly the constant vector fields.

For smooth V in S_eta, the conjugacy of C20 gives
  Acal_eta V=-Delta_eta V
    =-Div_a(D_aV A A^T).                                   (28.9)

The transported smooth core
  C_eta:=U_eta C_sigma
is graph dense in D(Acal_eta).
Equation (28.9) specifies the differential expression on the smooth core;
equations (28.7)--(28.8) specify its full closed L2 realization.

Define the closed quadratic form
  q_eta(V):=sum_j kappa_j |V_j|^2,
  D(q_eta):=U_eta H^1_sigma.                                (28.10)

The form norm is
  ||V||_{q_eta}^2:=||V||_2^2+q_eta(V)
                 =sum_j (1+kappa_j)|V_j|^2.
It is complete by completeness of weighted ell^2.
Finite Fourier sums are dense for this norm.
For V in D(Acal_eta),
  q_eta(V)=<V,Acal_eta V>;
for smooth V,
  q_eta(V)=integral |D_aV A|^2.                             (28.11)

28.4. Sharp mean-zero spectral gap and exact resolvent

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C36
ML-S01 = memℓp_gen_iff
ML-S02 = lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum
ML-S03 = HilbertBasis.hasSum_repr_symm
ML-S07 = isCompactOperator_of_tendsto
ML-F07 = UnitAddTorus.hasSum_sq_mFourierCoeff
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L22
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Retain the mean-zero restriction at lambda=0; prove both inverse identities and finite-rank compactness.
Full added signatures/source URLs: Sections 32--35.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

Write Acal_eta,0 for the restriction to the invariant Hilbert subspace
S_eta,0, with domain D(Acal_eta) intersect S_eta,0.

The coefficient inequalities give, for V in D(q_eta) intersect S_eta,0,
  q_eta(V)>=4*pi^2 ||V||_2^2.                              (28.12)

For V in D(Acal_eta,0),
  <V,Acal_eta,0 V> >=4*pi^2||V||_2^2,
  ||Acal_eta,0 V||_2>=4*pi^2||V||_2.                       (28.13)

Both constants are attained by phi_*^eta.
Thus the gap 4*pi^2 is exact.

Fix lambda>=0 and nu>0.
For f in S_eta,0, define the actual resolvent
  R_eta(lambda) f
    :=sum_{j in I_+}
       (lambda+nu*kappa_j)^(-1) f_j phi_j^eta.              (28.14)

This sum converges in L2 because
  0<(lambda+nu*kappa_j)^(-1)
       <=(lambda+4*pi^2*nu)^(-1).
Its value belongs to D(Acal_eta,0), since
  kappa_j/(lambda+nu*kappa_j)<=1/nu
implies
  sum_j kappa_j^2 |(R_eta(lambda)f)_j|^2
    <=nu^(-2)||f||_2^2.

Coordinate calculation now proves BOTH inverse identities:
  (lambda I+nu Acal_eta,0)R_eta(lambda)f=f
      for f in S_eta,0,
  R_eta(lambda)(lambda I+nu Acal_eta,0)V=V
      for V in D(Acal_eta,0).                              (28.15)

Consequently
  R_eta(lambda)=(lambda I+nu Acal_eta,0)^(-1)
is an everywhere-defined bounded operator from S_eta,0 into S_eta,0,
whose range is the operator domain D(Acal_eta,0).

Its exact operator norm is
  ||R_eta(lambda)||_{L2->L2}
       =1/(lambda+4*pi^2*nu).                              (28.16)

Upper bound: the multiplier bound and Parseval.
Lower bound: apply to the unit eigenvector phi_*^eta.
In particular, lambda=0 is allowed on S_eta,0.

On the full S_eta, lambda>0 gives the analogous inverse with norm 1/lambda,
attained by constants. At lambda=0 the full operator is not invertible,
because its kernel contains exactly those constants.

28.5. Compact resolvent by a finite-rank approximation

Let P_N^eta retain the transported Fourier modes with |k|<=N.
Each P_N^eta has finite rank, since only finitely many integer lattice
points satisfy this bound and each frequency has finite polarization
multiplicity. It preserves the solenoidal and mean-zero conditions.

For N>=1, on S_eta,0,
  ||R_eta(lambda)-P_N^eta R_eta(lambda)||
    <=sup_{|k|>N} 1/(lambda+4*pi^2*nu*|k|^2)
    <=1/(lambda+4*pi^2*nu*N^2)
    ->0.                                                   (28.17)

Each P_N^eta R_eta(lambda) is finite rank.
To verify compactness directly: for any epsilon>0 choose N so the
operator-norm error is below epsilon/2. The image of the unit ball
under the finite-rank approximation is bounded in a finite-dimensional
space and has a finite epsilon/2-net. The same centers give an epsilon-net
for R_eta(lambda) of the unit ball. Hence that image is totally bounded;
its closure is compact because S_eta,0 is complete.

Thus R_eta(lambda) is compact.
The same argument, including the three constant modes in P_N^eta,
proves compactness on the full S_eta for lambda>0.

The eigenbasis (phi_j^eta) already provides the complete diagonal
resolution. No spectral value below 4*pi^2 occurs on S_eta,0, and the
lower endpoint 4*pi^2 is an eigenvalue. Finite-dimensional mode cutoffs
are used only to prove these fixed linear operator facts.

28.6. Frozen auxiliary-time semigroup

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C37
ML-S01 = memℓp_gen_iff
ML-S02 = lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum
ML-S03 = HilbertBasis.hasSum_repr_symm
ML-S04 = lp.hasSum_single
ML-S08 = LinearIsometryEquiv.ofLinearIsometry
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L22
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = The configuration is frozen; the exact generator domain requires both directions of the coefficient argument.
Full added signatures/source URLs: Sections 32--35.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

For this FIXED eta and s>=0, define
  S_eta(s):=U_eta exp(s*nu*Delta) U_eta^{-1},
or equivalently
  S_eta(s)f:=sum_j exp(-nu*kappa_j*s) f_j phi_j^eta.         (28.18)

The bounded multipliers make this an everywhere-defined bounded L2
operator. Coordinate multiplication proves
  S_eta(0)=I,
  S_eta(s+r)=S_eta(s)S_eta(r),  s,r>=0.

For each f, strong continuity follows by finite-mode approximation:
on a finite set every scalar exponential is continuous, while the L2
tail is bounded by the corresponding tail of f uniformly for s>=0.
Thus this is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup.

Exact norms:
  ||S_eta(s)||_{S_eta->S_eta}=1,
  ||S_eta(s)||_{S_eta,0->S_eta,0}
       =exp(-4*pi^2*nu*s).                                 (28.19)
Constants attain the first norm; phi_*^eta attains the second.

Exact generator domain.
If f in D(Acal_eta), then for h>0
  |(exp(-nu*kappa_j*h)-1)/h|<=nu*kappa_j.
The weighted ell^2 condition and a finite-mode/tail argument imply
  lim_{h downarrow 0}(S_eta(h)f-f)/h=-nu Acal_eta f
in L2.
Conversely, if this L2 limit exists and equals g, continuity of each
coordinate yields
  g_j=-nu*kappa_j f_j.
Since g is in ell^2, f belongs to D(Acal_eta).
Therefore the generator is exactly
  -nu Acal_eta, with domain D(Acal_eta).                    (28.20)

For f in D(Acal_eta),
  d/ds S_eta(s)f=-nu Acal_eta S_eta(s)f,
with the right derivative at s=0.
For every s>0 and every integer m>=1,
  sup_{kappa>=0} kappa^m exp(-nu*kappa*s)
       <=(m/(e*nu*s))^m.
Hence S_eta(s)f belongs to every operator-power domain.
The exponential coefficient decay, Cauchy--Schwarz, and polynomial
lattice-point counting make every spatially differentiated Fourier
series absolutely convergent. Thus S_eta(s)f is smooth for s>0.

On S_eta,0, the norm bound (28.19) makes the Bochner integral
  integral_0^infinity exp(-lambda*s) S_eta(s)f ds
convergent for every lambda>=0. Pairing with each basis vector gives
the scalar integral 1/(lambda+nu*kappa_j). Fourier uniqueness therefore
proves the resolvent identity
  R_eta(lambda)f
    =integral_0^infinity exp(-lambda*s) S_eta(s)f ds.         (28.21)

PHYSICAL-TIME SCOPE.
The eta in (28.18)--(28.21) is frozen. For a physical material path eta(t),
both U_eta(t) and Acal_eta(t) vary with t, and the actual equation is
  P_eta(t) V_t=-nu Acal_eta(t)V,
not V_t=-nu Acal_eta(t)V.
No physical NSE solution, physical-time representation, or global
nonlinear regularity theorem is inferred from the frozen semigroup.

28.7. Rayleigh gradient and exact acceleration minimum principle

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
CHECKPOINTS = C38
ML-D01 = HasDerivAt.norm_sq
ML-D02 = HasDerivAt.inner
ML-D03 = ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt_of_bilinear
ML-H04 = MeasureTheory.L2.inner_def
ML-S02 = lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L23
SOURCE_STATUS = verified at the frozen revision; project compiler/audit absent.
SCOPE = Form domain H1, operator domain H2, L2 Riesz representative; minimizing acceleration is P_eta eta_tt.
Full added signatures/source URLs: Sections 32--35.
[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]

At fixed eta define, on the form domain,
  R_eta(V):=(nu/2)q_eta(V).
For V in D(Acal_eta), this is
  R_eta(V)=(nu/2)<V,Acal_eta V>.                            (28.22)
On smooth material tangent vectors this equals exactly the original
Rayleigh functional
  (nu/2) integral |D_aV A|^2.

For V in D(Acal_eta) and H in D(q_eta), the coefficient expansion gives
  d/d epsilon|_{epsilon=0} R_eta(V+epsilon H)
    =nu sum_j kappa_j V_j H_j
    =nu<Acal_eta V,H>.                                     (28.23)

The sum converges by Cauchy--Schwarz, since Acal_eta V and H are in L2.
The resulting functional extends continuously to every H in S_eta.
Its unique tangent L2 Riesz representative is
  grad_{L2,S_eta} R_eta(V)=nu Acal_eta V.                    (28.24)
Uniqueness also follows by testing the dense smooth tangent directions.

This is an L2-representable directional derivative at V in D(Acal_eta).
R_eta is not asserted to be a Frechet C1 functional on all of S_eta:
its form domain is U_eta H^1_sigma, and its operator domain is
U_eta H^2_sigma. On the graph/form domains the indicated differentiations
have their stated meanings.

For a fixed V in D(Acal_eta), define the strictly convex functional
on the entire tangent Hilbert space S_eta:
  J_{eta,V}(W):=(1/2)||W||_2^2+nu<Acal_eta V,W>.             (28.25)

Completing the square gives
  J_{eta,V}(W)
    =(1/2)||W+nu Acal_eta V||_2^2
      -(nu^2/2)||Acal_eta V||_2^2.
Therefore
  argmin_{W in S_eta} J_{eta,V}(W)
    ={-nu Acal_eta V},                                     (28.26)
and
  min J_{eta,V}=-(nu^2/2)||Acal_eta V||_2^2.

If V is smooth, the minimizer is a smooth tangent field.
For a physical smooth path eta(t) in Q, define its tangent acceleration
  W(t):=P_eta(t) eta_tt(t).
C21 and (28.9) now give the exact equivalence
  eta solves the constrained material NSE
    iff
  for every t, W(t) is the unique minimizer of J_{eta(t),V(t)}. (28.27)

The acceleration in this principle is P_eta eta_tt.
The normal acceleration and its pressure multiplier remain those of C22.
The minimization is instantaneous at fixed (eta,V); it is not a
minimization over physical solution trajectories.

For mean-zero V in D(q_eta), the sharp gap also yields
  R_eta(V)>=2*pi^2*nu*||V||_2^2.                            (28.28)
For V,W in D(Acal_eta) with the same mean,
  <nu Acal_eta(V-W),V-W>
    >=4*pi^2*nu*||V-W||_2^2.                               (28.29)
Thus the Rayleigh gradient is strongly monotone on every fixed-mean
operator-domain slice, with sharp constant 4*pi^2*nu.
On the full space its only zero-gradient directions are constant vectors.

29. ROUND VI: VOLUME-UNCONSTRAINED DIFFEOMORPHISM EQUATION
================================================================

Classification: ! B_TIER.
Checkpoints: C39--C42.
Domain: T^3=R^3/Z^3, normalized Lebesgue measure, 0<T<infinity,
constant viscosity nu>0, no external force, normalized density one.
All fields and configuration paths below are jointly C^infinity on the
stated closed time slab, with the endpoint convention of the root theorem.
Ordinary time derivatives occur on 0<t<T. Integrated identities extend
to 0<=s<=t<=T by continuity and one-sided endpoint limits.

29.1. Extended configuration class and fixed-time projection
----------------------------------------------------------------

Let Diff^infinity_{+,0}(T^3) denote the orientation-preserving smooth
diffeomorphisms in the identity component. Volume preservation is not a
defining premise of this class.

For an arbitrary smooth periodic initial field w0, define X_nu(w0;T)
to be the set of smooth paths eta:[0,T]->Diff^infinity_{+,0}(T^3)
such that

  eta(0,a)=a,       V:=eta_t,       V(0,a)=w0(a),

and the equation (EX) below holds. A lift eta(t,a)=a+xi(t,a), with xi
periodic in a and xi(0,a)=0, fixes the flat-coordinate interpretation of
V and V_t. The results are independent of integer translations of a lift.

Set

  F=D_a eta,       A=F^{-1},       J=det F>0,
  u(t,x)=V(t,eta(t)^{-1}(x)),
  U_eta f=f o eta,
  c=(u . grad_x)u=D_x u[u],
  d=div_x u.

For a vector field W on the label torus define the general-J material
Laplacian componentwise by

  Delta_eta^J W
    := J^{-1} Div_a(J D_a W A A^T).

The row-divergence convention is

  [Div_a M]_i = sum_alpha partial_{a_alpha} M_{i alpha}.

For a scalar f define

  Delta_eta^J f
    := J^{-1} div_a(J A A^T grad_a f).

Let P be the full periodic Leray projection, including its constant
mode. Its Fourier symbol is

  P_0=I,
  P_k=I-(k k^T)/|k|^2          (k in Z^3, k!=0).

Set Q=I-P. Then Q_0=0, and for every smooth periodic vector field f,

  div(Pf)=0,        P^2=P,        Q^2=Q,
  P grad g=0,      Q grad g=grad g

for every smooth periodic scalar g. Furthermore Pf=f whenever div f=0.
These identities hold at each fixed time and retain arbitrary velocity
mean.

Proof of the stated projection identities.
For k!=0, k^T P_k=0 and P_k^2=P_k by direct matrix multiplication.
For k=0 the divergence symbol is zero, P_0=I and Q_0=0.
The gradient symbol is 2*pi*i*k. Thus P annihilates gradients and Q is
the identity on them. If div f=0, then k dot f_hat(k)=0 for every k!=0,
so P_k f_hat(k)=f_hat(k), including k=0. The matrices P_k and Q_k
have Euclidean operator norm at most one. Their action preserves rapid
Fourier decay. Smooth Fourier synthesis proves all identities for the
actual smooth periodic fields. On compact time slabs the same estimates
apply after every time derivative; hence P and Q preserve joint smoothness.
This is a fixed-time spatial construction. It does not commute U_eta
with a time derivative.

The extended material equation is

  (EX)  V_t = nu Delta_eta^J V + U_eta Q c,
        V=eta_t,  u=V o eta^{-1},  c=(u . grad_x)u.

Equivalently, with Q_eta:=U_eta Q U_eta^{-1},

  V_t = nu Delta_eta^J V + Q_eta(D_a V A V).

The latter equality follows from U_eta c=D_a V A V.

For general J the correct change of variables is

  integral_{T^3} |f(x)|^2 dx
     = integral_{T^3} |U_eta f(a)|^2 J(a) da.

Consequently U_eta is an isometry into the space carrying measure J da.
The conjugated projection P_eta=U_eta P U_eta^{-1} is orthogonal for
that weighted inner product. No unweighted L^2 isometry or orthogonality
is asserted before J=1 has been proved.

29.2. C39: exact general-J material/Eulerian conjugacy
----------------------------------------------------------------

C39. Let eta be a smooth path in Diff^infinity_{+,0}(T^3), and define
V,u,F,A,J as above. Then

  (a)  U_eta(D_x u)=D_a V A,
  (b)  V_t=U_eta(u_t+c),
  (c)  Delta_eta^J V=U_eta Delta_x u,
  (d)  (EX) <=> u_t+P((u . grad_x)u)=nu Delta_x u.

No divergence-free or volume-preserving hypothesis is required for C39.

Proof.
(a) Differentiating V=u o eta in a gives

  D_a V=(D_x u o eta)F.

Multiplication on the right by A gives (a).

(b) Differentiating V=u(t,eta(t,a)) in t gives

  V_t=(u_t o eta)+(D_x u o eta)V
      =U_eta(u_t+(u . grad_x)u).

(c) The general-J Piola identity is

  sum_alpha partial_{a_alpha}(J A_{alpha i})=0.

For completeness,

  J A_{alpha i}
    = (1/2) sum_{j,k,beta,gamma}
        epsilon_{i j k} epsilon_{alpha beta gamma}
        F_{j beta} F_{k gamma}.

After differentiating in a_alpha, the terms containing
partial_{a_alpha}F_{j beta} cancel by symmetry in alpha,beta against
epsilon_{alpha beta gamma}; the terms differentiating F_{k gamma}
cancel by symmetry in alpha,gamma. This proves the identity without
setting J=1.

For any smooth Eulerian vector field z, the product and chain rules give

  J^{-1} sum_{alpha,i}
     partial_{a_alpha}(J A_{alpha i}(z_i o eta))
      = sum_i (partial_{x_i}z_i) o eta.

Indeed the differentiated cofactor terms vanish by Piola, and the
remaining contraction uses
sum_alpha F_{j alpha}A_{alpha i}=delta_{j i}.

Apply this identity to z=grad_x u_i, separately for each i.
The gradient chain rule gives

  (grad_x u_i) o eta=A^T grad_a V_i.

Therefore

  (Delta_x u_i) o eta
    =J^{-1} div_a(J A A^T grad_a V_i),

which is exactly (c) with the stated row convention.

(d) Substitute (b) and (c) into (EX), then compose with eta^{-1}:

  u_t+c=nu Delta_x u+Qc.

Since c-Qc=Pc, this is the projected Eulerian equation

  (PE)  u_t+Pc=nu Delta_x u.

Conversely (PE), (b) and (c) imply (EX). This proves C39. QED.

Scope of the converse configuration construction.
If a smooth periodic u on [0,T] satisfies (PE), its flow

  eta_t(t,a)=u(t,eta(t,a)),       eta(0,a)=a

exists throughout this finite slab because the prescribed smooth field
and its spatial derivative are bounded on the compact time-space domain.
Spatial smoothness, smooth parameter dependence and the inverse flow
follow from the previously derived flow construction. The flow belongs
to the identity component and has positive Jacobian. C39 then gives (EX).

This constructs the configuration from an already supplied smooth
solution u. It does not establish existence of a solution of the
nonlinear PDE (PE).

29.3. C40: divergence heat equation and volume invariance
----------------------------------------------------------------

C40. Every smooth solution of (PE), equivalently every smooth
configuration satisfying (EX), satisfies

  d_t=nu Delta_x d,             d=div_x u.

Its Jacobian satisfies

  J_t=J(d o eta),
  J(t,a)=exp(integral_0^t d(s,eta(s,a)) ds).

If div w0=0, then

  d(t,x)=0,       J(t,a)=1

for every (t,x) and (t,a) in the full slab.

Proof of divergence diffusion.
Taking divergence of (PE) gives

  div(u_t)+div(Pc)=nu div(Delta_x u).

The projection identity gives div(Pc)=0 for arbitrary c. Joint
smoothness and equality of mixed partials give, componentwise,

  div(u_t)=partial_t(div u),
  div(Delta_x u)=Delta_x(div u).

Thus d_t=nu Delta_x d. No divergence-free hypothesis was used in this
derivation.

Proof of propagation from d(0)=0.
For every 0<t<T, differentiate the scalar squared L^2 norm and integrate
by parts on the torus:

  (1/2) d/dt integral d^2 dx
     = integral d d_t dx
     = nu integral d Delta_x d dx
     = -nu integral |grad_x d|^2 dx.

The boundary terms cancel by periodicity. Integration and continuity
at the endpoints yield

  (1/2)||d(t)||_2^2
    +nu integral_0^t ||grad_x d(s)||_2^2 ds
      =(1/2)||d(0)||_2^2.

If div w0=0, the right side is zero. Both terms on the left are
nonnegative. Hence d(t)=0 in L^2 for every t. Smoothness converts this
to pointwise vanishing.

Proof of the Jacobian formula.
Differentiating F=D_a eta and using V=u o eta gives

  F_t=(D_x u o eta)F.

Jacobi's determinant formula therefore gives

  J_t=J tr(F^{-1}F_t)
     =J tr(D_x u o eta)
     =J(d o eta).

The initial condition eta(0)=id gives J(0)=1. Solving this scalar
linear equation along each label yields the displayed exponential
formula. If d=0, then J=1. Hence eta is volume preserving on the
entire slab. QED.

The conclusion J=1 uses both div w0=0 and eta(0)=id. For a general
initial diffeomorphism the corresponding formula contains its initial
Jacobian J(0,a); zero divergence alone preserves that initial Jacobian.

29.4. C41: exact bijection with the normalized-pressure root
----------------------------------------------------------------

Fix the original smooth solenoidal datum u0, with arbitrary spatial mean.
Let E_nu(u0;T) denote the original normalized-pressure Eulerian NSE
solution set. Let M_nu(u0;T) denote the original volume-preserving
material Newton solution set.

C41. There are canonical bijections

  E_nu(u0;T) <--> X_nu(u0;T) <--> M_nu(u0;T).

The original equivalences with N,V,D extend through these bijections.
The X class imposes no separate volume-preserving condition.

Pressure reconstruction for arbitrary smooth (PE) solutions.
For c=(u . grad_x)u define p by

  p_hat(0)=0,
  p_hat(k)= i (k dot c_hat(k))/(2*pi*|k|^2)     (k!=0).

The gradient Fourier coefficients are

  (grad p)_hat(k)
    =-(k k^T/|k|^2)c_hat(k)
    =-(Qc)_hat(k),

including the zero mode. Thus

  grad_x p=-Qc,
  -Delta_x p=div_x c,
  integral p dx=0.

Reality follows from c_hat(-k)=conjugate(c_hat(k)). Spatial and temporal
smoothness follow from rapid coefficient decay uniformly on every
compact time slab, after arbitrary time differentiation. The multiplier
has order minus one away from zero. Every differentiated Fourier series
is absolutely and uniformly convergent by choosing a sufficiently high
decay order. This is the same compact-slab argument used in the earlier
smooth pressure derivation. The normalized p is unique: the difference
of two such pressures has zero gradient and zero mean.

Define pi=p o eta. For general configurations the correct gauge is

  integral pi(a) J(a) da=0.

Once C40 proves J=1, this becomes the original material gauge
integral pi da=0.

Forward map from X to E and M.
Given eta in X_nu(u0;T), set u=eta_t o eta^{-1}. By C39, u satisfies
(PE). By C40 and div u0=0, div u=0 and J=1. The reconstructed pressure
therefore gives

  u_t+(u . grad_x)u+grad_x p=nu Delta_x u,
  div_x u=0,
  u(0)=u0,       integral p dx=0.

Hence (u,p) lies in E_nu(u0;T). The gradient chain rule gives

  U_eta grad_x p=A^T grad_a pi.

Using grad p=-Qc and J=1 in (EX) yields

  eta_tt
    =-A^T grad_a pi+nu Div_a(D_a eta_t A A^T),

with eta(0)=id, eta_t(0)=u0, det D_a eta=1 and integral pi da=0.
Thus (eta,pi) lies in M_nu(u0;T).

Reverse map from E.
Given (u,p) in E_nu(u0;T), let eta be its unique flow with eta(0)=id.
The root flow identities give J=1. Since div u=0 for every time,
both u_t and Delta_x u are divergence free. Applying Q to NSE gives

  Qc+grad p=0.

The material acceleration identity therefore yields

  V_t=U_eta(u_t+c)
     =nu U_eta Delta_x u+U_eta Qc
     =nu Delta_eta^J V+U_eta Qc.

Thus eta lies in X_nu(u0;T).

Inverse verification.
Starting from eta in X, the recovered field satisfies u o eta=eta_t.
Therefore eta is exactly the flow used by the reverse map, by ODE
uniqueness with eta(0)=id. Starting from (u,p) in E, the flow recovers
u by eta_t o eta^{-1}; the reconstructed pressure equals the original
p by the normalized-gradient uniqueness just proved. The same argument
and pi=p o eta establish the X<-->M inverse identities. QED.

In the solenoidal class only,

  c=div_x(u tensor u),
  -Delta_x p=sum_{i,j} partial_{x_i}partial_{x_j}(u_i u_j),

so the earlier quadratic pressure formula is recovered. Before C40,
the correct identities are instead

  div_x(u tensor u)=c+u d,
  div_x c=tr((D_x u)^2)+u . grad_x d.

Accordingly the unconstrained equation must retain c=(u . grad_x)u
unless the divergence defect has been accounted for.

C41 is a bijection of explicitly defined smooth solution sets. It
does not assert that either set is nonempty for arbitrary T. A finite
root solution does not imply Methlib GlobalSmoothNSE. The force in
(EX) contains second spatial derivatives and nonlocal projection;
the correspondence is not a generic Banach-space ODE existence theorem
and supplies no derivative-loss or global-regularity estimate.

29.5. C42: quantitative defect decay outside the root constraint
----------------------------------------------------------------

C42 is supplemental. Replace the solenoidal root datum u0 by an
arbitrary smooth periodic w0, and suppose that a smooth solution of
(EX), equivalently (PE), exists on [0,T]. No conclusion that this
trajectory belongs to the incompressible root is asserted.

For every 0<=s<=t<=T,

  ||d(t)||_2^2
     <= exp(-8*pi^2*nu*(t-s)) ||d(s)||_2^2,

where d=div_x u. Moreover

  J(t,a)=exp(integral_0^t d(r,eta(r,a)) dr),

and, writing H_d(t)=integral_0^t ||d(r)||_infinity dr,

  exp(-H_d(t)) <= J(t,a) <= exp(H_d(t)).

The equivalent material defect estimate is weighted:

  integral |d(t,eta(t,a))|^2 J(t,a) da
    <= exp(-8*pi^2*nu*(t-s))
       integral |d(s,eta(s,a))|^2 J(s,a) da.

Proof.
Every smooth periodic divergence has zero mean:

  integral d(t,x) dx
    =sum_i integral partial_{x_i}u_i(t,x) dx
    =0,

by cancellation of opposite periodic faces. Consequently the sharp
unit-torus scalar Poincare inequality applies:

  ||grad_x d||_2^2 >= 4*pi^2 ||d||_2^2.

To verify its precise domain and constant directly, the smooth
mean-zero Fourier expansion has d_hat(0)=0 and Parseval gives

  ||d||_2^2=sum_{k!=0}|d_hat(k)|^2,
  ||grad_x d||_2^2
    =4*pi^2 sum_{k!=0}|k|^2 |d_hat(k)|^2
    >=4*pi^2||d||_2^2.

The smooth expansion and its derivatives converge in L^2, so no
finite-Fourier-support premise is imposed here.

The scalar heat energy identity from C40 therefore yields

  d/dt ||d||_2^2
    =-2*nu||grad_x d||_2^2
    <=-8*pi^2*nu||d||_2^2.

Multiplying by exp(8*pi^2*nu*t), integrating and taking endpoint
limits proves the norm estimate. Equivalently, differentiation of
the smooth Fourier coefficients gives the exact modal identity

  d_hat(t,k)
    =exp(-4*pi^2*nu*|k|^2*(t-s)) d_hat(s,k),

with d_hat(t,0)=0.

The Jacobian identity was proved in C40 without the solenoidal
hypothesis. Its upper and lower bounds follow by bounding the time
integral in its exponent by H_d(t). The weighted estimate follows
from the general-J change of variables at times s and t. QED.

Sharpness and absence of volume restoration.
Fix a real amplitude beta!=0, set lambda=4*pi^2*nu, and define

  u(t,x)=beta exp(-lambda*t) sin(2*pi*x_1) e_1.

Then

  c=grad_x[(beta^2/2)exp(-2*lambda*t)sin^2(2*pi*x_1)],
  Pc=0,       u_t=nu Delta_x u.

Thus u is an actual smooth solution of (PE), with generally nonzero
initial divergence, and its smooth flow satisfies (EX). Its divergence is

  d(t,x)=2*pi*beta exp(-lambda*t) cos(2*pi*x_1).

The C42 squared-norm decay rate is attained with equality. At a label
with a_1=0 the flow stays on x_1=0, so

  J(t,a)
    =exp[(2*pi*beta/lambda)(1-exp(-lambda*t))].

This tends to exp(2*pi*beta/lambda), which differs from one. Therefore
even an exact exponentially decaying divergence defect does not imply
J(t)->1. The off-constraint class is an extension of the root dynamics,
not an additional assertion of incompressibility.

Further domain distinctions.
Before d=0, the pressure normalization is integral pi J da=0.
The unweighted material pressure gauge and unweighted material L^2
identities cannot be substituted. The usual incompressible kinetic
energy identity is likewise not asserted for this supplementary class.
The velocity mean need not be constant: direct integration of (PE) gives

  d/dt integral u dx = integral u d dx.

None of these distinctions affects C41, where C40 proves d=0 and J=1.

This section strengthens C30 without altering the finite-time root.
Let T>0, I=[0,T], and let f be any total extension of a finite trajectory.
Write D_S f(t) for its derivative within S when discussing ordinary
mathematical derivatives, and derivWithin f S t for Lean's totalized
derivative operator.

For 0<=t<T, the sets I and [0,infinity) have the same germ at t.
Indeed choose epsilon<(T-t). Their intersections with
(t-epsilon,t+epsilon) coincide.
For 0<t<T, I contains a neighborhood of t.
At t=T, the sets I and (-infinity,T] have the same germ, because
epsilon<T removes the lower endpoint zero.

Therefore locality gives the exact identities
  derivWithin f I t = derivWithin f (Ici 0) t, 0<=t<T,
  derivWithin f I t = deriv f t,              0<t<T,
  derivWithin f I 0 = derivWithin f (Ici 0) 0,
  derivWithin f I T = derivWithin f (Iic T) T.                 (30.1)

These totalized Lean identities follow from the recorded set-germ
congruence endpoint even before proving differentiability.
For the root trajectories, one-sided smoothness and unique
differentiability of the nondegenerate intervals identify these values
with the actual right, interior, and left derivatives respectively.

If f and g agree on I, their within-I derivatives agree at every point
of I. Their within-Ici-0 derivatives therefore agree for 0<=t<T.
No value beyond T enters these statements.

At t=T>0, Ici 0 contains a full neighborhood of T. Thus
  derivWithin f (Ici 0) T = deriv f T.
A compatible smooth extension gives equality with the left derivative.
An arbitrary extension need not have a two-sided derivative:
the finite zero trajectory extended by f(t)=t-T for t>T is an example.

Indexed source route:
  ML-T02 (set-germ congruence)
  + ML-T03/ML-T04 (function-germ congruence)
  + ML-T01 (neighborhood within derivative = ordinary derivative)
  + ML-T05 (identify a proved derivative with derivWithin)
  + ML-T06--ML-T08 (interval unique differentiability).

For M26--M28, the all-positive-time source hypotheses still require
localization. At an interior reference time t0, choose a smooth temporal
cutoff supported in a compact subinterval of (0,T), equal to one near t0.
Multiplying the finite velocity by this cutoff and extending by zero
gives a globally positive-time smooth periodic solenoidal test field.
This construction imposes no NSE equation on the extension.
The derivative conclusions transfer back by germ congruence.
For an energy identity using the NSE equation, localize the proof or
apply the derivative argument at each interior time, then integrate
and pass to the one-sided endpoints by continuity.

the project instantiation remains an external Lean obligation.

C43 CANONICAL_PARALLEL_FRAME.
Assume the root smooth volume-preserving trajectory on [0,T].
Let P_t=P_eta(t), acting on the fixed real material Hilbert space
H=L2(Omega;R3), and let dot P_t denote its operator-norm derivative
established in C31.

31.1. Bounded skew-adjoint generator

Define
  Gamma_t:=dot P_t P_t-P_t dot P_t.                              (31.1)

Since P_t and dot P_t are self-adjoint,
  Gamma_t^*=-Gamma_t.
Differentiating P_t^2=P_t gives
  dot P_t P_t+P_t dot P_t=dot P_t,
  P_t dot P_t P_t=0.
Consequently
  [Gamma_t,P_t]=dot P_t.                                        (31.2)

Relative to H=range(P_t) direct-sum ker(P_t), dot P_t has two
off-diagonal adjoint blocks. Gamma_t changes the sign of one block.
The ranges of those two blocks are orthogonal, so
  ||Gamma_t||=||dot P_t||<=||D_xu(t)||_{infinity,op}.              (31.3)

31.2. Construction of the unitary propagator

The continuous bounded-operator equation
  partial_t W(t,s)=Gamma_t W(t,s), W(s,s)=I                      (31.4)
has an operator-norm solution on the entire finite interval.
For t>=s construct it explicitly by the ordered integral series
  W(t,s)=I+
    sum_{n>=1} int_{s<=r_n<=...<=r_1<=t}
       Gamma_{r_1}...Gamma_{r_n} dr_n...dr_1.

With M=sup_{r in [0,T]}||Gamma_r||, the n-th term is bounded by
  M^n |t-s|^n/n!.
The series and its differentiated series converge uniformly on compact
time triangles. They satisfy (31.4).
The same construction for reversed time gives W(s,t).
For two solutions the difference satisfies an integral inequality;
Gronwall gives uniqueness. Hence composition and inverse laws hold:
  W(t,s)W(s,r)=W(t,r),
  W(t,s)W(s,t)=W(s,t)W(t,s)=I.                              (31.5)

For h,k in H, differentiation of their transported inner product gives
  partial_t <W(t,s)h,W(t,s)k>
    =<Gamma_tW(t,s)h,W(t,s)k>+<W(t,s)h,Gamma_tW(t,s)k>=0.
Together with the inverse laws, this proves W(t,s) is unitary
(orthogonal over the real scalar field), with W(t,s)^*=W(s,t).

Define W_t=W(t,0). By (31.2),
  partial_t(W_t^{-1}P_tW_t)
    =W_t^{-1}(dot P_t+P_tGamma_t-Gamma_tP_t)W_t=0.
Therefore
  P_t=W_tP_0W_t^{-1}.                                       (31.6)

All constant vector fields c satisfy P_tc=c for every t.
Thus dot P_tc=Gamma_tc=0 and W_tc=c.
Consequently W_t preserves means and maps the initial mean-zero
solenoidal subspace isometrically onto the material one at time t.

31.3. Exact acceleration equation in the parallel frame

For the physical material velocity, P_tV=V and
  V_t=nu Delta_eta V+dot P_tV.
The off-diagonal identity gives Gamma_tV=dot P_tV.

Set
  Z(t):=W_t^{-1}V(t),
  Atilde_t:=W_t^{-1} Acal_eta(t) W_t,
  D(Atilde_t):=W_t^{-1}D(Acal_eta(t)).

The ambient Hilbert space of Atilde_t is S_0=range(P_0).
Equation (31.6) restricts W_t to a unitary map
  W_t:S_0 -> S_eta(t)=range(P_t).
Thus D(Atilde_t) is dense in S_0. It is not asserted dense in the
entire vector-field space H.

Then
  Z_t=W_t^{-1}(V_t-Gamma_tV)
     =-nu Atilde_t Z.                                       (31.7)

At every fixed time, Atilde_t is self-adjoint and nonnegative
on S_0 with its displayed domain. Its kernel is the constant fields.
Its restriction to the mean-zero subspace of S_0 has the exact spectral gap
4*pi^2, since both conjugations are unitary.

The original acceleration decomposes exactly into
  tangent dissipation: -nu Acal_eta V,
  normal constraint force: dot P_tV.
The canonical parallel frame removes the normal component from the
velocity equation while preserving the kinetic norm and dissipation.

For the conserved mean m, Z-m lies in the fixed initial mean-zero
solenoidal Hilbert space and
  (1/2) partial_t ||Z-m||^2
    =-nu <Z-m,Atilde_t(Z-m)>.

31.4. Exact scope

W_t and Atilde_t depend on the evolving trajectory.
The statement provides a solution-associated operator representation.
It does not replace NSE by one fixed linear equation with prescribed
coefficients independent of the unknown solution.
No equation for a moving unbounded domain is solved merely by citing
the frozen-time semigroup.

The bounded ODE (31.4) is justified by its convergent series.
It does not establish local or global existence for the original
derivative-losing nonlinear PDE on the diffeomorphism group.

Source support:
  C31--C38; ML-O01--ML-O04 for abstract ODE infrastructure;
  ML-D02 and the additional operator-composition/projection endpoints;
  weighted-Fourier operator construction from Round V.
Remaining Lean work:
  bounded-operator ordered series or an equivalent linear-ODE proof,
  inverse/orthogonality/intertwining identities, moving-domain bookkeeping.

Status: ! B_TIER.

ADAPTER BOUNDARY

A. ContinuousLinearMap composition/application rules apply to P_eta after
   C31 supplies its operator-norm derivative. They are not applied to U_eta
   as if the transport pullback had a bounded L2 generator.

B. The derivative of U_t^{-1} is used only on jointly smooth fields:
   g(t)=U_t^{-1}H, H fixed smooth, implies g_t=−D_u g.
   This is a chain-rule identity on the smooth core. No generic Banach
   inverse-derivative theorem is needed or claimed for U_t.

C. Projection-difference bound:
   ||P_t−P_s||<=min(1,int_s^t ||Du(r)||_{infty,op} dr), 0<=s<=t<=T.
   The exact statement is proved in Round IV from orthogonal outputs and
   the dense-core derivative estimate. No retrieved source is represented
   as already proving this transported-fluid statement.

D. The C31–C34 fluid identities remain new Lean adapters:
   actual Leray commutator;
   bounded multiplication and transpose adjoint;
   dense-core operator integral;
   offdiagonal derivative identities;
   symmetric normal form;
   projected metric derivative and exact NSE correspondence.

the actual operator equality remain project proof obligations.

Contracts.lean:
abbrev Vec := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
abbrev Field := Vec → Vec
abbrev Velocity := ℝ → Field
abbrev Pressure := ℝ → Vec → ℝ
def SpatialPeriodic {E : Type*} (f : Vec → E) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Vec) (i : Fin 3), f (x + unitVector i) = f x
def coordinateDerivative (a : Field) (i : Fin 3) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  fderiv ℝ a x (unitVector i)
def divergence (a : Field) (x : Vec) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, coordinateDerivative a i x i
def laplacian (a : Field) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, fderiv ℝ (coordinateDerivative a i) x (unitVector i)
def convection (a : Field) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  fderiv ℝ a x (a x)
def timeDerivative (u : Velocity) (t : ℝ) (x : Vec) : Vec :=
  derivWithin (fun s : ℝ => u s x) (Ici (0 : ℝ)) t

SixChannels.lean:
abbrev Frequency := Fin 3 → ℤ
abbrev FourierCoeff := Frequency → Fin 3 → ℂ
def SpectralSolenoidal (a : FourierCoeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ k, ∑ c : Fin 3, (k c : ℂ) * a k c = 0

Galerkin.lean:
def coefficientLeray (k : Frequency) (v : Fin 3 → ℂ) : Fin 3 → ℂ :=
  if k = 0 then v else
    fun i => v i - (k i : ℂ) * (∑ j : Fin 3, (k j : ℂ) * v j) /
      (∑ j : Fin 3, (k j : ℂ) ^ 2)
def datumFourierCoeff (a : Field) : FourierCoeff :=
  fun k i => ∫ x in unitCube, datumFourierIntegrand a k i x

FourierSeriesCalculus.lean:
def RapidScalarFourier (b : Frequency → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : ℕ, Summable (fun k => ‖b k‖ * ‖fourierPhaseCLM k‖ ^ m)

SobolevSmoothRealization.lean:
def smoothFourierSynthesis (c : FourierCoeff) : Field :=

def laplacianFrequency (k : Frequency) : ℝ :=

ADAPTER AND SCOPE REGISTER

A. No selected source declaration directly states the full general-J
   diffeomorphism Laplacian pullback or the C39 configuration equation.
   Its formalization requires the actual Piola/cofactor, inverse derivative,
   chain-rule, and weighted change-of-variables adapters.

B. M29 and M30 support div(Pf)=0. They do not alone constitute an already
   compiled infinite-dimensional Leray operator with the exact root domain.
   Rapid summability, actual Fourier reconstruction, the zero-mode identity,
   reality, parameter smoothness, and the operator-to-physical-field bridge
   must be supplied with their original premises intact.

C. M31 is a vector-field Laplacian coefficient theorem. The scalar
   mixed-derivative identities
     ∂t(div u)=div(∂t u),  div(Δu)=Δ(div u)
   remain explicit adapters. Round VI proves them mathematically by smooth
   mixed-partial commutation; no source-level theorem with these exact
   conclusions is claimed by this register.

D. M32 and M33 support the scalar heat energy proof, not a preassembled heat
   equation theorem. The finite-interval and endpoint derivative adapters
   remain mandatory. The global-positive-time hypotheses of M33 cannot be
   inferred merely from a solution on [0,T].

E. M25 from the earlier register remains finite-synthesis Poincare only.
   C42 uses the full smooth mean-zero scalar Poincare argument proved
   mathematically by Fourier series; a full-domain Lean density/Parseval
   adapter is still required if M25 is used as an intermediate endpoint.

F. M36 is restricted to solenoidal fields. In the supplementary C42 class,
   neither the solenoidal tensor-divergence identity nor the root pressure
   quadratic formula is available before div u=0 is proved.

G. No source endpoint here asserts local existence on a Banach manifold of
   diffeomorphisms, absence of derivative loss, global smooth NSE existence,
   or discharge of AX6. Round VI is an exact correspondence and constraint
   propagation result within explicitly assumed smooth solution classes.

END M29--M36 REGISTER

36. COMPOSITION INDEX, EXACT REMAINING EDGES, AND REVISION AUDIT

36.1. Additional mathematical checkpoints

C31 TRANSPORTED_PROJECTOR_DERIVATIVE
  Smooth material flow -> operator-norm smooth P_t.
  P_t'=U_t[D_u,P]U_t^{-1}
      =(I-P_t)M_{D_xu o eta}P_t
        +P_tM_{(D_xu o eta)^T}(I-P_t).
  ||P_t'||<=||D_xu||_{infinity,op}.

C32 PROJECTOR_OFFDIAGONAL_IDENTITIES_AND_NORMAL_ACCELERATION
  P P'P=0 and (I-P)P'(I-P)=0.
  For the root trajectory, (I-P_t)V_t=P_t'V=-grad_eta pi.

C33 SYMMETRIC_BILINEAR_NORMAL_FORM
  B_eta(H,K)=U_eta(I-P)((h.grad)k) on smooth tangent fields.
  B_eta(H,K)=B_eta(K,H), with the stated derivative/norm estimates.

C34 PROJECTED_METRIC_CONNECTION_AND_COVARIANT_DAMPED_NEWTON
  nabla_t H=P_tH_t is the stated metric-compatible along-path derivative.
  Root NSE iff nabla_t V=-nu Acal_eta V, with root initial data.

C35 MATERIAL_STOKES_CLOSED_DOMAIN
  Actual real solenoidal Fourier Hilbert space, closed H2 operator domain,
  self-adjoint nonnegative realization, smooth graph core, closed H1 form,
  and constants kernel.

C36 MATERIAL_STOKES_GAP_RESOLVENT
  On mean-zero fields: sharp gap 4*pi^2, explicit inverse, exact resolvent
  norm and compactness by finite-rank approximation.

C37 FROZEN_STOKES_SEMIGROUP
  Fixed-configuration strongly continuous semigroup, exact generator
  domain, sharp norm, positive auxiliary-time smoothing, Laplace formula.

C38 RAYLEIGH_GRADIENT_ACCELERATION_MINIMUM
  At V in D(Acal_eta): unique L2 representative nu Acal_eta V.
  Unique minimum of J_eta,V(W) occurs at W=-nu Acal_eta V.
  The physical variable W is P_eta eta_tt.

C39 GENERAL_JACOBIAN_MATERIAL_EQUATION
  Positive-Jacobian smooth diffeomorphisms with Delta_eta^J and
  U_eta(I-P)((u.grad)u) give the exact projected Eulerian equation.

C40 DIVERGENCE_HEAT_AND_VOLUME_INVARIANCE
  The defined extended equation implies d_t=nu Delta d.
  d(0)=0 implies d=0 and, with J(0)=1, J=1.

C41 EXTENDED_CONFIGURATION_EQUIVALENCE
  Root NSE solutions are in explicit bijection with the extended
  configuration trajectories having the root initial data.

C42 CONSTRAINT_DEFECT_DECAY
  For stipulated smooth extended trajectories, the Eulerian divergence
  defect decays with exponent 8*pi^2*nu in squared L2 norm.
  Material transport uses the correct weight J before C40 applies.

C43 CANONICAL_PARALLEL_FRAME
  Gamma_t=[P_t',P_t] defines a bounded skew-adjoint generator.
  W_t'=Gamma_tW_t, W_0=I gives unitary intertwining
  P_t=W_tP_0W_t^{-1}. The solution-associated velocity
  Z=W_t^{-1}V satisfies Z_t=-nu(W_t^{-1}Acal_eta W_t)Z
  on the explicitly transported domain in S_0=range(P_0).

Every C31--C43 implication is mathematically derived in Sections 27--31.
All have status ! B_TIER.
No existence assertion for a smooth nonlinear NSE trajectory is added.

37. STRENGTHENING ROUND VII: VISCOUS KELVIN, WEBER, AND CAUCHY IDENTITIES

ROOT_SCOPE.
  Omega=R^3/Z^3, normalized volume 1; 0<T<infinity; nu>0.
  The root smooth finite-time regularity and time-endpoint convention apply.
  Velocity means are unrestricted. Pressure has spatial mean zero.
  The kinematic configuration is a smooth volume-preserving path eta(t),
  eta(0)=id, V=eta_t, V(0)=u0, and u=V circ eta^{-1}.
  The fixed datum u0 is smooth and divergence-free.
  No momentum equation is assumed until explicitly stated.

A kinematic path in this section therefore gives div_x u=0. Conversely,
the root flow construction supplies such a path for every root velocity.
The identity-normalized periodic lift has the form
  eta_tilde(t,a)=a+xi(t,a), xi(t,a+n)=xi(t,a), xi(0,a)=0,
  n in Z^3.
Write
  F=D_a eta_tilde, A=F^{-1}, det F=1,
  Delta_eta V=(Delta_x u) circ eta.
All fields below are periodic in a, including F and V.

C44--C47 supplement the existing root equivalence. They neither replace
the finite smooth hypotheses nor provide an existence theorem.

37.1.1. Covector convention and off-equation identity

For a smooth Eulerian one-form with coefficient column f, define
  eta^*(f dot dx)=(F^T(f circ eta)) dot da.                   (37.1)

The transpose factor is part of the pullback. The componentwise scalar
pullback U_eta f=f circ eta does not by itself give a one-form pullback.
In particular, set
  beta=F^T V,
  kappa=|V|^2/2,
  r_eta=nu F^T Delta_eta V
       =nu F^T((Delta_xu) circ eta).                        (37.2)

Define the Eulerian momentum residual without pressure,
  g=u_t+(u dot grad)u-nu Delta_xu.
The material chain rule gives
  g circ eta=V_t-nu Delta_eta V.                            (37.3)

Since F_t=D_aV, differentiation in components yields
  partial_t beta_alpha
    =sum_i (partial_alpha V_i)V_i+sum_i F_{i alpha}V_{i,t}.
Thus, for every stipulated kinematic path,
  beta_t=r_eta+grad_a kappa+F^T(g circ eta).                 (37.4)

For every smooth periodic scalar p, with pi=p circ eta,
  F^T((grad_xp) circ eta)=grad_a pi.                         (37.5)

Consequently, the root NSE is equivalent to
  beta_t=r_eta+grad_a(kappa-pi).                            (37.6)

37.1.2. Exact integrated Weber identity and canonical gauge

Define the viscous history and Weber covector
  I_eta(t,a)=int_0^t r_eta(s,a) ds,
  Wcal(t,a)=beta(t,a)-I_eta(t,a).
Since F(0)=I and V(0)=u0, Wcal(0)=u0.

For a root solution, define
  bar_kappa(t)=int_Omega kappa(t,a) da,
  Psi(t,a)=int_0^t [kappa(s,a)-pi(s,a)-bar_kappa(s)] ds.      (37.7)

Volume preservation gives int pi=0. Therefore
  int_Omega Psi(t,a) da=0, Psi(0,a)=0.
Time integration of (37.6), with spatial differentiation under the
smooth finite-time integral, gives
  Wcal(t)=u0+grad_a Psi(t).                                 (37.8)

Equivalently,
  F(t)^T V(t)
    =u0+nu int_0^t F(s)^T Delta_eta(s)V(s) ds
       +grad_a Psi(t).                                     (37.9)

The factor F(s)^T lies inside the history integral and is evaluated at
the history time s. The gradient is with respect to the fixed material
coordinate a. All terms have the same one-form coefficient convention.

Conversely, suppose a stipulated kinematic path satisfies (37.8) for a
smooth periodic scalar Psi. A time-only change of Psi does not affect
(37.8). Define
  pi=kappa-Psi_t-int_Omega(kappa-Psi_t) da,
  p=pi circ eta^{-1}.                                      (37.10)
Then int pi=int p=0. Differentiating (37.8) and using (37.4) gives
  F^T(g circ eta)=grad_a(Psi_t-kappa)=-grad_a pi.
The invertibility of F and (37.5) imply g=-grad_xp.
Thus (u,p) satisfies the exact root NSE.

If Psi is normalized by int Psi=0 at every time, (37.10) becomes
  pi=kappa-bar_kappa-Psi_t.                                (37.11)
The normalized Psi is unique: two such potentials have the same
gradient, hence differ by a spatial constant, and their means fix that
constant to zero. At t=0, (37.8) then forces Psi(0)=0.
The pressure recovered by (37.10) is the unique root pressure.

37.1.3. Fixed-reference Leray form

Let P_ref denote the full-mean Leray projection acting on the fixed
a-coordinate torus:
  P_ref(0)=I,
  P_ref(k)=I-kk^T/|k|^2 for k!=0.
It is distinct in role from the moving tangent projection P_eta.

Since div_a u0=0 and P_ref annihilates periodic gradients, (37.8) implies
  P_ref Wcal(t)=u0.                                        (37.12)

Conversely, (37.12) gives P_ref(Wcal-u0)=0. The smooth Helmholtz
decomposition already established in C23--C24 gives the unique
mean-zero smooth periodic Psi with Wcal-u0=grad_a Psi.
The zero Fourier mode vanishes because P_ref(0)=I.
For completeness, for z=Wcal-u0 and k!=0 its potential coefficients are
  Psi_hat(k)=(k dot z_hat(k))/(2*pi*i*|k|^2), Psi_hat(0)=0.
The transverse coefficients vanish by P_ref z=0. Uniform rapid decay
of every time derivative gives the joint smoothness of Psi on the
root finite slab.

Thus the pressure-free identity (37.12), with the stipulated kinematics,
is equivalent to the root NSE with uniquely reconstructed pressure.
In particular, (37.12) retains the three harmonic velocity modes.
The mean of F^TV is not identified with the physical mean of u.

37.2.1. All closed loops, including nonzero winding

A reference loop gamma is an oriented piecewise-C1 closed curve in Omega.
Choose a lift alpha:[0,1]->R^3 with
  alpha(1)=alpha(0)+n, n in Z^3.
Its winding vector is n. The material loop is
  gamma_t=eta(t) circ gamma.
The lift eta_tilde(t,alpha(s)) has the same winding vector n, since xi
is periodic. A loop of zero winding is contractible; a loop with
nonzero winding need not bound a surface in Omega.

Define its circulation by the piecewise interval integral
  C_gamma(t)
    =int_0^1 u(t,eta(t,alpha(s)))
                dot [F(t,alpha(s)) alpha'(s)] ds
    =int_0^1 beta(t,alpha(s)) dot alpha'(s) ds.              (37.13)

Periodicity makes this independent of the integer choice of lift.
The ordinary change-of-variable identity on each C1 subinterval gives
invariance under orientation-preserving piecewise-C1 reparametrization.
No spanning surface is required.

For fixed gamma, smoothness gives
  d_t C_gamma(t)=int_0^1 beta_t(t,alpha(s)) dot alpha'(s) ds.
A direct estimate justifies this also with one-sided endpoint quotients:
  |[C_gamma(t+h)-C_gamma(t)]/h
      -int_0^1 beta_t(t,alpha(s)) dot alpha'(s) ds|
    <=sup_a |[beta(t+h,a)-beta(t,a)]/h-beta_t(t,a)|
         *int_0^1 |alpha'(s)| ds
    ->0.                                                   (37.14)
The supremum tends to zero by uniform continuity of beta_t on the
compact slab, with t+h restricted to [0,T].

For any periodic smooth scalar q,
  int_0^1 grad_a q(alpha(s)) dot alpha'(s) ds
    =q(alpha(1))-q(alpha(0))=0.                             (37.15)
This holds for every winding vector n, not only for n=0.

Substituting (37.6) into (37.14)--(37.15) yields the exact viscous
Kelvin identity
  d_t C_gamma(t)
    =nu int_0^1 (Delta_xu)(t,eta(t,alpha(s)))
                    dot [F(t,alpha(s))alpha'(s)] ds
    =nu oint_{gamma_t} Delta_xu dot dx.                     (37.16)

For 0<=s<=t<=T, its integrated form is
  oint_{gamma_t} u(t) dot dx-oint_{gamma_s} u(s) dot dx
    =nu int_s^t oint_{gamma_r} Delta_xu(r) dot dx dr.        (37.17)

The pressure and kinetic-gradient terms disappear by periodic
exactness. The viscous circulation term remains. No conservation of
circulation is asserted when this term is nonzero.

37.2.2. Exact relation to the Weber defect

Let
  z(t)=Wcal(t)-u0.
Equation (37.13) and the definition of I_eta give
  oint_gamma z(t) dot da
    =oint_{gamma_t} u(t) dot dx-oint_gamma u0 dot da
       -nu int_0^t oint_{gamma_s} Delta_xu(s) dot dx ds.     (37.18)

Thus the t=0 version of (37.17) is exactly the vanishing of the
circulation of z(t) along the selected reference loops.
All-loop balance and contractible-loop balance impose different
conditions; their exact distinction is proved next.

37.3.1. Coordinate periodic-potential lemma

Let b:R^3->R^3 be a smooth Z^3-periodic coefficient field. The following
are equivalent:
  (a) every contractible closed-loop integral of b vanishes;
  (b) partial_i b_j=partial_j b_i for all i,j;
  (c) b=h+grad q, where h is a constant vector and q is a smooth
      periodic scalar.                                    (37.19)

Here h=int_Omega b, and q is unique after int_Omega q=0.
For every loop with winding n,
  oint_gamma b dot da=h dot n.                             (37.20)

Proof of (a)->(b).
The boundary of every sufficiently small coordinate rectangle is a
contractible piecewise-C1 loop. Applying one-dimensional FTC to its
four sides gives
  oint_boundary b dot da
    =int_0^epsilon int_0^delta
         (partial_i b_j-partial_j b_i)
           (a+s e_i+r e_j) dr ds
with the corresponding positive orientation. Divide by epsilon*delta
and let epsilon,delta decrease to zero. Continuity gives (b).

Proof of (b)->(c).
On R^3 define the rectangular-path primitive
  q_tilde(x)
    =int_0^{x_1} b_1(s,0,0) ds
      +int_0^{x_2} b_2(x_1,s,0) ds
      +int_0^{x_3} b_3(x_1,x_2,s) ds.                     (37.21)

Signed interval integrals cover negative coordinate values.
Differentiating the last term gives partial_3 q_tilde=b_3.
For partial_2, use partial_2 b_3=partial_3 b_2 and FTC:
  partial_2 q_tilde
    =b_2(x_1,x_2,0)
       +b_2(x_1,x_2,x_3)-b_2(x_1,x_2,0)
    =b_2(x).
For partial_1, the identities
  partial_1 b_2=partial_2 b_1,
  partial_1 b_3=partial_3 b_1
give the telescoping expression
  partial_1 q_tilde
    =b_1(x_1,0,0)
       +b_1(x_1,x_2,0)-b_1(x_1,0,0)
       +b_1(x_1,x_2,x_3)-b_1(x_1,x_2,0)
    =b_1(x).
Therefore grad q_tilde=b.

For each n in Z^3, q_tilde(x+n)-q_tilde(x) has zero gradient and is
constant in x. These constants add under lattice translation.
Set h_j=q_tilde(e_j)-q_tilde(0). Then
  q_tilde(x+n)-q_tilde(x)=h dot n.
Consequently q=q_tilde-h dot x is periodic and b=h+grad q.
Subtracting the mean of q fixes its normalization.

The integral of each periodic derivative is zero, by FTC and
periodicity on opposite faces of the unit cube. Thus int b=h.
Uniqueness follows from the same integral identity and then from
vanishing gradient. Integrating b=h+grad q along a lifted loop proves
(37.20), and (c)->(a) follows for n=0.

Consequences.
A smooth periodic b is a gradient of a periodic scalar if and only if
all its closed-loop integrals vanish. Equivalently, b is closed and its
three fundamental periods vanish; equivalently, b is closed and int b=0.
For a closed b, the integral along any coordinate generator
  s |-> a_*+s e_j, 0<=s<=1,
equals h_j independently of a_*.

For a jointly smooth b(t,a), the same construction yields jointly
smooth h(t) and normalized q(t,a): every expression in (37.21) is an
integral over a finite parameter interval of a jointly smooth
integrand. Differentiation under these finite integrals and under the
normalizing unit-cube integral is justified by compact local bounds.
This supplies the time regularity required by the converses below.

37.3.2. All-loop converse and three-generator reduction

Suppose the kinematic path satisfies (37.17) for every closed loop and
every 0<=s<=t<=T. By (37.18), every period of z(t) vanishes.
The coordinate lemma gives a unique jointly smooth mean-zero Psi with
  z(t)=grad_a Psi(t).
C44 reconstructs the unique normalized pressure and the root NSE.

The converse is C45. It is enough to impose the balance from time 0,
since subtraction then gives every time pair.

An equivalent sufficient loop family consists of:
  all contractible loops;
  the three fixed reference coordinate generators.
The contractible loops enforce closedness of z, and the three
generator balances eliminate its three periods.
The three generator checks alone do not impose closedness.

37.3.3. Contractible-loop converse with exactly three mean constraints

Assume only the contractible-loop version of (37.17).
By (37.18)--(37.19), z(t) is closed:
  partial_alpha z_beta-partial_beta z_alpha=0.
Time differentiation preserves this identity.

For every smooth Eulerian one-form coefficient f, component
differentiation gives
  d_a[F^T(f circ eta) dot da]_{alpha beta}
    =sum_{i,j} F_{i alpha}F_{j beta}
           (partial_i f_j-partial_j f_i) circ eta.          (37.22)
The second derivatives of eta cancel by symmetry.
Since F is invertible, its pullback of a two-form is zero exactly when
that two-form is zero.

From z_t=grad_a kappa+F^T(g circ eta), equation (37.22) implies
  partial_i g_j=partial_j g_i.
Apply (37.19) in Eulerian coordinates:
  g=c(t)+grad_x chi(t), int chi=0,
  c(t)=int_Omega g(t,x) dx.                                (37.23)

Write
  m(t)=int_Omega u(t,x) dx=int_Omega V(t,a) da.
Periodicity and div u=0 give
  int_Omega (u dot grad)u dx
    =int_Omega div(u tensor u) dx=0,
  int_Omega Delta_xu dx=0.
Therefore
  c(t)=m'(t).                                              (37.24)

It follows that contractible-loop balance together with
  m(t)=m(0) for every t in [0,T]                            (37.25)
implies g=grad chi. Taking p=-chi gives the root NSE and its normalized
pressure. Conversely, the root NSE gives contractible-loop balance
and (37.25).

The mean condition is equivalently the three constant Eulerian test
identities
  d_t int_Omega u dot e_j dx=0, j=1,2,3,
with the root initial mean. No zero-mean velocity hypothesis is added.

37.3.4. Exact harmonic defect under contractible-loop balance

The preceding implication can be sharpened. Under the contractible-loop
balance, let
  h_a(t)=int_Omega z(t,a) da.
The coordinate lemma gives z=h_a+grad_a Psi with int Psi=0.

Using eta_tilde=a+xi and (37.23),
  F^T(g circ eta)
    =F^T c+grad_a(chi circ eta)
    =c+grad_a[c dot xi+chi circ eta].
Together with (37.4),
  z_t=c+grad_a[kappa+c dot xi+chi circ eta].
Taking the material mean gives
  h_a'(t)=c(t)=m'(t).
Since z(0)=0, h_a(0)=0. Hence
  h_a(t)=m(t)-m(0),                                        (37.26)
  Wcal(t)=u0+[m(t)-m(0)]+grad_a Psi(t),                    (37.27)
  P_ref Wcal(t)=u0+[m(t)-m(0)].                            (37.28)

Thus the missing harmonic information is exactly the change of physical
velocity mean, after closedness has been established.
Equation (37.26) concerns the complete Weber defect z, including the
viscous history and the initial covector. It does not identify int F^TV
alone with m(t).

For a loop with winding n, the entire Kelvin-balance defect is
  oint_{gamma_t}u(t) dot dx-oint_gamma u0 dot da
    -nu int_0^t oint_{gamma_s}Delta_xu(s) dot dx ds
      =[m(t)-m(0)] dot n.                                 (37.29)

37.3.5. Sharp counterexample to omission of the harmonic condition

Let c:[0,T]->R^3 be any smooth nonconstant vector function and set
  u(t,x)=c(t),
  eta_tilde(t,a)=a+int_0^t c(s) ds.
Then F=I, det F=1, V=c(t), Delta u=0, and
  beta=c(t), r_eta=0, omega=curl u=0.

Every contractible-loop circulation is zero, so every contractible
viscous Kelvin identity holds. Every vorticity identity below also
holds. For a loop of winding n,
  C_gamma(t)=c(t) dot n.
The noncontractible Kelvin identities therefore detect c(t)-c(0).

A periodic pressure satisfying the root NSE would have
  grad p=-c'(t).
Integrating this identity over Omega gives c'(t)=0.
Thus a nonconstant c supplies a kinematically admissible path that
satisfies all contractible-loop and vorticity equations but fails NSE.
All closed loops, or the additional conserved-mean condition, exclude
exactly this harmonic obstruction.

37.4.1. Two-form and curl transformation

For a coefficient field f, define
  (df)_{ij}=partial_i f_j-partial_j f_i,
  curl f=(partial_2 f_3-partial_3 f_2,
          partial_3 f_1-partial_1 f_3,
          partial_1 f_2-partial_2 f_1).
For vectors v,w,
  df(v,w)=(curl f) dot (v cross w).

Equation (37.22) says precisely
  d_a[F^T(f circ eta)]=F^T[(d_xf) circ eta]F.               (37.30)

For any invertible real 3x3 matrix F, with J=det F,
  (Fv) cross (Fw)=J F^{-T}(v cross w).                     (37.31)
Indeed, scalar multiplication by Fz gives
  (Fz) dot [(Fv) cross(Fw)]
    =det[Fz,Fv,Fw]
    =J det[z,v,w]
    =J z dot(v cross w).
Here the bracketed determinant may be taken with columns; transpose
invariance identifies it with the row convention of ML-K04.
Since this holds for every z and F is invertible, (37.31) follows.

Combining (37.30)--(37.31) yields the general covector-curl identity
  curl_a[F^T(f circ eta)]
    =J A[(curl_x f) circ eta].                             (37.32)
In the root volume-preserving scope J=1.

Let omega=curl_x u and omega0=curl u0. Then
  curl_a beta=A(omega circ eta),                           (37.33)
  curl_a r_eta=nu A[(Delta_x omega) circ eta].              (37.34)
Equation (37.34) uses commutation of coordinate derivatives and
Delta_x, justified by smoothness.

37.4.2. Exact Cauchy formula with viscous source

Taking curl_a in the integrated Weber identity (37.9), the scalar
potential disappears and (37.33)--(37.34) give
  A(t,a) omega(t,eta(t,a))
    =omega0(a)
       +nu int_0^t A(s,a)(Delta_xomega)(s,eta(s,a)) ds.       (37.35)

Equivalently,
  omega(t,eta(t,a))
    =F(t,a)omega0(a)
       +nu F(t,a)int_0^t
            A(s,a)(Delta_xomega)(s,eta(s,a)) ds.             (37.36)

The factor F(t,a) outside the integral is evaluated at the final time;
the factor A(s,a) inside it is evaluated at the history time.
This is an exact formula with a viscous source. The source contains the
unknown solution's Laplacian. It is not a prescribed forcing and does
not close a finite-dimensional particle ODE.

Differentiating (37.35) gives
  d_t[A(omega circ eta)]
    =nu A[(Delta_xomega) circ eta].                         (37.37)

The material matrix equations give
  F_t=[(D_xu) circ eta]F,
  A_t=-A[(D_xu) circ eta].
Therefore direct differentiation gives
  d_t[A(omega circ eta)]
    =A[(omega_t+(u dot grad)omega-(omega dot grad)u)
           circ eta].
Equation (37.37) is consequently equivalent to
  omega_t+(u dot grad)omega
    =(omega dot grad)u+nu Delta_xomega.                    (37.38)

The initial relation A(0)=I converts (37.37) back to (37.35) by FTC.
Neither (37.35) nor (37.38) asserts that A(omega circ eta) is constant
when nu>0. Also, A[(Delta_xomega) circ eta] is not replaced by
Delta_a[A(omega circ eta)].

37.4.3. Coordinate vorticity identity and exact converse

For completeness, direct expansion of the cross product gives
  (u dot grad)u=grad_x(|u|^2/2)-u cross omega,
  curl(u cross omega)
    =u div omega-omega div u
       +(omega dot grad)u-(u dot grad)omega.
Mixed derivatives give div omega=0, while the kinematic scope gives
div u=0. Hence
  curl g
    =omega_t+(u dot grad)omega
       -(omega dot grad)u-nu Delta_xomega.                 (37.39)

Thus (37.38) is equivalent to curl g=0. By C46, this implies only
  g=m'(t)+grad chi
until the physical mean is fixed.

Alternatively, (37.35) is equivalent, by (37.33)--(37.34), to
  curl_a z(t)=0.
The coordinate lemma then identifies (37.35) exactly with the
contractible-loop Kelvin identities. Therefore the following three
conditions are equivalent for the stipulated kinematic path:
  contractible-loop viscous Kelvin balance;
  the viscous Cauchy formula (37.35);
  the vorticity equation (37.38).                           (37.40)

Adding the single vector condition m(t)=m(0) to any of them gives the
exact root NSE with its unique normalized pressure.
The counterexample in Section 37.3.5 proves that this additional
condition cannot be omitted in the full-mean root scope.


37.5. EXACT EQUIVALENCE REGISTER

For every stipulated smooth volume-preserving identity-normalized path,
with V(0)=u0 and no restriction on the initial velocity mean, the
following statements are equivalent:

  VII.A  There exists a smooth mean-zero pressure p such that (u,p)
         satisfies the root NSE.

  VII.B  The Weber covector identity (37.8) holds with a smooth periodic
         potential Psi, equivalently with its unique mean-zero version.

  VII.C  P_ref Wcal(t)=u0 for every t.

  VII.D  The viscous Kelvin balance holds for all closed reference loops,
         including noncontractible loops.

  VII.E  The viscous Kelvin balance holds for all contractible loops and
         for three coordinate-generator loops.

  VII.F  The viscous Kelvin balance holds for all contractible loops and
         m(t)=m(0).

  VII.G  The viscous Cauchy formula (37.35) holds and m(t)=m(0).

  VII.H  The vorticity equation (37.38) holds and m(t)=m(0).

Proof dependencies:
  VII.A <-> VII.B <-> VII.C: C44.
  VII.A -> VII.D: C45.
  VII.D <-> VII.E -> VII.B: coordinate-potential lemma, C46.
  VII.A <-> VII.F: harmonic residual and mean identity, C46.
  VII.F <-> VII.G <-> VII.H: C47.

The pressure in every equivalent formulation is uniquely specified by
(37.10), or by p=-chi after the conserved-mean condition removes the
constant residual. The root pressure normalization is preserved by
eta because det F=1.

The all-loop assertions concern arbitrary piecewise-C1 loops; they do
not assume that every loop bounds a torus surface. The three-generator
reduction is valid only after the local closedness condition has been
established. The velocity mean is retained, rather than set to zero.
The one-form pullback F^T and the vorticity factor A arise from different
tensor transformations and are not interchanged.

A_TIER_PROMOTION = NONE.

38. STRENGTHENING ROUND VIII: EXACT RESIDUAL CERTIFICATION AND COMPARISON

Scope: the unit-volume torus \(\Omega=\mathbb T^3\), the viscosity
\(\nu>0\), and the finite interval \([0,T]\) of Sections 1--2.
Let \((u,p)\in\mathscr E_\nu(u_0;T)\) be a supplied smooth exact solution.
Let \(v\) be any supplied jointly smooth periodic vector field on
\([0,T]\times\Omega\), with \(\operatorname{div}v=0\). Its initial value and
its spatial mean need not agree with those of \(u\).

All derivatives at temporal endpoints retain the one-sided convention
of Sections 1 and 30. All scalar comparison formulas below hold for
\(0\le s\le t\le T\), including \(s=0\), \(t=T\), and \(s=t\).
The assumptions do not include existence of an exact solution for
arbitrary data: the comparison implications are conditional on the
displayed supplied \((u,p)\).

Notation:
  \(B(a,b):=(a\cdot\nabla)b\),
  \(\overline h:=\int_\Omega h\,dx\),
  \(P:=\) the full Leray orthogonal projection, with \(P_0=I\),
  \(Q:=I-P\),
  \(\lambda_1:=4\pi^2\).

The symbol \(Q\) in this section denotes the complementary projection;
the configuration manifold remains the group defined in Section 1.3.
Spatial \(L^2\) norms use normalized volume. Spatial vector and matrix
norms are Euclidean and Frobenius, except where \(\mathrm{op}\) appears.

38.1. C48: exact projected residual, normalized pressure, and mean

Define the actual projected residual of \(v\) by
\[
 r:=P\bigl(v_t+B(v,v)-\nu\Delta v\bigr)
   =v_t+PB(v,v)-\nu\Delta v.                              \tag{38.1}
\]
The equality uses \(\operatorname{div}v_t=0\) and
\(\operatorname{div}\Delta v=0\). In particular
\(\operatorname{div}r=0\). The Fourier definition of \(P\), with multiplier
\(I-k\otimes k/|k|^2\) for \(k\ne0\) and \(I\) for \(k=0\), preserves
smooth periodic fields and all time derivatives on the compact slab.

Put \(c_v:=B(v,v)\). Define \(q=q(v)\) by
\[
 \widehat q(t,0)=0,\qquad
 \widehat q(t,k)=\frac{i\,k\cdot\widehat c_v(t,k)}
                      {2\pi|k|^2}\quad(k\ne0).             \tag{38.2}
\]
Smooth rapid decay of the coefficients and their time derivatives gives
a real jointly smooth periodic scalar. Reality follows from
\(\widehat c_v(-k)=\overline{\widehat c_v(k)}\). Direct multiplication by
\(2\pi i k\) gives
\[
 \nabla q=-Qc_v,\qquad \int_\Omega q=0.                    \tag{38.3}
\]
The \(k=0\) gradient coefficient and the \(k=0\) coefficient of \(Qc_v\)
both vanish. Fourier uniqueness proves (38.3) as an identity of actual
fields, and the fixed zero coefficient proves uniqueness of this
normalized \(q\).

Substitution of (38.3) into (38.1) gives the exact forced identity
\[
 v_t+B(v,v)+\nabla q-\nu\Delta v=r.                        \tag{38.4}
\]
Consequently
\[
 r\equiv0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (v,q(v))\in\mathscr E_\nu(v(0);T).                        \tag{38.5}
\]
In the reverse implication any normalized NSE pressure agrees with
(38.2), by (38.3) and its uniqueness. Thus zero residual certifies the
original exact equation for the supplied field, including its actual
initial datum and normalized pressure.

For every component,
\[
 \int_\Omega B(v,v)_i
   =\int_\Omega\partial_j(v_jv_i)=0,\qquad
 \int_\Omega\Delta v_i=0.
\]
The divergence-free hypothesis is used in the first equality.
The full zero mode of \(P\) therefore gives
\[
 \frac{d}{dt}\overline v=\overline r,\qquad
 \overline u(t)=\overline{u_0}.                            \tag{38.6}
\]
Set
\[
 w:=u-v,\qquad
 m(t):=\overline w(t),\qquad z:=w-m(t).
\]
Then
\[
 m'(t)=-\overline r(t),\qquad
 m(t)=m(s)-\int_s^t\overline r(\tau)\,d\tau,\qquad
 \overline z=0,\quad \operatorname{div}z=0.                \tag{38.7}
\]
In particular the mean difference is determined exactly by the initial
mean difference and the mean of the measured residual.

The corresponding reduced virtual-work defect is also exact. For every
smooth divergence-free \(h\), vanishing at \(t=0,T\), periodic integration
by parts in (38.4) gives
\[
 \int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega
  v\cdot\bigl(h_t+[v,h]\bigr)
   -\nu D_xv:D_xh\,dx\,dt
 =-\int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega r\cdot h\,dx\,dt.               \tag{38.8}
\]
Here \([v,h]=B(v,h)-B(h,v)\). The additional term from
\(-v\cdot B(h,v)=-h\cdot\nabla(|v|^2/2)\) integrates to zero.
The pressure pairs to zero with \(h\). The constant spatial modes of
\(h\) are retained; (38.8) therefore includes (38.6).

C48 is (38.1)--(38.8), including uniqueness of the pressure and the
unrestricted mean identity. QED.
