38.2. C49: mean-corrected error identity and sharp comparison

38.2.1. Exact error and forcing identities

Subtract (38.4) from the equation for \(u\). The algebraic identity
\[
 B(u,u)-B(v,v)=B(u,w)+B(w,v)
\]
gives
\[
 w_t+B(u,w)+B(w,v)+\nabla(p-q)-\nu\Delta w=-r.             \tag{38.9}
\]
Since \(m\) is spatially constant and satisfies (38.7), define
\[
 f:=r-\overline r+B(m,v).                                 \tag{38.10}
\]
Then the centered error satisfies
\[
 z_t+B(u,z)+B(z,v)+\nabla(p-q)-\nu\Delta z=-f.             \tag{38.11}
\]
Every term in \(f\) is smooth. Also
\[
 \overline f=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}f=0.
\]
For the term \(B(m,v)\), these statements follow from periodicity,
spatial constancy of \(m\), and
\(\operatorname{div}B(m,v)=m\cdot\nabla\operatorname{div}v=0\).
In particular no zero-mean hypothesis on \(r\) or on \(u_0-v(0)\) has been
added to derive (38.11).

38.2.2. One-sided strain and the energy identity

Define the one-sided strain coefficient by the actual compact supremum
\[
 a_v(t):=\max_{\substack{x\in\Omega\\|\xi|=1}}
           \bigl[-\xi^{\mathsf T}D(v)(t,x)\xi\bigr].        \tag{38.12}
\]
Equivalently, it is \(\max_x\lambda_{\max}(-D(v)(t,x))\).
The compact supremum formulation does not require an abstract spectral
theorem. Since \(\operatorname{tr}D(v)=0\), the three coordinate
Rayleigh quotients have sum zero, so \(a_v(t)\ge0\). Moreover
\[
 a_v(t)\le\|D(v)(t)\|_{L^\infty,\mathrm{op}},\qquad
 |a_v(t)-a_v(s)|
 \le\|D(v)(t)-D(v)(s)\|_{L^\infty,\mathrm{op}}.             \tag{38.13}
\]
Joint smoothness on the compact slab makes the latter norm tend to zero
as \(t\to s\). Thus \(a_v\) is continuous and bounded on \([0,T]\).

Let
\[
 Y(t):=\|z(t)\|_2^2,\quad
 G(t):=\|\nabla z(t)\|_2,\quad
 \beta(t):=\|f(t)\|_2.
\]
Smoothness on a compact spatial domain permits differentiation of the
squared norm. Pairing (38.11) with \(z\) gives
\[
 \frac12Y'+\nu G^2
  =-\int_\Omega z^{\mathsf T}D(v)z\,dx-\langle f,z\rangle.
                                                               \tag{38.14}
\]
The separate cancellations are
\[
 \int_\Omega z\cdot B(u,z)
   =\frac12\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}(u|z|^2)=0,
 \qquad
 \int_\Omega z\cdot\nabla(p-q)=0.
\]
The first uses \(\operatorname{div}u=0\), not \(u=z\).
For the remaining nonlinear term,
\(z^{\mathsf T}D_xv\,z=z^{\mathsf T}D(v)z\), because the skew-symmetric
part has zero quadratic form. The Laplacian pairing is
\(-\|\nabla z\|_2^2\).

The actual zero mean of \(z\) and the Fourier Poincare inequality give
\[
 G^2\ge\lambda_1Y,\qquad \lambda_1=4\pi^2.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \frac12Y'\le\sigma Y+\beta\sqrt Y,\qquad
 \sigma(t):=a_v(t)-\nu\lambda_1.                           \tag{38.15}
\]
The coefficient \(a_v\) is the least pointwise coefficient controlling
all Rayleigh quotients of \(-D(v)\); \(\lambda_1\) is the attained first
nonzero eigenvalue of \(-\Delta\) on this torus. This statement does not
claim that their combination optimizes every solution-dependent bound.

38.2.3. Integrating factor, including zeros of the error

Put
\[
 \Phi_\sigma(t,s):=\exp\left(\int_s^t\sigma(\tau)\,d\tau\right).
\]
Then, for \(0\le s\le t\le T\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|z(t)\|_2
 \le\Phi_\sigma(t,s)\|z(s)\|_2+
       \int_s^t\Phi_\sigma(t,\tau)\beta(\tau)\,d\tau.
 \quad}                                                   \tag{38.16}
\]

Proof without division by \(\|z\|_2\).
For \(\epsilon>0\), set
\(y_\epsilon:=\sqrt{Y+\epsilon^2}\). It is differentiable at interior
times and has the prescribed one-sided derivatives at endpoints.
From (38.15),
\[
 y_\epsilon'
  =\frac{Y'}{2y_\epsilon}
  \le \sigma\frac{Y}{y_\epsilon}
        +\beta\frac{\sqrt Y}{y_\epsilon}
  \le \sigma y_\epsilon+\beta+\epsilon|\sigma|.           \tag{38.17}
\]
Indeed
\(-\sigma\epsilon^2/y_\epsilon\le\epsilon|\sigma|\).
This correction is retained when \(\sigma<0\).

Multiplication by
\(\exp(-\int_s^\tau\sigma)\) and integration over \([s,t]\) gives
\[
 y_\epsilon(t)
 \le\Phi_\sigma(t,s)y_\epsilon(s)
   +\int_s^t\Phi_\sigma(t,\tau)
           \bigl(\beta(\tau)+\epsilon|\sigma(\tau)|\bigr)d\tau.
\]
All coefficients are continuous and bounded on the compact interval.
Also \(0\le y_\epsilon-\sqrt Y\le\epsilon\).
The extra integral is at most
\(\epsilon(t-s)e^{(t-s)\|\sigma\|_\infty}\|\sigma\|_\infty\).
Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves (38.16), even if \(z\) vanishes
at isolated times or throughout an interval.

Only derivatives on \((s,t)\) and continuity on \([s,t]\) are needed for
this integration. Therefore the conclusion applies unchanged at
\(s=0\) and \(t=T\). For \(s=t\), it is the identity bound.

For an explicit certificate from time zero define
\[
 \mathcal B(t):=
 \Phi_\sigma(t,0)\|z(0)\|_2+
 \int_0^t\Phi_\sigma(t,\tau)
      \|r(\tau)-\overline r(\tau)+(m(\tau)\cdot\nabla)v(\tau)\|_2\,d\tau,
                                                               \tag{38.18}
\]
where \(m(\tau)\) is the exact expression (38.7).
This quantity depends on \(u_0\), \(v\), and its actual residual.
Orthogonality of constants and zero-mean functions gives
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|u(t)-v(t)\|_2^2
 =|m(t)|^2+\|z(t)\|_2^2
 \le |m(t)|^2+\mathcal B(t)^2.
 \quad}                                                   \tag{38.19}
\]
If \(m(0)=0\) and \(\overline r(t)=0\) for every \(t\), then \(m=0\),
\(z=w\), and \(f=r\); the full velocity error has the spectral gap in
(38.16). Without those two conditions it is the centered error which
has that gap. The exact mean term in (38.19) remains.

If \(r=0\) and \(u_0=v(0)\), then \(m=0\), \(z(0)=0\), and
\(\mathcal B=0\). Hence \(u=v\), and normalized pressure uniqueness
gives \(p=q\). This recovers the uniqueness implication within the
original root scope.

The decay coefficient is attained in the zero-forcing case:
\(v=0\) and
\(u(t,x)=A e^{-4\pi^2\nu t}\sin(2\pi x_2)e_1\), with constant
\(A\ne0\), satisfy \(a_v=0\), \(m=0\), and equality in (38.16).
This example verifies the sharpness of the viscous spectral constant.

38.2.4. Dual residual alternative with an explicit absorption parameter

For the already mean-zero \(f\) in (38.10), define
\[
 \beta_{-1}(t)^2:=
 \sum_{k\ne0}\frac{|\widehat f(t,k)|^2}{4\pi^2|k|^2}.
\]
Parseval and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 |\langle f,z\rangle|\le\beta_{-1}\|\nabla z\|_2.
\]
For any fixed \(0<\theta\le1\), completion of the square gives
\[
 \beta_{-1}G\le
 \theta\nu G^2+\frac{\beta_{-1}^2}{4\theta\nu}.
\]
The constant \(1/(4\theta\nu)\) is the smallest constant for this
prescribed quadratic absorption: the maximum over \(G\ge0\) of
\(\beta_{-1}G-\theta\nu G^2\) is exactly
\(\beta_{-1}^2/(4\theta\nu)\).

Thus, with
\(\sigma_\theta:=a_v-(1-\theta)\nu\lambda_1\),
\[
 Y'\le2\sigma_\theta Y+\frac{\beta_{-1}^2}{2\theta\nu},
\]
and direct integrating-factor integration yields
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 Y(t)\le e^{\,2\int_s^t\sigma_\theta}Y(s)
   +\frac1{2\theta\nu}
      \int_s^t e^{\,2\int_\tau^t\sigma_\theta}
                   \beta_{-1}(\tau)^2\,d\tau.
 \quad}                                                   \tag{38.20}
\]
The Fourier series converges uniformly in time after a uniform smooth
coefficient bound; hence \(\beta_{-1}^2\) is continuous. Formula (38.20)
has the same endpoint scope as (38.16). It is an alternative estimate,
with its stated dissipation/forcing tradeoff, not an added root premise.

C49 is (38.9)--(38.20). QED.

38.3. C50: exact pressure difference bounds

Put
\[
 a:=u-\overline u,\qquad b:=v-\overline v.
\]
Then \(a-b=z\). For a divergence-free field, pressure obeys
\[
 \Delta p=-\partial_i\partial_j(u_i u_j).
\]
Every tensor term involving a spatially constant mean is annihilated
by this double divergence, because \(\operatorname{div}a=0\).
The same statement applies to \(q(v)\), even when \(\overline v\)
depends on time. Hence, with \(\pi_*:=p-q\),
\[
 \widehat{\pi_*}(0)=0,\qquad
 \widehat{\pi_*}(k)
 =-\frac{k_i k_j}{|k|^2}
       \widehat{(a_i a_j-b_i b_j)}(k),\quad k\ne0.         \tag{38.21}
\]

For \(k\ne0\), the matrix \(k\otimes k/|k|^2\) has Frobenius norm one.
Cauchy--Schwarz for its contraction with each matrix Fourier
coefficient, followed by Parseval, proves
\[
 \|\pi_*\|_2\le\|a\otimes a-b\otimes b\|_2.
\]
The pointwise factorization
\[
 a\otimes a-b\otimes b=z\otimes a+b\otimes z
\]
and \(|c\otimes d|=|c||d|\) then yield
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|p(t)-q(t)\|_2
 \le\bigl(\|u(t)-\overline u\|_\infty+
          \|v(t)-\overline v(t)\|_\infty\bigr)\|z(t)\|_2.
 \quad}                                                   \tag{38.22}
\]
In particular \(\|z(t)\|_2\) can be replaced on the right by
\(\mathcal B(t)\). The coefficient still includes the actual exact
solution's centered \(L^\infty\) norm. The \(L^2\) certificate alone
does not supply that stronger norm.

A weaker pressure norm admits a bound using only the certified
\(L^2\) error and approximate data. Define, for a normalized scalar,
\[
 \|\pi_*\|_{\dot H^{-2}}^2:=
 \sum_{k\ne0}(4\pi^2|k|^2)^{-2}|\widehat{\pi_*}(k)|^2,
 \qquad
 C_\Omega^2:=\sum_{k\ne0}(4\pi^2|k|^2)^{-2}<\infty.
\]
Finiteness follows by partitioning \(\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}\) into
dyadic shells \(2^j\le|k|<2^{j+1}\), \(j\ge0\).
Each shell has at most \(C\,2^{3j}\) lattice points and its summands are
at most \((4\pi^2)^{-2}2^{-4j}\); the resulting bound is a convergent
geometric series.

For \(T_{ij}:=a_i a_j-b_i b_j\), every coefficient in (38.21) has modulus
at most \(\int_\Omega|T|\,dx\). Therefore
\[
 \|\pi_*\|_{\dot H^{-2}}
 \le C_\Omega\|a\otimes a-b\otimes b\|_1
 \le C_\Omega(\|a\|_2+\|b\|_2)\|z\|_2.
\]
Since \(\|a\|_2\le\|b\|_2+\|z\|_2\), (38.18) gives the explicit bound
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|p(t)-q(t)\|_{\dot H^{-2}}
 \le C_\Omega\bigl(2\|v(t)-\overline v(t)\|_2+
                         \mathcal B(t)\bigr)\mathcal B(t).
 \quad}                                                   \tag{38.23}
\]
This norm and its constant have been defined explicitly; no
\(L^1\)-boundedness of the order-zero pressure multiplier is asserted.
Both pressure bounds include arbitrary and differing means, because
their contributions were removed by the exact double-divergence
calculation, rather than by a hypothesis of zero mean.

C50 is (38.21)--(38.23). QED.

38.4. C51: material residual and canonical trajectory certificates

38.4.1. Exact residual conjugacy

Let \(\eta_v\) be the identity-normalized flow of the supplied field \(v\),
and put
\[
 V_v:=\partial_t\eta_v,\quad
 U_v h:=h\circ\eta_v,\quad
 P_v:=U_vPU_v^{-1},\quad
 \pi_v:=q(v)\circ\eta_v.
\]
The field \(v\) is smooth and divergence free on the finite compact
slab. The established flow construction consequently gives a smooth
volume-preserving diffeomorphism path \(\eta_v\), including both temporal
endpoints. This construction needs no premise that \(r=0\).

Use the previously derived transported operators
\[
 \operatorname{grad}_{\eta_v}:=U_v\nabla U_v^{-1},\quad
 \Delta_{\eta_v}:=U_v\Delta U_v^{-1},\quad
 \mathcal A_{\eta_v}:=U_v(-\Delta)U_v^{-1}
\]
on their stated spaces; \(V_v\) is smooth and belongs to the
solenoidal domain of \(\mathcal A_{\eta_v}\).
The material chain rule applied to (38.4) gives
\[
 (V_v)_t+\operatorname{grad}_{\eta_v}\pi_v
              -\nu\Delta_{\eta_v}V_v=U_vr.                \tag{38.24}
\]
Its transported pressure remains normalized because \(U_v\) preserves
volume. Since \(r\) is solenoidal, \(P_vU_vr=U_vr\). Projection of
(38.24) gives
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 P_v(V_v)_t+\nu\mathcal A_{\eta_v}V_v=U_vr,\qquad
 \|P_v(V_v)_t+\nu\mathcal A_{\eta_v}V_v\|_2=\|r\|_2.
 \quad}                                                   \tag{38.25}
\]
The equality of norms is the actual \(L^2\) isometry of the
volume-preserving pullback. The normal part is exactly
\[
 (I-P_v)(V_v)_t=-\operatorname{grad}_{\eta_v}\pi_v.
\]
Thus the projected material acceleration defect has exactly the
Eulerian projected residual norm. This identity is along the actual
time-dependent flow; it is not a frozen-configuration heat solution.

38.4.2. Same-label Euclidean lift comparison

Let \(\widetilde\eta_u,\widetilde\eta_v:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3\) denote
the canonical flow lifts, both equal to \(a\) at time zero and satisfying
the lifted periodic ODEs. They obey
\(\widetilde\eta_\ell(t,a+n)=\widetilde\eta_\ell(t,a)+n\)
for \(n\in\mathbb Z^3\), \(\ell\in\{u,v\}\).
Their difference
\[
 \delta(t,a):=\widetilde\eta_u(t,a)-\widetilde\eta_v(t,a)
\]
is therefore a well-defined periodic \(\mathbb R^3\)-valued field,
with \(\delta(0)=0\). This identity normalization fixes the lift
ambiguity and compares the same material label in the two flows.

Extend \(u,v,w\) periodically to \(\mathbb R^3\), and set
\[
 b_v(t):=\|D_xv(t)\|_{L^\infty,\mathrm{op}}.
\]
The straight-line fundamental theorem of calculus in \(\mathbb R^3\)
gives
\[
 |v(t,x)-v(t,y)|\le b_v(t)|x-y|\quad(x,y\in\mathbb R^3).
\]
Subtracting the two lifted ODEs yields the exact identity
\[
 \delta_t
 =w(t,\widetilde\eta_u)
     +v(t,\widetilde\eta_u)-v(t,\widetilde\eta_v).
\]
The volume preservation of \(\eta_u\), the triangle inequality in
\(L^2\), and the displayed Lipschitz inequality imply
\[
 \|\delta_t(t)\|_2
 \le\|u(t)-v(t)\|_2+b_v(t)\|\delta(t)\|_2.                 \tag{38.26}
\]

Let \(D(t):=\|\delta(t)\|_2\) and \(g(t):=\|u(t)-v(t)\|_2\).
For \(\epsilon>0\),
\(D_\epsilon:=\sqrt{D^2+\epsilon^2}\) satisfies
\[
 D_\epsilon'
 =\frac{\langle\delta,\delta_t\rangle}{D_\epsilon}
 \le g+b_vD_\epsilon.
\]
Here \(b_v\ge0\), \(D/D_\epsilon\le1\), and
\(D^2/D_\epsilon\le D_\epsilon\).
Multiplying by the integrating factor and using
\(D_\epsilon(0)=\epsilon\), then letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\), gives
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 D(t)\le\int_0^t
         e^{\,\int_\tau^t b_v(s)\,ds}\,g(\tau)\,d\tau
 \le\int_0^t
         e^{\,\int_\tau^t b_v(s)\,ds}
         \sqrt{|m(\tau)|^2+\mathcal B(\tau)^2}\,d\tau.
 \quad}                                                   \tag{38.27}
\]
Define \(\mathcal D(t)\) to be the final integral in (38.27).
The canonical same-label material velocities satisfy, by (38.26),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \|V_u(t)-V_v(t)\|_2
 \le \sqrt{|m(t)|^2+\mathcal B(t)^2}+b_v(t)\mathcal D(t).
 \quad}                                                   \tag{38.28}
\]
The identity \(V_u-V_v=\delta_t\) uses the canonical lifts. It does not
insert the time-dependent relabeling used by the aligned velocity
identity of C26.

All scalar functions entering these integrals are continuous.
For \(L^2\) norms this follows from uniform continuity of the smooth
fields on the compact slab. For \(b_v\) it follows from
\[
 |b_v(t)-b_v(s)|
 \le\|D_xv(t)-D_xv(s)\|_{L^\infty,\mathrm{op}}.
\]
For the centered negative norms, uniform Fourier tail estimates give
continuity as described above. The lifted displacement is a smooth
periodic field, so its Hilbert-valued time derivative is its actual
pointwise time derivative: the Taylor remainder tends uniformly to
zero and hence also in \(L^2\). The same argument supplies the
Hilbert-valued derivatives used in (38.14) and (38.17).

Accordingly, the FTC and regularized norm proofs use the interior
derivative and continuous endpoint values, or the one-sided derivative
where appropriate. No derivative beyond the finite interval is assumed.
Equations (38.24)--(38.28) hold at \(t=0,T\) with exactly that convention.

C51 is (38.24)--(38.28). QED.

38.5. Scope and deterministic dependence

C48 constructs the unique normalized pressure and all residual identities
from the supplied smooth divergence-free \(v\).
C49 uses the supplied exact \(u\) only through the exact equation and its
initial datum in the computable certificate (38.18)--(38.19).
C50 supplies the stated pressure comparisons, with their distinct norms
and explicit coefficients.
C51 transports the actual residual and compares canonical material
trajectories and velocities.

The mathematical dependency chain is
\[
 \text{smooth }v
 \Longrightarrow (r,q,m,f)
 \Longrightarrow (\mathcal B,\mathcal D)
 \Longrightarrow
 \begin{cases}
  \|u-v\|_2^2\le |m|^2+\mathcal B^2,\\
  \|p-q\|_{\dot H^{-2}}
       \le C_\Omega(2\|v-\overline v\|_2+\mathcal B)\mathcal B,\\
  \|\widetilde\eta_u-\widetilde\eta_v\|_2\le\mathcal D,\\
  \|V_u-V_v\|_2\le\sqrt{|m|^2+\mathcal B^2}+b_v\mathcal D,
 \end{cases}
\]
conditional throughout the comparisons on the supplied exact solution.
The separate equivalence (38.5), with a supplied \(v\) whose actual
residual vanishes, verifies that very \(v\) as an exact root solution.

No unresolved analytic witness has been discharged by a small but
nonzero residual. No global regularity, solution-set nonemptiness, or
finite-dimensional exactness statement has been added.
The mathematical conclusions are B_TIER. The source endpoints below are
read-only source-verified; no matching external Lean compiler evidence
or theorem-level axiom audit is asserted.

39. ROUND IX: QUANTITATIVE SPECTRAL GALERKIN CONVERGENCE
================================================================

Classification: ! B_TIER.
Checkpoints: C52--C55.
Scope: unit-volume T^3; constant nu>0; a fixed finite T>0; the original
unforced density-one root equation; arbitrary velocity mean.

STIPULATED REFERENCE PREMISE.
A particular smooth normalized-pressure root solution (u,p) on [0,T]
with datum u0 is given. Every estimate below is conditional on this
premise. No existence of such a reference for arbitrary T is asserted.
The Galerkin trajectories exist globally as finite ODE trajectories;
their comparison with the root is restricted to its supplied smooth slab.

All spatial derivatives use the flat torus metric. Time identities hold
in the interior with the root one-sided endpoint convention. Integrated
estimates extend to the closed slab by continuity.

39.1. Fourier projection, mean, and two distinct residuals
----------------------------------------------------------------

Write B(v,w):=(v dot grad)w. Let P be the full periodic Leray projection,
with P_0=I and P_k=I-kk^T/|k|^2 for k!=0. Let K_N retain all Fourier modes
|k|<=N, including k=0, and set

  Pi_N:=K_N P,                 N an integer, N>=1,
  E_N:=range(Pi_N) on real vector L2.

Thus E_N is the finite real space of divergence-free trigonometric
polynomials with Fourier radius at most N, including all constants.
Pi_N is the orthogonal L2 projection, commutes with spatial derivatives,
Delta, translations and P, and is a contraction in every Fourier H^s norm.
On the solenoidal reference u, Pi_N u=K_N u.

Define

  z_N:=Pi_N u,
  tau_N:=u-z_N,
  R_N:=Pi_N[B(z_N,z_N)-B(u,u)].

R_N is the consistency residual of the projected reference. Separately,
u_N denotes the actual finite Galerkin trajectory constructed below, and

  r_N^{PDE}:=(I-Pi_N)P B(u_N,u_N)

is its full projected-PDE residual. These quantities are not identified.

Let

  m:=integral u0 dx.

The root momentum identity gives integral u(t) dx=m. Constants are
retained in E_N, and the Galerkin mean will also equal m.

39.2. C52: actual finite trajectories and their full PDE residual
----------------------------------------------------------------

C52. There is a unique global forward smooth finite trajectory

  partial_t u_N+Pi_N B(u_N,u_N)=nu Delta u_N,
  u_N(0)=Pi_N u0,              u_N(t) in E_N.                (39.1)

It satisfies, for every t>=0,

  integral u_N(t) dx=m,
  (1/2)||u_N(t)||_2^2
     +nu integral_0^t ||D_x u_N(s)||_2^2 ds
       =(1/2)||Pi_N u0||_2^2
       <=(1/2)||u0||_2^2.                                  (39.2)

In particular the finite coefficient state is uniformly bounded in
forward time for each fixed N. Also

  ||D_x u_N(0)||_2<=||D_x u0||_2.                           (39.3)

Proof of the finite ODE and global continuation.
Choose a real L2-orthonormal basis (phi_j)_{j=1}^{d_N} of E_N and write

  u_N=sum_j a_j phi_j.

Testing (39.1) against each phi_j gives a polynomial vector field
a'=F_N(a), with a linear viscous term and a quadratic transport term.
It is locally Lipschitz on the actual finite-dimensional real space.
Hence the finite initial-value problem has a unique local trajectory.

Since Pi_N is self-adjoint and fixes u_N,

  <Pi_N B(u_N,u_N),u_N>
     =integral u_N dot (u_N dot grad)u_N dx
     =(1/2)integral u_N dot grad |u_N|^2 dx
     =0,

using periodicity and div u_N=0. Periodic integration by parts gives

  <Delta u_N,u_N>=-||D_x u_N||_2^2.

This proves the differential energy identity and (39.2) on every
existence interval. Since |a|=||u_N||_2, the coordinate state stays in
a fixed finite-dimensional closed ball. F_N is bounded and Lipschitz
on a slightly larger ball. If a maximal forward time were finite, the
bounded derivative would give a limiting coordinate state at that time;
local existence there would continue the trajectory, a contradiction.
Thus the forward solution is global. Polynomial smoothness gives its
smoothness on every finite time slab.

Testing (39.1) against each constant vector gives mean conservation:
the integral of Delta u_N vanishes, and

  integral B(u_N,u_N) dx
     =integral div(u_N tensor u_N) dx=0.

The initial mean is m. Finally (39.3) follows because Pi_N commutes
with derivatives and is an L2 contraction. QED.

Actual normalized pressure and exact residual.
Let q_N be the unique smooth mean-zero scalar with

  grad q_N=-(I-P)B(u_N,u_N).

Equivalently,

  -Delta q_N=div B(u_N,u_N),       integral q_N dx=0.

Its coefficients are computed from the full finite product:

  q_N_hat(0)=0,
  q_N_hat(k)
    =i [k dot B(u_N,u_N)_hat(k)]/(2*pi*|k|^2), k!=0.

The product B(u_N,u_N) has Fourier support |k|<=2N. Consequently q_N
has the same possible radius 2N. A pressure truncated only to retained
radius N is not substituted for this q_N.

Equation (39.1) gives the exact physical residual identity

  partial_t u_N+B(u_N,u_N)+grad q_N-nu Delta u_N
    =(I-Pi_N)P B(u_N,u_N)
    =r_N^{PDE}.                                            (39.4)

This residual is solenoidal, real, mean zero and supported in

  N<|k|<=2N.

It is orthogonal to E_N; in particular

  <r_N^{PDE},u_N>=0.                                       (39.5)

Thus finite energy cancellation does not imply that the full PDE
residual vanishes. More precisely,

  (u_N,q_N) belongs to E_nu(Pi_N u0;T)
    if and only if r_N^{PDE}=0 throughout [0,T].

Membership in the original E_nu(u0;T) additionally requires Pi_Nu0=u0.
The projected initial datum is not identified with u0 without that
extra equality.

Every coefficient in (39.4) is obtained by finite convolution, the
explicit Leray matrix, and removal of retained modes. The residual is
therefore an actual finite computable defect, not an unspecified limit
or closure assumption.

39.3. C53: reference consistency and uniform spectral tails
----------------------------------------------------------------

Use the actual Fourier Sobolev norm

  ||f||_{H^s}^2
    :=sum_{k in Z^3}(1+4*pi^2*|k|^2)^s |f_hat(k)|^2,
  s>=0,

where the vector coefficient norm is Euclidean. Put

  w(k):=sqrt(1+4*pi^2*|k|^2),
  Lambda_N:=sqrt(1+4*pi^2*N^2),
  mu_s(t):=||u(t)-m||_{H^s},
  M_s:=sup_{0<=t<=T} mu_s(t).

Every M_s is finite for the stipulated smooth reference. More generally,
all compact-slab Sobolev norms of every time derivative are finite.
This follows either from the integer derivative characterization of
periodic H^s or from repeated integration by parts in the actual Fourier
coefficients and compactness of the time-space slab.

Define the universal finite constants

  c_0:=[sum_k w(k)^(-6)]^(1/2),
  c_1:=[sum_k (2*pi*|k|)^2 w(k)^(-6)]^(1/2).                 (39.6)

Their squares have lattice tails bounded by constants times |k|^-6
and |k|^-4 respectively. Counting lattice points in successive shells
proves summability in dimension three.

C53. The projected reference satisfies exactly

  partial_t z_N+Pi_N B(z_N,z_N)
     =nu Delta z_N+R_N.                                    (39.7)

For all nonnegative integers r,q,

  ||tau_N(t)||_{H^r}
     <=Lambda_N^(-q) mu_{r+q}(t).                           (39.8)

In particular,

  ||tau_N(t)||_2<=Lambda_N^(-(q+1)) mu_{q+1}(t),
  ||D_x tau_N(t)||_2<=Lambda_N^(-q) mu_{q+1}(t).             (39.9)

Uniform smooth spatial tails, including time derivatives of the
reference, satisfy the following precise statement. For any time order
ell>=0, spatial multi-index alpha, and q>=0, put

  M_{ell,s}:=sup_{0<=t<=T}
       ||partial_t^ell(u(t)-m)||_{H^s}.

Then

  sup_{t,x}|partial_t^ell partial_x^alpha tau_N(t,x)|
    <=c_0 Lambda_N^(-q) M_{ell,|alpha|+q+3}.                 (39.10)

All endpoint time derivatives use the fixed smooth closed-slab convention.
Equation (39.10) concerns the reference tail, not an unproved
time-differentiated Galerkin error.

Proof of the consistency identity.
The exact root equation after Leray projection is

  u_t+P B(u,u)=nu Delta u.

Apply Pi_N. Since Pi_N P=Pi_N and the projection commutes with time
differentiation and Delta,

  z_N,t+Pi_N B(u,u)=nu Delta z_N.

Adding Pi_N[B(z_N,z_N)-B(u,u)] gives (39.7).

Proof of the tail bounds.
The Fourier support of tau_N is |k|>N, and its coefficients equal those
of u-m there. On this support w(k)>=Lambda_N. Thus

  sum_{|k|>N} w(k)^(2r)|u_hat(k)|^2
    <=Lambda_N^(-2q)
       sum_{|k|>N} w(k)^(2(r+q))|u_hat(k)|^2.

This proves (39.8), and (39.9) follows because ||D f||_2<=||f||_{H^1}.
For (39.10), differentiate the absolutely convergent Fourier series.
Cauchy--Schwarz, (2*pi*|k|)^|alpha|<=w(k)^|alpha|, and the tail inequality
give

  sum_{|k|>N}(2*pi*|k|)^|alpha|
             |partial_t^ell u_hat(k)|
    <=c_0 Lambda_N^(-q)
       ||partial_t^ell(u-m)||_{H^(|alpha|+q+3)}.

Uniform compact-slab coefficient estimates justify the indicated
differentiations and yield the supremum. QED.

Uniform low-mode and strain bounds.
The same Fourier Cauchy--Schwarz argument gives

  ||z_N(t)-m||_infinity<=c_0 mu_3(t),
  ||D_x u(t)||_{infinity,op}<=c_1 mu_3(t),
  ||D_x z_N(t)||_{infinity,op}<=c_1 mu_3(t).                 (39.11)

Let

  S_{z_N}:=(D_x z_N+D_x z_N^T)/2,
  sigma_N(t):=||S_{z_N}(t)||_{infinity,op}.

Then sigma_N(t)<=c_1 mu_3(t), independently of N.

The consistency residual has the explicit estimate

  ||R_N(t)||_2
    <=Lambda_N^(-q) mu_3(t) mu_{q+1}(t)
          [c_0+c_1/Lambda_N]
    <=(c_0+c_1)Lambda_N^(-q)mu_3(t)mu_{q+1}(t).              (39.12)

Proof.
Bilinearity gives

  B(z_N,z_N)-B(u,u)
    =-B(z_N,tau_N)-B(tau_N,u).

The term B(m,tau_N) has Fourier support outside the cutoff and is
annihilated by Pi_N. Also B(tau_N,m)=0. Hence

  R_N=-Pi_N[B(z_N-m,tau_N)+B(tau_N,u-m)].

L2 contraction, multiplication estimates, (39.9) and (39.11) imply

  ||R_N||_2
    <=||z_N-m||_infinity ||D tau_N||_2
       +||D u||_{infinity,op}||tau_N||_2,

which is (39.12). In particular the consistency bound is independent
of the conserved mean m. QED.

39.4. C54: exact error identity and quantitative convergence
----------------------------------------------------------------

Set

  e_N:=u_N-z_N,
  y_N(t):=||e_N(t)||_2^2,
  g_N(t):=||D_x e_N(t)||_2^2.

The error is in E_N, is divergence free and has mean zero. Its initial
value is exactly zero. Subtracting (39.7) from (39.1) yields

  e_N,t+Pi_N[B(u_N,e_N)+B(e_N,z_N)]
    =nu Delta e_N-R_N.                                    (39.13)

C54. The exact error energy identity is

  (1/2)y_N'(t)+nu g_N(t)
    =-integral e_N^T S_{z_N} e_N dx-<R_N,e_N>.              (39.14)

Only the strain of the known reference cutoff appears in this identity.
No norm of D_x u_N is used in its stability coefficient.

Proof.
The nonlinear difference is exactly

  B(u_N,u_N)-B(z_N,z_N)=B(u_N,e_N)+B(e_N,z_N).

Pi_N fixes e_N. Periodicity and div u_N=0 give

  <B(u_N,e_N),e_N>
    =(1/2)integral u_N dot grad |e_N|^2 dx=0.

The second nonlinear pairing equals

  <B(e_N,z_N),e_N>=integral e_N^T D_x z_N e_N dx
                  =integral e_N^T S_{z_N}e_N dx,

since the skew part has zero quadratic form. The Laplacian pairing
is -g_N. This proves (39.14). QED.

Finite mean-zero Poincare and Young inequalities give

  ||e_N||_2<=(2*pi)^(-1)||D_x e_N||_2,
  2|<R_N,e_N>|
     <=nu g_N+||R_N||_2^2/(4*pi^2*nu).

Therefore

  y_N'+nu g_N
    <=2 sigma_N y_N+||R_N||_2^2/(4*pi^2*nu).                (39.15)

Let h_N(t):=2 integral_0^t sigma_N(r) dr. Multiplication by exp(-h_N)
and integration give the stronger weighted inequality

  exp(-h_N(t))y_N(t)
    +nu integral_0^t exp(-h_N(s))g_N(s) ds
      <=(4*pi^2*nu)^(-1)
           integral_0^t exp(-h_N(s))||R_N(s)||_2^2 ds.       (39.16)

Since h_N is nondecreasing,

  y_N(t)+nu integral_0^t g_N(s) ds
    <=exp(h_N(t))/(4*pi^2*nu)
          integral_0^t ||R_N(s)||_2^2 ds.                  (39.17)

For every integer q>=1 define the explicit reference-dependent constant

  mathfrakC_q:=
    [(c_0+c_1)^2/(4*pi^2*nu)]
    exp[2*c_1 integral_0^T mu_3(s) ds]
    integral_0^T mu_3(s)^2 mu_{q+1}(s)^2 ds.                 (39.18)

It is finite under the stipulated reference premise. Equations
(39.12),(39.17) imply separately

  sup_{0<=t<=T}||e_N(t)||_2^2
      <=mathfrakC_q Lambda_N^(-2q),
  integral_0^T||D_x e_N(t)||_2^2 dt
      <=nu^(-1)mathfrakC_q Lambda_N^(-2q).                  (39.19)

Because e_N and tau_N have disjoint Fourier supports, they are
orthogonal in every Fourier H^s inner product. Thus

  ||u_N-u||_2^2=||e_N||_2^2+||tau_N||_2^2,
  ||u_N-u||_{H^1}^2=||e_N||_{H^1}^2+||tau_N||_{H^1}^2.

Combining these exact equalities with the preceding estimates gives

  sup_t ||u_N(t)-u(t)||_2^2
    <=Lambda_N^(-2q)
         [mathfrakC_q+Lambda_N^(-2) M_{q+1}^2],             (39.20)

  integral_0^T ||u_N-u||_{H^1}^2 dt
    <=Lambda_N^(-2q)
         [(T+nu^(-1))mathfrakC_q
             +integral_0^T mu_{q+1}(t)^2 dt].               (39.21)

Hence u_N converges to the given u in L^infinity([0,T];L2) and in
L2([0,T];H1), with every prescribed polynomial rate as the available
smooth reference norms increase. No estimate on a possible smooth
continuation beyond T is implicit in mathfrakC_q.

Higher fixed spatial norms.
For every nonnegative integer s and every e in E_N,

  ||e||_{H^s}<=Lambda_N^s||e||_2.                            (39.22)

This follows directly from the retained Fourier weights. Apply
(39.19) with exponent q+s, and (39.8) with r=s. Orthogonality gives

  epsilon_N^{(s)}:=
     sup_{0<=t<=T}||u_N(t)-u(t)||_{H^s},

  [epsilon_N^{(s)}]^2
     <=Lambda_N^(-2q)
          [mathfrakC_{q+s}+M_{q+s}^2],  q>=1.              (39.23)

Thus for every fixed integer s and every q>=1 there is an explicit
finite constant depending only on the displayed reference norms,
nu and T, such that epsilon_N^{(s)}=O(Lambda_N^(-q)).

For any fixed k>=0 and |alpha|<=k, Fourier Cauchy--Schwarz gives

  sup_{t,x}|partial_x^alpha(u_N-u)(t,x)|
    <=c_0 epsilon_N^{(k+3)}.                                (39.24)

Consequently every fixed spatial C^k norm also converges uniformly
in time at arbitrary polynomial rate. This conclusion is obtained
by finite-space inverse bounds after the L2 error estimate; no
uniform high-norm a priori theorem for arbitrary Galerkin sequences
is assumed. No convergence of all time derivatives is claimed here.

39.5. C55: Hamiltonian branch and actual mechanical reconstructions
----------------------------------------------------------------

C55. The zero-cotangent finite Hamiltonian branches of Section 13,
initialized by the projections of u0, have physical velocity projections
converging to the given smooth root. Their normalized full-product
pressures, identity-normalized flow lifts and same-label material
velocities converge as described below.

Canonical finite branch.
With the real orthonormal coordinates from C52, define

  H_N(a,b):=b dot F_N(a).

Its canonical equations are

  a'=F_N(a),        b'=-DF_N(a)^T b.

The invariant branch b=0 therefore gives exactly the unique a_N
corresponding to u_N. Let

  iota_N(a):=sum_j a_j phi_j.

Then iota_N(a_N)=u_N, and (39.20)--(39.24) give the stated convergence
in the common physical function spaces. The dimensions d_N vary;
no equality of different coordinate spaces is assumed.

The Hamiltonian satisfies H_N(a_N,0)=0 for every N and time. It is not
the physical kinetic energy. The convergence uses the finite kinetic
energy identity and the stipulated smooth reference, not a bound
obtained from H_N.

Arbitrary-mean source adapter.
The source Methlib cutoff omits k=0. For m=integral u0, use precisely

  v(t,x)=u(t,x+m t)-m,
  v(0)=u0-m.

The field v solves the mean-zero root equation. Let v_N be its source
mean-zero Galerkin trajectory and define

  u_N(t,x)=m+v_N(t,x-m t).                                  (39.25)

Translations commute with the radial Fourier cutoff, Leray projection
and Delta. Direct differentiation gives

  partial_t u_N=(partial_t v_N-m dot grad v_N)(t,x-mt),
  B(u_N,u_N)
     =(m dot grad v_N+B(v_N,v_N))(t,x-mt).

The mean-advection terms cancel in the Galerkin equation. Thus (39.25)
is exactly the full-mean trajectory of C52 with initial value Pi_Nu0.
Uniqueness identifies it with the direct finite construction. Simply
adding m without the translation would omit the mean-advection term.

All spatial Sobolev error norms are translation invariant. The reference
norms mu_s equal the corresponding norms of v; hence the estimates above
transfer exactly through C27. This is the required interface to the
source zero-mean cutoff, not a change to the root datum.

Normalized pressure convergence.
Let q_N be the full-product pressure in (39.4), and p the root pressure.
For solenoidal fields with common mean m, the scalar Fourier multiplier
for pressure is a contraction from matrix-valued L2 to scalar L2.
Indeed its nonzero symbol is the Frobenius pairing with
-kk^T/|k|^2, whose Frobenius norm is one. Parseval and the tensor identity
a tensor a-b tensor b=(a-b) tensor a+b tensor(a-b) give

  ||q_N(t)-p(t)||_2
     <=[||u_N(t)-m||_infinity+||u(t)-m||_infinity]
           ||u_N(t)-u(t)||_2.

Using (39.11),(39.24),

  sup_t ||q_N(t)-p(t)||_2
     <=c_0[2 M_3+epsilon_N^{(3)}] epsilon_N^{(0)}.            (39.26)

Therefore the normalized pressures converge uniformly in time in L2,
at every prescribed polynomial rate. No pressure gauge depending on N
is introduced.

Flow and material velocity convergence.
Let eta_N and eta be the actual flows of u_N and u, both initialized
by id. Smoothness on the compact slab gives their existence and unique
identity-normalized lifts to R3. Since both velocities are solenoidal,
both flows preserve volume. Denote the lift difference by

  delta_N(t,a):=eta_tilde_N(t,a)-eta_tilde(t,a).

It is periodic in a. Put

  b(t):=||D_xu(t)||_{infinity,op},
  K(t):=integral_0^t b(s) ds,
  b_*:=sup_{0<=t<=T}b(t),
  D_N(t):=||delta_N(t)||_{L2_a}.

The exact decomposition is

  delta_N,t
     =(u_N-u)(t,eta_N)
       +u(t,eta_N)-u(t,eta).

Volume preservation and the global Lipschitz bound of the periodic
lift of u yield the integral inequality

  D_N(t)<=integral_0^t
       [||u_N(s)-u(s)||_2+b(s)D_N(s)] ds.

Gronwall, or direct iteration of this scalar integral inequality, gives

  D_N(t)<=integral_0^t
       exp[K(t)-K(s)]||u_N(s)-u(s)||_2 ds,

  sup_t D_N(t)<=T exp(K(T))epsilon_N^{(0)}.                  (39.27)

Only the reference Lipschitz norm appears. No uniform bound on D_xu_N
is needed for this comparison.

Set V_N=u_N o eta_N and V=u o eta. The same decomposition gives

  ||V_N(t)-V(t)||_2
     <=||u_N(t)-u(t)||_2+b(t)D_N(t),

  sup_t||V_N-V||_2
     <=[1+b_* T exp(K(T))]epsilon_N^{(0)}.                   (39.28)

These are genuine same-label material velocity and lifted-position
convergences, unlike an Eulerian comparison silently relabeled.

With pi_N=q_N o eta_N and pi=p o eta, let
G_p:=sup_{t,x}|grad_x p(t,x)|, finite for the reference. Splitting at p
and using volume preservation similarly gives

  sup_t||pi_N-pi||_2
     <=sup_t||q_N-p||_2+G_p T exp(K(T))epsilon_N^{(0)}.        (39.29)

Both material pressure gauges are zero mean because both flows are
volume preserving.

Actual full PDE defect also converges.
The finite trajectory is not asserted to be an exact root for fixed N.
Nevertheless its computable residual from C52 converges strongly.
For any integer q>=1 define

  U_s:=sup_t||u(t)||_{H^s},
  B_q:=sup_t||P B(u(t),u(t))||_{H^q},

both finite on the supplied slab. Since Pi_N is an L2 contraction,

  ||r_N^{PDE}||_2
    <=||B(u_N,u_N)-B(u,u)||_2
       +||(I-Pi_N)P B(u,u)||_2.

Use B(u_N,u_N)-B(u,u)=B(u_N-u,u_N)+B(u,u_N-u),
the full Fourier tail estimate, and (39.24) at k=0. Uniformly in time,

  ||r_N^{PDE}||_2
    <=c_0 epsilon_N^{(3)}[U_1+epsilon_N^{(1)}]
       +c_0 U_3 epsilon_N^{(1)}
       +Lambda_N^(-q) B_q.                                 (39.30)

By (39.23), this tends to zero at every prescribed polynomial rate.
This conclusion follows after the reference-based high-norm convergence;
it is not inferred solely from the finite ODE or its energy balance.

At each N, the reconstructed material variables satisfy the exact
forced material equation obtained by pulling back (39.4), with force
r_N^{PDE} o eta_N. That force has the same L2 norm as r_N^{PDE}.
Equations (39.27)--(39.30) therefore supply actual mechanical
reconstruction convergence to the stipulated unforced root.

Certification and limit scope.
No limit theorem in an infinite-dimensional cotangent dual space,
symplectic isomorphism with the physical root, well-posed infinite
cotangent Hamiltonian flow, or global smooth NSE existence is asserted.
The exact finite Hamiltonian lifts and their physical projections are
specified separately. The smooth root is the explicit comparison premise.

     -> (39.20)--(39.21), then finite inverse inequality
     -> every fixed spatial H^s and C^k convergence rate.

     -> convergence of physical projections of the finite b=0 branches,
        actual pressure/flow/material variables, and the PDE defect.

Galilean restoration, pressure comparison and actual flow maps.

SixChannels.lean:
abbrev Frequency := Fin 3 → ℤ
abbrev FourierCoeff := Frequency → Fin 3 → ℂ
def SpectralSolenoidal (a : FourierCoeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ k, ∑ c : Fin 3, (k c : ℂ) * a k c = 0
def SpectralReality (a : FourierCoeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ k c, a (-k) c = star (a k c)

Galerkin.lean:
def galerkinFreqSq (k : Frequency) : ℤ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, (k i) ^ 2
def cutoffModes (N : ℕ) : Finset Frequency :=
  let s : Finset ℤ := Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) (N : ℤ)
  (((s.product s).product s).image
    (fun q : (ℤ × ℤ) × ℤ => ![q.1.1, q.1.2, q.2])).filter
      (fun k => k ≠ 0 ∧ galerkinFreqSq k ≤ (N : ℤ) ^ 2)
def datumFourierCoeff (a : Field) : FourierCoeff :=
  fun k i => ∫ x in unitCube, datumFourierIntegrand a k i x
def finiteSynthesis (N : ℕ) (c : FourierCoeff) : Field :=
  fun x => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin 3 =>
    (∑ k ∈ cutoffModes N, fourierCharacter k x * c k i).re)
def coefficientTransport (N : ℕ) (c : FourierCoeff) (k : Frequency)
    (i : Fin 3) : ℂ :=
  ∑ p ∈ cutoffModes N,
    (∑ j : Fin 3,
      c p j * (((2 * Real.pi * ((k j - p j : ℤ) : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) *
      c (k - p) i
def GalerkinSolution.velocity {ν : ℝ} {a : Field} {N : ℕ}
    (g : GalerkinSolution ν a N) : Velocity :=
  fun t => finiteSynthesis N (g.coeff t)

COMPOSITION AND PREMISE AUDIT

C52:
  M16,M17,M41 provide concrete finite-vector-field/global existence support;
  M39 identifies initialization; M40 gives physical forward uniqueness;
  M14,M15,M38,M42 identify the exact energy normalization;
  M37 identifies the actual full finite product before output projection.

C53:
  M21,M22,M44 support all-order actual Fourier regularity;
  M45 connects physical integrals to the torus Fourier Hilbert coordinates;
  existing ML-F01--ML-F07 supply full Fourier representation/Parseval;
  M43 is only an initial cutoff derivative-norm contraction.

C54:
  M38 supports finite pairings; existing periodic integration-by-parts
  endpoints M01--M05 support cancellation after bilinear polarization;
  M25 is sufficient only for the finite mean-zero error's Poincare step.
  The residual/error differential identity and explicit Gronwall constants
  remain newly derived project statements.

C55:
  The zero-mean source trajectories correspond to full-mean approximants by
  the already proved Galilean transformation C27:
    v(t,x)=u(t,x+mt)-m,
    u_N(t,x)=m+v_N(t,x-mt).
  Merely adding m to a mean-zero Galerkin trajectory omits mean advection.
  Coordinate Hamiltonian lift construction remains C16/L13, with b=0.
  No source endpoint supplies a full infinite-dimensional cotangent limit.

DISTINCT RESIDUALS:
  R_N is consistency of the exact smooth reference cutoff z_N=Pi_N u.
  rho_N=(I-Pi_N)P B(u_N,u_N) is the full PDE residual of the actual
  finite trajectory. The finite ODE does not force rho_N to vanish.
  Normalized physical pressure of u_N uses its full product through 2N;
  a pressure synthesized using only retained N modes is not substituted.

CERTIFICATION:
  Source-verified entries are not externally compiled project adapters.
  The stipulated finite-slab smooth NSE reference is an explicit premise.
  Global finite ODE existence and uniform L2 energy do not discharge
  AX6 or establish global 3D smooth NSE existence.

END M37--M45 REGISTER

All solution-associated statements quantify over a stipulated smooth
trajectory on the stated finite interval. In the approximation statements,
the smooth reference solution is an explicit premise. Neither construction
of a finite Galerkin trajectory nor decay of a consistency defect removes
that premise.

The source declarations in Sections 40--42 retain their exact signatures,
namespaces, ambient typeclasses, source paths, blob identifiers, and frozen

not declarations present in Mathlib or Methlib. An edge is not considered
proved in Lean by publishing its signature or an opaque placeholder.

43.2. Circulation, covector transport, and vorticity edges

L28 VISCOUS_WEBER_COVECTOR_IDENTITY_AND_CONVERSE
  MATHEMATICAL_DERIVATION = ID28; Section 47; ! B_TIER.
  LEAN_EVIDENCE = exact external compilation and theorem-level axiom audit pending.
  Target checkpoint: C44; mathematical proof: Section 37.
  Inputs: the smooth divergence-free velocity, its identity-normalized
    material flow, nu>0, finite T, and the explicit initial datum.
  L28.a: From eta_t=u o eta and F=D_a eta, derive
    F_t=(D_xu o eta) F and
    d_t(F^T V)=F^T[(u_t+(u.grad)u) o eta]
                 +grad_a[(|u|^2/2) o eta].
  L28.b: Define the viscous covector history with its literal integrand
    nu F^T[(Delta u) o eta]; apply finite-interval FTC componentwise.
  L28.c: Identify the normalized-pressure contribution as an exact
    reference gradient and recover the integrated Weber identity.
  L28.d: Use the fixed-reference full-mean Leray projection, with P(0)=I,
    to prove the converse. Inverting F^T converts a reference exact
    gradient into the Eulerian gradient of a periodic scalar.
  Sources: ML-O08--ML-O10, ML-O18--ML-O20; ML-K01;
    ML-R01--ML-R02; ML-F01--ML-F07; M06--M10.
  Type boundary: F^T V is a covector pullback. It is not componentwise
    pullback U_eta V and does not acquire the latter's L2-isometry claim.

L29 VISCOUS_KELVIN_TRANSPORT
  MATHEMATICAL_DERIVATION = ID29; Section 47; ! B_TIER.
  LEAN_EVIDENCE = exact external compilation and theorem-level axiom audit pending.
  Target checkpoint: C45; mathematical proof: Section 37.
  Inputs: any closed piecewise smooth reference loop, including a loop
    with nonzero winding, and the same smooth material path.
  L29.a: Define the line integral by componentwise integration along a
    lift, with periodic field values and the lift's tangent vector.
  L29.b: Differentiate each smooth segment's integral under the integral
    sign. Compact-parameter domination follows from the given smoothness.
  L29.c: Apply the product and chain rules; the gradient of kinetic
    energy integrates to zero on each closed loop.
  L29.d: Convert NSE into the exact circulation derivative, retaining
    the viscous line integral. Apply the converse only after L30.
  Sources: ML-K01--ML-K02; ML-R01--ML-R02; ML-D02;
    ML-O08--ML-O10 and ML-T01--ML-T08.
  Type boundary: a periodic primitive annihilates all closed-loop
    periods. Local curl cancellation alone annihilates only the
    contractible-loop periods.

L30 PERIODIC_EXACTNESS_AND_HARMONIC_DEFECT
  MATHEMATICAL_DERIVATION = ID30; Section 47; ! B_TIER.
  LEAN_EVIDENCE = exact external compilation and theorem-level axiom audit pending.
  Target checkpoint: C46; mathematical proof: Section 37.
  L30.a: Small rectangular-loop periods imply equality of mixed
    coordinate derivatives of the residual one-form.
  L30.b: Construct its primitive on R^3 and prove that each lattice
    increment is independent of the basepoint.
  L30.c: Subtract the harmonic constant vector to obtain a periodic
    scalar primitive; identify the constant with the spatial mean.
  L30.d: Prove that the three winding periods vanish iff this constant
    vanishes. For the mechanical residual its mean is d_t integral u.
  L30.e: Transfer a constant covector through eta=a+xi using
    F^T c=c+grad_a(c dot xi), retaining the harmonic mean-defect ledger.
  L30.f: Establish both exact converses: all-loop viscous balance; or
    contractible-loop viscous balance together with conserved mean.
  Sources: ML-O18--ML-O21, ML-K01--ML-K02,
    ML-F01--ML-F07, M01,M32,M33, and the periodic integral adapters.
  Type boundary: a time-dependent spatially constant velocity is an
    explicit counterexample to the converse with only contractible loops.

L31 VISCOUS_CAUCHY_AND_VORTICITY_CONVERSE
  MATHEMATICAL_DERIVATION = ID31; Section 47; ! B_TIER.
  LEAN_EVIDENCE = exact external compilation and theorem-level axiom audit pending.
  Target checkpoint: C47; mathematical proof: Section 37.
  L31.a: Define curl by its three coordinate components; prove the
    convection/curl identity with the div-free premise retained.
  L31.b: Differentiate A=F^(-1) using AF=I; derive
    d_t[A(omega o eta)]=nu A[(Delta omega) o eta].
  L31.c: Integrate and reverse the computation to obtain the exact
    viscous Cauchy formula and its differential equivalent.
  L31.d: Identify pullback of the vorticity two-form with the matrix
    cofactor identity. Retain det F in the general identity and use
    det F=1 only after volume preservation.
  L31.e: Apply L30 to the curl-free mechanical residual, with its
    conserved-mean premise, to recover normalized NSE.
  Sources: ML-K03--ML-K06, ML-O11--ML-O17, ML-O18,
    ML-R01--ML-R02, M31, and C01--C03.
  Type boundary: the viscosity integral is not discarded. The inviscid
    Cauchy invariant is not asserted for a general positive-viscosity flow.

43.3. Residual, pressure, and trajectory edges

44.0. Shared quantified data and coordinate interfaces

Unless an individual identity explicitly uses weaker hypotheses, fix
\[
 \nu>0,\quad 0<T<\infty,\quad
 \Omega=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3,\quad \int_\Omega1=1,
 \quad u_0\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3),\quad\operatorname{div}u_0=0.
\]
All root fields are jointly smooth on the finite slab in the stipulated
one-sided endpoint sense. Velocity means are arbitrary. Pressure means
are zero. None of these identities assumes existence of a smooth NSE
solution for arbitrary initial data.

The source real vector space is
\[
 E=\operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\mathbb R(\operatorname{Fin}3).
\]
Let e_j be its coordinate unit vectors. For a differentiable f:E->E,
\[
 Df(x)h=\sum_jh_jDf(x)e_j,\qquad
 [D_{\rm mat}f(x)]_{ij}=(Df(x)e_j)_i.                       \tag{44.0a}
\]
Thus the continuous-linear-map chain rule becomes matrix multiplication:
\[
 [D(g\circ f)]_{ij}
   =\sum_k[Dg(f(x))]_{ik}[Df(x)]_{kj}.                    \tag{44.0b}
\]
For a scalar q, its derivative on h is
\(\sum_j(\partial_jq)h_j\); its gradient column is
\((\partial_jq)_j\). This proves, rather than assumes, the row-gradient
and gradient-transpose interfaces used below.

The Methlib definitions consequently have the literal component values
\[
 \begin{split}
 (\mathrm{coordinateDerivative}\ f\ j)_i&=\partial_jf_i,\\
 \mathrm{divergence}\ f&=\sum_i\partial_if_i,\\
 (\mathrm{gradient}\ q)_i&=\partial_iq,\\
 (\mathrm{laplacian}\ f)_i&=\sum_j\partial_j^2f_i,\\
 (\mathrm{convection}\ f)_i&=\sum_j f_j\partial_jf_i.
 \end{split}                                               \tag{44.0c}
\]
The finite-dimensional coordinate identification includes the
EuclideanSpace/WithLp coordinate wrapper; no change of norm is made.

The quotient \(\Omega\) is identified with
\(\operatorname{UnitAddTorus}(\operatorname{Fin}3)\) by coordinate
reduction modulo one. Integer-periodic lifts are exactly the functions
descending through this quotient. ML-I01, with d=Fin 3 and a=0,
identifies integration with the half-open unit cube. The difference
between that cube and Methlib's closed unitCube is contained in six
coordinate faces, each of Lebesgue measure zero by Fubini. Hence every
continuous periodic scalar or vector field has the same integral in
the two conventions.

For later local arguments the following partition construction is fixed.
Given a finite coordinate cover of a compact set, choose finitely many
smaller coordinate balls whose closures lie in the cover members and
still cover the compact set. On each choose a nonnegative smooth bump,
positive on the smaller ball and supported in its cover member.
Such a bump is obtained by rescaling
\(\exp[-1/(1-|x|^2)]\) on \(|x|<1\), extended by zero.
Divide each bump by their sum on a neighborhood of the compact set.
The resulting finite functions \(\rho_\ell\) satisfy
\[
 \sum_\ell\rho_\ell=1,\qquad \sum_\ell D\rho_\ell=0.        \tag{44.0d}
\]
Coordinate bumps extend by zero, so this construction also applies on
the flat torus. It supplies the partitions used in ID02 and ID05.

Only spatial Methlib theorems are applied directly to fixed time slices
in this section. Finite-slab temporal derivatives are within [0,T];
ordinary derivatives are used only in its interior. The existing C30
locality identities supply the required right/left neighborhood changes.
No Methlib global-time NSE predicate is substituted for the root.


ID01 SMOOTH_PERIODIC_FLOW_AND_VARIATIONAL_EQUATION
COVERS = L01
OLD_CHECKPOINTS = C01
SOURCE_INPUTS = ML-O01,ML-O02,ML-O03,ML-O04,ML-O05,ML-O06,ML-O07,ML-O08,ML-O09,ML-O10,ML-R02

[LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]
MATHEMATICAL_IDENTITY = ID01; Section 44.
PLANNED_LEAN_ADAPTERS = L01
ML-O01 = IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
ML-O02 = IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_hasDerivWithinAt_continuousOn
ML-O03 = ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_right
ML-O04 = ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_left
ML-O05 = lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le
ML-O06 = ContDiffAt.to_localInverse

EXACT_SOURCE_REGISTERS = Sections 22--24,32--35,40--42.
SPECIALIZATION = the explicit source substitutions and derivation in this identity group.

[END_LEAN_ENDPOINT_INDEX]


Quantified hypotheses.
Let u:[0,T]xOmega->R^3 be jointly smooth; divergence zero is not needed
for this identity. Let \(\widetilde u\) be its periodic lift. Define
\[
 U_*=\sup_{[0,T]\times\Omega}|u|,\qquad
 K_*=\sup_{[0,T]\times\Omega}\|D_xu\|_{\rm op}.
\]
These quantities are finite. Periodicity gives the same global
spatial bounds on the lift.

Derived identities.
There is a unique jointly smooth lifted flow, with smooth inverse,
\[
 \widetilde\eta_t=\widetilde u(t,\widetilde\eta),\qquad
 \widetilde\eta(0,a)=a,
 \qquad
 \widetilde\eta(t,a+n)=\widetilde\eta(t,a)+n.                \tag{44.1}
\]
It descends to a diffeomorphism path on Omega. With
\[
 F=D_a\widetilde\eta,\quad B=(D_xu)\circ\eta,\quad A=F^{-1},
\]
\[
 F_t=BF,\quad F(0)=I,\qquad A_t=-AB,\quad A(0)=I.           \tag{44.2}
\]
For \(\zeta(t,x)=\eta(t)^{-1}(x)\),
\[
 D_x\zeta=A\circ\zeta,\qquad
 \zeta_t=-(AV)\circ\zeta,\qquad V=\eta_t.                   \tag{44.3}
\]

Derivation and source instantiation.
For source total time functions use the continuous extension
\(\widetilde u(\min(T,\max(0,t)),x)\). Only its restriction to [0,T]
enters the ODE. No smoothness across the extension's corners is used.

In ML-O05 take scalar field R, E=G as above, f(x)=u(t,x), and the
nonnegative bound K_*. Equation (44.0a) identifies its Fréchet derivative
with D_xu, so its hypotheses yield global spatial Lipschitz constant K_*.

For ML-O01/ML-O02 set tmin=0, tmax=T, t0=0, source E as above,
source f=\(\widetilde u\), and x0 any initial center. For an initial
radius r>=0 choose ambient radius R>=r+U_*T. The source parameters are
a=R, r=r, L=U_*, K=K_*, viewed as nonnegative reals. Their four premises are
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}(f(t),\overline B(x_0,R))\le K_*,
 \quad f(\cdot,x)\text{ continuous},\quad |f|\le U_*,
 \quad U_*T\le R-r.
\]
Thus the source finite-slab existence and joint-continuity conclusions
apply without a restriction \(K_*T<1\).
The construction covers every initial point by varying x0 and r.

For ML-O03 take source v=f, source state set s(t)=E, source K=K_*,
and the two candidate curves with identical initial values.
All range premises are automatic. C30 converts the within-[0,T]
derivatives to the source right derivatives at t<T. This proves
uniqueness and agreement of overlapping constructions.
The curves \(\eta(t,a+n)\) and \(\eta(t,a)+n\) have the same ODE and
initial value, proving equivariance. Time reversal, followed by
ML-O01 and backward uniqueness ML-O04 with s(t)=E, gives the inverse
trajectory from every terminal point. Hence each \(\eta(t)\) is bijective.

Joint continuity from ML-O02 is upgraded by an explicit derivative
argument, not by changing that source conclusion. The linear matrix
equation \(F_t=BF,F(0)=I\) has the convergent ordered-integral series;
its n-th term is bounded by \((K_*T)^n/n!\).
For a unit coordinate direction e and h!=0 define
\[
 Q_h=\frac{\eta(t,a+he)-\eta(t,a)}h,\quad
 B_h=\int_0^1 D_xu\bigl(t,\eta(t,a)
       +\theta[\eta(t,a+he)-\eta(t,a)]\bigr)d\theta.
\]
One-dimensional FTC gives
\[
 (Q_h)_t=B_hQ_h,\quad Q_h(0)=e,\quad |Q_h|\le e^{K_*t}.
\]
The difference from Fe obeys
\[
 \sup_{t\in[0,T]}|Q_h-Fe|
 \le T e^{K_*T}\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\|B_h-B\|_{\rm op}\to0.     \tag{44.4}
\]
The convergence is locally uniform in a, by joint continuity and the
uniform continuity of D_xu on a periodic compact cell. This proves
\(D_a\eta=F\) as an actual derivative.

For m>=2 the candidate m-th derivative has initial value zero and solves
\[
 \partial_tY_m=BY_m+
 \sum_{\substack{\mathcal P=\{C_1,\ldots,C_\ell\}\\\ell\ge2}}
 D_x^\ell u(t,\eta)
 [Y_{|C_1|}[h_i:i\in C_1],\ldots,Y_{|C_\ell|}[h_i:i\in C_\ell]],
                                                               \tag{44.5}
\]
the sum over partitions of {1,...,m}. Every forcing factor has order
less than m. Applying (44.4)'s difference-quotient argument inductively
identifies these continuous tensors with \(D_a^m\eta\).
The ODE then gives all time and mixed derivatives. This is the
smooth-dependence proof of C01, Section17.6, with its initial-point and
source-bound substitutions made explicit.

The analogous ordered series for \(A_t=-AB,A(0)=I\) gives
\((AF)'=0\), hence AF=I; finite-dimensional square-matrix algebra gives
FA=I. At interior times, apply ML-O06/ML-O07 to the spacetime map
\((t,a)\mapsto(t,\eta(t,a))\). Its derivative and inverse are
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\V&F\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-AV&A\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Take the source continuous linear equivalence represented by these
matrices, scalar field R, and smoothness order infinity.
ML-O08--ML-O10 give (44.3) by differentiation of the inverse identity.
The formulas and continuity extend all inverse derivatives to the
endpoints by induction with one-sided time derivatives.

The same proof permits an additional finite-dimensional smooth
parameter lambda in the vector field. Its first parameter derivative Z
satisfies
\[
 Z_t=(D_xu)Z+\partial_\lambda u
\]
along the flow, with the differentiated initial value. Higher
parameter derivatives have the same partition structure.
This parameter statement supplies the actual variations in ID09.

COMPOSITION_OUTPUT = unique identity-normalized smooth periodic flow,
smooth inverse, and (44.1)--(44.3), available without an NSE premise.

Quantified hypotheses.
First use the flow of ID01, allowing nonzero divergence. Then specialize
to divergence-free u. The change-of-variables argument also applies to
any fixed smooth orientation-preserving torus diffeomorphism eta.
Write J=det F, A=F^{-1}.

Derived determinant identities.
For every differentiable invertible matrix path,
\[
 \frac d{dt}\det F
   =\sum_{i,\alpha}(\operatorname{cof}F)_{i\alpha}(F_t)_{i\alpha}
   =J\operatorname{tr}(AF_t).                              \tag{44.6}
\]
For the flow,
\[
 J_t=J(\operatorname{div}u)\circ\eta,\qquad J(0)=1.          \tag{44.7}
\]
In particular,
\[
 \operatorname{div}u=0\Longrightarrow J=1.
\]
Conversely, for a smooth diffeomorphism path with J=1 and
\(u=\eta_t\circ\eta^{-1}\), (44.7) gives div u=0.

Proof of the determinant interface.
In ML-O11 take the matrix F in Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R.
Differentiate its six cubic monomials with ML-O12, applied to real-valued
entry functions. Collecting the coefficients of \((F_t)_{i\alpha}\)
gives the cofactors and the first equality in (44.6).
ML-O14 gives \(F\operatorname{adj}F=JI\).
Invertibility from ID01 gives det F!=0, hence the IsUnit determinant
premise of ML-O15/ML-O16 over R. Multiplication by A and transposition
give \(\operatorname{cof}F=JA^T\), proving the second equality.
Substitute \(F_t=BF\); direct finite-index contraction gives
\[
 \sum_{\alpha,i,k}A_{\alpha i}B_{ik}F_{k\alpha}
   =\sum_{i,k}B_{ik}\delta_{ki}=\operatorname{tr}B.
\]
This proves (44.7). For divergence zero, ML-R02 applied to each scalar
path J(\(\cdot,a\)) gives \(J(t,a)-1=\int_0^t0=0\).

Derived integral identity.
For every Borel A0 subset Omega and every continuous f, or every
nonnegative measurable f, or every integrable f on eta(A0),
\[
 \int_{\eta(A_0)} f(x)\,dx
   =\int_{A_0} f(\eta(a))J(a)\,da.                         \tag{44.8}
\]
Vector identities hold componentwise. This is a domain identity, not
only a whole-torus periodic integration rule.

Coordinate derivation of (44.8).
The one-dimensional substitution rule follows from FTC and the chain
rule: for continuous h take its integral primitive H; then
\((H\circ\phi)'=(h\circ\phi)\phi'\), integrate on an interval, and
reverse endpoints if phi is decreasing. Approximating interval indicators
by bounded continuous functions gives equality of the two locally finite
measures on intervals. Uniqueness of finite measures on bounded intervals
then gives equality on Borel sets; exhaustion treats unbounded intervals.
Nonnegative simple functions and their increasing limits give the rule
for nonnegative measurable h. ML-R01/ML-R02 instantiate the continuous
primitive step with scalar codomain R.

An elementary invertible linear transformation is a composition of
coordinate permutations, nonzero coordinate scalings, and shears.
Fubini and this one-dimensional rule give substitution for each such
map, with the absolute value of its determinant. Gaussian elimination
therefore proves substitution for every fixed invertible matrix.

For a local C1 diffeomorphism Phi near x0, compose its target with
\(D\Phi(x_0)^{-1}\) and a translation. The normalized derivative at x0
is I. After shrinking the neighborhood, all leading principal minors
are nonzero. Define
\[
 G_j(x)=(\Phi_1(x),\ldots,\Phi_j(x),x_{j+1},\ldots,x_3),
 \qquad G_0=\mathrm{id}.
\]
ML-O06, with their invertible derivative matrices as continuous linear
equivalences, gives simultaneous local inverse neighborhoods for the
four maps. Each transition \(G_j\circ G_{j-1}^{-1}\) changes only the
j-th coordinate. On every fixed complementary-coordinate fiber, its
open domain is a countable union of intervals; its derivative is
nonzero on each interval, and injectivity makes the interval images
disjoint. Apply the one-dimensional substitution rule on these
intervals and Fubini in the other coordinates. The product of the
three scalar Jacobians is det D Phi by ML-O08 and ML-K05.
Undoing the fixed linear normalization proves local substitution.

Use the finite bump partition (44.0d) on source neighborhoods on which
eta and its image are represented in flat coordinates. Torus chart
changes are translations, hence have determinant one. Summing the local
identities gives the global formula for continuous functions. Equality
of these locally constructed finite measures extends it to Borel
indicators and then nonnegative and integrable functions. Equivalently,
continuous approximation on compact sets and monotone approximation
of open sets give the same extension. Taking the indicator of eta(A0)
proves the displayed set version. This proves (44.8), including the
domain-sensitive statement required by ID05.

Measure and norm outputs.
For J=1, the diffeomorphism and its inverse are continuous, hence define
a measurable equivalence
\[
 e_\eta:\Omega\simeq_{\rm measurable}\Omega.
\]
Equation (44.8) gives its measure-preserving property:
\[
 (e_\eta)_*\mathrm{volume}=\mathrm{volume}.
\]
In ML-I02 set alpha=beta=Omega, the source measurable equivalence f=e_eta,
both source measures equal to normalized volume, and choose g with
codomain R, E, or any of the finite-dimensional matrix spaces used here.
Its previously missing hypothesis is now proved, and it yields
\[
 \int_\Omega g\circ\eta=\int_\Omega g.                      \tag{44.9}
\]
ML-I01 identifies this measure with the source product-circle and cube
measures as in (44.0).

Thus \(U_\eta f=f\circ\eta\) has inverse \(U_{\eta^{-1}}\) and
\[
 \|U_\eta f\|_{L^p}=\|f\|_{L^p}\quad(1\le p\le\infty),
 \quad \langle U_\eta f,U_\eta g\rangle=\langle f,g\rangle. \tag{44.10}
\]
For finite p use (44.9) on \(|f|^p\); for infinity use preservation of
null sets in both directions. These facts also make the maps
well-defined on equivalence classes modulo null sets.
For \(\pi=p\circ\eta\),
\[
 \int\pi=\int p,\qquad
 \tfrac12\int|V|^2=\tfrac12\int|u|^2,\quad V=u\circ\eta.    \tag{44.11}
\]

COMPOSITION_OUTPUT = J=1, the actual measure-preserving measurable
equivalence required by ML-I02, domain substitution, pullback isometry,
and exact preservation of the pressure gauge and velocity mean.

Quantified hypotheses.
Let eta be a C-infinity orientation-preserving diffeomorphism in a
coordinate neighborhood, or a torus diffeomorphism with its local lifts.
Let \(F_{i\alpha}=\partial_\alpha\eta_i\), \(A=F^{-1}\), \(J=\det F>0\).
No incompressibility hypothesis is needed here. Let Q be a smooth
Eulerian 3-by-3 matrix field with row divergence
\((\operatorname{div}_xQ)_i=\partial_jQ_{ij}\).

Derived identities.
\[
 \operatorname{cof}F=JA^T,\qquad
 \partial_\alpha(JA_{\alpha j})=0,                        \tag{44.12}
\]
\[
 \operatorname{Div}_a[J(Q\circ\eta)A^T]
   =J(\operatorname{div}_xQ)\circ\eta.                    \tag{44.13}
\]

Derivation.
ML-O13, with coefficient ring R and matrix F, gives the nine quadratic
adjugate entries. Transpose them to obtain the cofactor entries:
\[
 C_{i\alpha}
   =\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{\alpha\beta\gamma}
                    F_{j\beta}F_{k\gamma}.
\]
The inverse/adjugate contraction in ID02 gives C=JA^T; this is the same
matrix identity as the first part of (44.12).

Differentiate the finite sum with ML-O19/ML-O20. ML-O18 is instantiated
with scalar field R, source domain E, codomain R, function eta_j, order
infinity, and directions e_alpha,e_beta (and then e_alpha,e_gamma).
Its second-derivative symmetry gives
\(\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta\eta_j
 =\partial_\beta\partial_\alpha\eta_j\).
Consequently
\[
 \begin{split}
 \partial_\alpha C_{i\alpha}
 =\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{\alpha\beta\gamma}
 [(\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta\eta_j)F_{k\gamma}
  +F_{j\beta}(\partial_\alpha\partial_\gamma\eta_k)]=0.
 \end{split}
\]
In the first sum exchanging alpha and beta leaves the derivative
unchanged and negates epsilon. In the second exchange alpha and gamma.
Each real finite sum is therefore its own negative and is zero.

For the flux matrix, the i-alpha entry is
\(JQ_{ij}(\eta)A_{\alpha j}\). Apply ML-O08 to each scalar Q_ij,
with inner function eta, then ML-O19 and the proven cofactor divergence:
\[
 \begin{split}
 \partial_\alpha[JQ_{ij}(\eta)A_{\alpha j}]
 &=JA_{\alpha j}(\partial_kQ_{ij})(\eta)F_{k\alpha}\\
 &=J(\partial_jQ_{ij})(\eta).
 \end{split}
\]
The final equality uses \(FA=I\), supplied with the actual determinant
unit premise by ML-O15. This proves (44.13).

The scalar-divergence version, for a vector field h, is
\[
 \operatorname{div}_a[JA(h\circ\eta)]
   =J(\operatorname{div}_xh)\circ\eta.                    \tag{44.14}
\]
It is the same component calculation without the free row index.

COMPOSITION_OUTPUT = the exact row-divergence transformation for every
smooth Eulerian flux; J is retained until incompressibility is applied.
LEAN_STATUS = L03 remains pending external elaboration and theorem-level axiom audit.

Quantified hypotheses.
Let eta(t) be a smooth diffeomorphism path, with F,A,J as above,
\(V=\eta_t\), \(u=V\circ\eta^{-1}\). For arbitrary smooth Eulerian
h and scalar q put \(H=h\circ\eta\), \(\theta=q\circ\eta\).

Derived identities.
\[
 (D_xh)\circ\eta=D_aH\,A,\quad
 (\nabla_xq)\circ\eta=A^T\nabla_a\theta,\quad
 (\operatorname{div}_xh)\circ\eta=\operatorname{tr}(D_aH A),\tag{44.15}
\]
\[
 (\Delta_xh)\circ\eta
   =J^{-1}\operatorname{Div}_a(JD_aH\,AA^T),               \tag{44.16}
\]
\[
 \partial_t[h(t,\eta(t,a))]
   =[h_t+(u\cdot\nabla)h]\circ\eta.                       \tag{44.17}
\]
In particular \(V_t=[u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u]\circ\eta\).

Proof and source substitutions.
Apply ML-O08 with the inner map eta:E->E and outer map h:E->E.
Equation (44.0b) gives \(D_aH=[(D_xh)\circ\eta]F\).
Right multiplication by A using ML-O15 proves the first identity.
For scalar q the same derivative evaluated on e_alpha gives
\(\partial_\alpha\theta=F_{i\alpha}(\partial_iq)\circ\eta\).
This is \(\nabla_a\theta=F^T[(\nabla_xq)\circ\eta]\);
ML-O16/ML-O17 give the inverse-transpose formula.
Taking the trace proves the divergence formula.

Apply ID03 to the Eulerian matrix \(Q=D_xh\), then substitute the first
part of (44.15). Its flux is exactly
\(J D_aH A A^T\), proving (44.16). The two inverse matrices have this
order because the first A arises from the derivative chain rule and
the A^T arises from Piola. No commuting of the factors is used.

For ML-O10 take the graph curve \(t\mapsto(t,\eta(t,a))\) with derivative
\((1,V)\). In ML-O09 take the outer spacetime function
\((s,x)\mapsto h(s,x)\). Its derivative on \((\tau,z)\) is
\(h_t\tau+D_xh\,z\). Evaluation on (1,V), followed by
\(V=u\circ\eta\), is (44.17). Within-slab endpoint derivatives follow
from the same difference quotient and C30.

For J=1 define the material differential operators by these identities:
\[
 D_\eta H=D_aH A,\quad \operatorname{div}_\eta H=\operatorname{tr}(D_aH A),
 \quad \operatorname{grad}_\eta\theta=A^T\nabla_a\theta,
 \quad \Delta_\eta H=\operatorname{Div}_a(D_aH AA^T).       \tag{44.18}
\]
For a scalar theta,
\(\Delta_\eta\theta=\operatorname{div}_a(AA^T\nabla_a\theta)\).
Each is the corresponding Eulerian operator conjugated by the
componentwise pullback, with its stated vector/scalar domain.

Additional differentiated-constraint identity.
Let \(B=D_aV A\). Differentiate AF=I entrywise with ML-O12, use
\(F_t=D_aV\), and multiply by A:
\[
 A_t=-AD_aV A=-AB,\qquad
 B_t=D_aV_t A-B^2.                                       \tag{44.19}
\]
For a volume-preserving path, \(\operatorname{tr}B=0\); therefore
\[
 \operatorname{div}_\eta V_t=\operatorname{tr}(B^2).       \tag{44.20}
\]
If \(V_t=-\operatorname{grad}_\eta\pi+\nu\Delta_\eta V\),
then the conjugacy identities and div u=0 give
\[
 -\Delta_\eta\pi=\operatorname{tr}(B^2).                  \tag{44.21}
\]
The right-hand side is \(\sum_{i,j}B_{ij}B_{ji}\), with no replacement
by \(\sum_{i,j}B_{ij}^2\).

Eulerian momentum, pressure gradients, viscosity, and incompressibility
into the material system, including the correct diffusion order.

Quantified hypotheses.
Let u,p be smooth periodic fields on [0,T], div u=0, u(0)=u0,
int p(t)=0. Let eta be the ID01 flow, hence J=1 by ID02. Put
\[
 \sigma=-pI+\nu(D_xu+D_xu^T).
\]
An admissible material region A0 is an open torus domain with smooth
compact boundary; small coordinate balls and the whole torus are
included. Compact smooth boundary has a finite cover by smooth graph
patches, by its defining local charts and compactness.

Derived identity for every admissible A0.
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\frac d{dt}\int_{\eta(t,A_0)}u(t,x)\,dx
      -\int_{\partial\eta(t,A_0)}\sigma(t,x)n\,dS\\
 &\qquad =
 \int_{A_0}
   [\,V_t-(\operatorname{div}_x\sigma)\circ\eta\,]\,da\\
 &\qquad =
 \int_{A_0}
  [\,u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p-\nu\Delta u\,]\circ\eta\,da.
 \end{split}                                             \tag{44.22}
\]

Complete region-sensitive derivation.
First prove the divergence formula on a Euclidean graph patch.
Suppose the domain is locally
\(D=\{(y,z):z<g(y)\}\), y=(x1,x2), and X is a C1 vector field compactly
supported inside the patch. Extend it by zero away from the patch.
Fubini and one-dimensional FTC give
\[
 \int_D\partial_3X_3=\int_{\mathbb R^2}X_3(y,g(y))\,dy.
\]
For j=1,2 differentiate
\(H_j(y)=\int_{-\infty}^{g(y)}X_j(y,z)\,dz\):
\[
 \partial_jH_j
   =\int_{-\infty}^{g(y)}\partial_jX_j(y,z)\,dz
      +X_j(y,g(y))\partial_jg(y).
\]
H_j is compactly supported, so its integrated j-derivative is zero.
Adding the three identities yields
\[
 \int_D\operatorname{div}X
  =\int_{\mathbb R^2}(-X_1g_1-X_2g_2+X_3)(y,g(y))\,dy
  =\int_{\partial D}X\cdot n\,dS,                         \tag{44.23}
\]
because \(n=(-g_1,-g_2,1)/\sqrt{1+|\nabla g|^2}\) and
\(dS=\sqrt{1+|\nabla g|^2}\,dy\).
If D is above the graph the same computation reverses the normal sign.

A fixed orthogonal coordinate change preserves divergence, volume,
and this normal pairing, by the chain rule and the fixed-linear
substitution already proved in ID02. Interior patches have no boundary
term: the integral of a compactly supported coordinate derivative
vanishes by Fubini and FTC.

Use the finite partition (44.0d) subordinate to the boundary graph
patches and interior patches. Apply the local result to
\(X_\ell=\rho_\ell X\). On summation,
\(\sum_\ell\operatorname{div}(\rho_\ell X)
 =\operatorname{div}X\) and
\(\sum_\ell\rho_\ell X\cdot n=X\cdot n\).
This proves (44.23) for every admissible torus domain. Applying it to
each row of a matrix field proves
\[
 \int_{\partial D}Qn\,dS=\int_D\operatorname{div}Q\,dx.     \tag{44.24}
\]
This proof establishes the arbitrary-domain traction identity.
No whole-torus cancellation endpoint M01--M05 is substituted for it.

Next use ID02 on the moving region:
\[
 \int_{\eta(t,A_0)}u(t,x)\,dx=\int_{A_0}V(t,a)\,da.
\]
For difference quotients restricted to the slab, their derivative error
is bounded by
\[
 |A_0|\sup_a\left|
 \frac{V(t+h,a)-V(t,a)}h-V_t(t,a)\right|\to0.
\]
Thus the moving-region derivative equals \(\int_{A_0}V_t\), including
one-sided endpoint derivatives. No boundary differentiation is needed.
More generally the same proof with J retained gives
\[
 \frac d{dt}\int_{\eta(t,A_0)}f
 =\int_{A_0}[(f_t+u\cdot\nabla f+f\,\operatorname{div}u)
                   \circ\eta]J\,da,
\]
which is the smooth Reynolds identity under the displayed hypotheses.

Apply (44.24) to \(D=\eta(t,A_0)\), \(Q=\sigma\), and then use (44.8).
This proves the first equality in (44.22).
Direct component differentiation gives
\[
 (\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i
  =-\partial_ip+\nu\sum_j\partial_j^2u_i
       +\nu\partial_i\sum_j\partial_ju_j
  =-\partial_ip+\nu\Delta u_i.
\]
Mixed derivatives commute by ML-O18 and div u=0. ID04 supplies
\(V_t=[u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u]\circ\eta\), proving (44.22).

The surface Piola substitution is also exact:
\[
 n_x\,dS_x=JA^Tn_a\,dS_a,\qquad
 \int_{\partial\eta(A_0)}\sigma n_x\,dS_x
   =\int_{\partial A_0}J(\sigma\circ\eta)A^Tn_a\,dS_a.      \tag{44.25}
\]
To verify it on a parametrized patch, transform its two tangent
vectors by F. ML-K03--ML-K06, instantiated over R and Fin 3, give
\((Fv)\times(Fw)=J A^T(v\times w)\); the orientation is positive
because J>0. The cross-product norm is the surface area density, and
the vector itself supplies the oriented normal density. Partitioning
the boundary proves (44.25).

Localization and converse.
If the left-hand side of (44.22) vanishes for every A0, fix a time and
write its smooth material integrand as h(a). If a component h_i(a*) is
nonzero, continuity gives a sufficiently small coordinate ball on
which that component has a strict fixed sign. Its integral cannot be
zero, contradicting the asserted identity for that ball. Hence h=0
at every point and every time. Composing by eta^{-1} yields NSE.
Conversely, NSE makes the integrand zero, hence every material-region
Newton balance holds.

Source instantiation.
ML-R01/ML-R02 are used on real coordinate primitives and compactly
supported one-dimensional slices in the graph proof.
ML-O08--ML-O10 and ML-O19--ML-O20 supply coordinate composition,
products, and finite sums. ML-O18 is used on u_i and eta_i to commute
the stated second derivatives. ML-I02 is instantiated with e_eta from
identity ID02 and the indicator-weighted integrand, or equivalently (44.8).
The cross-product endpoints have the explicit R/Fin 3 instantiation
just stated. The finite graph partition and the sign localization are
proved above as parts of this identity; they are not claimed to be
already indexed source theorems.

COMPOSITION_OUTPUT = Newton balance on every smooth material region
if and only if pointwise normalized NSE; the constitutive law and
all-region quantifier remain part of the statement.
LEAN_STATUS = L05 remains pending external elaboration and theorem-level axiom audit.

ID06 REAL_SOLENOIDAL_TESTS_AND_FULL_MEAN_FOURIER_PROJECTION
COVERS = L06

Quantified hypotheses.
Let r:Omega->R^3 be smooth and suppose
\[
 \int_\Omega r\cdot\varphi=0
 \quad\text{for every smooth real }\varphi
       \text{ with }\operatorname{div}\varphi=0.           \tag{44.26}
\]
The conclusion below also applies independently at each time of a
jointly smooth family. Constants are part of the displayed test class.

Derived Fourier identities.
With
\(\widehat r(k)=\int_\Omega r(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x}\,dx\),
\[
 \widehat r(0)=0,\qquad
 \left(I-\frac{kk^T}{|k|^2}\right)\widehat r(k)=0
       \quad(k\ne0).                                     \tag{44.27}
\]
These identities are equivalent to (44.26).

Derivation of the missing modes.
Take \(\varphi=e_j\); this gives the three zero-mode equations.
For k!=0 and any real z with z dot k=0, the two fields
\(z\cos(2\pi k\cdot x)\) and \(z\sin(2\pi k\cdot x)\) are divergence-free.
Their test identities give
\[
 z\cdot\operatorname{Re}\widehat r(k)=0,\qquad
 z\cdot\operatorname{Im}\widehat r(k)=0.
\]
Both real vectors are parallel to k. Their complex combination is
therefore \(k(k\cdot\widehat r(k))/|k|^2\), proving (44.27).
No complex-valued test has been added to the real hypothesis.

Actual Hilbert-space interface.
Define the real closed subspace
\[
 H_\sigma=\{f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):
                      k\cdot\widehat f(k)=0\text{ for every }k\}.
\]
Each coefficient functional is continuous by Cauchy--Schwarz and
volume(Omega)=1. Thus H_sigma is an intersection of closed kernels.
The coefficient condition is equivalent to distributional divergence
zero: testing real Fourier characters proves one direction; for the
other, approximate the gradient of each smooth periodic scalar test by
its finite Fourier sums in L2 and pass to the limit.

Set
\[
 P(0)=I,\qquad P(k)=I-kk^T/|k|^2\quad(k\ne0),\qquad
 \widehat{Pf}(k)=P(k)\widehat f(k).                        \tag{44.28}
\]
For each k these matrices are self-adjoint idempotent contractions.
Finite partial sums of the proposed projected coefficients are Cauchy
in L2 by Parseval. Completeness produces Pf, and coefficient
continuity proves (44.28). The matrices are real and even in k, so they
preserve the reality relation \(\widehat f(-k)=\overline{\widehat f(k)}\).
Parseval gives
\[
 P^2=P,\quad P^*=P,\quad\|Pf\|_2\le\|f\|_2,\quad
 \operatorname{ran}P=H_\sigma,\quad Pc=c
                 \text{ for every constant vector }c.   \tag{44.29}
\]
The finite symmetric Fourier cutoffs of every H_sigma element are
smooth real solenoidal fields and converge in L2. Hence (44.26)
extends by density to all of H_sigma. Using (44.29),
\[
 (44.26)\ \Longleftrightarrow\
 r\in H_\sigma^\perp\
 \Longleftrightarrow Pr=0\
 \Longleftrightarrow (44.27).                              \tag{44.30}
\]

Source instantiation.
In ML-F01 use d=Fin 3 and codomain C for each complexified real
component r_i. ML-F02 makes the zero-frequency character one, so
its coefficient is exactly the component integral. ML-I01 and the
null cube faces in (44.0) identify this coefficient with
Methlib datumFourierCoeff of the periodic lift.

In M21 take source field a equal to the periodic lift of a smooth
test field, derivative order m=1, and coordinate j. Its
ContDiff/SpatialPeriodic hypotheses follow from the actual test field.
Through (44.0c), it gives
\(\widehat{\partial_j\varphi_i}(k)=2\pi i k_j\widehat\varphi_i(k)\).
Summing j proves the solenoidal coefficient condition.
M29 is instantiated at each k and coefficient column \(\widehat f(k)\);
its displayed sum proves that the source coefficientLeray is
solenoidal. Its defining zero/nonzero cases agree with (44.28).

For ML-F03/ML-F04/ML-F07 take each component of the L2 representative,
with the unit product-torus measure. They identify the actual
coefficients with Hilbert Fourier coordinates, reconstruct the L2
field, and give Parseval. Summing three scalar identities gives the
vector norm statements used above.

In ML-H01 take scalar field R, ambient real Hilbert space
\(L^2(\Omega;E)\), submodule K=H_sigma, and vector r.
ML-H04 identifies its inner product with the displayed spatial
integral. Closedness and completeness give K.HasOrthogonalProjection,
so ML-H02 applies. The range, kernel, and self-adjoint identities in
(44.29) identify this orthogonal projection with P; uniqueness follows
because both decompositions have components in K and K-perp.
ML-H03 then gives the same contraction bound.

COMPOSITION_OUTPUT = zero residual mean and longitudinal nonzero
coefficients, together with the actual full-mean orthogonal Leray
projection. Smooth solenoidal fields are used as a dense test class,
not treated as an already closed Hilbert subspace.
