Quantified hypotheses.
Let r:[0,T]xOmega->R^3 be jointly smooth. Assume (44.26) at every time,
equivalently the coefficient identities (44.27). No assumption on the
mean of the velocity from which r may have arisen is introduced.

Derived pressure coefficients and field.
\[
 \widehat p(t,0)=0,\qquad
 \widehat p(t,k)
   =-\frac{k\cdot\widehat r(t,k)}{2\pi i|k|^2}
   =\frac{i\,k\cdot\widehat r(t,k)}{2\pi|k|^2}\quad(k\ne0),
                                                               \tag{44.31}
\]
\[
 p(t,x)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}\widehat p(t,k)e^{2\pi i k\cdot x},
 \qquad
 r=-\nabla p,\quad p\text{ real and jointly smooth},\quad \int p=0.
                                                               \tag{44.32}
\]
This p is unique.

Uniform analytic derivation.
For every integer ell>=0, differentiation under the compact spatial
integral gives
\[
 \partial_t^\ell\widehat r(t,k)
       =\widehat{\partial_t^\ell r}(t,k).
\]
The difference-quotient error is bounded by the uniform spatial
difference-quotient error of \(\partial_t^{\ell-1}r\).
This proves the formula at interior times and with one-sided
quotients at the endpoints. ML-K02 can be instantiated at an interior
time with scalar parameter R, spatial measure volume, and component
integrand \(r_i(t,x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x}\); compact local derivative
bounds provide every measurability, integrability, and domination
premise. The endpoint conclusion uses the direct within-slab argument.

Coordinate integration by parts on the unit cube gives
\[
 \widehat{\partial_j f}(k)=2\pi i k_j\widehat f(k).          \tag{44.33}
\]
For k_j!=0, instantiate ML-F06 with a=0,b=1,n=k_j, and the complex
coordinate slice f; periodicity cancels its literal boundary term.
For k_j=0 the integrated derivative is zero by FTC and opposite-face
periodicity. Fubini gives (44.33) in three dimensions.
M21 supplies the same identity for each iterated coordinate derivative.

For every N>=0,
\[
 (1+4\pi^2|k|^2)^N\partial_t^\ell\widehat r(t,k)
  =\widehat{(1-\Delta)^N\partial_t^\ell r}(t,k).
\]
The right side has norm at most
\[
 C_{\ell,N}:=
  \sup_{t\in[0,T]}\int_\Omega
             |(1-\Delta)^N\partial_t^\ell r(t,x)|\,dx<\infty.
\]
Hence
\[
 \sup_t|\partial_t^\ell\widehat r(t,k)|
 \le C_{\ell,N}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)^{-N}.                     \tag{44.34}
\]
These are uniform bounds for every time derivative, rather than
separate spatial smoothness statements at individual times.

Formula (44.31) gives, for k!=0,
\[
 |\partial_t^\ell\widehat p(t,k)|
 \le (2\pi|k|)^{-1}
       |\partial_t^\ell\widehat r(t,k)|.
\]
For every multi-index alpha, choose N large enough that
\(2N>|\alpha|+4\). Then the series of
\((2\pi i k)^\alpha\partial_t^\ell\widehat p(t,k)\)
is uniformly absolutely summable on [0,T].
Indeed the number of lattice points in the shell
\(2^j\le|k|<2^{j+1}\) is at most C*2^{3j}; the resulting geometric
majorant converges. This also proves the coefficient moment bounds
required below.

For finite Fourier sums, all derivatives are literal finite
derivatives. Their derivative series converge uniformly by these
bounds. Integrate each finite derivative along a coordinate or time
segment, pass the limit through the integral using the uniform error
bound, and apply FTC. This identifies the derivative of the limiting
series with the limiting derivative series. Repeating at every order
proves joint C-infinity regularity, including the continuous one-sided
endpoint derivatives.

Since r is real,
\(\widehat r(t,-k)=\overline{\widehat r(t,k)}\).
Substitution in (44.31) gives the same reality relation for p.
The symmetric absolutely convergent series is therefore real.
Its zero coefficient is zero, so its spatial integral is zero.
Finally,
\[
 -2\pi i k\,\widehat p(t,k)
 =k(k\cdot\widehat r(t,k))/|k|^2
 =\widehat r(t,k)\quad(k\ne0),
\]
and the k=0 coefficients also agree. Fourier reconstruction proves
\(r=-\nabla p\) as an identity of actual smooth fields.

Literal composition with M06--M10 and M24.
At fixed time define the source FourierCoeff
\[
 b(k)(i)=\operatorname{datumFourierCoeff}(r(t,\cdot))(k)(i).
\]
The coordinate/cube interface identifies b with \(\widehat r\).
Reality proves SpectralReality b. For each source moment m, choose
N with \(2N>m+3\) in (44.34). The phase functional satisfies
\(\|\mathrm{fourierPhaseCLM}(k)\|\le2\pi|k|\), directly by
Cauchy--Schwarz in its defining coordinate sum. Thus
\[
 \sum_k\|b(k)(i)\|\,\|\mathrm{fourierPhaseCLM}(k)\|^m<\infty,
\]
which is exactly the source RapidScalarFourier premise.
Alternatively M22 applied to the source field
\(\partial_t^\ell r(t,\cdot)\), with smoothness and periodicity supplied,
gives the same polynomial bounds; compactness bounds its displayed
decay constant uniformly in t. M22 alone would not supply that last
uniformity step.

M24, instantiated with c=b, these rapid bounds, and SpectralReality b,
gives coefficients(smoothFourierSynthesis b)=b.
The synthesis is smooth and periodic by the convergent series just
proved. M10 is therefore applicable with its two actual fields
\(a=\mathrm{smoothFourierSynthesis}\ b\) and \(b_{\rm field}=r(t,\cdot)\);
all four continuity/periodicity hypotheses hold, and its coefficient
premise is exactly M24. Hence
\[
 \mathrm{smoothFourierSynthesis}\ b=r(t,\cdot).             \tag{44.35}
\]

For M06 take its k arbitrary, v=b(k), and i arbitrary. Equation (44.27)
identifies its right side coefficientLeray k v i with zero, including
k=0. Its pressureFromTransport coefficient is precisely (44.31).
M07, with the same b and rapid premises, now gives
\[
 r(t,\cdot)+\mathrm{gradient}
                 (\mathrm{infiniteTransportPressure}\ b)=0,
\]
because its projected synthesis has every coefficient zero.
M08 gives spatial ContDiff at this time, and M09 gives the source
PressureMeanZero predicate, including IntegrableOn and zero cube
integral. ID02/ML-I01 transfer that gauge to Omega.
The uniform argument above is the additional temporal interface; it
is not inferred from M08.

ML-F04 or ML-F05, instantiated componentwise with the actual continuous
field and the established summable coefficients, gives the equivalent
torus reconstruction route. Any L2 equality first obtained from
ML-F04 is pointwise here: a continuous nonzero difference would have
positive norm on a nonempty ball of positive measure.

For uniqueness, the difference of two candidates has zero derivative.
ML-O21, applied to the lifted scalar difference on connected R^3,
makes it a spatial constant. The zero integral fixes that constant to
zero. This also proves equality between the torus-series pressure and
the Methlib real-part synthesis.

COMPOSITION_OUTPUT = a unique real normalized jointly smooth pressure,
the actual field identity r=-grad p, and verified substitutions for
every coefficient, rapid-decay, reality, continuity, and gauge premise
used in the existing recovery endpoints.

Quantified hypotheses.
Let u be a jointly smooth divergence-free periodic velocity with
u(0)=u0. Let
\[
 \mathscr W=\{w\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\Omega;\mathbb R^3):
       \operatorname{div}w=0,\ w(0)=w(T)=0\}.
\]
At a fixed material configuration eta in Q, let v and W be tangent
vectors, with u=v circ eta^{-1}, w=W circ eta^{-1}.

Derived Rayleigh identities.
For every smooth solenoidal u,w,
\[
 2\int D(u):D(w)=\int D_xu:D_xw,\qquad
 \nu\int|D(u)|^2=\frac\nu2\int|D_xu|^2.                  \tag{44.36}
\]
At fixed eta,
\[
 \begin{split}
 D_vR(\eta,v)[W]
   &=\nu\int_\Omega D_xu:D_xw
    =-\nu\int_\Omega\Delta u\cdot w\\
   &=\nu\int_\Omega(D_av A):(D_aW A)\,da.
 \end{split}                                             \tag{44.37}
\]

Proof of the coefficient and fixed-fibre interface.
Expansion of the two symmetric gradients gives
\[
 2\int D(u):D(w)
 =\int D_xu:D_xw+
             \sum_{i,j}\int(\partial_ju_i)(\partial_iw_j).
\]
The last sum equals
\(-\sum_i\int u_i\partial_i(\operatorname{div}w)=0\)
by periodic integration by parts and mixed-derivative symmetry.
This proves (44.36), including its diagonal specialization.

At fixed eta, v+sW pulls back to u+s w; A does not vary with s.
The exact quadratic expansion is
\[
 R(\eta,v+sW)
 =R(\eta,v)+s\nu\int D_xu:D_xw
       +\frac{\nu s^2}{2}\int|D_xw|^2.
\]
Its derivative at zero is the first expression in (44.37).
One more periodic integration by parts gives its Laplacian form.
Identity ID04 supplies the derivative matrices and ID02 changes variables,
proving the last expression. This is the fibre derivative in W.
It is not the total variation of R along a changing configuration.

Derived virtual-work identity.
Define \(r=u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u-\nu\Delta u\). For every w in W,
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega
 u\cdot[w_t+(u\cdot\nabla)w-(w\cdot\nabla)u]
      -\nu D_xu:D_xw\\
 &\hspace{35mm}=-\int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega r\cdot w.
 \end{split}                                             \tag{44.38}
\]
The four substitutions are
\[
 \int u\cdot w_t=-\int u_t\cdot w,\quad
 \int u\cdot(u\cdot\nabla)w=-\int (u\cdot\nabla)u\cdot w,
\]
\[
 \int u\cdot(w\cdot\nabla)u
  =\int w\cdot\nabla(|u|^2/2)=0,\qquad
 -\nu\int D_xu:D_xw=\nu\int\Delta u\cdot w.
\]
All time boundary terms vanish because w(0)=w(T)=0.

Concrete source substitutions.
ML-I01 transfers each periodic spatial integral to unitCube.
M01 is applied to scalar products of smooth periodic components;
M02 is applied componentwise or to vector products to integrate them
by parts. Specifically:
  - for the transport term use M02 with source fields
    \(u_{\rm source}=u_j u\), \(v_{\rm source}=w\), coordinate j,
    then sum j; the extra coefficient is div u=0;
  - for the mixed Laplacian pairing use
    \(u_{\rm source}=\partial_j u\), \(v_{\rm source}=w\), coordinate j;
  - M04 is used with source vector v=w and scalar f=|u|^2/2.
Every source field is smooth and coordinate-unit-periodic.
M03 with its field equal to u gives the diagonal relation
\(\int u\cdot\Delta u=-\int|D_xu|^2\);
its physicalDissipation has no factor one-half.

For ML-I03 take A=R, a=0, b=T, the two scalar functions
t->u_i(t,x) and t->w_i(t,x), and their actual time derivatives.
Its derivative premises concern (0,T), so no extension beyond T is
needed. Compact-slab smoothness supplies continuity and interval
integrability. Its boundary terms vanish; integrate in x and sum i.
ML-R02 supplies the equivalent integrated product-derivative form.

For the Hilbert formulation of the fibre derivative, use ML-D01 on
the L2 matrix-valued curve \(s\mapsto D_xu+sD_xw\).
Its derivative is the constant L2 element D_xw, as follows directly
from the linear increment. ML-H04 identifies the Hilbert pairing
with the matrix integral; multiplying by nu/2 gives (44.37).
ML-I02 has the measure-preserving e_eta and integrands supplied by ID02.

Exact temporal localization.
Suppose the left side of (44.38) is zero for every w in W.
For a fixed smooth solenoidal phi set
\(g_\varphi(t)=\int_\Omega r(t,x)\cdot\varphi(x)\,dx\).
This is continuous. Tests \(w=\chi(t)\varphi(x)\), with smooth chi
compactly supported in (0,T), give \(\int\chi g_\varphi=0\).
If \(g_\varphi(t_*)>0\) at an interior time, continuity gives a small
interval on which it is bounded below by a positive constant.
A rescaled nonnegative bump from (44.0d), supported in this interval
and not identically zero, makes the integral positive, a contradiction.
The negative case is identical. Thus g_phi=0 in (0,T), and continuity
gives the two endpoints. In particular phi may be any constant vector.

Identities ID06 and ID07 now give the unique normalized pressure with
\(r=-\nabla p\), which is NSE. Conversely, if NSE holds, M04 with
source vector w and scalar p makes the right side of (44.38) zero.

COMPOSITION_OUTPUT = the exact Rayleigh coefficient, fixed-eta fibre
force, and reduced virtual work if and only if normalized NSE.
LEAN_STATUS = L08 remains pending external elaboration and theorem-level axiom audit.

Quantified hypotheses.
Let eta:[0,T]->Q be a smooth path with eta(0)=id and eta_t(0)=u0.
An actual variation is a jointly smooth family eta_s(t) in Q, for
s in a neighborhood of zero, with
\[
 \eta_0(t)=\eta(t),\qquad \eta_s(0)=\eta(0),\qquad
 \eta_s(T)=\eta(T).
\]
Set
\[
 W=\partial_s\eta_s|_0,\quad w=W\circ\eta^{-1},\quad
 u_s=(\partial_t\eta_s)\circ\eta_s^{-1},\quad
 u=\eta_t\circ\eta^{-1}.
\]
Thus u is the field u_s at variation parameter s=0; the prescribed
initial datum remains u0.

Derived correspondence.
\[
 \operatorname{div}w=0,\quad w(0)=w(T)=0,\qquad
 \delta u:=\partial_su_s|_0
    =w_t+(u\cdot\nabla)w-(w\cdot\nabla)u.                  \tag{44.39}
\]
Conversely, every w in the exact class W of ID08 is realized by an
actual variation satisfying these identities.

Proof.
Differentiate \(\det D_a\eta_s=1\) with respect to s, using the
determinant polynomial derivation (44.6) with s in place of t:
\[
 0=\operatorname{tr}(F^{-1}D_aW)
   =(\operatorname{div}w)\circ\eta.
\]
The last equality is the trace of the chain-rule matrix in ID04.
Endpoint fixation gives W(0)=W(T)=0 and hence the endpoint conditions.

Differentiate \(\partial_t\eta_s=u_s\circ\eta_s\) in s:
\[
 W_t=(\delta u)\circ\eta+(D_xu\circ\eta)W.
\]
Differentiate W=w circ eta in t:
\[
 W_t=[w_t+(u\cdot\nabla)w]\circ\eta.
\]
Subtract and compose with eta^{-1}; this is (44.39).
ML-O08--ML-O10 supply the two chain rules, and ML-O18 applied to the
joint (s,t,a) components supplies the interchange of s and t.

For the converse, fix w in W and solve, in the variation parameter s,
\[
 \partial_s\Theta(s,t,x)=w(t,\Theta(s,t,x)),\qquad
 \Theta(0,t,x)=x.
\]
Use the parameter version proved in ID01, with external parameter t.
The smooth compact-slab bounds of w supply one common two-sided
s-interval, for example [-1,1], and the source ML-O01 bound package
with evolution time s0=0. ID02 gives
\(\det D_x\Theta(s,t)=1\).
At t=0 and t=T the vector field w(t,.) is zero, so ML-O03/ML-O04
identify its flow with the identity for positive and negative s.
Define
\[
 \eta_s(t)=\Theta(s,t)\circ\eta(t).
\]
Every eta_s(t) lies in Q, both endpoint configurations are fixed, and
\(\partial_s\eta_s|_0=w\circ\eta=W\).
This realizes every reduced test by actual volume-preserving maps.
The varied paths need not preserve the initial velocity for s!=0:
the root variational definition fixes endpoint configurations, while
eta_t(0)=u0 is a condition on the unvaried solution path.

Derived action and force identities.
Let
\[
 S(\eta)=\frac12\int_0^T\int_\Omega|\eta_t|^2\,da\,dt.
\]
Then
\[
 \delta S
 =\int_0^T\int_\Omega V\cdot W_t\,da\,dt
 =\int_0^T\int_\Omega
       u\cdot[w_t+(u\cdot\nabla)w-(w\cdot\nabla)u]\,dx\,dt,
                                                               \tag{44.40}
\]
\[
 \int_0^T D_vR(\eta,V)[W]\,dt
   =\nu\int_0^T\int_\Omega D_xu:D_xw\,dx\,dt.              \tag{44.41}
\]

The first equality in (44.40) follows by differentiating the smooth
quadratic integrand on the compact parameter/time/space set.
For the second, each eta_s preserves volume, so
\(S(\eta_s)=\tfrac12\int|u_s|^2\). Differentiate and use (44.39).
Equivalently, pull W_t back by ID04 and note that
\(\int u\cdot(w\cdot\nabla)u=0\) by ID08; the two computations agree.
Equation (44.41) is the fixed-configuration fibre derivative (44.37).

For source-level norm differentiation in (44.40), the actual L2
derivative is supplied by the uniform Taylor remainder:
\[
 \left\|\frac{V_s-V_0}{s}-W_t\right\|_{L^2}
 \le\sup_a\left|\frac{V_s-V_0}{s}-W_t\right|\to0.
\]
ML-D01 then applies to the L2 velocity curve and ML-D02 to its
pairings, with real Hilbert scalar field. ML-I02 uses the separately
proved measurable equivalence for each eta_s. ML-K02 may be
instantiated with parameter s, the finite time-space measure, and
the quadratic integrand; compact smooth bounds supply domination.
ML-O11/ML-O12 are instantiated on the s-dependent matrix entries
for the tangent-volume calculation.

Subtracting (44.41) from (44.40) identifies the actual material
Lagrange-d'Alembert variation with the left side of (44.38).
Every actual variation supplies a w in W, and every w in W is
realizable. Hence universal quantification over actual variations
is exactly equivalent to universal quantification over the reduced
tests. Both expressions depend only on the first variation W.

if and only if the reduced virtual-work identity.

Quantified hypotheses and predicates.
Fix precisely the root data in (44.0). Use the five solution sets of
Section2, with no nonemptiness premise:
  E: smooth (u,p), div u=0, u(0)=u0, int p=0, and NSE;
  N: the same common constraints, specified Newtonian stress, and the
     momentum balance for every smooth material region;
  M: smooth (eta,pi), eta(t) in Q, eta(0)=id, V(0)=u0, int pi=0, and
     \(V_t=-A^T\nabla_a\pi+\nu\operatorname{Div}_a(D_aV AA^T)\);
  Vred: smooth solenoidal u with u(0)=u0 and the reduced virtual-work
        identity for every endpoint-fixed solenoidal test;
  Dmat: smooth paths in Q with the same initial configurations and
        velocities and the material identity for every actual variation.
The symbols Vred and Dmat here distinguish the solution sets from the
material velocity V; they are the existing sets mathscr V and mathscr D.

Derived maps.
\[
 \Phi(u,p)=(\eta_u,p\circ\eta_u),\qquad
 \Psi(\eta,\pi)=(\eta_t\circ\eta^{-1},\pi\circ\eta^{-1}).    \tag{44.42}
\]
They satisfy
\[
 \Psi\Phi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr E},\qquad
 \Phi\Psi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr M}.                        \tag{44.43}
\]

Membership derivation.
Given (u,p) in E, ID01 supplies eta_u, ID02 supplies J=1 and the
pressure-mean equality. ID04 substitutes the actual acceleration,
gradient, and Laplacian identities into NSE, giving the displayed M
equation with no change of diffusion order. The ODE at t=0 gives
eta_u(0)=id and eta_{u,t}(0)=u0. Thus Phi maps E into M.

Given (eta,pi) in M, its reconstructed u,p are smooth. The inverse
derivative formulas (44.3) apply to this smooth diffeomorphism path;
they also follow by differentiating its inverse identity.
Since J=1, the general Jacobian identity in ID02 gives div u=0.
Identity ID04 pushes the material equation through eta^{-1} and yields NSE.
At t=0, eta=id and V=u0, so the velocity datum is exactly u0.
Identity ID02 transfers the zero mean of pi to p. Thus Psi maps M into E.

Inverse-map derivation and exact source inputs.
For (u,p) in E,
\[
 (\eta_{u,t}\circ\eta_u^{-1},(p\circ\eta_u)\circ\eta_u^{-1})
 =(u,p)
\]
by the flow equation and inverse composition, proving Psi Phi=id.
For (eta,pi) in M, the reconstructed u satisfies
\(\eta_t=u\circ\eta,\eta(0)=id\). Apply ML-O03 with the two curves
t->eta(t,a) and t->eta_u(t,a), source state set all of E, and the
bounded spatial Lipschitz constant of this reconstructed u.
The right-derivative and continuity premises are those proved in ID01
and C30. Their common initial value is a. Hence eta_u=eta, and the
pressure compositions are literal inverses. This proves Phi Psi=id.

If p1,p2 give the same u, their difference has zero spatial derivative.
ML-O21 on its periodic lift makes it constant; normalization makes
the constant zero. ML-I02, with the e_eta already constructed in ID02,
is the exact source substitution transferring that normalization.

Remaining equivalences and pressure recovery.
Identity ID05 gives E=N as sets of the same (u,p) pairs.
Identity ID08 gives a bijection
\[
 (u,p)\longmapsto u:\mathscr E\to\mathscr V,
\quad
 u\longmapsto(u,p[u]):\mathscr V\to\mathscr E,              \tag{44.44}
\]
where p[u] is ID07 applied to
\(r=u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u-\nu\Delta u\).
Identity ID09 gives the exact equivalence of the material variation predicate
and the reduced one under \(u=\eta_t\circ\eta^{-1}\).
Consequently
\[
 \mathscr E=\mathscr N,\qquad
 \mathscr E\cong\mathscr M\cong\mathscr D,\qquad
 \mathscr E\cong\mathscr V.                               \tag{44.45}
\]
For M->D the map forgets pi. Its inverse keeps eta and recovers
\(p[u]\circ\eta\); pressure uniqueness makes this the original pi.
For E->D the map keeps only eta_u. Its inverse reconstructs u and
then p[u]. Uniqueness of the normalized flow makes these inverse maps.

Preserved quantities.
For every paired Eulerian/material state,
\[
 E_{\rm material}
   =\tfrac12\int|V|^2=\tfrac12\int|u|^2=E_{\rm Eulerian},
\]
\[
 R(\eta,V)
   =\frac\nu2\int|D_aV A|^2
   =\frac\nu2\int|D_xu|^2
   =\nu\int|D(u)|^2.                                     \tag{44.46}
\]
The viscous kinetic-energy dissipation is \(2R=\nu\int|D_xu|^2\).
The identities follow from ID02, ID04, and ID08, retaining the source
physicalDissipation normalization. Initial data, both pressure gauges,
and the arbitrary velocity mean are preserved. Fixing eta(0)=id
removes material relabeling freedom; fixing the pressure mean removes
the additive time-function freedom.

Restriction identity.
For every 0<T'<=T,
\[
 \operatorname{res}_{T'}\Phi_T
   =\Phi_{T'}\operatorname{res}_{T'},\qquad
 \operatorname{res}_{T'}\Psi_T
   =\Psi_{T'}\operatorname{res}_{T'}.                      \tag{44.47}
\]
The first follows from ML-O03 flow uniqueness on [0,T']; the second is
literal restriction of composition and differentiation, with the
one-sided endpoint convention. Pressure recovery is pointwise in time
through its exact Fourier multiplier, so it commutes with restriction.

For the variational predicates, restriction is justified through their
proved equivalence with E: restrict the pointwise equation and then
apply ID08/ID09 on [0,T']. No test with a nonzero terminal derivative
is extended by zero as if that extension were automatically smooth.
Thus the same commuting identities hold for all five representations.

If a compatible family exists on every finite interval, the formulas
agree on overlaps by these identities and give the corresponding
compatible representations. No existence of such a family is inferred.

proved ID01--ID09 substitutions, with inverse maps and restriction laws.

DATA.
  A stipulated smooth root pair (u,p). For the comparison identities,
  (v,q) is a second smooth root pair with the same nu and time interval;
  the initial data may differ. F=D_a eta_u and A=F^(-1).

IDENTITY ID11.a: actual L2 derivative.
For any smooth vector field f on the compact slab, its class [f(t)] in
H=L2(Omega;R^3) has the actual Hilbert derivative [f_t(t)]. Indeed,

  ||[f(t+h)-f(t)]/h-f_t(t)||_H
    <=sup_x |int_0^1 [f_t(t+theta h,x)-f_t(t,x)] dtheta|
    <=sup_{theta,x}|f_t(t+theta h,x)-f_t(t,x)| -> 0,

with h restricted to the slab at either endpoint. Uniform continuity
on the compact slab proves the last limit. In particular,

  d_t (1/2)||f(t)||_2^2 = <f(t),f_t(t)>_H,
  d_t int_Omega f(t,x) dx = int_Omega f_t(t,x) dx.            (ID11.1)

The second statement follows from the same difference-quotient bound
and volume(Omega)=1. It is a statement about actual functions and their
Hilbert classes; no choice of an almost-everywhere representative is
used to infer pointwise differentiability.

IDENTITY ID11.b: cancellation and exact kinetic balance.
For any smooth solenoidal a and smooth vector b,

  int b dot ((a dot grad)b) dx
    =(1/2)int div(a |b|^2) dx=0.                            (ID11.2)

The component proof expands
  partial_j(a_j |b|^2)=partial_j a_j |b|^2
                        +2 a_j sum_i b_i partial_j b_i,
sums over j, and integrates each periodic derivative over a full unit
period. Likewise,

  int b dot grad phi dx=-int phi div b dx,
  int b dot Delta b dx=-sum_j int |partial_j b|^2 dx.       (ID11.3)

Apply (ID11.1)--(ID11.3) to u_t=-B(u,u)-grad p+nu Delta u:

  E(t):=(1/2)||u(t)||_2^2,
  E'(t)=-nu||D_xu(t)||_2^2,
  E(t)+nu int_s^t||D_xu(r)||_2^2 dr=E(s).                  (ID11.4)

Taking the spatial integral of the vector equation gives

  m(t):=int u(t) dx=m(0),                                 (ID11.5)

because B(u,u)=div(u tensor u), and all periodic derivatives have zero
integral. Thus e(t):=E(t)-|m|^2/2=(1/2)||u(t)-m||_2^2 has the same
derivative as E.

IDENTITY ID11.c: actual infinite-field Poincare and sharp decay.
For mean-zero smooth f, apply the coefficient derivative identity from
ID06--ID07 to each partial_j f. Componentwise Parseval then gives

  ||D f||_2^2=sum_{k!=0}4*pi^2 |k|^2 |f_hat(k)|^2
              >=4*pi^2 sum_{k!=0}|f_hat(k)|^2
              =4*pi^2||f||_2^2.                            (ID11.6)

There is no finite-support premise in (ID11.6). Applying it to u-m,
and differentiating exp(8*pi^2*nu*t)e(t), proves

  ||u(t)-m||_2^2
    <=exp[-8*pi^2*nu*(t-s)]||u(s)-m||_2^2.                 (ID11.7)

FTC gives the inequality also at s=0 and t=T. A first-frequency shear
in ID12 attains equality, so the spectral factor cannot be increased
in a universal estimate of this form.

IDENTITY ID11.d: mixed relative-energy calculation.
Set w=u-v. Subtracting the two equations and using bilinearity gives

  w_t+B(u,w)+B(w,v)+grad(p-q)=nu Delta w.

Apply (ID11.2) with a=u and b=w. The transport term vanishes although
a and b are different fields. Since div w=0,

  (1/2)d_t||w||_2^2+nu||D w||_2^2
    =-int w^T D(v) w dx.                                  (ID11.8)

The antisymmetric part of D_xv has zero quadratic form, giving the
symmetric strain D(v) in the right side. Let S(t)=||D(v(t))||_{infinity,op}.
Multiplication of the scalar inequality by exp(-2 int_s^t S) yields

  ||w(t)||_2^2<=exp(2 int_s^t S)||w(s)||_2^2.               (ID11.9)

If the two initial means agree, (ID11.5) implies mean(w)=0 and the
additional use of (ID11.6) yields

  ||w(t)||_2^2
    <=exp[2 int_s^t S-8*pi^2*nu*(t-s)]||w(s)||_2^2.         (ID11.10)

In particular equal initial velocities imply u=v; normalized-pressure
uniqueness gives p=q. Equations (ID11.8)--(ID11.10) use only a scalar
upper bound on the derivative of squared norm, not a bound on the
absolute value of that derivative.

IDENTITY ID11.e: distortion and ellipticity.
Let L(t)=||D_xu(t)||_{infinity,op}, K(t)=int_0^t L(r) dr. The flow
equations give F_t=(D_xu o eta)F and A_t=-A(D_xu o eta). For fixed a,z,

  d_t |Fz|^2<=2L |Fz|^2,
  d_t |A^Tz|^2<=2L |A^Tz|^2.

Initial matrices are I. The same scalar integrating-factor proof gives
||F||_op,||A||_op<=exp K, uniformly in a. Since
  |z|=|F^T A^Tz|<=||F||_op |A^Tz|,
one obtains

  exp(-2K)|z|^2<=z^T AA^T z<=exp(2K)|z|^2.                 (ID11.11)

SOURCE INSTANTIATION.
  ML-D01/ML-D02: scalar field R, Hilbert space H, curves [u] or [w],

  ML-H04: identify the Hilbert pairing with the actual spatial integral.
  M01: f=|b|^2 a_j, p, partial_j u_i, or u_i u_j as appropriate;

  M02/M03: instantiate with the smooth periodic fields used in (ID11.3).
  M04/M05: instantiate at each fixed time with u,p; their solenoidality

    M05 alone is not used for the mixed cancellation in (ID11.8).
  ML-F07: apply scalar Parseval to each of the three actual Fourier

  M28/M33: use the explicit local temporal extensions of ID17, then

  ML-R01/ML-R03: the continuous scalar coefficients S,L define actual

  ML-I02: transport each norm/energy through the actual volume-preserving

COMPOSITION.
  ID02+ID04+(ID11.1)--(ID11.11) give the Eulerian and material energy,

DATA.
  An integer k>=1, kappa=2*pi*k, lambda=nu*kappa^2>0;
  q is smooth on [0,T], q(0)=0, q'(0)=a0.
  s(a)=sin(kappa*a_2), c(a)=cos(kappa*a_2).

Define the actual torus map and its lift by
  eta_q(t,a)=a+q(t)s(a)e_1,
  eta_q(t)^(-1)(x)=x-q(t)sin(kappa*x_2)e_1.
They are inverse by substitution: neither map changes coordinate 2.
Let N=e_1 tensor e_2; then N^2=0, so

  F=I+q kappa c N,
  A=I-q kappa c N,
  FA=AF=I, det F=1.                                       (ID12.1)

The determinant is one directly from the triangular coordinate matrix.
The path at time zero is id. Its Eulerian velocity is

  u_q=q' sin(kappa*x_2)e_1,
  div u_q=0, B(u_q,u_q)=0, Delta u_q=-kappa^2 u_q.          (ID12.2)

Hence

  (u_q,0) solves NSE with datum a0 sin(kappa*x_2)e_1
    <-> q''+lambda q'=0, q(0)=0, q'(0)=a0.                 (ID12.3)

For the reverse scalar implication, evaluate the first component at a
point where sin(kappa*x_2)=1. Alternatively pair with the same sine mode.
If a normalized pressure is initially allowed in the ansatz, the other
components force independence from x_2,x_3; periodicity in x_1 then
forces q''+lambda q'=0 and p=0.

Since integral_0^1 sin^2(2*pi*k*x) dx=1/2, direct integration gives

  E(u_q)=q'^2/4,
  R(u_q)=nu||D_xu_q||_2^2/2=lambda*q'^2/4,
  d_t(partial_{q'}L)+partial_{q'}R
    =(1/2)q''+(lambda/2)q'.                                (ID12.4)

Here L=q'^2/4. The effective mass is 1/2 and the damping coefficient is
lambda/2. The trigonometric integral follows from
sin^2(theta)=(1-cos(2theta))/2 and periodic endpoint cancellation.

Multiplying q''+lambda q'=0 by exp(lambda t) gives
  d_t[exp(lambda t)q']=0.
FTC and q(0)=0 therefore give the unique trajectory

  q'(t)=a0 exp(-lambda t),
  q(t)=a0[1-exp(-lambda t)]/lambda.                         (ID12.5)

DATA.
  A finite real solenoidal Fourier space E_N, closed under Delta, with an
  L2-orthonormal real basis phi_1,...,phi_d; Pi_N is its orthogonal
  projection. Define J(a)=sum_j a_j phi_j, a in R^d.

By orthonormality, J is a real linear isometry onto E_N:

  <Ja,Jb>_L2=a dot b,
  J^(-1)f=(<f,phi_j>)_j.                                  (ID13.1)

Define the coordinate matrices and tensors by actual integrals,

  L_ij=<Delta phi_j,phi_i>,
  B_ijk=<(phi_j dot grad)phi_k,phi_i>,
  F_i(a)=nu sum_j L_ij a_j-sum_{j,k}B_ijk a_j a_k.

All sums are finite. Therefore

  J F(a)=nu Delta(Ja)-Pi_N B(Ja,Ja),
  a'=F(a) <-> (Ja)_t+Pi_N B(Ja,Ja)=nu Delta(Ja).           (ID13.2)

The derivative is the explicitly linear map

  DF(a)h=nu Lh-B_N(h,a)-B_N(a,h),                           (ID13.3)

where (B_N(b,c))_i=sum_{j,k}B_ijk b_j c_k. This bilinear map is continuous
on the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces. For example, applying
Cauchy--Schwarz to the finite tensor gives
  |B_N(b,c)|<= (sum_{i,j,k}|B_ijk|^2)^(1/2)|b||c|.
No corresponding bounded L2 x L2 -> L2 PDE convection map is asserted.

On R^d x R^d put H(a,b)=b dot F(a). Its full differential is

  DH(a,b)(h,k)=k dot F(a)+b dot DF(a)h,
  grad_b H=F(a), grad_a H=DF(a)^T b.                       (ID13.4)

The canonical Hamiltonian equations are consequently

  a'=F(a), b'=-DF(a)^T b.                                 (ID13.5)

Every base trajectory a gives the lifted trajectory (a,0). Conversely,
suppose (a,b) satisfies (ID13.5) and b(0)=0. On the compact time slab,
continuity of DF(a(t)) gives a finite K with ||DF(a(t))||_op<=K. Hence
|b'|<=K|b|; the zero-initial-value uniqueness estimate implies b=0.
Thus

  Sol(a'=F(a),a(0)=a0)
    ~= Sol((ID13.5),a(0)=a0,b(0)=0)                       (ID13.6)

by a -> (a,0) and projection (a,b) -> a, with both inverse laws proved.
Also H(a,0)=0 for every a. Conservation of H therefore supplies no
coercive bound on a along this branch.

EXACT REALITY ADAPTER.
For a nonzero Fourier pair +/-k choose real orthonormal polarizations
e_{k,1},e_{k,2} perpendicular to k. Choose one representative from each
pair. The real basis consists of
  sqrt(2)e_{k,j} cos(2*pi*k dot x),
  sqrt(2)e_{k,j} sin(2*pi*k dot x).
If their real coordinates are alpha_{k,j},beta_{k,j}, then

  c(k)=sum_j (alpha_{k,j}-i beta_{k,j})e_{k,j}/sqrt(2),
  c(-k)=conj(c(k)), k dot c(k)=0,
  |c(k)|^2+|c(-k)|^2=sum_j(alpha_{k,j}^2+beta_{k,j}^2).    (ID13.7)

The identities follow by the exponential formulas for cosine and sine,
then orthonormality of the polarizations. Conversely, the real and
imaginary polarization coordinates of a reality-symmetric transverse
array recover alpha,beta by these formulas. Constants, when present,
have coefficient c(0)=m and contribute |m|^2. Source finiteSynthesis
omits this constant mode; ID16/ID36 provide the exact mean adapter.

SOURCE INSTANTIATION.

    synthesis convention, without confusing complex and real dimension.
  M37: supply the explicit cutoff support and reality identities to

    f(a,b)=b, g(a,b)=F(a).
  ML-D02: differentiate the finite coordinate pairings when needed.
  M14/M15: (ID13.1),(ID13.2) and the physical normalization identify the

  M17/M41: for the source mean-zero invariant state, the actual datum,

DATA.
  First: a stipulated unforced smooth NSE trajectory with
    D_xu(t_*) not identically zero at one time t_*.
  Second: the formal infinite cotangent linearization at the base u=0.

By continuity and positivity of the volume of a small coordinate ball,
D_xu(t_*) not identically zero implies ||D_xu(t_*)||_2^2>0. ID11 gives

  E'(t_*)=-nu||D_xu(t_*)||_2^2<0.                          (ID14.1)

For an autonomous Poisson evolution generated by H, antisymmetry gives
  d_t H={H,H}=-{H,H},
and hence d_t H=0 over R. In a Hilbert realization this calculation is
  d_t H=<grad H,J grad H>=-<J grad H,grad H>=0
when J^*=-J and the displayed pairings are defined. Therefore (ID14.1)
excludes precisely a pure autonomous realization with H equal to the
physical kinetic energy along the identified trajectory. No assertion
about a different Hamiltonian or auxiliary-state realization follows.

For the explicit shear of ID12 with a0!=0,
  E(t)=a0^2 exp(-2 lambda t)/4,
  E'(t)=-lambda*a0^2 exp(-2 lambda t)/2<0,
so the excluded class has an explicit exact counterexample.

At the zero base trajectory, the derivative of quadratic convection is
zero. Since Delta is symmetric on periodic smooth fields, the formal
base and cotangent linear equations are

  u_t=nu Delta u, b_t=-nu Delta b.                          (ID14.2)

Take the smooth solenoidal periodic auxiliary initial field
  b0(x)=e_2 sum_{n>=1} exp(-n) cos(2*pi*n*x_1).
Every differentiated series converges uniformly because
sum n^r exp(-n)<infinity for every fixed integer r. Thus b0 is smooth,
has mean zero, and is divergence free. For k=n e_1, its second component
Fourier coefficient is exp(-n)/2. Equation (ID14.2), tested against the
fixed smooth Fourier character and integrated as a scalar ODE, forces

  b_hat_2(t,n e_1)=(1/2)exp(4*pi^2*nu*n^2*t-n).            (ID14.3)

Any distribution B on the compact torus has a finite-order bound
  |B(phi)|<=C max_{|alpha|<=m}||partial^alpha phi||_infinity.
This follows directly from continuity of the linear functional on the
Frechet test-function space: a basic zero-neighborhood restricts only
finitely many derivative seminorms; scaling gives the displayed bound.
Testing it on a character gives

  |B_hat(k)|<=C'(1+|k|)^m.                                (ID14.4)

For every fixed t>0 the right side of (ID14.3) exceeds every polynomial
in n: the logarithm of its ratio to (1+n)^m tends to +infinity.
It violates (ID14.4). Consequently no distribution-valued solution of
the auxiliary equation with these prescribed Fourier evolutions exists
at any positive time.

SOURCE INSTANTIATION.
  ML-D02: real pairings in the finite/Hilbert antisymmetry calculation;
    the exact NSE energy derivative is ID11, not a new source assumption.
  ML-F07: the displayed smooth Fourier data and L2 coefficients have
    the same normalization as the source Fourier basis.
  ML-R02: for each fixed frequency, integrate the scalar linear ODE to
    obtain (ID14.3). The finite-order distribution bound is derived
    explicitly here; it is not attributed to an unindexed source theorem.

COMPOSITION.

  Actual smooth b0 + (ID14.2)--(ID14.4) -> failure of a general forward
  auxiliary distribution evolution. Neither implication conflicts

DATA.
  eta is a stipulated smooth volume-preserving path with eta(0)=id;
  V=eta_t and u=V o eta^(-1). Its initial velocity is the specified u0.
  U^0_eta acts on scalar fields and U^1_eta on vector fields by composition
  with eta. P is the full-mean Fourier Leray projection and Q=I-P.

The two pullbacks are unitary on their respective L2 spaces by ID02.
On smooth fields define

  P_eta=U^1_eta P (U^1_eta)^(-1), Q_eta=I-P_eta,
  grad_eta=U^1_eta grad (U^0_eta)^(-1),
  Delta_eta=U^1_eta Delta (U^1_eta)^(-1).

Direct composition gives

  P_eta^2=P_eta, P_eta^*=P_eta,
  P_eta U^1_eta=U^1_eta P,
  Q_eta U^1_eta=U^1_eta Q,
  P_eta c=c for every constant vector c.                   (ID15.1)

These follow respectively from P^2=P, P^*=P, and P_0=I; no time
differentiation of U or P is involved. Orthogonality of P,Q and
unitarity of U imply ||P_eta H||_2<=||H||_2.

Set g=u_t+B(u,u)-nu Delta u. The chain rule from ID04 gives

  U^1_eta g=V_t-nu Delta_eta V,
  P_eta(V_t-nu Delta_eta V)=U^1_eta P g.                   (ID15.2)

Because div u=0, both Delta u and u_t are solenoidal. Hence
P_eta Delta_eta V=Delta_eta V. The exact full-mean Helmholtz result
ID06--ID07 now gives the equivalences

  P_eta V_t=nu Delta_eta V
    <-> P g=0
    <-> exists! p smooth, mean(p)=0, g=-grad p
    <-> V_t=-grad_eta pi+nu Delta_eta V,
        pi=U^0_eta p, mean(pi)=0.                           (ID15.3)

Each inverse pressure map is p=pi o eta^(-1). In the last equation,
(I-P_eta)V_t=-grad_eta pi. The identity P_eta V=V has a time-dependent
projection; no claim P_eta V_t=V_t is made.

For the explicit constraint-force scalar identity, let B_a=D_aV A.
Since div_eta V=tr B_a=0 and A_t=-A D_aV A, differentiation gives

  0=tr(D_aV_t A)-tr(B_a^2),
  div_eta V_t=tr(B_a^2).

Applying div_eta to the last equation of (ID15.3), and using
div_eta Delta_eta V=U^0_eta(div Delta u)=0, yields

  -Delta_eta pi=tr((D_aV A)^2).                            (ID15.3a)

The trace is the trace of a matrix square; it is not the squared
Frobenius norm. This follows from ID04's inverse-matrix and
divergence identities, with no sign restriction on the trace.

On an exact trajectory, mean(u)=m is constant and
  grad p=-Q B(u,u)=-Q B(u-m,u-m).
The equality holds because B(m,u-m) is a directional derivative of a
solenoidal field, hence is solenoidal, while B(u-m,m)=0. Therefore

  ||grad p||_2
    <=min{||u-m||_infinity ||D u||_2,
           ||D u||_{infinity,op}||u-m||_2}.                 (ID15.4)

The normalized pressure Fourier coefficients also satisfy
  p_hat(k)=-(k_i k_j/|k|^2) ((u_i-m_i)(u_j-m_j))_hat(k)
for k!=0. The multiplier matrix has Frobenius norm one. Parseval gives

  ||p||_2<=||(u-m) tensor (u-m)||_2=||u-m||_4^2.           (ID15.5)

Since grad_eta pi=A^T grad_a pi=U^1_eta grad p,

  ||A^T grad_a pi||_2=||grad p||_2,
  ||grad_a pi||_2<=||F||_{infinity,op}||grad p||_2.         (ID15.6)

Finally take two stipulated smooth solenoidal fields u,v, their flows,
and rho=eta_v^(-1) o eta_u. Differentiate eta_v(t,rho(t,a))=eta_u(t,a):

  rho_t=(A_v o rho)(V_u-V_v o rho),
  V_u-V_v o rho=(u-v) o eta_u,
  ||V_u-V_v o rho||_2=||u-v||_2.                           (ID15.7)

SOURCE INSTANTIATION.

DATA.
  q:R^3->Omega is the quotient map, with the usual unit-period cover;
  the source Vec=EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3) is identified with coordinate
  vectors using its standard real inner product. m is a fixed vector.

Define lift(f)=f o q. For a periodic g define descend(g)(q(x))=g(x).
If q(x)=q(y), then y-x is an integer vector, so periodicity makes this
definition independent of the representative. Direct substitution gives

  descend(lift(f))=f,
  lift(descend(g))=g.                                      (ID16.1)

On any quotient chart of side length less than one, q is a translation
of Euclidean coordinates. Thus smoothness and all coordinate derivative
identities transport in both directions, including

  partial_j lift(f)=lift(partial_j f),
  div lift(f)=lift(div f), Delta lift(f)=lift(Delta f),
  partial_t lift(f)=lift(partial_t f).                     (ID16.2)

The probability Haar measure on the quotient is the pushforward of
Lebesgue measure on [0,1)^3. Consequently, for integrable f,

  int_Omega f dx=int_[0,1)^3 lift(f)(x) dx.                 (ID16.3)

The integral is unchanged by replacing the half-open cube with the
source unitCube=[0,1]^3: their difference is contained in finitely many
coordinate faces, each of measure zero by one-dimensional singleton
measure zero and Fubini. This proves the exact measure normalization,
not merely an equality up to a geometric constant. It also identifies
the source actual Fourier integrals with the quotient Fourier coefficients.

Define the fixed-mean Galilean maps

  G_m u(t,x)=u(t,x+mt)-m,
  G_m p(t,x)=p(t,x+mt).

Their inverse is G_{-m}. For v=G_m u and q_m=G_m p,

  v_t=(u_t+m dot grad u)(t,x+mt),
  B(v,v)=((u-m) dot grad u)(t,x+mt),
  v_t+B(v,v)=(u_t+B(u,u))(t,x+mt),
  Delta v=(Delta u)(t,x+mt),
  grad q_m=(grad p)(t,x+mt).                               (ID16.4)

Therefore G_m carries the exact NSE equation to itself and preserves
the pressure gauge. If m=mean(u0), ID11 gives mean(v(t))=0 for all t,
and v(0)=u0-m. No requirement mean(u0)=0 is imposed on the original root.

For the identity-normalized lifts, direct differentiation gives

  eta_v(t,a)=eta_u(t,a)-mt,
  V_v=V_u-m, F_v=F_u, A_v=A_u,
  pi_v(t,a)=q_m(t,eta_v(t,a))=pi_u(t,a).                   (ID16.5)

The two maps have the same initial configuration and the appropriately
shifted initial velocity. Since translation preserves volume,

  E(G_m u)=E(u)-m dot mean(u)+|m|^2/2,
  ||D(G_m u)||_2=||D u||_2.                               (ID16.6)

For m=mean(u), the energy identity becomes E(G_m u)=E(u)-|m|^2/2.

The source normalization is now exact. For the source periodic lift a,

  physicalEnergy(a)=int_unitCube |a|^2=2 E(descend(a)),
  physicalDissipation(a)
    =sum_j int_unitCube |coordinateDerivative a j|^2
    =||D(descend(a))||_2^2.                                (ID16.7)

For a finite real Fourier synthesis, M38 and (ID13.7) similarly give
  coefficientEnergy N c=physicalEnergy(finiteSynthesis N c)
                        =2 E(finiteSynthesis N c).
Its viscous dissipation normalization is unchanged by this factor 1/2
on energy: multiplying the source energy identity by 1/2 gives exactly
E(t)+nu int_0^t||Du||_2^2=E(0).

SOURCE INSTANTIATION.
  ML-I01: d=Fin 3, a=0, unit period, the actual scalar/vector component

  ML-I02: apply to torus translations x -> x+mt, which preserve Haar

  M45/ML-F03: for every actual continuous periodic field a and component

  ML-O08/ML-O09: fixed-time affine translation and the time curve x+mt

At t=T choose a neighborhood lying strictly above 0. On that neighborhood,
  Icc(0,T) and Iic(T) agree.
Hence, as identities of the totalized within-derivative operators,

  derivWithin f (Icc 0 T) t=derivWithin f (Ici 0) t,
      0<=t<T,
  derivWithin f (Icc 0 T) T=derivWithin f (Iic T) T.         (ID17.1)

For 0<t<T the interval is itself a neighborhood, so the within derivative
equals the ordinary derivative. At T>0, however, Ici(0) is a full
neighborhood. It does not encode the final-time one-sided derivative.
No equality with that operator at T is inferred from finite-slab data.

EXPLICIT LOCAL EXTENSION FOR ALL-POSITIVE-TIME SOURCE TESTS.
Fix t0 in (0,T), and choose
  0<a0<a1<t0<b1<b0<T.
Set
  g(s)=0 for s<=0 and g(s)=exp(-1/s) for s>0,
  S(s)=g(s)/(g(s)+g(1-s)),
  chi(t)=S((t-a0)/(a1-a0)) S((b0-t)/(b0-b1)).

The denominator is strictly positive for every real s. Every derivative
of g on s>0 is a finite polynomial in 1/s times exp(-1/s); it tends to
zero at s=0. Thus g, S and chi are smooth; chi=0 outside [a0,b0] and
chi=1 on [a1,b1]. Define the total field

  f_tilde(t,x)=chi(t)f(t,x) for 0<t<T,
  f_tilde(t,x)=0 otherwise.                                (ID17.2)

It is jointly smooth on all real times, since it vanishes on neighborhoods
of 0 and T. Its spatial periodicity is inherited from f. If div f=0,
then div f_tilde=chi div f=0. Its actual time derivative is

  d_tilde=chi' f+chi f_t on (0,T), zero outside,
  partial_t f_tilde=d_tilde,
  f_tilde=f, d_tilde=f_t on (a1,b1) x Omega.               (ID17.3)

This supplies the actual global positive-time test-field premises of
M26/M27, and the actual joint-continuity/derivative premises of M28/M33.
It is not an extension preserving the NSE equation; no such property
is required by those four general differentiation endpoints.

Apply M28 at t0 to f_tilde,d_tilde. In source normalization it yields

  d_t physicalEnergy(f_tilde(t))|t0
    =2 physicalFieldInner(f_tilde(t0),d_tilde(t0)).

The scalar energy functions agree on a neighborhood of t0, and their
values agree at t0. Locality and (ID17.3) therefore give

  d_t physicalEnergy(f(t))|t0
    =2 int_Omega f(t0,x) dot f_t(t0,x) dx.                 (ID17.4)

The identical argument using M33 gives, for a real scalar f,

  d_t int_Omega f(t,x)dx|t0=int_Omega f_t(t0,x)dx.          (ID17.5)

Thus source statements with all-positive-time test premises compose
with actual finite-slab data through a proved local construction.
The all-positive-time NSE hypotheses in M12/M13 are not supplied by
(ID17.2); those endpoints cannot be substituted into this local argument.

ENDPOINT DERIVATIVES.
At t=0 or T, with h restricted to the slab, the identity

  [f(t+h,x)-f(t,x)]/h-f_t(t,x)
    =int_0^1 [f_t(t+theta h,x)-f_t(t,x)]dtheta

has a remainder tending uniformly to zero on Omega. Spatial integration
proves the one-sided versions of (ID17.4)--(ID17.5); the squared-norm
version also follows from ID11.1. UniqueDiffWithinAt on the appropriate
nondegenerate interval identifies each supplied derivative with Lean's
totalized derivWithin value. No solution beyond T is invoked.

SOURCE INSTANTIATION.
  ML-T02: the two explicitly proved set germ equalities in (ID17.1).
  ML-T01: neighborhood membership only at strict interior points, or
    for Ici(0) at T when explaining its different two-sided meaning.
  ML-T03/ML-T04: f_tilde=f on a genuine neighborhood of t0, with equality
    also at t0; use these to transfer within derivatives, then the
    neighborhood identification for ordinary derivatives.
  ML-T05/ML-T06: T>0 gives unique differentiability of Icc(0,T);
    ML-T07/ML-T08 supply the relevant right/left half-line instances.
  M26/M27: instantiate their global positive-time solenoidal test with
    the actual f_tilde when f is solenoidal. No zero-mean premise is added.
  M28/M33: supply f_tilde,d_tilde and their explicit global joint
    continuity and derivative identity (ID17.3), then use locality.
  ML-K02: alternatively differentiate the restricted compact spatial
    integral at interior times using the uniform derivative majorant.
  ML-K01: one-sided finite-time primitives require their actual
    FTCFilter and continuity-within premises. ML-R01 applies at ordinary
    interior points; ML-R02 integrates on the closed interval using
    continuity there and derivatives only on its interior.

COMPOSITION.
  Finite-slab smooth field -> (ID17.2)--(ID17.3) -> source differentiation
  at t0 -> germ identity -> (ID17.4)--(ID17.5); direct uniform remainder
  -> endpoints. ID26 supplies the separate operator-level set-germ proof
  in the transported-operator chain.

46.0. Common exact data and representations

Fix the unit-volume torus \(\Omega=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3\) and
\(\mathcal H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)\), as a real Hilbert space.
Time-dependent statements have \(T>0\), \(I=[0,T]\); viscous statements
have \(\nu>0\). Smooth data retain the root endpoint convention.
Define
\[
 \mathcal H_\sigma=\{f\in\mathcal H:\operatorname{div}f=0
                                  \text{ in distributions}\},
 \quad \mathcal H_{\sigma,0}=\{f\in\mathcal H_\sigma:\bar f=0\}.
\]
For actual componentwise complexified Fourier coefficients,
\[
 \widehat f(k)=\int_\Omega f(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x}\,dx,\quad
 P_0=I_3,\quad P_k=I_3-\frac{k\otimes k}{|k|^2}\ (k\ne0),\quad Q=I-P.
\]
Thus \(\widehat f(0)=\bar f\); constants are retained.

SOURCE REPRESENTATION.
The Mathlib torus is UnitAddTorus (Fin 3) with its product probability
measure. Methlib uses periodic fields on Vec=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3).
ML-I01 identifies the torus integral with the product cell (0,1]^3.
The Methlib unitCube is [0,1]^3 in Vec; C28's null-face and Euclidean
coordinate identification equates those two cell integrals. ML-F01/F02 at k=0
identify the mean; ML-F07 on each complexified component and ML-H04 give
\[
 \|f\|_2^2=\sum_k|\widehat f(k)|^2,\qquad
 \langle f,g\rangle=\int_\Omega f\cdot g.
\]
C06/C24 supply actual field/Fourier identification, including reality.

For fixed smooth volume-preserving \(\eta\), define
\[
 U_\eta f=f\circ\eta,\quad U_\eta^{-1}H=H\circ\eta^{-1},\quad
 \mathcal S_\eta=U_\eta\mathcal H_\sigma,\quad
 P_\eta=U_\eta P U_\eta^{-1},\quad Q_\eta=I-P_\eta.
\]
C19 gives both inverse laws and the norm equality.
Measure preservation makes pullback respect almost-everywhere equality;
measurability of eta and eta_inverse makes both maps well-defined on L2
classes. The inverse and norm equalities are therefore identities of
Hilbert-space elements, as well as of their smooth representatives.
In ML-S08,
\(f=U_\eta\), \(g=U_{\eta^{-1}}\), and both scalar homomorphisms are
the identity on \(\mathbb R\); its h1,h2 are exactly these inverse laws.
This constructs the real linear isometric equivalence.
ML-N09 with p=H_sigma and f=U_eta gives the orthogonal projection P_eta
onto the closed S_eta. ML-N13 gives U_eta*=U_eta_inverse.
The mean and every constant vector field are preserved.
General positive Jacobian requires the weighted measure in ID24.

QUANTIFIED_INPUT.
For every \(u\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)\) with div u=0, define
\(D_uf=(u\cdot\nabla)f\) on smooth fields,
\(M_uf=(D_xu)f\) on \(\mathcal H\), and
\(b=\|D_xu\|_{L^\infty,\mathrm{op}}\).

DERIVED_IDENTITY.
\[
 [D_u,P]f=K_uf\quad(f\in C^\infty),\qquad
 K_u=QM_uP+PM_u^*Q\in\mathcal L(\mathcal H),                \tag{ID18.1}
\]
\[
 M_u^*f=(D_xu)^{\mathsf T}f,\qquad K_u^*=K_u,\qquad
 \|K_u\|\le b,\qquad K_uc=0\text{ for every constant }c.    \tag{ID18.2}
\]

DERIVATION.
The pointwise matrix estimate gives
\(\|M_uf\|_2^2\le b^2\|f\|_2^2\).
Multiplication by the smooth matrix D_xu preserves measurable
representatives and almost-everywhere equality; this inequality proves
membership in L2. Pointwise linearity therefore defines an actual
bounded linear operator on the L2 quotient.
Integration of
\(((D_xu)f)\cdot g=f\cdot((D_xu)^{\mathsf T}g)\)
identifies the adjoint and gives its same bound.
For smooth divergence-free h,
\[
 \operatorname{div}(D_uh)
 =(\partial_i u_j)(\partial_jh_i)
 =\operatorname{div}((D_xu)h).
\]
The omitted terms are
\(u_j\partial_j\operatorname{div}h\) and
\(h_j\partial_j\operatorname{div}u\), both zero. Hence
\(QD_uP=QM_uP\).
Every smooth Qf is an actual periodic gradient by C06/C24. For scalar phi,
\[
 D_u\nabla\phi=\nabla(D_u\phi)-(D_xu)^{\mathsf T}\nabla\phi,
\]
so \(PD_uQ=-PM_u^*Q\). Expansion with \(P+Q=I\) proves (ID18.1).

The two outputs \(QM_uPf\) and \(PM_u^*Qf\) are orthogonal. Therefore
\[
 \|K_uf\|_2^2
 \le b^2(\|Pf\|_2^2+\|Qf\|_2^2)=b^2\|f\|_2^2.
\]
Reversing composition under adjoints proves \(K_u^*=K_u\).
Smooth Fourier polynomials are dense; this is the unique bounded
extension of the core commutator. For constant c, Pc=c and D_uc=0,
so the core identity gives K_uc=0.

ENDPOINT_SPECIALIZATION.
  ML-N05/ML-N07/ML-N12:
    scalar=ℝ, E=H, submodule=H_sigma;
    outputs Q=I−P, norm Pythagoras, and projection self-adjointness.
  ML-H04:
    vectors M_u f,g and f,M_u^*g; the actual integral pairing identifies
    the transpose multiplication operator as the adjoint.
  ML-N10:
    compositions Q∘(M_u∘P) and P∘(M_u^*∘Q);
    outputs their mutually adjoint off-diagonal terms.
  ML-N11: bounded input A=K_u; A*=A was proved above.
  ML-N14: f=K_u, M=b≥0, with the all-vector norm inequality.
  M29: k arbitrary and v=f_hat(k); output k·P_k f_hat(k)=0.
  M30: c(k)=P_k f_hat(k); smooth f gives rapid component moments,
    bounded symbols preserve them, and actual synthesis is Pf.
  M06/M07: the actual f_hat family gives f+grad(p_f)=Pf;
    thus Qf=−grad(p_f), with the required sign and zero mode.
MATHEMATICAL_EDGE = completed; D_u is not claimed bounded on all L2.

QUANTIFIED_INPUT.
For every smooth volume-preserving path eta on I, set

 U_t=U_{\eta(t)},\quad P_t=U_tPU_t^{-1},\quad Q_t=I-P_t,

 \quad \mathsf M_tH=B_tH,\quad b(t)=\|D_xu(t)\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Volume preservation gives div u=0; ID18 applies.

DERIVED_IDENTITY.
In the fixed material bounded-operator space,
\[
 \dot P_t=\mathsf K_t
 =Q_t\mathsf M_tP_t+P_t\mathsf M_t^*Q_t
 =U_tK_{u(t)}U_t^{-1},                                    \tag{ID19.1}
\]
\[
 P_t-P_s=\int_s^t\mathsf K_r\,dr,\quad
 \|P_t-P_s\|\le\min\{1,\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\}
                              \quad(0\le s\le t\le T),    \tag{ID19.2}
\]
\[
 P_t\dot P_tP_t=0,\quad Q_t\dot P_tQ_t=0,\quad
 \dot P_t=Q_t\dot P_tP_t+P_t\dot P_tQ_t.                    \tag{ID19.3}
\]
For every C1 Hilbert-valued tangent curve H(t), P_tH(t)=H(t),
\[
 Q_t\dot H(t)=\dot P_tH(t).                                \tag{ID19.4}
\]
Derivatives are in operator norm, with one-sided values at 0,T.

DERIVATION.
For fixed smooth material H, g(t)=U_t^{-1}H has g_t=−D_ug by the
material chain rule. Consequently
\(\partial_t(P_tH)=U_t(D_uP-PD_u)g=\mathsf K_tH\).
Integrating this L2 identity on the smooth core and using ID18 gives
\(\|(P_t-P_s)H\|\le(\int_s^tb)\|H\|\).
Density extends this inequality to all H, so P_t is norm continuous.
Compact-slab smoothness gives
\[
 \|\mathsf M_t-\mathsf M_s\|
 \le\sup_a\|B_t(a)-B_s(a)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The displayed polynomial formula now makes K_t norm continuous.
Its Bochner integral exists in L(H); equality on the dense core proves
the operator identity in (ID19.2). For admissible nonzero h,
\[
 \left\|\frac{P_{t+h}-P_t}{h}-\mathsf K_t\right\|
 \le\sup_{r\text{ between }t,t+h}\|\mathsf K_r-\mathsf K_t\|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
This also proves the endpoint derivatives directly.
ID18 and conjugation give \((\dot P_t)^*=\dot P_t\),
\(\|\dot P_t\|\le b(t)\), and \(\dot P_tc=0\) for constants.

The bounded-operator product rule applied to \(P_t^2=P_t\) gives
\(\dot P_tP_t+P_t\dot P_t=\dot P_t\); multiplication by P_t and Q_t
gives (ID19.3). Differentiating P_tH=H gives (ID19.4).
For orthogonal projections P1,P2,
\[
 P_1-P_2=P_1(I-P_2)-(I-P_1)P_2.
\]
The outputs are orthogonal and their squared norms are bounded by
\(\|(I-P_2)x\|^2,\|P_2x\|^2\); therefore \(\|P_1-P_2\|\le1\).
This completes (ID19.2).

QUANTIFIED_INPUT.
Fix a smooth volume-preserving eta and smooth H,K in S_eta, with
h=U_eta_inverse H, k=U_eta_inverse K. For along-path identities use
ID19 and smooth tangent curves H(t),K(t).

DERIVED_IDENTITY.
\[
 \mathcal B_\eta(H,K)=U_\eta Q((h\cdot\nabla)k)
    =\mathcal B_\eta(K,H)\in\operatorname{range}(Q_\eta),   \tag{ID20.1}
\]
\[
 \|\mathcal B_\eta(H,K)\|_2
 \le\min\{\|Dk\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}\|h\|_2,\,
          \|Dh\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}\|k\|_2\}.             \tag{ID20.2}
\]
With \(\nabla_t^\eta H=P_t\dot H\),
\[
 \dot H=\nabla_t^\eta H+\mathcal B_\eta(V,H),\quad
 \nabla_t^\eta H=U_t(h_t+P((u\cdot\nabla)h)),               \tag{ID20.3}
\]
\[
 \frac d{dt}\langle H,K\rangle
 =\langle\nabla_t^\eta H,K\rangle+
    \langle H,\nabla_t^\eta K\rangle.                      \tag{ID20.4}
\]
For eta(0)=id, V(0)=u0, div u0=0, the root equation for
u=V∘eta_inverse and its unique normalized pressure is equivalent to
\[
 \nabla_t^\eta V=-\nu\mathcal A_{\eta(t)}V.                 \tag{ID20.5}
\]
On smooth tangent fields Acal_eta=−Delta_eta; its domain is ID21.

DERIVATION.
The divergence of (h·grad)k−(k·grad)h vanishes: terms containing div h
or div k vanish, and the first-derivative products cancel after index
exchange. Applying Q proves symmetry. Image and tame estimates follow
from PQ=0, contraction of Q, and unitarity of U_eta.
For H=U_th, the chain rule gives
\(\dot H=U_t(h_t+(u\cdot\nabla)h)\).
Since div h_t=0, its normal part is B_eta(V,H), also equal to dot P_tH
by ID19. This proves (ID20.3).
The Hilbert product rule and self-adjointness of P_t, which fixes H,K,
give (ID20.4), and \(\nabla_t^\eta(fH)=f'H+f\nabla_t^\eta H\).

Projecting the material NSE gives (ID20.5). Conversely, (ID20.3) and
Delta_eta V=U_t Delta u turn (ID20.5) into
\(u_t+P((u\cdot\nabla)u)=\nu\Delta u\).
For c=(u·grad)u take
\[
 \widehat p(0)=0,\qquad
 \widehat p(k)=\frac{i\,k\cdot\widehat c(k)}{2\pi|k|^2}.
\]
C06/C24 give the actual smooth scalar with grad p=−Qc. Adding the
gradient recovers the root equation and normalized pressure.
C01/C04 give both inverse flow/reconstruction identities. Moreover
\[
 \dot P_tV=\mathcal B_\eta(V,V)
       =-\operatorname{grad}_\eta(p\circ\eta),\qquad
 \dot V=-\nu\mathcal A_\eta V+\dot P_tV.                    \tag{ID20.6}
\]
The normal pressure force has zero pairing with V, and
\[
 \frac12\partial_t\|V\|_2^2
   =-\nu\langle V,\mathcal A_\eta V\rangle
   =-\nu\|D_aV(D_a\eta)^{-1}\|_2^2.
\]

 =\{f\in\mathcal H_\sigma:\sum_j\kappa_j^2|c_j|^2<\infty\}

                  \subset\mathcal S_\eta\to\mathcal S_\eta,\qquad

QUANTIFIED_INPUT.

Neither volume preservation nor solenoidality is assumed here. Set
\[
 F=D_a\eta,\ A=F^{-1},\ J=\det F>0,\ V=\eta_t,\quad

\[
 \operatorname{grad}_\eta\pi=A^{\mathsf T}\nabla_a\pi,\qquad

DERIVED_INTERFACE.
\[
 U_\eta:\mathcal H_x\simeq L^2(\Omega,\mu_\eta;\mathbb R^3)
       \quad\text{is a real linear isometric equivalence}, \tag{ID24.1}

 D_aVA=(D_xu)\circ\eta,\quad V_t=U_\eta(u_t+c),\quad
 \Delta_\eta^JH=U_\eta\Delta(U_\eta^{-1}H),                 \tag{ID24.2}

DERIVATION.
The actual change of variables for a positive-Jacobian diffeomorphism is
\[
 \int f(x)\,dx=\int f(\eta(a))J(a)\,da.
\]
Applied to squared norms/pairings and combined with eta_inverse, it
gives the isometry and both inverse laws. Projection orthogonality
follows by isometric conjugation with these measures.

The two chain rules give the first two identities in (ID24.2).
The general Piola identity of C02 is
\[
 \partial_{a_\alpha}(JA_{\alpha i})=0.
\]
Its explicit cofactor formula is
\[
 JA_{\alpha i}
   =\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{\alpha\beta\gamma}
                                      F_{j\beta}F_{k\gamma}.
\]
Differentiation cancels each second derivative against the alternating
tensor in its two symmetric material indices. Therefore, for smooth z,
\[
 J^{-1}\partial_{a_\alpha}
       (JA_{\alpha i}(z_i\circ\eta))
          =(\operatorname{div}_xz)\circ\eta.
\]
Apply this to z=grad_x(U_eta_inverse H)_i componentwise, using
\((\nabla_x(U_\eta^{-1}H)_i)\circ\eta
 =A^{\mathsf T}\nabla_aH_i\). This proves the Laplacian identity with
the stated row-divergence convention.
It also gives, for smooth periodic H,K,
\[
 \int H\cdot\Delta_\eta^JK\,J\,da
   =-\int(D_aHA):(D_aKA)\,J\,da,
\]
by periodic integration by parts.

Substitution into the left side of (ID24.3) gives
\(U_\eta(u_t+c)=U_\eta(\nu\Delta u+Qc)\).
Invertibility of U_eta and c−Qc=Pc prove both directions.
Also \(U_\eta c=D_aVA\,V\), so the extended material equation equals
\(V_t=\nu\Delta_\eta^JV+Q_\eta(D_aVA\,V)\).

For this arbitrary smooth c, define
\[
 \widehat p(0)=0,\quad
 \widehat p(k)=\frac{i\,k\cdot\widehat c(k)}{2\pi|k|^2}
                                  \quad(k\ne0),\qquad \pi=p\circ\eta.
\]
Uniform rapid decay after every time derivative constructs the actual
smooth pressure. Multiplication by 2*pi*i*k proves grad p=−Qc.
Consequently
\[
 U_\eta\nabla p=\operatorname{grad}_\eta\pi,\qquad
 \int\pi J\,da=0,                                        \tag{ID24.4}
\]
and the extended equation also reads
\(V_t=-\operatorname{grad}_\eta\pi+\nu\Delta_\eta^JV\).
Before constraint propagation, the gauge and Hilbert identities retain J da.

QUANTIFIED_INPUT.
Let T>0, I=[0,T], E a real normed vector space, and f:ℝ→E any total
extension of a function on I. Derivative-value identification uses
actual HasDerivWithinAt evidence; the set-germ equalities themselves
require no differentiability premise.

DERIVED_INTERFACE.
\[
 \operatorname{derivWithin}f\,I\,t
 =\operatorname{derivWithin}f\,[0,\infty)\,t
                                      \quad(0\le t<T),     \tag{ID26.1}
\]
\[
 \operatorname{derivWithin}f\,I\,t=\operatorname{deriv}f\,t
                                      \quad(0<t<T),        \tag{ID26.2}
\]
\[
 \operatorname{derivWithin}f\,I\,T
 =\operatorname{derivWithin}f\,(-\infty,T]\,T.              \tag{ID26.3}
\]
The operators here are the source totalized derivative operators.
Any two extensions agreeing on I have the same within-I derivative
at every point of I.

DERIVATION.
For 0≤t<T, choose 0<epsilon<T−t. In the epsilon neighborhood of t,
membership in I and [0,infinity) agrees.
For 0<t<T, a radius below min(t,T−t) gives a neighborhood inside I.
At T, any radius below T makes I and (−infinity,T] agree locally.
Set-germ congruence and the neighborhood derivative theorem give
(ID26.1)--(ID26.3).

Agreement on I gives both agreement at t and eventual agreement within I.
Function-germ congruence therefore equates the totalized derivatives,
and transfers actual within-derivative proofs. Since T>0, the interval
is uniquely differentiable at every member; the same holds at the
appropriate half-line endpoints. A supplied derivative proof therefore
identifies the totalized value with the actual derivative.

At T>0, [0,infinity) instead contains a full neighborhood of T.
Its within derivative is the ordinary two-sided derivative of the chosen
extension. For the real extension f(r)=r when r≤T and f(r)=T when r>T,
the finite-interval derivative is 1, while the two-sided derivative
does not exist and the totalized ordinary derivative is 0.
Thus finite data alone do not give equality with a terminal
within-[0,infinity) derivative.

QUANTIFIED_INPUT.
Let P_t be the operator-norm C1 orthogonal projection path of ID19
on the fixed real material Hilbert space H.
For the physical equation suppose the root trajectory of ID20 is given.
Set S_0=range(P_0).

DERIVED_INTERFACE.
With \(\Gamma_t=\dot P_tP_t-P_t\dot P_t\),
\[
 \Gamma_t^*=-\Gamma_t,\quad [\Gamma_t,P_t]=\dot P_t,\quad
 \|\Gamma_t\|=\|\dot P_t\|\le b(t).                         \tag{ID27.1}
\]
A unique norm-C1 family W(t,s) satisfies
\[
 \partial_tW(t,s)=\Gamma_tW(t,s),\quad W(s,s)=I,
\]
\[
 W(t,s)W(s,r)=W(t,r),\quad W(t,s)^{-1}=W(s,t)=W(t,s)^*,\quad
 P_t=W(t,s)P_sW(s,t).                                    \tag{ID27.2}
\]
It fixes every constant field. For W_t=W(t,0), its restriction is
a unitary map S_0→S_eta(t). The actual unbounded operator is
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal A}_t
     =W_t^{-1}\mathcal A_{\eta(t)}W_t
                         \quad\text{on }\mathcal S_0,
\]
\[
 D(\widetilde{\mathcal A}_t)
   =W_t^{-1}U_{\eta(t)}H^2_\sigma
   =\{z\in\mathcal S_0:W_tz\in D(\mathcal A_{\eta(t)})\}.    \tag{ID27.3}
\]
For \(Z=W_t^{-1}V\),
\[
 Z(t)\in D(\widetilde{\mathcal A}_t),\qquad
 Z_t=-\nu\widetilde{\mathcal A}_tZ.                        \tag{ID27.4}
\]

DERIVATION.
Self-adjointness of P_t and dot P_t gives Gamma_t*=−Gamma_t.
The two equations P_t dot P_t P_t=0 and
dot P_t P_t+P_t dot P_t=dot P_t give its commutator.
Relative to the tangent/normal orthogonal decomposition, dot P_t has
two off-diagonal adjoint blocks. Gamma_t changes one sign. Their ranges
are orthogonal, so ||Gamma_t x||=||dot P_t x|| for every x.
This proves its exact norm.

With M=sup_I||Gamma_t||, for t≥s the ordered series
\[
 W(t,s)=I+\sum_{n\ge1}
 \int_{s\le r_n\le\cdots\le r_1\le t}
      \Gamma_{r_1}\cdots\Gamma_{r_n}\,dr_n\cdots dr_1
\]
converges in operator norm; its n-th term has bound
\(M^n|t-s|^n/n!\). Its derivative series is bounded by the corresponding
exponential series and gives W'=Gamma W.
Time reversal constructs it for t<s.
The difference D of two solutions with the same initial value obeys
\(\|D(t)\|\le M\int_s^t\|D(r)\|\,dr\).
Repeated substitution bounds it by its finite interval supremum times
\(M^n|t-s|^n/n!\), which tends to zero. This proves uniqueness.
Applying uniqueness to the composed propagators proves both composition
and inverse identities.

For fixed h,k∈H,
\[
 \partial_t\langle W(t,s)h,W(t,s)k\rangle=0
\]
by skew-adjointness. The initial and inverse identities therefore make
W(t,s) a real unitary operator. The inverse difference identity
\[
 W_{t+h}^{-1}-W_t^{-1}
   =-W_{t+h}^{-1}(W_{t+h}-W_t)W_t^{-1}
\]
gives \((W_t^{-1})'=-W_t^{-1}\Gamma_t\) in operator norm. Consequently
\[
 \partial_t(W_t^{-1}P_tW_t)
  =W_t^{-1}(\dot P_t+P_t\Gamma_t-\Gamma_tP_t)W_t=0,
\]
which proves intertwining.
For constant c, P_tc=c, dot P_tc=0, hence Gamma_tc=0.
Uniqueness gives W_tc=c, and unitarity gives
〈W_tf,c〉=〈f,c〉. Thus means are preserved.

At fixed time, restriction of W_t gives the displayed solenoidal
unitary equivalence. ID21's adjoint-domain calculation with this
equivalence gives
\[
 D(\widetilde{\mathcal A}_t^*)=D(\widetilde{\mathcal A}_t),\qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal A}_t^*=\widetilde{\mathcal A}_t\ge0
                                   \text{ on }\mathcal S_0.
\]
Its domain is dense in S_0, not asserted dense in the full H.
Its orthonormal eigenbasis is \(W_t^{-1}U_{\eta(t)}\phi_j\), with
eigenvalues kappa_j. Constants are its exact kernel; on their
orthogonal complement in S_0, its attained spectral gap is 4*pi².

For physical V, P_tV=V and ID20 gives
\(\dot V=-\nu\mathcal A_\eta V+\dot P_tV\).
ID19 gives \(P_t\dot P_tV=0\), so Gamma_tV=dot P_tV.
The bounded-operator/vector derivative rule yields
\[
 \dot Z=W_t^{-1}(\dot V-\Gamma_tV)
       =-\nu W_t^{-1}\mathcal A_\eta V,
\]
which is (ID27.4) on exactly (ID27.3).
For the conserved mean m,
\[
 \|Z\|_2=\|V\|_2=\|u\|_2,\quad\bar Z=m,\quad
 \tfrac12\partial_t\|Z-m\|_2^2
   =-\nu\langle Z-m,\widetilde{\mathcal A}_t(Z-m)\rangle
   =-\nu\|\nabla_xu\|_2^2.                                \tag{ID27.5}
\]
No common time-independent operator domain is assumed.
W_t and Atilde_t depend on the supplied trajectory. The fixed-eta
semigroup of ID22 has not been substituted for this physical equation.

INPUTS
A stipulated smooth volume-preserving path eta, eta(0)=id,
V=eta_t, V(0)=u0 with div u0=0; F=D_a eta, A=F^{-1},
u=V o eta^{-1}. No NSE equation is initially assumed. Put

r_eta=nu F^T[(Delta u) o eta], and I_eta(t)=integral_0^t r_eta.
The kinematic determinant identity from C03 gives
0=J_t=J(div u) o eta with J=1, hence div u=0 throughout the slab.

DERIVATION
ID28.a. From V=u o eta,
 D_aV=(D_xu o eta)F,  F_t=D_aV,  V_t=(u_t+B(u,u)) o eta.
Componentwise product differentiation yields
 beta_t=(D_aV)^T V+F^TV_t
       =grad_a kappa+r_eta+F^T(g o eta).                    (ID28.1)
For every scalar p and pi=p o eta,
 grad_a pi=F^T[(grad_x p) o eta].                           (ID28.2)

ID28.b. The continuous primitive satisfies (I_eta)_t=r_eta,
I_eta(0)=0. Its spatial derivatives pass through the finite integral:
on each compact set the differentiated integrands are uniformly bounded,
so the difference quotients converge uniformly. Set W=beta-I_eta;
then W(0)=u0 and W_t=grad kappa+F^T(g o eta).

ID28.c. If g=-grad p with mean p=0, volume preservation gives mean pi=0.
Define
 Psi(t)=integral_0^t[kappa-pi-mean(kappa)] ds.
Then mean Psi=0, Psi(0)=0, and integration of (ID28.1) gives
 W=u0+grad_a Psi.                                         (ID28.3)
Conversely (ID28.3) for smooth periodic Psi gives
 F^T(g o eta)=grad_a(Psi_t-kappa).
Set pi=kappa-Psi_t-mean(kappa-Psi_t), p=pi o eta^{-1}.
Multiplication by F^{-T} and (ID28.2) give g=-grad p; both gauges
vanish. Thus (u,p) is the root with the stated initial datum.

ID28.d. On the fixed label torus, P_ref W=u0 iff P_ref(W-u0)=0.
The zero mode is retained, so z=W-u0 has mean zero. For k!=0 set
 Psi_hat(k)=(k.z_hat(k))/(2*pi*i*|k|^2), Psi_hat(0)=0.
P_ref z=0 gives 2*pi*i*k Psi_hat(k)=z_hat(k).
Uniform rapid decay after arbitrary time derivatives gives jointly
smooth Psi, and Fourier uniqueness gives z=grad Psi. This proves the
pressure-free converse. P_ref is not replaced by the moving P_eta.

INPUTS
ID28 kinematics and a closed piecewise-C1 loop with lift alpha:
alpha(1)=alpha(0)+n, n in Z^3. Its transported lift is eta_tilde o alpha.

DERIVATION
ID29.a. The actual circulation is
 C_alpha(t)=integral_0^1 u(t,eta(t,alpha(s))).F(t,alpha(s))alpha'(s) ds
           =integral_0^1 beta(t,alpha(s)).alpha'(s) ds.      (ID29.1)
Integer changes of lift leave this value unchanged by periodicity.
The transported endpoints differ by n, so winding is preserved.

ID29.b. Work separately on each C1 segment. At an interior t0, choose
a compact time neighborhood contained in (0,T). Uniform boundedness of
beta_t gives the integrable majorant C|alpha'(s)|. Therefore
 C_alpha'(t)=integral_0^1 beta_t(t,alpha(s)).alpha'(s) ds.
At either endpoint the error of the one-sided difference quotient is
bounded by
 ||[beta(t+h)-beta(t)]/h-beta_t(t)||_infinity
       integral_0^1 |alpha'(s)| ds ->0.
Summing the finitely many segments proves the same derivative identity.

ID29.c. For every periodic scalar psi, the one-dimensional chain rule
and segment FTC give
 integral_0^1 grad psi(alpha).alpha' ds
   =psi(alpha(1))-psi(alpha(0))=0.
This applies to kappa and to pi, including nonzero winding.

ID29.d. Substitute ID28.1 with g=-grad p:
 C_alpha'(t)=integral r_eta(t,alpha).alpha' ds
           =nu oint_{eta(t)alpha} Delta u(t).dx.
Finite-interval FTC gives the exact viscous circulation difference.
For z=beta-I_eta-u0 its defect is precisely oint_alpha z.da.
Thus all-loop balance is equivalent to vanishing of every period of z;
ID30 supplies the converse and its harmonic condition.

INPUTS
A jointly smooth periodic coefficient one-form b(t,x). For the mechanical
application use z=beta-I_eta-u0 and g from ID28.

DERIVATION
ID30.a. A small coordinate rectangle has contractible boundary.
Its period equals the double integral of partial_i b_j-partial_j b_i,
by FTC on the four sides. If all such periods vanish, divide by the
rectangle area and shrink it. Continuity gives db=0.

ID30.b. For a closed b on R^3 define the signed-coordinate primitive
 phi(x)=integral_0^{x1} b1(s,0,0)ds
       +integral_0^{x2} b2(x1,s,0)ds
       +integral_0^{x3} b3(x1,x2,s)ds.
Using partial_i b_j=partial_j b_i, its three differentiated expressions
telescope to partial_i phi=b_i. For example partial_1 phi is
 b1(x1,0,0)+[b1(x1,x2,0)-b1(x1,0,0)]
            +[b1(x)-b1(x1,x2,0)]=b1(x).
Every phi(x+n)-phi(x) has zero gradient and hence is constant in x.

ID30.c. These constants add in n. Set h_j=phi(e_j)-phi(0).
Then phi(x+n)-phi(x)=h.n and psi=phi-h.x is periodic.
Normalize mean psi=0. Integrating b=h+grad psi over the unit cube gives
 h=mean b, since all periodic derivative integrals vanish.
The construction is jointly smooth in t: every parameter integral and
its derivatives have uniform bounds on the compact parameter domains.

ID30.d. A loop of winding n has period h.n. Thus:
 all periods zero <=> db=0 and h=0
                  <=> b=grad psi with periodic mean-zero psi.
Contractible periods alone impose db=0. The three coordinate generator
periods determine h exactly. Uniqueness follows by taking means and
then applying derivative-zero constancy to the primitive difference.

ID30.e. Assume only contractible Kelvin balance. Then dz=0, hence dz_t=0.
The component identity
 d_a[F^T(f o eta)]=F^T[(d_xf) o eta]F
follows by product differentiation: the second derivatives of eta
cancel in antisymmetrization. ID28 gives dg=0, since F is invertible.
Apply the preceding decomposition in Eulerian coordinates:
 g=c(t)+grad chi, c=mean g.
Because div u=0,
 mean B(u,u)=mean Delta u=0, so c=d_t mean u.
For the canonical lift eta=a+xi,
 F^T c=c+grad_a(c.xi).
Hence
 z_t=c+grad_a[kappa+c.xi+chi o eta].
Taking the label mean and integrating z(0)=0 yields
 mean_a z(t)=mean_x u(t)-mean_x u(0).                       (ID30.1)
This is a statement about the complete Weber defect, not mean(F^TV).

ID30.f. All-loop Kelvin balance gives z=grad Psi and ID28 gives NSE.
Contractible balance plus conserved mean gives c=0, hence
g=grad chi=-grad p with p=-chi normalized. Conversely NSE gives both.
If u(t,x)=c(t), then eta=a+integral c, beta=c(t), r_eta=0.
Contractible periods and vorticity identities hold for every c(t), but
periodic-pressure NSE requires c'=0. This proves necessity of the
harmonic/mean condition in the stated converse.

DERIVATION
ID31.a. Define curl f=(partial_2 f3-partial_3 f2,
partial_3 f1-partial_1 f3,partial_1 f2-partial_2 f1).
Mixed partials give div omega=0 and curl Delta u=Delta omega.
Expansion of the three components gives
 curl B(u,u)=B(u,omega)-B(omega,u)
under div u=0. Thus
 curl g=omega_t+B(u,omega)-B(omega,u)-nu Delta omega.        (ID31.1)

ID31.b. Differentiate AF=I and F_t=(D_xu o eta)F:
 A_t=-A(D_xu o eta).
The chain rule then gives the off-equation identity
 d_t[A(omega o eta)]
   =A[(curl g+nu Delta omega) o eta].                      (ID31.2)

ID31.c. Therefore curl g=0 iff the following differential and integrated
identities hold:
 d_t[A(omega o eta)]=nu A[(Delta omega) o eta],
 A(t)(omega(t) o eta(t))
   =omega0+nu integral_0^t A(s)[Delta omega(s) o eta(s)] ds. (ID31.3)
The initial value is A(0)=I. Multiplication by F(t) gives the viscous
Cauchy formula for omega(t) o eta(t); every historical A(s) remains
inside the integral.

ID31.d. Before setting J=1, antisymmetrized product differentiation gives
 d_a[F^T(f o eta)]=F^T[(d_xf) o eta]F.
For arbitrary columns v,w,
 (Fv) cross (Fw)=J F^{-T}(v cross w):
pair with Fz, convert the scalar triple products into determinants,
use det(F[z,v,w])=det F det[z,v,w], and use invertibility.
Consequently
 curl_a[F^T(f o eta)]=J A[(curl_x f) o eta].                (ID31.4)
Only now substitute J=1. For f=u and f=nu Delta u this gives
curl_a beta=A(omega o eta) and
curl_a r_eta=nu A[(Delta omega) o eta].
Thus (ID31.3) is equivalent to curl_a z=0, hence to the contractible
Kelvin identities of ID30.

ID31.e. By ID30, curl g=0 plus conserved Eulerian mean implies
g=-grad p with unique normalized pressure. The converse is immediate.
The viscosity integral in (ID31.3) is retained; no inviscid invariant
is substituted.

INPUTS
A supplied root (u,p) and a supplied v from ID32 on the common finite slab.
Write w=u-v, q=q(v), m=mean w, z=w-m, and r=residual(v).

DERIVATION
ID33.a. Bilinearity gives
 w_t+B(u,w)+B(w,v)+grad(p-q)-nu Delta w=-r.
For Y_w=||w||_2^2 and G_w=||Dw||_2,
 (1/2)Y_w'+nu G_w^2=-integral w^T S_v w-<r,w>.             (ID33.1)
Indeed integral w.B(u,w)=0 by div u=0; the pressure pairing vanishes,
the skew part of Dv has zero quadratic form, and the Laplacian pairing
is -G_w^2.

ID33.b. Set a_v(t)=max_{x,|xi|=1}[-xi^T S_v(t,x)xi].
Compactness gives attainment; trace S_v=0 implies a_v>=0.
Also |a_v(t)-a_v(s)|<=||S_v(t)-S_v(s)||_infinity,op.
Thus a_v is finite continuous and -integral y^T S_v y<=a_v||y||_2^2.

ID33.c. Dropping viscosity in (ID33.1) gives
 (1/2)Y_w'<=a_v Y_w+||r||_2 sqrt(Y_w).
The scalar argument in ID33.e--f below with alpha=a_v and beta=||r||_2
yields the arbitrary-mean comparison
 ||w(t)||_2<=exp(integral_s^t a_v)||w(s)||_2
       +integral_s^t exp(integral_tau^t a_v)||r(tau)||_2 dtau.

ID33.d. ID32.2 gives m'=-mean r and
m(t)=m(s)-integral_s^t mean r. Define
 f=r-mean r+B(m,v).
Then mean f=div f=0 and
 z_t+B(u,z)+B(z,v)+grad(p-q)-nu Delta z=-f.
For Y=||z||_2^2, G=||Dz||_2, beta=||f||_2,
 (1/2)Y'+nu G^2=-integral z^T S_v z-<f,z>.
Since mean z=0, Parseval gives G^2>=lambda_1 Y. Hence
 (1/2)Y'<=alpha Y+beta sqrt(Y), alpha=a_v-nu lambda_1.       (ID33.2)

ID33.e. For epsilon>0 put y_epsilon=sqrt(Y+epsilon^2)>0.
Actual differentiation and (ID33.2) give
 y_epsilon'<=alpha y_epsilon+beta+epsilon|alpha|.            (ID33.3)
The final term follows from
-alpha epsilon^2/y_epsilon<=epsilon|alpha|.
It is retained when alpha<0. No division by sqrt Y is performed.

ID33.f. Put E_alpha(t,s)=exp(integral_s^t alpha).
Multiply (ID33.3) by exp(-integral_s^t alpha), apply finite-interval FTC
to its derivative majorant, and multiply back:
 y_epsilon(t)<=E_alpha(t,s)y_epsilon(s)
    +integral_s^t E_alpha(t,tau)[beta(tau)+epsilon|alpha(tau)|]dtau.
Because 0<=y_epsilon-sqrt Y<=epsilon, and the extra integral is at most
epsilon(t-s)exp((t-s)||alpha||_infinity)||alpha||_infinity,
epsilon->0 proves

                +integral_s^t E_alpha(t,tau)beta(tau)dtau. (ID33.4)
At s=0 call this right side mathcalB(t). Orthogonality to constants gives
 ||u-v||_2^2=|m|^2+||z||_2^2<=|m|^2+mathcalB^2.
The mean-zero gap applies to the full error only if m(0)=0 and mean r=0.
If r=0 and v(0)=u0, both terms vanish, proving root uniqueness.

ID33.g. For the mean-zero f define

Weighted Parseval/Cauchy--Schwarz gives |<f,z>|<=beta_minus1 G.
For 0<theta<=1,

Completion of the square proves this coefficient is sharp for the
specified absorption. Thus

With alpha_theta=a_v-(1-theta)nu lambda_1, integrate to obtain

  +(2theta nu)^(-1)integral_s^t
       exp(2 integral_tau^t alpha_theta)beta_minus1(tau)^2 dtau. (ID33.5)
The retained dissipation is exactly 2(1-theta)nu; theta=1 removes it.

 ||p-q||_{dot H^-2}<=C_Omega||T||_1
   <=C_Omega(||a||_2+||b||_2)||z||_2

This is a weighted coefficient estimate, not an L1 bound for the

Membership in E_nu(u0;T) ALSO requires Pi_Nu0=u0.

The composition rule is ordinary specialization and implication:
