theorem infiniteTransportPressure_coeff (b : FourierCoeff)
    (hb : ∀ i : Fin 3, RapidScalarFourier (fun k => b k i))
    (hreal : SpectralReality b) (k : Frequency) :
    (∫ x in unitCube, star (fourierCharacter k x) * (infiniteTransportPressure b x : ℂ)) =
      infinitePressureCoefficient b k

ROLE:
C62 / ID46: exact scalar Fourier coefficient of the actual normalized
pressure, including its zero mode, for polarization and quadratic remainder.
C63 / ID47: identification of the nonlinear ansatz pressure
p+epsilon q+epsilon^2 p[z].

EXACT_SPECIALIZATION:
For solenoidal smooth a,b define
c=(B(a,b)+B(b,a))/2 and use its actual FourierCoeff array.
Rapid moments follow from the actual compact-slab smooth bounds in
ID07, and SpectralReality from conjugating the Fourier integrals.
The derivative/tensor identities give
div c=partial_i partial_j(a_i b_j).
The source coefficient
infinitePressureCoefficient c_hat k=pressureFromTransport k(c_hat k)
therefore equals -(k_i k_j/|k|^2)(a_i b_j)_hat(k) for k!=0,
and equals zero for k=0.
M07--M09 retain actual recovery, spatial smoothness, and normalized gauge;
M10 gives actual-field uniqueness. Joint temporal smoothness is the
uniform Fourier adapter already proved in ID07, not a conclusion of M50.

REMAINING_LEAN_ADAPTER:
Retain hb and hreal and construct the actual smooth mixed transport c.
Transfer the cube integral through the established normalized quotient
measure identification. No global-time solution, Galerkin budget, or
AX6 premise is present or supplied by this theorem.

53. REFINEMENT COMPOSITION, EXACT SCOPE, AND EXTERNAL LEAN INTERFACES

53.1. Immutable root and additional quantified conclusions

The root remains C11, with exactly the data and predicates of Sections 0--2:
  nu>0, 0<T<infinity, u0 smooth and solenoidal on the unit-volume T^3;
  arbitrary initial velocity mean; zero spatial pressure mean;
  E_nu(u0;T)=N_nu(u0;T),
  E_nu(u0;T) ~= M_nu(u0;T) ~= D_nu(u0;T),
  E_nu(u0;T) ~= V_nu(u0;T).

Sections 49--51 derive C56--C64. Their common base is a stipulated smooth
trajectory, field, or coefficient family on the stated finite slab.
Their individual hypotheses determine whether that base must satisfy NSE.
An identity valid off the equation is distinguished from its specialization
at a solution. The root solution sets are not asserted nonempty.

For the linearized correspondence, the varying-datum parameter h0 is
explicit. The original fixed-u0 specialization is h0=0. A smooth solution
of the linearized equations need not be asserted to arise by differentiating
a family of nonlinear solutions. The kinematic family construction only
realizes the displayed variation of smooth fields and their flows.

For the quadratic approximation, each exact perturbed trajectory is an
input at its actual datum u0+epsilon*z0 and on the same time interval.
For velocity, material position/velocity, and negative-norm pressure,
uniform constants depend only on the displayed base, linearized field,
viscosity, time interval, and parameter bound. The optional unweighted
pressure estimates additionally depend on the expressly stipulated
uniform exact-velocity bound M_*. None of these estimates manufactures
exact perturbed trajectories.

53.2. Three exact composition routes

Route X: differentiated mechanics.
  ID01--ID04 and ID16--ID17
    -> parameter-dependent flow/coordinate identities in ID40
    -> the off-equation differentiated residual in ID41
    -> the linearized correspondence and stability in ID42.

For an arbitrary orientation-preserving family, the decisive identity
uses the full Jacobian-weighted residual:
  R_M^J(eta_s,pi_s)
    =eta_s,tt+A_s^T grad_a pi_s
       -nu J_s^(-1) Div_a(J_s D_a eta_s,t A_s A_s^T)
    =R_E(u_s,p_s) o eta_s.
At s=0, with W=partial_s eta_s,
  partial_s R_M^J
    =(partial_s R_E) o eta+(D_x R_E o eta)W.
At a volume-preserving base, arbitrary deformations still contribute
the term -nu(D_aV A A^T)grad_a j, where j=partial_s J_s.
For volume-preserving tangent variations j=0, the formula reduces to
the derivative of the root material operator. At an exact base solution
the term (D_x R_E o eta)W also vanishes. These two restrictions are
separate. The inverse and pressure variations retain their exact gauges.

Route XI: differential/integral representation.
  actual Fourier coefficients, rapid decay, and ID21--ID22
    -> ID43 finite-slab heat/Duhamel identity
    -> ID44 smooth projected/pressure/classical equivalence
    -> ID45 two-time material representation.

For s<=t, the material heat transport is
  G_eta(t,s)=U_eta(t) S_nu(t-s) U_eta(s)^(-1).
Its derivative contains both material transport and the material
Laplacian. The time arguments on the two pullbacks are different.
No substitution of the fixed-configuration semigroup S_eta(t-s) for this
two-time operator occurs. The nonlinear source remains explicit.

Route XII: exact quadratic remainder and material comparison.
  pointwise bilinear evaluation + actual pressure reconstruction
    -> ID46 polarized nonlinear and pressure identities;
  ID46 + a stipulated exact base + a stipulated linearized field
    -> the actual epsilon^2 residual in ID47;
  that residual + ID33's forced relative-energy comparison
    -> the conditional uniform quadratic velocity/error estimates;
  ID40's kinematic variation + ID35's actual flow comparison + ID47
    -> ID48 material residual, displacement, and velocity estimates.

The source pressure of u+epsilon*z is the full normalized quadratic
pressure. Its epsilon^2 contribution is retained when identifying the
projected residual. An unprojected pressure omission would change the
residual and is not an allowed composition.

53.4. Preserved type, mean, time, and regularity guards

MEANS:
  P_0=I. Base velocity means are arbitrary. Linearized means are conserved.
  A mean-zero linearized field admits the homogeneous spectral-gap bound.
  Centering a nonzero-mean variation introduces its explicit forcing term.

PRESSURE:
  Every reconstructed pressure has zero spatial mean. Pressure differences
  and derivatives retain that normalization. The negative-Sobolev pressure
  estimate in Section 51 has its stated norm and does not assert an
  unweighted L2 estimate under weaker hypotheses.

TIME:
  Ordinary temporal derivatives are used in the open finite interval.
  Endpoint conclusions use the stipulated one-sided derivatives and
  continuity. Source predicates requiring all positive times are used
  only after the explicit localization adapters in ID17/ID26.

NONLINEARITY:
  Pointwise first-jet evaluation is a continuous bilinear map between
  finite-dimensional/operator normed spaces. This does not identify
  convection with a bounded map L2 x L2 -> L2.

MATERIAL GEOMETRY:
  Flow differences use the fixed identity-normalized lifts. L2 bounds are
  transported using actual volume-preserving maps. No C1 flow estimate
  is inferred from L2 velocity control alone.

SOURCE ADMISSIONS:
  M18--M20 remain optional catalog entries. No AX6 admission or unresolved
  global existence assertion enters the new identities or the root.

54.0. Data and logical scope

I=[0,T], nu>0, lambda_1=4 pi^2, |Omega|=1.
All space/time fields and parameter families are jointly smooth, with
continuous one-sided temporal derivatives at the endpoints, as in §1.
B(a,b)=(a dot grad)b; P is the full-mean Leray projection, P_0=I.
The actual symmetric normalized pressure K is exactly (51.2):
  K(a,b)_hat(0)=0,
  K(a,b)_hat(k)=-sum_ij k_i k_j |k|^(-2)(a_i b_j)_hat(k), k!=0,
for smooth solenoidal a,b. Thus
  K(a,b)=K(b,a),
  grad K(a,b)=-Q[B(a,b)+B(b,a)]/2,
  K(a,b)=K(a^circ,b^circ),     p[a]=K(a,a).              (54.1)
No new pressure convention is introduced.

The projected linearized operator is
  L_u h=h_t+P[B(u,h)+B(h,u)]-nu Delta h.
The pressure-retaining operator is
  L_u^p(h,r)=h_t+B(u,h)+B(h,u)+grad r-nu Delta h.
The superscript p labels this two-input operator; its coefficients
only involve u. All supplemental evolution fields below are supplied
smooth fields. Their existence for arbitrary data is not asserted.

54.1.1. Mixed residual identity, including nonzero mixed field jet

Let (u^{s,r},p^{s,r}) be any smooth two-parameter family. At (s,r)=(0,0)
write
  u=u^{0,0}, p=p^{0,0},
  z_1=partial_s u, z_2=partial_r u, h=partial_s partial_r u,
  q_1=partial_s p, q_2=partial_r p, q_{12}=partial_s partial_r p.
With R_E as in (48.1), the exact identity is
  partial_s partial_r R_E(u^{s,r},p^{s,r})
    =L_u^p(h,q_{12})+B(z_1,z_2)+B(z_2,z_1).            (54.2)
In particular the mixed jet h need not vanish.

Derivation: for every component i,
  partial_s partial_r(sum_j u_j partial_j u_i)
   =sum_j[h_j partial_j u_i+u_j partial_j h_i
          +(z_1)_j partial_j(z_2)_i
          +(z_2)_j partial_j(z_1)_i].
The other residual terms are linear and commute with parameter
derivatives. ML-O18 applies to each actual jointly smooth finite-
dimensional component. M49 identifies the component expression;
ML-B01--ML-B03 apply only to the finite jet evaluation (M,x) |-> M x.
No bilinear L2 convection estimate is used.

At t=0 or T, ML-V02 applies to the bounded finite-dimensional
bilinear evaluation beta(M,x)=Mx, with f(t)=D_xu(t,x), g(t)=u(t,x),
their supplied within derivatives on Icc 0 T, and the real scalar
field. Repeated coordinate derivatives give the corresponding endpoint
jet expressions without converting a within derivative into an
unrestricted derivative.

For the coefficient/mean extraction steps, let X=C(Omega;R^3) with
its sup norm. Joint smoothness on compact parameter/space subslabs
makes each parameter field map C^n into X: the ordinary Taylor
remainder is uniform in x, and induction applies to every parameter
partial. Each fixed Fourier coefficient and the mean is a bounded
real-linear map from X into its finite real or complex target;
its norm is at most one by |Omega|=1 and character modulus one.
ML-V05 preserves C^n under these bounded maps. ML-V06 identifies
iterated within derivatives with the bounded map applied to the
iterated derivative: use an open parameter rectangle, its UniqueDiffOn
property, membership at the base, and explicit i<=n. Real and imaginary
parts are handled as real-linear coordinates. This gives actual mixed
coefficient/mean derivative commutation; it does not apply ML-V06 to
unbounded convection or the Laplacian on L2.

If every family member is solenoidal, then div z_1=div z_2=div h=0.
If every family member is an exact NSE root, (54.2) yields
  L_u h+P[B(z_1,z_2)+B(z_2,z_1)]=0.                    (54.3)
Equation (54.3) is also considered independently for supplied smooth
u,z_1,z_2,h. The family interpretation is an implication, not an
existence theorem for a parameter-dependent nonlinear solution map.

54.1.2. Exact mixed pressure and zero-mode ledger

Assume u,z_1,z_2,h are smooth solenoidal fields and (54.3) holds.
Define the actual normalized scalar
  q_{12}=2K(u,h)+2K(z_1,z_2).                           (54.4)
Equation (54.1) gives
  grad q_{12}
    =-Q[B(u,h)+B(h,u)+B(z_1,z_2)+B(z_2,z_1)].
Since h_t and Delta h are solenoidal, (54.3) implies
  L_u^p(h,q_{12})+B(z_1,z_2)+B(z_2,z_1)=0.             (54.5)
Conversely, applying P to (54.5) gives (54.3). If another normalized
smooth scalar satisfies (54.5), subtraction gives grad difference=0;
Fourier injectivity and the zero mode give equality to (54.4).
Thus (54.3) is equivalent to (54.5) with its unique normalized pressure.

For the additional source route, set
 C=B(u,h)+B(h,u)+B(z_1,z_2)+B(z_2,z_1),
 b=datumFourierCoeff C.
Smoothness and the uniform coefficient estimates give exactly
  forall i, RapidScalarFourier (fun k => b k i);
reality of C gives SpectralReality b. M53 supplies rapid normalized
pressure coefficients. M54 then gives the literal Fourier integrals
  datumFourierCoeff(gradient(infiniteTransportPressure b))
       =fun k i => coefficientLeray k (b k) i-b k i.
M50 and the finite coordinate multiplier calculation identify this
normalized scalar with (54.4). M10 identifies the actual smooth
gradient with -Q C. The zero coefficient remains included, with
coefficientLeray 0=I and the normalized scalar coefficient equal to
zero. Joint time/parameter smoothness still uses the independent
uniform derivative argument, not M53 or M54 alone.

For an actual exact family, uniqueness gives p^{s,r}=K(u^{s,r},u^{s,r}).
Twice differentiating the bilinear formula proves (54.4) directly.
All differentiations of the Fourier series have the uniform rapid
coefficient bounds from ID07 and ID46 on compact parameter subslabs.
M08 alone is not used to infer joint parameter/time smoothness.

Periodic integration of B(a,b)=div(b tensor a), div a=0, gives
  mean h(t)=mean h(0),
for every solution of (54.3). Likewise first jets satisfying L_u z_i=0
have mean z_i(t)=mean z_i(0). Constant velocity modes are retained.
A constant h or z_i can contribute to the projected transport in
(54.3), although K eliminates constant modes in its two arguments.

54.1.3. Symmetry and explicit uniqueness

The forcing in (54.3) and pressure (54.4) are symmetric in z_1,z_2.
For fixed u,z_1,z_2 and initial h(0), two supplied solutions differ by
k with L_u k=0 and k(0)=0. The first-variation energy estimate ID42,
or its direct periodic inner-product calculation, gives k=0.
Therefore the mixed second jet is symmetric whenever the swapped
problems have the same mixed initial datum. This uniqueness result
does not assert the existence of either second-jet problem.

L49.a = actual mixed derivative formula (54.2), including h.
L49.b = projected/full equation equivalence and pressure (54.4).
L49.c = arbitrary-mean conservation, joint smoothness, normalized uniqueness.
L49.d = swap symmetry conditional on supplied solutions and equal initial jet.

54.2.1. Exact second kinematic and pressure pullback identities

For the actual identity-normalized flows eta^{s,r} of u^{s,r}, define
  eta=eta^{0,0}, F=D_a eta, A=F^{-1},
  W_1=partial_s eta, W_2=partial_r eta, H=partial_s partial_r eta,
  pi^{s,r}=p^{s,r} o eta^{s,r},
  rho_i=partial_i pi, rho_{12}=partial_s partial_r pi.
The symbol H in this section denotes the mixed displacement, not D_aW.
All compositions in the following display are at the base eta:

  H_t=(D_xu o eta)H+h o eta
       +(D_xz_1 o eta)W_2+(D_xz_2 o eta)W_1
       +(D_x^2u o eta)[W_1,W_2],                         (54.6)
  rho_{12}=q_{12} o eta+(D_xq_1 o eta)W_2
       +(D_xq_2 o eta)W_1+(D_x^2p o eta)[W_1,W_2]
       +(D_xp o eta)H.                                  (54.7)
Here D of a scalar is its row covector acting on the displayed vector.
Both formulas follow by applying (49.4) twice and collecting the
four first-derivative terms and the Hessian term. ML-O18 supplies
mixed partial symmetry. In particular H(0)=0 and H_t(0)=h(0), since
eta^{s,r}(0)=id and W_1(0)=W_2(0)=0.

Conversely, for given u,z_1,z_2,h the first kinematic equations (49.5)
and (54.6), with zero initial displacements, are linear ODEs in the
unknown displacement at each successive order. Their coefficients
and forcing are smooth and bounded on the compact slab. Integrating-
factor/Picard iteration and the finite-slab continuation in ID01 give
unique smooth W_1,W_2,H. Equations (49.5),(54.6),(54.7) then have literal
inverse formulas for z_i,h,q_i,q_{12}, by subtracting their displayed
transport terms and composing with eta^{-1}.

Actual realization of these jets requires no nonlinear NSE family:
  v^{s,r}=u+s z_1+r z_2+s r h,
  p^{s,r}=p+s q_1+r q_2+s r q_{12}.
This is a supplied smooth periodic family on a compact parameter
rectangle. Its flows exist on I by the compact-torus ODE construction
in ID01; parameter smoothness is the variational induction of §17.6.
Differentiating those flows and using ODE uniqueness identifies their
jets with W_1,W_2,H. If all four velocity fields are solenoidal, every
v^{s,r} is solenoidal and these actual flows preserve volume.

54.2.2. Second determinant and second pressure-gauge constraints

Set M_i=D_aW_i A and M_{12}=D_aH A. At J=det F=1,
  J_i=tr M_i,
  J_{12}=tr M_{12}+tr M_1 tr M_2-tr(M_1 M_2),            (54.8)
  A_{12}=A(D_aW_1)A(D_aW_2)A
         +A(D_aW_2)A(D_aW_1)A-A(D_aH)A.                (54.9)
To derive (54.8), differentiate J_s=J tr(F^{-1}F_s), use
A_r=-AF_r A, and cyclicity of finite trace. Formula (54.9) is the
second derivative of AF=I. Every matrix inverse is taken at invertible
F; the concrete Fin 3 determinant identity ML-O11 and inverse
identities ML-O15/ML-O16 retain that hypothesis.

For first solenoidal jets tr M_1=tr M_2=0, the second volume constraint is
  J_{12}=0  <->  tr(D_aH A)=tr(M_1 M_2).                 (54.10)
It is not tr(D_aH A)=0 in general.

More precisely, differentiate the exact Jacobian equation
J_t=J (div v^{s,r}) o eta^{s,r} twice. At a solenoidal base and for
solenoidal first jets all terms except one vanish, giving
  partial_t J_{12}=(div h) o eta,   J_{12}(0)=0.          (54.11)
Thus, under the displayed kinematic reconstruction and first tangent
constraints, div h=0 iff J_{12}=0. This proves both directions of the
second-order volume correspondence without postulating volume
preservation of a hypothetical exact NSE family.

At the base J=1, change of variables followed by two parameter
 derivatives of the fixed-domain integral gives
  integral q_{12}
   =integral[rho_{12}+rho_1 J_2+rho_2 J_1+pi J_{12}].     (54.12)
The two first-J terms remain for arbitrary deformations. When the
first and second volume constraints hold,
  mean q_{12}=0  <->  mean rho_{12}=0.                    (54.13)
The mixed parameter derivative can pass through the integral because
all derivatives are uniformly bounded on the compact parameter/time/
space slab. ML-K02 is applied successively with these actual bounded
integrable majorants. This also follows from twice applying uniform
finite-interval FTC. No pressure gauge is dropped in the converse.

54.2.3. Full second off-shell residual identity

Use the actual J-weighted residual R_M^J from (49.14), including when
nearby family members are not volume preserving. At (s,r)=(0,0), set
  E=R_E(u,p), E_i=partial_i R_E, E_{12}=partial_s partial_r R_E.
Twice differentiating R_M^J=R_E o eta gives the exact five-term formula
  partial_s partial_r R_M^J
    =E_{12} o eta+(D_xE_1 o eta)W_2+(D_xE_2 o eta)W_1
       +(D_x^2E o eta)[W_1,W_2]+(D_xE o eta)H.           (54.14)
This holds before the base or first variations satisfy any equation.
The five terms are respectively the mixed field residual, two moving-
evaluation first residuals, the Hessian of the base residual, and the
base-gradient/mixed-displacement term. The J-dependent Piola and
Laplacian factors are contained in the actual R_M^J; they are not
silently replaced by the volume-preserving formula off shell.

If E=E_1=E_2=0, then their spatial derivatives also vanish, and (54.2)
yields
  partial_s partial_r R_M^J
   =U_eta{L_u^p(h,q_{12})+B(z_1,z_2)+B(z_2,z_1)}.        (54.15)
Since U_eta is invertible, this residual vanishes iff (54.5) holds.
With (54.10),(54.13), the maps (54.6),(54.7) give a bijection of the
supplied normalized second Eulerian/material jet solution sets over
fixed supplied first jets and fixed second initial datum. For a
solenoidal realizing family J identically equals one and the same
mixed residual is the root material residual. This is an exact jet
bijection, not a new assertion of family existence or global regularity.

L50.a = second kinematic/pressure pullbacks and literal inverse maps.
L50.b = determinant and inverse formulas (54.8)--(54.11).
L50.c = mixed normalization with all Jacobian terms (54.12)--(54.13).
L50.d = all five off-shell terms in (54.14), followed by (54.15).
L50.e = actual polynomial-family realization and second-jet inverse laws.

54.3.1. Explicit polynomial residual and full pressure

Supply a smooth root u, a first jet z and a diagonal second jet h with
  L_u z=0,
  L_u h+2P B(z,z)=0,
  div z=div h=0, z(0)=z0, h(0)=h0.                       (54.16)
The data z0,h0 are smooth solenoidal, with arbitrary means. Set
  q=2K(u,z), r=2K(u,h)+2K(z,z),
  v^epsilon=u+epsilon z+(epsilon^2/2)h,
  p_2^epsilon=p+epsilon q+(epsilon^2/2)r.
The exact normalized pressure of the ansatz is
  p_app^epsilon=K(v^epsilon,v^epsilon)
    =p_2^epsilon+epsilon^3 K(z,h)+(epsilon^4/4)K(h,h).     (54.17)
Define actual smooth solenoidal mean-zero fields
  g_3=P[B(z,h)+B(h,z)]/2,
  g_4=P B(h,h)/4.
Bilinear expansion using (54.16) gives
  R_E(v^epsilon,p_app^epsilon)
     =epsilon^3 g_3+epsilon^4 g_4=:f^epsilon.             (54.18)
The factors 1/2 and 1/4 originate from the Taylor coefficient epsilon^2/2.
For the truncated pressure p_2^epsilon the residual is instead
  R_E(v^epsilon,p_2^epsilon)
    =(epsilon^3/2)[B(z,h)+B(h,z)]
      +(epsilon^4/4)B(h,h).                              (54.19)
These projected and unprojected residuals are distinguished explicitly.

For example,
 ||g_3||_2 <= (||z||_infinity ||Dh||_2
                          +||h||_infinity ||Dz||_2)/2,
 ||g_4||_2 <= ||h||_infinity ||Dh||_2/4.
Full means remain in these transport bounds. Periodic divergence
identities give mean f^epsilon=0 and
  mean v^epsilon=mean u0+epsilon mean z0
                              +(epsilon^2/2)mean h0.     (54.20)

54.3.2. Uniform order-three Eulerian certificate

Fix epsilon_*>0. For each |epsilon|<=epsilon_*, quantify over ANY
supplied smooth exact root (u^epsilon,p^epsilon) on the SAME slab I
with datum
  u0+epsilon z0+(epsilon^2/2)h0.                          (54.21)
There is no assertion that such roots exist for every epsilon.
Define known reference functions
  a_u(t)=max_{x,|xi|=1}[-xi^T S_u(t,x)xi],
  a_*(t)=a_u(t)+epsilon_*||S_z(t)||_infinity,op
                    +(epsilon_*^2/2)||S_h(t)||_infinity,op,
  alpha_*=a_*-nu lambda_1,
  b_*=||g_3||_2+epsilon_*||g_4||_2,
  E_*(t,s)=exp(integral_s^t alpha_*(r)dr),
  C_3(t)=integral_0^t E_*(t,s)b_*(s)ds.                  (54.22)
All are continuous and finite; a_*>=0 because div u=0. For any allowed
epsilon, the negative strain of v^epsilon is bounded by a_* and
||f^epsilon||_2<=|epsilon|^3 b_*.

Put e=u^epsilon-v^epsilon, Y=||e||_2^2. Initial e and its mean vanish.
Subtracting (54.18) from the exact equation, and pairing with e, gives
 (1/2)Y'+nu||De||_2^2
    =-integral e^T S_{v^epsilon}e-<f^epsilon,e>.          (54.23)
The exact velocity u^epsilon appears only in a cancelling solenoidal
transport term B(u^epsilon,e). Thus no derivative bound on u^epsilon
enters the certificate. Parseval and mean e=0 give
 (1/2)Y'<=alpha_*Y+|epsilon|^3 b_* sqrt(Y).
For y_delta=sqrt(Y+delta^2),
 y_delta'<=alpha_*y_delta+|epsilon|^3 b_*+delta|alpha_*|.
Multiplying by exp(-integral_0^t alpha_*), applying finite-slab FTC,
and letting delta decrease to zero gives
  ||u^epsilon(t)-u(t)-epsilon z(t)-(epsilon^2/2)h(t)||_2
      <=|epsilon|^3 C_3(t).                              (54.24)
This also covers negative alpha_* and zeros of Y.
Returning to (54.23) before the gap was absorbed yields
 (1/2)||e(t)||_2^2+nu integral_0^t||De||_2^2
    <=|epsilon|^6 integral_0^t[a_* C_3^2+b_* C_3].         (54.25)
Hence, with C_3^max=sup_I C_3 and J_3=int_0^T[a_*C_3^2+b_*C_3],
 ||e||_{L2(I;H1)}
    <=|epsilon|^3[T(C_3^max)^2+J_3/nu]^(1/2).            (54.26)
For epsilon!=0, the actual supplied family therefore satisfies
 ||2(u^epsilon-u-epsilon z)/epsilon^2-h||_{L_infinity L2}
       <=2|epsilon| C_3^max.                             (54.27)
The family and common slab remain premises of this statement.

54.3.3. Pressure certificate in the fixed stated negative norm

Use exactly dot H^-2 and C_Omega from (51.11). Set
 N_*=||u^circ||_2+epsilon_*||z^circ||_2
                         +(epsilon_*^2/2)||h^circ||_2.
The actual tensor difference and (51.12) give
 ||p^epsilon-p_app^epsilon||_{dot H^-2}
   <=C_Omega[2N_*+|epsilon|^3 C_3]|epsilon|^3 C_3.         (54.28)
Combining this with (54.17) yields
 ||p^epsilon-p_2^epsilon||_{dot H^-2}
   <=|epsilon|^3 C_Omega{
       [2N_*+epsilon_*^3 C_3]C_3
       +||z^circ||_2||h^circ||_2
       +(epsilon_*/4)||h^circ||_2^2}.                     (54.29)
Only reference norms occur. This is not a uniform unweighted L2
pressure estimate; no such additional conclusion is claimed here.

54.3.4. Order-three material certificate at fixed labels

Let eta^epsilon and chi^epsilon be the actual normalized flows of
u^epsilon and v^epsilon, and use their canonical periodic Euclidean
lifts with identical initial lift. Define
 ell_1=||Du||_infinity,op+epsilon_*||Dz||_infinity,op
                         +(epsilon_*^2/2)||Dh||_infinity,op,
 D_3(t)=integral_0^t exp(integral_s^t ell_1(r)dr)C_3(s)ds.
Volume preservation of eta^epsilon and the Lipschitz bound on the
known v^epsilon give, by the same L2 feedback calculation as ID48,
 ||eta_tilde^epsilon-chi_tilde^epsilon||_2<=|epsilon|^3D_3,
 ||(eta^epsilon)_t-(chi^epsilon)_t||_2
      <=|epsilon|^3(C_3+ell_1D_3).                        (54.30)
Indeed their difference derivative is
 e o eta^epsilon+v^epsilon o eta^epsilon-v^epsilon o chi^epsilon;
its first term has L2 norm ||e||_2 by volume preservation. Integrating
this exact identity with a regularized norm proves (54.30).

An explicit third-parameter-derivative bound converts chi^epsilon to
the genuine second material jet. For j=1,2,3 and j=0,1,2 respectively,
set
 ell_j=||D^j u||_infinity+epsilon_*||D^j z||_infinity
                           +(epsilon_*^2/2)||D^j h||_infinity,
 A_j=||D^j z||_infinity+epsilon_*||D^j h||_infinity,
 H_j=||D^j h||_infinity, j=0,1.
Derivative tensors use the multilinear operator norm; D^0 is the
field norm. These definitions agree with ell_1 above.
Define B_1,B_2,B_3 by zero initial values and scalar equations
 B_1'=ell_1 B_1+A_0,
 B_2'=ell_1 B_2+ell_2 B_1^2+2A_1 B_1+H_0,
 B_3'=ell_1 B_3+3ell_2 B_1B_2+ell_3 B_1^3
                    +3A_1 B_2+3A_2 B_1^2+3H_1 B_1.     (54.31)
Their explicit meaning is the finite integrating-factor integrals;
all B_i are nonnegative. Let K_3 be the entire right side of the last
equation.

To verify every coefficient, write X=partial_epsilon chi^epsilon,
Y=partial_epsilon^2 chi^epsilon, Z=partial_epsilon^3 chi^epsilon and
v=v^epsilon. The parameter-differentiated flow equations are
 X_t=Dv X+v_epsilon,
 Y_t=Dv Y+D^2v[X,X]+2Dv_epsilon X+v_epsilon,epsilon,
 Z_t=Dv Z+3D^2v[X,Y]+D^3v[X,X,X]
                  +3Dv_epsilon Y+3D^2v_epsilon[X,X]
                  +3Dv_epsilon,epsilon X.               (54.32)
Every coefficient is evaluated at chi^epsilon; v_epsilon=z+epsilon h,
v_epsilon,epsilon=h and v_epsilon,epsilon,epsilon=0. Applying the
pointwise norm inequality successively and then taking the label
supremum gives ||X||_infinity<=B_1, ||Y||_infinity<=B_2,
||Z||_infinity<=B_3 and ||Z_t||_infinity<=K_3, uniformly for the closed
parameter interval. These derivatives exist by the same actual smooth
parameter-flow construction used in ID50.

At epsilon=0 set W=X|_0, H=Y|_0, V=u o eta. Equations (54.6) for equal
first directions identify these as the first and diagonal second
material jets. Three one-dimensional FTC integrations, including for
negative epsilon by interval reversal, give the Taylor bound
 ||chi_tilde^epsilon-eta_tilde-epsilon W-(epsilon^2/2)H||_infinity
       <=|epsilon|^3 B_3/6,
 ||(chi^epsilon)_t-V-epsilon W_t-(epsilon^2/2)H_t||_infinity
       <=|epsilon|^3 K_3/6.                              (54.33)
Combining (54.30),(54.33), and |Omega|=1, gives the actual material
second-jet certificate
 ||eta_tilde^epsilon-eta_tilde-epsilon W-(epsilon^2/2)H||_2
       <=|epsilon|^3(D_3+B_3/6),
 ||(eta^epsilon)_t-V-epsilon W_t-(epsilon^2/2)H_t||_2
       <=|epsilon|^3(C_3+ell_1D_3+K_3/6).                 (54.34)
Every derivative norm on the right belongs to the stipulated reference
u,z,h. No spatial derivative norm of the exact perturbed flow appears.

54.3.5. Source specialization and independent edge obligations

with the displayed positive regularization and its vanishing delta
correction. All FTC and comparison hypotheses are on the finite slab;
ID17 is used if a source theorem is stated for locally extended curves.

continuous positive integrating-factor kernels in (54.30)--(54.34).
The third-parameter chain rules in (54.32) are finite-coordinate product
and composition rules, repeated after the actual smoothness proof;
there is no unverified Banach-space convection derivative premise.

55.0. Exact common data and operator conventions

Fix nu>0, T>0, I=[0,T], Omega=R^3/Z^3 with volume one.
All fields below are real and jointly smooth on I x Omega, including
continuous one-sided temporal derivatives of every order at endpoints.
Let v be ANY supplied smooth solenoidal field. Its mean may depend on
time; v need not satisfy NSE. P is the full-mean orthogonal Leray
projection from (50.1), Q=I-P, and B(a,b)=(a dot grad)b.
Pairings and norms without further subscripts are real L2(Omega).

Define, on smooth solenoidal fields,

 A_v z := P[B(v,z)+B(z,v)]-nu Delta z,
 A_v^dagger psi := P[-B(v,psi)+(D_xv)^T psi]-nu Delta psi,
 L_v z := z_t+A_v z.                                      (55.1)

The dagger in (55.1) denotes the actual spatial pairing transpose on
the smooth solenoidal core. No equality of maximal unbounded-operator
adjoint domains is asserted by this notation.

Let h in C_infinity_sigma(Omega) and
 g in C_infinity(I x Omega;R^3), div g=0.
The goal on any smooth solenoidal z is

 J_{g,h}(z)=<z(T),h>+integral_0^T <z(t),g(t)> dt.           (55.2)

General smooth vector h,g yield the same goal after replacing them
by Ph,Pg. Constants are included in P; no mean-zero goal assumption
occurs.

55.1.1. Literal spatial pairing identity

For smooth solenoidal z,psi, periodic integration by parts gives

 <B(v,z),psi>=-<z,B(v,psi)>,
 <B(z,v),psi>=<z,(D_xv)^T psi>,
 <Delta z,psi>=-sum_j <partial_j z,partial_j psi>
               =<z,Delta psi>.

The first equality follows by integrating
 partial_j(v_j z_i psi_i), summing i,j and using div v=0.
The second is the finite transpose identity for the matrix D_xv.
The third is M51 applied first to (psi,z), then to (z,psi),
with real inner-product symmetry. Orthogonality of P and Pz=z,
Ppsi=psi then gives

                 <A_v z,psi>=<z,A_v^dagger psi>.          (55.3)

M51 requires exactly smoothness and periodicity of both spatial
arguments; these hold for every displayed time slice. Its conclusion
is bilinear Laplacian integration by parts, not merely self-energy.
M02 is applied to the componentwise products above after the smooth
product/coordinate-derivative identities. ML-N08 moves the actual
orthogonal P between the two L2 arguments. ID16 identifies the torus
pairings with the source unitCube integrals.

55.1.2. Finite-slab adjoint existence with no nonlinear existence premise

The theorem proved in this subsection is

 forall nu>0,T>0,v,g,h as in 55.0,
 exists! psi in C_infinity(I x Omega;R^3):
   div psi=0,
   -psi_t+A_v^dagger psi=g,
   psi(T)=h.                                             (55.4)

Proof. Put tau=T-t, a(tau)=v(T-tau), b(tau)=g(T-tau),
and Theta(tau)=psi(T-tau). The forward equation is

 Theta_tau+P[-B(a,Theta)+(D_xa)^T Theta]-nu Delta Theta=b,
 Theta(0)=h.                                             (55.5)

Let Pi_N retain all Fourier frequencies |k|<=N, INCLUDING k=0.
It preserves real fields and solenoidality, commutes with derivatives
and P, and is self-adjoint and contractive in each Fourier Sobolev
norm. Its range on real solenoidal fields is finite dimensional.
Define Theta_N by the actual finite system

 Theta_N' + Pi_N P[-B(a,Theta_N)+(D_xa)^T Theta_N]
                -nu Delta Theta_N = Pi_N b,
 Theta_N(0)=Pi_N h.                                      (55.6)

In a real orthonormal basis this is c_N'=M_N(tau)c_N+d_N(tau),
with smooth matrix and vector coefficients on [0,T]. Picard iteration
on the integral equation, or ML-O01 followed by its bounded linear
continuation, defines its solution on the entire finite interval.
More explicitly, if ||M_N||<=K_N and ||d_N||<=D_N, consecutive integral
iterates have a bound C_N K_N^j T^(j+1)/(j+1)!, so their series
converges uniformly on [0,T]; termwise integration gives the solution.
The corresponding homogeneous difference is zero by ML-O03 or the
same iterated bound. This construction imposes no N-uniform matrix
bound and uses no nonlinear Galerkin solution predicate.

For every integer m>=0 define
 |w|_m^2=sum_{|alpha|<=m} ||partial^alpha w||_2^2.
For each alpha the highest transport term is
 -B(a,partial^alpha Theta_N). Its pairing with
 partial^alpha Theta_N vanishes because div a=0.
The remaining transport terms are exactly

 -sum_{0<beta<=alpha} binom(alpha,beta)
      B(partial^beta a,partial^(alpha-beta)Theta_N).

They contain at most m derivatives of Theta_N. The stretching terms
are exactly

 sum_{beta<=alpha} binom(alpha,beta)
    (D_x partial^beta a)^T partial^(alpha-beta)Theta_N,

and contain at most m derivatives of Theta_N and m+1 derivatives of a.
Pi_N and P disappear in the tested pairing, since every differentiated
Theta_N remains in their range. Cauchy--Schwarz, the finite product
sums and 2ab<=a^2+b^2 therefore yield a constant c_m>0 such that

 (1/2)partial_tau |Theta_N|_m^2
       +nu sum_{|alpha|<=m}||D partial^alpha Theta_N||_2^2
 <= c_m(1+||a(tau)||_{C^(m+1)}) |Theta_N|_m^2
       +(1/2)|b(tau)|_m^2.                               (55.7)

Here ||a||_{C^(m+1)} is the maximum of all componentwise derivative
suprema through m+1, with a fixed finite-dimensional norm convention;
c_m absorbs the finite combinatorial constants. All coefficients are
continuous and bounded on [0,T]. The integrating-factor argument of
ID33, now applied to the nonnegative squared norm, proves

 sup_N sup_tau |Theta_N(tau)|_m <=K_m<infinity              (55.8)

for every m. Norm equivalence with
 ||w||_{H^m}^2=sum_k(1+4*pi^2|k|^2)^m |what(k)|^2
is a finite polynomial comparison; hence (55.8) holds in Fourier H^m.
The equation and the bounds at m+2 additionally give

 sup_N sup_tau ||Theta_N'(tau)||_{H^m}<=K'_m<infinity.    (55.9)

Indeed multiplication by smooth a and D_xa is bounded at each integer
Sobolev order by the same Leibniz calculation, transport uses one
spatial derivative, and Delta uses two. Pi_N and P are contractions.

For fixed m, bounded sets in H^(m+2) have uniformly small H^m Fourier
tails: for R>=1,

 ||(I-Pi_R)w||_{H^m} <= (1+4*pi^2 R^2)^(-1)||w||_{H^(m+2)}.

Together with (55.9), the finite coefficient curves Pi_R Theta_N
are bounded and equicontinuous on [0,T]. Finite-dimensional compactness
on a countable dense time grid and the uniform Lipschitz bound give a
subsequence convergent uniformly in time for each finite R. A diagonal
selection in R and the displayed uniform tail bound gives convergence
in C([0,T];H^m). A second diagonal selection over integer m gives one
subsequence and one Theta with

 Theta_N -> Theta in C([0,T];H^m) for EVERY m>=0.          (55.10)

This compactness step follows directly from finite coefficient
extraction and the Fourier tail bound; it does not require a strong
compactness assertion about the full time-derivative sequence.
Using (55.10) at m+2, every right side of (55.6) converges uniformly
in H^m to the right side of (55.5). For Pi_N acting on the limiting
right side, use its uniform higher-Sobolev bound and the same Fourier
tail inequality. Passing to the integral equation proves
Theta in C^1([0,T];H^m), its actual derivative equal to (55.5), and
Theta(0)=h. Since a,b are smooth, differentiation of (55.5) and
induction give Theta in C^r([0,T];H^m) for every r,m, with one-sided
endpoint derivatives. Specifically, the r-th derivative equation
contains only derivatives of a,b through r and derivatives of Theta
through r; two additional spatial orders are available from (55.10).

For any integer ell>=0, Fourier Cauchy--Schwarz gives

 sum_k |k|^ell |what(k)| <= C_ell ||w||_{H^(ell+2)},

because sum_k(1+|k|^2)^(-2)<infinity in three dimensions. Thus every
mixed time/space derivative has a uniformly convergent Fourier series.
Theta, and hence psi(t)=Theta(T-t), has the stipulated joint smoothness
through both temporal endpoints. Reality and solenoidality pass to
the limit coefficientwise. This establishes existence in (55.4).

55.1.3. Adjoint energy, uniqueness, pressure and mean

Set S_v=(D_xv+(D_xv)^T)/2 and
 a_v(t)=max_{x,|xi|=1}[-xi^T S_v(t,x)xi]>=0.
The maximum exists and is continuous; trace S_v=0 gives nonnegativity.
Pairing (55.5) with Theta gives exactly

 (1/2)partial_tau ||Theta||_2^2+nu||DTheta||_2^2
   =-integral Theta^T S_a Theta+<b,Theta>.                (55.11)

The zero-safe regularized norm argument of ID33 proves

 ||psi(t)||_2 <= exp(integral_t^T a_v)||h||_2
   +integral_t^T exp(integral_t^s a_v)||g(s)||_2 ds.       (55.12)

Apply (55.12) to the difference with h=g=0: uniqueness in (55.4).
No homogeneous spectral-gap term is added: the adjoint mean is not
in general conserved. Its exact ledger is

 -partial_t mean psi(t)+integral (D_xv)^T psi=mean g(t),
 mean psi(T)=mean h.                                     (55.13)

This follows by integrating the full-mean projected equation; the
transport integral vanishes, while the stretching integral is retained.

For c^dagger=-B(v,psi)+(D_xv)^T psi, the actual normalized pressure
chi is defined by ID07's Fourier reconstruction:

 chihat(0)=0,
 chihat(k)=-[k dot chat^dagger(k)]/[2*pi*i*|k|^2], k!=0.

Uniform time/spatial smooth decay of c^dagger implies joint smoothness
of chi; its gradient is -Q c^dagger. Thus (55.4) is equivalent to

 -psi_t-B(v,psi)+(D_xv)^T psi+grad chi-nu Delta psi=g,
 div psi=0, mean chi=0, psi(T)=h.                         (55.14)

This normalized adjoint pressure is unique. It is not identified with
NSE pressure or with the forward linearized pressure q_u[z].

55.1.4. Exact two-sided duality

Let z be ANY stipulated smooth solenoidal field and f=L_v z.
Differentiate its actual L2 pairing with psi, using (55.3)--(55.4):

 partial_t <z,psi>
 =<f-A_v z,psi>+<z,A_v^dagger psi-g>
 =<f,psi>-<z,g>.

Integration gives

 J_{g,h}(z)=<z(0),psi(0)>+integral_0^T <L_v z,psi> dt.    (55.15)

No evolution-existence assumption for z is needed. In particular,
L_v z=f may be either a stipulated linearized equation or the exact
residual identity of a supplied field.

Additional quantified input: (u,p) is any supplied smooth root solution
on I. The comparison v remains arbitrary smooth and solenoidal.
Define

 r_v=v_t+P B(v,v)-nu Delta v,
 e=u-v,
 p[v]=the actual normalized pressure with grad p[v]=-Q B(v,v).

Then

 R_E(v,p[v])=r_v,
 div r_v=0,
 mean r_v=partial_t mean v.                              (55.16)

This identity retains arbitrary mean drift. It follows from P v_t=v_t,
P Delta v=Delta v, and the normalized pressure formula, without
assuming mean v is constant. Subtracting the exact NSE equation and
expanding the bilinear convection gives

             L_v e=-r_v-P B(e,e).                        (55.17)

Let psi be the adjoint from ID52 for the chosen (v,g,h), and define

 E_{g,h}(v;u0):=<u0-v(0),psi(0)>
                   -integral_0^T <r_v,psi> dt.           (55.18)

This depends on the supplied initial datum u0, comparison v and the
constructed linear adjoint; it does not use the unknown error e.
Insert (55.17) into (55.15). Because Ppsi=psi and div e=0,

 <B(e,e),psi>
  =-integral e_i e_j partial_j psi_i
  =-integral e^T S_psi e,
 S_psi=(D_xpsi+(D_xpsi)^T)/2.

Consequently the exact signed error identity is

 J_{g,h}(u)-J_{g,h}(v)
   =E_{g,h}(v;u0)+integral_0^T integral_Omega e^T S_psi e.
                                                               (55.19)

The plus sign in the quadratic correction is fixed by TWO minus
signs: the forcing -P B(e,e) in (55.17) and periodic integration by
parts of B(e,e). Symmetry removes only the antisymmetric part of Dpsi.
No pressure term is omitted: both p and p[v] are normalized, their
gradient difference pairs to zero with the solenoidal psi by M04.

A fully explicit reference-based certificate follows from ID33.
Let

 b_v(t)=||r_v(t)||_2,
 d0=||u0-v(0)||_2,
 Y_v(t)=exp(integral_0^t a_v)d0
           +integral_0^t exp(integral_s^t a_v)b_v(s) ds.

The exact energy identity is

 (1/2)partial_t ||e||_2^2+nu||De||_2^2
   =-integral e^T S_v e-<r_v,e>.                          (55.20)

For its transport cancellation use
 B(u,u)-B(v,v)=B(u,e)+B(e,v); div u=div e=0.
The regularized norm comparison gives ||e(t)||_2<=Y_v(t), even with
nonzero or time-dependent mean e. Therefore

 |J_{g,h}(u)-J_{g,h}(v)-E_{g,h}(v;u0)|
 <= integral_0^T ||S_psi(t)||_{infinity,op} Y_v(t)^2 dt.   (55.21)

Every coefficient on the right is determined by nu,T,u0,v,g,h.
The smooth adjoint constructed in ID52 makes the right side finite.
This is a conditional certificate for a supplied smooth NSE solution;
it proves no existence of that nonlinear solution.

If mean v is constant and equals mean u0, then mean e=0 and the
separate refined certificate replaces a_v by a_v-nu*4*pi^2 in Y_v.
These extra hypotheses are necessary for this homogeneous gap version.
If r_v=0 and v(0)=u0, (55.20) gives e=0, consistently with root
uniqueness; (55.19) then has both estimator and correction equal to zero.

Let eta be the identity-normalized flow of v, independent of any
variation parameter. Since div v=0, eta is volume preserving even
when r_v!=0. Put

 U_t f=f o eta(t), P_t=U_t P U_t^{-1}, S_t=range P_t,
 F=D_a eta, A=F^{-1}, B_t=(D_xv) o eta,
 Delta_t=U_t Delta U_t^{-1},
 Z=U_t z, Psi=U_t psi, F_f=U_t f, G=U_t g,
 H_T=U_T h.                                              (55.22)

Z is the componentwise pullback of an Eulerian perturbation.
It is not delta V, the velocity variation of a varying flow.
For H in S_t set

 nabla_t H=P_t H_t,
 C_t H=P_t(B_t H),
 C_t^dagger H=P_t(B_t^T H).                              (55.23)

At fixed t, C_t is bounded on S_t, C_t^dagger is its actual bounded
Hilbert adjoint, by the finite matrix transpose and P_t symmetry.
Delta_t is symmetric on smooth S_t fields by unitary conjugacy and
M51. These facts do not identify U_t A_v^dagger U_t^{-1} with
C_t^dagger-nu Delta_t: the transport derivative must be included.

The smooth pullback chain rule gives

 P_t Z_t=U_t[z_t+P B(v,z)],
 P_t Psi_t=U_t[psi_t+P B(v,psi)].

Therefore the exact coupled forward/adjoint equations are

 L_v z=f
   iff nabla_t Z+C_t Z-nu Delta_t Z=F_f,

 -psi_t+A_v^dagger psi=g
   iff -nabla_t Psi+C_t^dagger Psi-nu Delta_t Psi=G,
       Psi(T)=H_T.                                      (55.24)

Both sides in each equation are tangent to S_t. Formula (55.24)
holds for arbitrary off-shell v. The chain rule is applied to smooth
fields; no operator-norm differentiability of U_t on all L2 is assumed.

Differentiate P_t Z=Z and P_t Psi=Psi. ID19 gives the bounded
operator derivative dot P_t, and P_t dot P_t P_t=0. Hence

 (I-P_t)Z_t=dot P_t Z,
 (I-P_t)Psi_t=dot P_t Psi,

 Z_t=-C_t Z+nu Delta_t Z+F_f+dot P_t Z,
 Psi_t=C_t^dagger Psi-nu Delta_t Psi-G+dot P_t Psi.        (55.25)

The normal terms dot P_t Z and dot P_t Psi are generally nonzero.
Their pairings with tangent fields vanish separately. Thus

 partial_t <Z,Psi>_a
   =<nabla_t Z,Psi>_a+<Z,nabla_t Psi>_a
   =<F_f,Psi>_a-<Z,G>_a.                               (55.26)

This is metric compatibility of the actual moving constraint.
Integrating yields

 <Z(T),H_T>_a+integral_0^T <Z,G>_a
  =<Z(0),Psi(0)>_a+integral_0^T <F_f,Psi>_a.             (55.27)

Each pairing is exactly its Eulerian counterpart because U_t is a
measure-preserving L2 isometry. The terminal datum is U_T h, not h
at an unchanged spatial label.

For the nonlinear error of ID53, write

 Xi=U_t e, R=U_t r_v,
 mathfrakB_t(H,K)=(D_aK A)H,
 mathfrakS_t(Psi)=((D_aPsi A)+(D_aPsi A)^T)/2.

Then U_t P B(e,e)=P_t mathfrakB_t(Xi,Xi), and (55.17) becomes

 nabla_t Xi+C_t Xi-nu Delta_t Xi
       =-R-P_t mathfrakB_t(Xi,Xi).                       (55.28)

Since D_aPsi A=(D_xpsi) o eta, volume preservation gives

 integral_Omega e^T S_psi e dx
   =integral_Omega Xi^T mathfrakS_t(Psi) Xi da,
 ||Xi||_2=||e||_2,
 ||mathfrakS_t(Psi)||_{infinity,op}=||S_psi||_{infinity,op}.
                                                               (55.29)

Thus the complete goal identity and certified quadratic remainder are
representation invariant:

 J_{g,h}(u)-J_{g,h}(v)
  =<Xi(0),Psi(0)>_a-integral_0^T <R,Psi>_a
       +integral_0^T integral Xi^T mathfrakS_t(Psi)Xi,     (55.30)

 |quadratic remainder|
  <=integral_0^T ||mathfrakS_t(Psi)||_{infinity,op}Y_v^2.

No loss or extra ellipticity constant occurs in this identity: the
metric in the material strain is D_aPsi A, exactly the transported
Eulerian derivative.

55.3.1. On-shell tangent and off-shell residual guards

For the actual varying-flow tangent W of ID40,

 z o eta=W_t-B_t W.                                     (55.31)

Hence the boundary pairing for a supplied linearized field is
 <z,psi>=<W_t-B_t W,Psi>_a. The term B_t W cannot be deleted by
renaming delta V=W_t as the transported perturbation Z.

If v is a root solution, the on-shell identity of ID41 identifies
its Eulerian and material linearized residuals, so (55.24)--(55.27)
compose with the exact linearized bijection of ID42.
For an off-shell varying family, the exact preexisting identity is

 delta R_M^J=U_t(delta R_E)+(D_xR_E o eta)W.              (55.32)

Consequently its pairing has the extra term
 <delta R_M^J,Psi>_a
   =<delta R_E,psi>_x+<(D_xR_E o eta)W,Psi>_a.

This correction vanishes when R_E=0 but is not removed for arbitrary
v. Identities (55.24)--(55.30) instead use one FIXED reference flow,
so they do not differentiate U_t with respect to a family parameter
and do not require or conceal the missing term in (55.32).

  K(a,b)=K(b,a),

56.1.1. Recursive velocity and pressure jets

For every smooth solenoidal field v on Omega, define actual smooth fields
J_n[v] and scalar fields H_n[v] recursively:

  J_0[v]=v,
  J_{n+1}[v]
    =nu Delta J_n[v]
       -sum_{j=0}^n binom(n,j) P B(J_j[v],J_{n-j}[v]),     (56.1)

  H_n[v]
    =sum_{j=0}^n binom(n,j) K(J_j[v],J_{n-j}[v]).          (56.2)

Induction in n gives smoothness, reality, periodicity and solenoidality
of J_n[v]. For n>=1,
  mean J_n[v]=0.                                          (56.3)
Indeed, the Laplacian has zero mean and, for any solenoidal a,
  integral B(a,b)_i dx
    =sum_j integral partial_j(a_j b_i) dx
       -integral (div a)b_i dx=0.
P preserves the zero Fourier coefficient. The induction does not require
mean v=0. Every H_n[v] has zero mean by its definition.

For every (u,p) in E_nu(u0;T), every integer n>=0 and t in [0,T],

  partial_t^n u(t)=J_n[u(t)],
  partial_t^n p(t)=H_n[u(t)].                             (56.4)

Proof. The projected equation is
  u_t=nu Delta u-P B(u,u),                                (56.5)
and normalized pressure uniqueness gives p=K(u,u). Uniform rapid
Fourier decay of all joint derivatives, proved in ID07, permits
termwise time differentiation of P, K and their actual smooth Fourier
series. Delta commutes with time differentiation by joint smoothness.
Repeated product differentiation gives
  partial_t^n B(u,u)
    =sum_{j=0}^n binom(n,j)
        B(partial_t^j u,partial_t^{n-j}u),
and the same identity with K in place of B. Induction, using (56.5),
proves (56.4) in the interior. Continuous one-sided endpoint derivatives
and the same uniform Fourier estimates extend every equality to 0,T.

In particular,
  u_t(t)=nu Delta u(t)-P B(u(t),u(t)),
  u_tt(t)=nu Delta J_1[u(t)]
       -P[B(J_1[u(t)],u(t))+B(u(t),J_1[u(t)])],
  p_t(t)=2K(u(t),J_1[u(t)]).
These formulas concern actual derivatives, not merely formal jets.

56.1.2. Velocity-only interface hypothesis

Fix s>0 and h>0. Suppose
  (u^-,p^-) in E_nu(u0;s),
  (u^+,p^+) in E_nu(v0;h),
  u^-(s)=v0=u^+(0).                                      (56.6)
Define the piecewise pair on [0,s+h] by
  u(t)=u^-(t), p(t)=p^-(t)                  for 0<=t<=s,
  u(t)=u^+(t-s), p(t)=p^+(t-s)              for s<=t<=s+h. (56.7)

For every n>=0 and spatial multi-index alpha, (56.4) gives
  partial_x^alpha partial_t^n u^-(s)
    =partial_x^alpha J_n[v0]
    =partial_x^alpha partial_t^n u^+(0),                  (56.8)
  partial_x^alpha partial_t^n p^-(s)
    =partial_x^alpha H_n[v0]
    =partial_x^alpha partial_t^n p^+(0).                  (56.9)
Thus pressure matching and every higher temporal matching condition
follow from the single velocity-field equality in (56.6).

For completeness, the all-order gluing argument is explicit. If F^- and
F^+ are two component functions with matching endpoint values, and their
one-sided first time derivatives have a common continuous piecewise
extension G, the one-sided fundamental theorem yields on both sides
  F(t,x)=F(s,x)+integral_s^t G(r,x) dr.
Consequently
  [F(s+delta,x)-F(s,x)]/delta
    =integral_0^1 G(s+theta delta,x) dtheta
      ->G(s,x)                                           (56.10)
as delta tends to zero through either sign. On compact coordinate
patches convergence is uniform in x. The spatial derivatives at t=s
are the derivatives of the common smooth trace F(s,.); their two
piecewise extensions agree and are continuous by (56.8)--(56.9).
Apply (56.10) successively to every mixed derivative. Induction gives
all continuous mixed partial derivatives across t=s, hence joint
C-infinity smoothness in the ordinary finite-dimensional charts.

The equation, divergence condition and normalized pressure condition
hold on each side and at the seam by continuity. Therefore
  (u,p) in E_nu(u0;s+h).                                 (56.11)
Conversely, restriction and time translation of a root on [0,s+h]
give (56.6). The two operations are literal inverses.

56.2.1. Two-time flow and reset formulas

For a stipulated root on [0,T], let eta_t be its identity-normalized flow.
For any 0<=s,t<=T define
  chi(t,s)=eta_t circ eta_s^{-1}.
Then
  chi(s,s)=id,
  chi(t,r) circ chi(r,s)=chi(t,s),
  chi(t,s)^{-1}=chi(s,t),                                 (56.12)
  partial_t chi(t,s)=u(t) circ chi(t,s),
  partial_s chi(t,s)(x)=-D_x chi(t,s)(x) u(s,x).            (56.13)
The group identities are substitutions of eta_r^{-1} circ eta_r=id.
The first derivative follows from eta_t'=u(t) circ eta_t. Differentiating
eta_s^{-1} circ eta_s=id gives
  partial_s eta_s^{-1}(x)=-D_x eta_s^{-1}(x)u(s,x),
which proves the second derivative by the chain rule. Every identity
is an identity of torus maps/tangent vectors and retains the exact
one-sided endpoint derivatives. No choice of an inconsistent torus
lift enters the group law.

For 0<=s<T and 0<=tau<=T-s set
  u^[s](tau)=u(s+tau),          p^[s](tau)=p(s+tau),
  eta^[s](tau)=eta(s+tau) circ eta(s)^{-1},
  pi^[s](tau)=pi(s+tau) circ eta(s)^{-1}.                  (56.14)
Then
  eta^[s](0)=id,
  partial_tau eta^[s](0)=u(s),
  (u^[s],p^[s]) in E_nu(u(s);T-s),
  (eta^[s],pi^[s]) in M_nu(u(s);T-s).                    (56.15)
The spatial pressure mean remains zero because eta(s) preserves volume.
Eulerian reconstruction of (eta^[s],pi^[s]) gives exactly the first line
of (56.14), so the material equation follows from ID04 and ID10.
Thus restriction, time translation, and initial-label reset commute
with every root bijection. Reset twice at s and then r equals reset at
s+r whenever 0<=r<T-s; this follows either directly or from (56.12).

For the gluing inputs (56.6), write g=eta^-(s). The glued material fields
are, on the right interval,
  eta(s+tau)=eta^+(tau) circ g,
  V(s+tau)=V^+(tau) circ g,
  pi(s+tau)=pi^+(tau) circ g.                             (56.16)
At tau=0 the position equals g and
  V^+(0) circ g=v0 circ g=V^-(s).
The path in (56.16) is a trajectory of the already-glued Eulerian
velocity with the correct initial labels. ODE uniqueness identifies it
with that velocity's actual smooth flow. Therefore it is jointly smooth
at the seam, and the material equation and pressure normalization hold.

The derivative matrices and pullbacks retain their composition order:
  F(s+tau,a)=F^+(tau,g(a)) D_ag(a),
  A(s+tau,a)=(D_ag(a))^{-1} A^+(tau,g(a)),
  U_{eta(s+tau)}=U_g U_{eta^+(tau)}.                      (56.17)
Because g is volume preserving, every L^p velocity norm and the exact
material dissipation integral agree under this right-label composition.
ML-E02 splits their time integrals at s with both integrability
hypotheses supplied by compact-slab smoothness.

56.2.2. Exact reduced variational transmission condition

Before imposing (56.6), take arbitrary smooth roots on [0,s] and [0,h]
with respective initial data u0 and v0. Define the broken velocity u by
(56.7), ignoring its value at the single seam for the time integral.
For a globally smooth solenoidal w on [0,s+h] with w(0)=w(s+h)=0, define
the broken reduced virtual-work functional by the sum of its two
integrals, using their own smooth fields. Periodic integration by parts
and time integration by parts on each closed slab give
  V_broken(w)
    =integral_Omega [u^-(s)-u^+(0)] dot w(s) dx.            (56.18)
The signs are fixed by the upper endpoint of the left integral and the
lower endpoint of the right integral. The interior terms vanish because
each slab solves NSE and pressure pairs to zero with solenoidal w.

The jump j=u^-(s)-u^+(0) is itself smooth and solenoidal. Choose a smooth
scalar chi with chi(0)=chi(s+h)=0 and chi(s)=1, and put w(t)=chi(t)j.
Equation (56.18) gives
  [forall w, V_broken(w)=0]
    iff ||j||_2^2=0
    iff u^-(s)=u^+(0).                                   (56.19)
The last implication is pointwise because j is continuous. With the
matching condition, ID55 upgrades the broken trajectory to the smooth
root class, and (56.18) is precisely its ordinary reduced LdA identity.

The same condition has a material expression. Glue positions by g as in
(56.16), even before matching velocities. This gives a continuous,
piecewise smooth volume-preserving path. For W(t)=w(t) circ eta(t),
the broken material action and fibre-force variation satisfy
  D_broken(W)
    =integral_Omega [V^-(s)-V^+(0) circ g] dot W(s) da
    =integral_Omega [u^-(s)-u^+(0)] dot w(s) dx.            (56.20)
The first equality follows from integration by parts in time on the
two slabs; the spatial tangent-force terms vanish by the material root
equations. The second is the volume-preserving change of variables
x=g(a). These piecewise virtual displacements are realized by applying
the same smooth, parameter-dependent solenoidal Eulerian variation flow
from ID09 on both pieces; the interface configuration remains common.
Only after (56.19) is established is the glued object asserted to belong
to the root's globally smooth material variational class.

56.3.1. Actual compatible-family bijection

Fix a strictly increasing sequence 0<T_0<T_1<... with T_n tending to
infinity. Let E_n=E_nu(u0;T_n), and write res_n^m for restriction when
n<=m. Define the set
  Lim(E_n)={ (x_n)_n : x_n in E_n and
             res_n^m(x_m)=x_n for every n<=m }.            (56.21)
This is an explicit set of compatible families; the notation introduces
no category-theoretic completeness assumption.

Restriction defines
  Res:E_global -> Lim(E_n).
For a compatible family x_n=(u_n,p_n), define
  u(t,x)=u_n(t,x), p(t,x)=p_n(t,x) whenever t<=T_n.         (56.22)
Compatibility makes these values independent of n. At every finite
time t choose n with t<T_n. On a neighborhood of t inside [0,infinity),
the fields agree with that single finite-slab root. Hence all joint
derivatives exist with the required one-sided convention at zero, and
the NSE identities, initial datum and pressure gauge hold locally.
Restriction to any [0,T] agrees with x_n restricted from a T_n>T.
Therefore (56.22) belongs to E_global. It is inverse to Res pointwise:
  E_global ~= Lim(E_n).                                  (56.23)

The same construction applies to each of N,M,V,D. For N, the moving
region balance is local in time along the compatible flow. For V and D,
each finite-slab predicate is transported through the already proved
root bijections; arbitrary test fields have finite temporal domain.
For M, the identity-normalized configurations are already compatible,
and inverses/derivatives agree on every compact slab by ID01 and ID26.
The naturality in ID56 makes (56.23) commute with all root bijections.

New source specialization.
  ML-V08 = ContDiffOn.iUnion_of_isOpen:
    first construct the actual common function (56.22). On every
    positive-time OPEN spacetime chart with closure in (0,T_n) times
    a spatial chart, use compatibility to identify it with u_n or p_n.
    The source then assembles ContDiffOn over the open union. Its
    hypotheses include smoothness for every patch and openness of
    every set. At t=0 use the first finite slab and ID26 instead.
    ML-V08 supplies no compatibility, no compactness extraction, and
    no finite-slab existence assertion.

56.3.2. Where compatibility comes from

The smooth uniqueness proof ID11 shows each E_n is a subsingleton:
two elements have identical velocities and, by normalized pressure
uniqueness, identical pressures. Therefore
  [forall n, E_n is nonempty]
    iff Lim(E_n) is nonempty
    iff E_global is nonempty.                            (56.24)
For the forward implication, let x_n be the unique element of E_n.
For n<=m, restriction of x_m belongs to E_n, hence equals x_n by
uniqueness. Formula (56.22) then supplies the global solution. Conversely,
a global solution restricts to every E_n. This argument does not require
separately postulating compatibility after uniqueness has been proved.
The statement is an equivalence conditional on the displayed all-n
existence premise. It does not prove that premise for any new datum.

At source level, finite-dimensional ODE uniqueness ML-O03 is used for
material flow compatibility only. It is not the smooth NSE uniqueness
theorem; the latter is the completed energy derivation ID11. The
existence of global finite-dimensional Galerkin solutions M17 likewise
does not discharge the premise on the left of (56.24).

56.3.3. Exact continuation-domain identity from a supplied prefix

Fix a supplied (u,p) in E_nu(u0;s), s>0. For every h>0,
  E_nu(u0;s+h) is nonempty
    iff E_nu(u(s);h) is nonempty.                         (56.25)
Forward: any extended solution agrees with the supplied prefix on [0,s]
by ID11; restriction/time translation is therefore a solution from the
actual datum u(s). Reverse: a supplied solution from u(s) glues to the
prefix by ID55. The normalization and all seam derivatives are supplied
by (56.8)--(56.9), so no additional matching-pressure assumption is
needed. ID56 transports (56.25) to the material and both LdA classes.

Define the finite existence-time set I_E(v) as in Section 11.4. Then
  { h>0 : s+h in I_E(u0) }=I_E(u(s)).                     (56.26)
This is a set identity, valid without a finite/infinite supremum
convention. It transfers any separately established continuation
criterion between the formulations; it supplies no new regularity
criterion and no extension beyond the stipulated prefix by itself.

L55.a ACTUAL_PDE_TIME_JET_RECURSION

58.2. Finite-order normed-curve adapter at temporal endpoints

APPLIES_TO = L49.c,L52.g,L55.a,L55.c; ML-V01,ML-V05,ML-V06.
This expands an already-stated adapter; it adds no new analytic premise.

Let X be either C(Omega;R^d) with the supremum norm, or the corresponding
real L2 space. Choose arbitrary total representatives f_j:R->X,
0<=j<=n, whose restrictions to [0,T] are continuous and satisfy
f_j'=f_{j+1} on (0,T) for j<n, with the stipulated continuous one-sided
derivatives at 0,T. Values outside [0,T] are immaterial. For actual
smooth fields take f_j(t)=partial_t^j f(t,.) on the given slab.
These are X-continuous by compact uniform continuity, since
  ||g||_2 <= ||g||_infinity                         (|Omega|=1).
The fundamental theorem gives, for all s,t in [0,T],
  f_j(t)-f_j(s)=integral_s^t f_{j+1}(r)dr, j<n.
Consequently the actual within-set derivative and every successive
normed derivative are f_{j+1}; the norm remainder is bounded by
  |h| sup_{r between t and t+h} ||f_{j+1}(r)-f_{j+1}(t)||_X=o(|h|).

Fix a FINITE natural order n. Define a function on all real times by
  F_n(t)=sum_{j=0}^n t^j f_j(0)/j!                       if t<0,
  F_n(t)=f_0(t)                                         if 0<=t<=T,
  F_n(t)=sum_{j=0}^n (t-T)^j f_j(T)/j!                  if t>T.
At each seam, all derivatives through order n match. The preceding
integral difference quotient proves two-sided differentiability of
each derivative of order <n, while the nth derivative is continuous.
Induction gives F_n in C^n(R;X), with F_n=f_0 on [0,T]. Set-congruence
of within-set smoothness transfers this conclusion to the chosen
total representative f_0. Thus
  ContDiffOn R n f_0 (Icc 0 T)
and the corresponding ContDiffWithinAt statements hold at both
endpoints for every finite n. No single analytic extension and no
NSE solution outside the original interval is asserted or needed.

Each Fourier component functional
  Lambda_{k,i}(w)=integral_Omega exp(-2*pi*i*k.x) w_i(x) dx
and the mean functional is bounded real-linear on these X, with norm
at most one by the character modulus and unit-volume Cauchy--Schwarz.
For the complex coefficient codomain use its real normed structure.
ML-V05 applies to this ACTUAL continuous linear map and the preceding
normed curve. ML-V06 applies with n a finite order, i<=n, t in Icc 0 T,
and UniqueDiffOn R (Icc 0 T) from ML-T06 using T>0. Its conclusion is
literal coefficient/mean differentiation at the temporal endpoints.
ML-V01 similarly uses the actual Hilbert within-derivative witnesses.
The Laplacian, convection and nonlinear pressure assignment are not
substituted for these bounded coefficient/mean functionals.

For parameter directions of ID49, the base lies in an open rectangle;
uniform multivariable Taylor remainders give the analogous normed
Frechet derivatives there. No temporal endpoint extension is required
for that open-parameter application.
